role: All-rounder elemental combo controller with conditional burst, AoE chip + control, and stacking debuffs
signature_mechanic: Avatar Cycle: starts Air-aligned (mag 0); each skill matching current alignment advances Air->Water->Earth->Fire (0->1->2->3), and Fire Kick while Fire-aligned resets to 0. Matching alignment grants per-skill bonuses (+5 Air Sphere & delay, +5 Water Whip & all-damage-reduction, +1 Earth Pillars cap-stack, +15 Fire Kick). Each skill also leaves a 1-turn self-mark that powers up a specific OTHER skill if used next turn, forming a combo chain (Air->Fire, Water->Air, Earth->Water, Fire->Earth). NOTE: the JSON/passive text promises an 'Aang Avatar State' transformation on completing the cycle, but NO such effect is implemented in code (only Korra has an Avatar State).

abilities.name: Air Sphere
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage (to 25) if Air-aligned; also applies a 1-turn skill delay when Air-aligned. If Water Whip was used last turn, applies a -20 all-damage debuff to target for 1 turn.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Normal single-target. Air-aligned: +5 dmg + delays target's next skill 1 turn (soft-cc) and advances Avatar Cycle to Water. Water Whip combo: target deals -20 damage for 1 turn. Leaves self-mark improving Fire Kick.

abilities.name: Water Whip
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage (to 15) if Water-aligned; aligned version reduces ALL damage instead of just Affliction. Earth Pillars combo adds a multi-class stun.
abilities.effects_summary: 10 Normal AoE to enemy team + a ~1-turn 10 Normal DoT on each + a -10 damage debuff (Affliction-only, or all-damage if Water-aligned) for 2 turns. Water-aligned: +5 dmg & advances Cycle to Earth. Earth Pillars combo: stuns Physical/Affliction/Strategic skills first turn (multi-class cc). Leaves self-mark improving Air Sphere.

abilities.name: Earth Pillars
abilities.conditional_scaling: Earth-aligned: caps next 2 skills instead of 1 (2 damage-cap stacks). Fire Kick combo: adds 10 Affliction/turn DoT while the cap effect persists.
abilities.effects_summary: Pure control: caps the damage of the target's next skill at 10 (next 2 skills if Earth-aligned), consumed when target acts. Earth-aligned advances Cycle to Fire. Fire Kick combo: applies 10 Affliction/turn (resolves 10 immediately, persists until cap consumed). Leaves self-mark improving Water Whip.

abilities.name: Fire Kick
abilities.conditional_scaling: +15 damage (to 55) if Fire-aligned (and resets Cycle to Air). Air Sphere combo adds a 5 Affliction/turn team AoE DoT (2 turns) that bypasses Invulnerability.
abilities.effects_summary: 40 Affliction single-target (55 if Fire-aligned) — bypasses barriers/shields/DR. Air Sphere combo: also applies 5 Affliction/turn to the whole enemy team for 2 turns, bypassing Invulnerability (resolves 5 immediately). Leaves self-mark improving Earth Pillars.

abilities.name: Avatar Cycle
abilities.conditional_scaling: Tracks alignment via a self-MARK (mag 0=Air,1=Water,2=Earth,3=Fire); advances when a matching-element skill is used. The 'completing the cycle grants Aang Avatar State' clause in the description is NOT implemented in code.
abilities.effects_summary: Passive bookkeeping: applies a permanent self-mark indicating current elemental alignment and an explainer effect. Each visible skill checks and advances this mark to gate its alignment bonus. No transformation/stat effect is actually granted by cycle completion (stale description).

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No true ramp/stacking scaling — damage is fixed and only swings by fixed alignment bonuses (Fire Kick 40->55, Water Whip 10->15, Air Sphere 20->25). Peak single-target is Fire Kick Fire-aligned = 55 Affliction (bypasses shields/DR). Peak instantaneous AoE is Water Whip Water-aligned 15 + its ~10 DoT tick = ~25/enemy; Fire Kick's Air-combo adds a team-wide 5/turn x2. Sustained DoT tops out around ~15/turn on one target (Earth Pillars Fire-combo 10 + Fire Kick team 5).
damage_profile.notes: Affliction on Fire Kick (and the DoTs) bypasses barriers/shields/DR, making the 40-55 surprisingly hard to mitigate; the Air-combo team DoT also bypasses Invulnerability. damage_amount for aang3 is 0 (pure control). Real value is control/debuff density, not raw damage.

economy.color_dependency: Heavily four-color: White(Air Sphere), Blue(Water Whip), Green(Earth Pillars), Red x2(Fire Kick) — one specific pip of each of Green/Blue/White plus 2 Red, and 1 random. To use the whole kit in a turn you need all four energy colors, making Aang very energy-color-greedy and reliant on diverse team energy generation. Individual skills are cheap (1-2 pips each).
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast/flexible: Air Sphere 0 CD (spammable), Fire Kick 1 CD, Water Whip & Earth Pillars 2 CD. Low cooldowns enable tight turn-to-turn combo sequencing.
economy.ramp_dependency: Soft ramp: no stat ramp, but power comes from sequencing — alignment must be advanced to the matching element for bonuses, and combos require using the correct skill the turn AFTER its setup skill. Mis-sequencing or energy starvation collapses the payoff. Avatar Cycle order (Air->Water->Earth->Fire) means hitting an element's bonus turn-by-turn requires deliberate play.

hard_cc: Water Whip class-stun (Physical/Affliction/Strategic skills) on Earth Pillars combo
soft_cc: Air Sphere 1-turn skill delay (Air-aligned)
Earth Pillars damage-cap-10 on next 1-2 enemy skills

internal_synergies: Combo chain via self-marks: Air Sphere -> Fire Kick (adds team AoE affliction DoT that bypasses invuln); Earth Pillars -> Water Whip (adds multi-class stun); Water Whip -> Air Sphere (adds -20 damage debuff); Fire Kick -> Earth Pillars (adds 10 affliction/turn DoT).
Avatar Cycle alignment gates the bonus version of each skill, so optimal lines try to be in the right alignment AND in the right combo window simultaneously.
Earth Pillars damage-cap pairs with the Water Whip damage-reduction debuff and Air Sphere delay to heavily neuter a single threat's output for a turn.
Fire Kick's Affliction + the affliction DoTs ignore shields/DR; Water Whip's affliction-damage-reduction is anti-synergistic with relying on those DoTs unless water-aligned converts it to all-damage.
win_conditions: Out-tempo and lock down a single key enemy by stacking Air Sphere delay + Earth Pillars damage-cap + Water Whip damage-debuff, then burst with Fire Kick (40-55 unmitigable affliction).
Chip the whole enemy team with Water Whip AoE + DoT + the Air-combo Fire Kick team affliction DoT while debuffing their damage output.
Win the attrition/control war via debuff density and damage prevention rather than raw burst; close out low targets with Affliction that bypasses defenses.
strengths: Exceptional control/debuff density for the cost: skill delay, damage-cap, damage-reduction debuffs, and a multi-class stun all in one cheap kit.
Affliction Fire Kick (40-55) bypasses barriers/shields/DR; combo DoTs bypass Invulnerability — strong against defensive/turtle comps.
Low cooldowns and a 0-CD opener give high turn-to-turn flexibility and combo potential.
Both single-target (Fire Kick) and team-wide (Water Whip, Air-combo DoT) reach.
Cheap per-skill costs; only 6 total pips for the full kit.
weaknesses: Severe four-color energy dependency (needs Green+Blue+White+2Red to fire the whole kit) — punishing without diverse energy generation; bad energy draws cripple the combo.

Payoff is sequencing-locked: combo marks only last one turn and alignment bonuses require being in the matching element, so disruption, forced retargeting, or being forced to skip a turn breaks the chain.
Low raw burst ceiling (max 55 single-target) and no scaling — flat numbers mean he can be out-damaged by dedicated assassins/scalers.
No self-sustain: zero healing, shields, cleanse, or invuln/counter — fragile if focused.
The advertised 'Avatar State' transformation is not implemented, so there is no late-game power spike the kit's flavor implies (functional shortfall / possible bug).
Earth Pillars deals no direct damage and its control is reactive (cap on next skill), giving low value vs passive or DoT-reliant enemies.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, control-heavy elemental combo character with cheap, low-cooldown skills and unusually dense debuff/lockdown tools (delay, damage-cap, damage-reduction, multi-class stun) plus shield-bypassing Affliction burst capped at 55 single-target and ~25 team AoE. He genuinely threatens both single targets and teams and is excellent into defensive/invuln comps. But he is held back by extreme four-color energy dependency, fragile sequencing-locked combos (1-turn marks + alignment gating), no self-sustain, flat non-scaling damage, and the unimplemented 'Avatar State' that the kit's flavor (and JSON) promises but never delivers. Strong in a tuned, energy-rich draft; mediocre when starved or disrupted. Lands around average-to-slightly-above.
outlier_flags: DESCRIPTION/CODE MISMATCH: passive and JSON claim 'When he completes the cycle, he gains Aang Avatar State' but no Avatar State / transformation effect is implemented in aang5.gd or anywhere for Aang (only Korra has one). transformation=false despite flavor.
Four-color energy requirement (Green+Blue+White+Red) is an outlier vs typical 1-2 color kits — high color dependency.
Earth Pillars has 0 base damage (pure utility), unusual for an attack-bar skill.
Multiple effects rely on tight 1-turn combo windows (self-marks dur 3) that are easily disrupted.

role: single-target/AoE ramping affliction-DoT bruiser
signature_mechanic: DR-to-Affliction conversion: accumulated flat Damage Reduction is added to Ace's Affliction damage (Flame Commandment passive), letting him tank and ramp damage simultaneously.

abilities.name: Fire Fist
abilities.conditional_scaling: Adds Affliction damage equal to the sum of Ace's current flat Damage Reduction magnitudes (Flame Commandment). Starts at 0; grows ~5 per Flame Pillar cast and +10 while Firefly DR is active.
abilities.effects_summary: Spammable (0 cd, 1 Blue) single-target nuke. 15 Normal (JSON stale at 10) + variable DR-scaled Affliction that ignores shields/barriers/DR. Also serves as the 'new damage' trigger that detonates Firefly marks.

abilities.name: Firefly
abilities.conditional_scaling: Detonation scales with mark stacks: 10 Energy per Firefly stack consumed when Ace next deals new damage; repeated casts increase the burst.
abilities.effects_summary: Applies 1 stackable Firefly mark (DAMAGE_RECEIVE_TRIGGER, dur -1) to ALL enemies. Next time Ace deals new damage to a marked enemy, consumes ALL its marks for 10 Energy each, then fully removes Firefly. Also grants Ace +10 flat DR until end of his next turn (feeds the DR->Affliction loop and his tankiness).

abilities.name: Flame Emperor
abilities.conditional_scaling: Affliction component = sum of Ace's flat DR; ALSO applies a permanent stacking Affliction DoT equal to that DR value to all enemies (stack_mag), so each cast adds another DR-sized affliction tick per turn going forward.
abilities.effects_summary: 40 Normal to main target + DR-scaled Affliction to ALL enemies (skipped on a target already carrying the Flame Emperor DoT) + applies/stacks a permanent per-turn Affliction DoT (magnitude = current DR) on all enemies. Primary AoE ramp tool; the DoT bypasses shields/DR.

abilities.name: Flame Pillar
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 flat DR is permanent and stacking (dur -1, stack_mag), so it compounds every cast and permanently raises his Affliction output via the passive.
abilities.effects_summary: Self-buff / panic button: 50% Damage Reduction for 1 turn (dur 2) + 5 flat permanent stacking Damage Reduction. The flat DR is the engine of his ramp (boosts Fire Fist/Flame Emperor Affliction via Flame Commandment) while the 50% gives a defensive turn. 3-turn cd gates the ramp.

abilities.name: Flame Commandment
abilities.conditional_scaling: Defines the core scaling identity: Affliction damage dealt increases by Ace's current total flat DR.
abilities.effects_summary: Passive mark on Ace: his flat Damage Reduction is added to all new Affliction damage he deals. Implemented in ace1/ace3 by summing DR effect magnitudes into base_aff. No standalone action (PASS).

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Unbounded but slow. Each Flame Pillar (3-turn cd) adds +5 permanent DR, which adds +5 to every Fire Fist/Flame Emperor Affliction hit AND +5 to every stacked Flame Emperor DoT tick. Firefly adds +10 temporary DR per active window. After many turns DR can reach 30-50+, making Fire Fist deal 15 Normal + 40-50 Affliction and Flame Emperor stack multiple large per-turn DoTs; late-game single target with full marks + high DR can exceed 150.
damage_profile.notes: Early: Fire Fist ~15 Normal + ~10-15 Affliction (~25-30). Mid (~20 DR): Fire Fist 15+20 Aff = 35, plus detonating ~3 Firefly stacks (30) on the same 'new damage' = ~65 single-target; Flame Emperor 40 Normal + 20 Aff = 60 plus a Firefly detonation 30 ~= 90-110 single-target burst. Pure Normal/Energy burst is modest; the real threat is the DR-scaled Affliction (shield/barrier/DR-ignoring) plus the stacking permanent Flame Emperor DoT. Damage is back-loaded and needs several turns of DR accumulation; Firefly burst is conditional on Ace landing 'new damage' while marks are up.

economy.color_dependency: Heavy mono-Blue: 4 of 6 visible pips are Blue (Fire Fist Blue:1, Flame Emperor Blue:2, Flame Pillar Blue:1); only Firefly and one Flame Emperor pip are Random.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Low cost, mixed cadence. Fire Fist is spammable (0 cd, 1 Blue) bread-and-butter; Firefly cd 1; Flame Emperor cd 2 (AoE/ramp); Flame Pillar cd 3 gates the DR ramp, making scaling deliberately slow.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Weak before stacking DR; both damage and tankiness scale off Flame Pillar/Firefly DR accumulation over many turns. Short games or early focus-fire shut the ramp down.

win_conditions: Survive the early game and stack flat Damage Reduction (Flame Pillar every 3 turns, Firefly) until Fire Fist / Flame Emperor Affliction becomes lethal and unblockable.
Grind teams down with stacking permanent Flame Emperor Affliction DoTs plus repeated Firefly detonations while tanking through his own DR.
Out-attrition shield/DR-reliant compositions, since his Affliction damage ignores those defenses.
internal_synergies: Flame Pillar -> Flame Commandment: every +5 permanent DR directly increases Fire Fist and Flame Emperor Affliction (offense and defense from one button).
Firefly's +10 DR window also feeds the passive, briefly spiking his Affliction output as well as the detonation.
Fire Fist as the cheap 0-cd 'new damage' trigger detonates Firefly marks every turn for 10 per stack.
Flame Emperor double-dips: immediate DR-scaled Affliction + plants a permanent DR-scaled DoT that grows as DR grows.
strengths: Unblockable scaling: DR-fueled Affliction and the Flame Emperor DoT bypass shields, barriers, and DR, beating defensive teams.
Self-sufficient tankiness: 50% DR panic button + permanent stacking flat DR, no support needed.
Very cheap, spammable primary (Fire Fist 0 cd / 1 Blue) keeps consistent pressure and triggers Firefly detonations.
AoE reach via Firefly (all enemies) and Flame Emperor (all-enemy DoT) for board-wide attrition.
Offense and defense scale off the same resource (flat DR) — every defensive cast is also an offensive investment.
weaknesses: Slow ramp: low damage until DR accumulates; Flame Pillar's 3-turn cd throttles scaling, so he is weak in short games or under early burst.
Heavy mono-Blue dependency (4/6 pips Blue) makes him color-hungry and vulnerable to energy denial/control.
No CC, no cleanse, no healing, no team utility — a self-contained damage/tank with zero support.
His own flat DR does not protect against Affliction/Bleed/Piercing/True, so enemy affliction teams punish him.
Firefly burst is conditional on Ace landing 'new damage' while marks are up; if he is locked out of acting, marks sit inert.
Stun or DR-removal effects can both stop his attacks and reset/cap his accumulated scaling.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-designed scaling bruiser with a clean offense=defense identity. The DR->Affliction loop plus the stacking permanent Flame Emperor DoT gives genuine unblockable late-game scaling, and layered DR makes him hard to kill. But the payoff is deliberately gated: cheap pips and a 3-turn Flame Pillar mean ramp is slow, and he brings zero CC/utility/support, so before he comes online he is an easily-pressured mono-Blue target who folds to early burst, energy denial, or affliction damage. Strong in long grind matchups vs shield/DR teams, mediocre in fast games. Solidly mid-tier in isolation.
outlier_flags: unbounded flat-DR / Affliction scaling (no hard cap)
permanent stacking AoE DoT (Flame Emperor) can snowball in long games
JSON-vs-gd damage mismatch on Fire Fist (gd 15 vs JSON 10)

role: single-target delayed-execute assassin
signature_mechanic: "One Cut Killing": mark a target with Red-Eyed Killer, then hit it for 15 Normal damage and apply a ticking death trigger that instant-kills the target after 2 turns regardless of remaining HP (HP-bypassing guaranteed kill, ignores the damage pipeline entirely so shields/DR are irrelevant).

abilities.name: Red-Eyed Killer
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Applies the 'Red-Eyed Killer' mark to one enemy (mark dur 5 = ~2 enemy-facing turns). The mark is the targeting prerequisite that lets One Cut Killing (akame2) hit that enemy. No damage. Cheap (1 White) setup enabler.

abilities.name: One Cut Killing
abilities.target_type: SINGLE enemy (must be marked by Red-Eyed Killer, or any enemy while Little War Horn active)
abilities.conditional_scaling: Binary: against a valid (marked) target it applies a guaranteed delayed instant-kill that ignores HP entirely. Effective value = full enemy HP, not the 15 listed damage.
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 15 Normal damage immediately, then applies a TICKING_TRIGGER death effect (dur 5) that, when it counts down to 1 (after 2 enemy-facing turns), calls instant_kill on the target regardless of HP/shields. Trigger is bypassing and remove_on_death=false. Gated by Red-Eyed Killer mark (or Little War Horn for any-target). Cooldown 0 so it can be re-applied repeatedly.

abilities.name: Little War Horn
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self-buff for ~2 turns (mark dur 3, invuln dur 4): (1) Akame becomes invulnerable to Physical-class skills; (2) the 'Little War Horn' mark lets One Cut Killing be used on ANY target, removing the Red-Eyed Killer mark requirement (skips the akame1 setup turn). Enables faster execute chains and partial defensive uptime. Long 5cd.

abilities.name: Rapid Deflection
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: default_defend: Akame becomes fully invulnerable for 1 turn (panic button). 1 flexible pip, cd 4. Protects her through the 2-turn delay window while a death trigger ticks on an enemy.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Listed direct damage is trivial (15 Normal). The true ceiling is the delayed instant-kill: One Cut Killing guarantees a target's death after 2 turns regardless of its HP, so effective burst equals the victim's full health pool. With Little War Horn (any-target) and 0 cooldown on One Cut Killing, Akame can stack multiple death timers on different enemies, threatening up to one guaranteed kill per turn during a horn window.
damage_profile.notes: Damage numbers massively understate Akame. Direct damage output is one of the lowest in the game (15 per One Cut Killing, 0 elsewhere), but the kit kills via an unconditional HP-bypassing execute timer rather than damage. The kill is not affected by shields, barriers, DR, or remaining HP; counterplay is denying her energy, cleansing/removing the death trigger, killing her first, or protecting/swapping the marked target before the timer resolves.

economy.color_dependency: Tri-color leaning White/Red/Green (character_colors = [White, Red, Green]). The core combo needs White (mark) + Green/Red (One Cut Killing) + Red (Little War Horn). Red is the most load-bearing color (One Cut Killing core pip + Little War Horn). Moderate color dependency for a 4-skill kit; 2 of 6 pips are flexible.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Asymmetric: One Cut Killing has cooldown 0 (spammable), Red-Eyed Killer cd 2 (one mark every other turn by default). Defensive/utility tools are on long cooldowns: Little War Horn cd 5, Rapid Deflection cd 4. Tempo is dictated by the 2-turn death-timer delay, not by cooldowns.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low mechanical ramp but high setup tempo cost: each kill normally takes a minimum of ~3 turns (turn 1 mark, turn 2 One Cut Killing, +2 turns until death resolves). Little War Horn shortcuts the mark step. No stacking/scaling resource to build.

invuln_or_counter: Rapid Deflection: full invuln 1 turn (cd 4)
Little War Horn: Physical-class invuln ~2 turns (cd 5)

win_conditions: Land Red-Eyed Killer + One Cut Killing on a priority target and survive the 2-turn timer to score a guaranteed HP-ignoring kill.
Use Little War Horn to skip the mark step and stack multiple death timers on enemies during its window, threatening sequential guaranteed kills.
Stall behind her two invuln tools (Rapid Deflection / Little War Horn's Physical-invuln) while death triggers tick, trading her defensiveness for inevitable executes.
internal_synergies: Red-Eyed Killer (akame1) is the targeting key for One Cut Killing (akame2) — mark then execute.

Little War Horn (akame3) removes the Red-Eyed Killer prerequisite, letting One Cut Killing hit any target and compressing the kill from 2 setup actions into 1; it also gives Physical invuln to protect Akame during the timer.
One Cut Killing's cooldown 0 + Little War Horn's any-target unlock = multiple concurrent death timers across the enemy team.
Rapid Deflection (akame4) and Little War Horn give defensive uptime to survive the delay between applying a death trigger and it resolving.
strengths: Guaranteed, HP-bypassing execute that ignores shields, barriers, damage reduction, and current HP — kills tanks/high-HP threats as easily as squishies.
One Cut Killing has 0 cooldown and the kill scales to full target HP, so effective 'damage' is enormous relative to its tiny listed numbers.
Two independent invulnerability tools give strong self-survivability to outlast the death timer.
Cheap setup (1 White mark, 1 Red horn) and flexible random pips keep the combo affordable.
weaknesses: Pure single-target with zero AoE and zero team utility (no heals, shields, cleanse, or energy denial) — weak on swing turns and slow in many-vs-many.
Telegraphed and slow: the kill takes ~3 turns minimum and a visible 2-turn timer, giving opponents time to cleanse/remove the death trigger, protect/swap the target, or burst Akame down first.
Highly counterable by trigger-removal, target invuln/swap, and especially by killing Akame during the delay.
Negligible direct damage means she contributes almost nothing if her execute is answered; she has no fallback damage profile.
Defensive cooldowns (4 and 5) are long, so a determined focus on Akame can catch her without invuln up.

power_assessment.reasoning: A specialist single-target assassin whose power is entirely in a guaranteed HP-bypassing execute rather than raw numbers. The instant-kill is extremely strong against tanks and any high-HP/shielded target and trivializes some matchups, but it is heavily telegraphed (2-turn timer, ~3-turn setup), single-target only, and highly counterable via cleanse, target protection/swap, or simply killing Akame first. With no AoE, healing, or team support and long defensive cooldowns, her ceiling is high in a focus-kill role but her floor is low against teams with trigger removal or peel. Solid but swingy; rated mid-high in isolation.
outlier_flags: guaranteed-instant-kill-mechanic
effective-damage-decoupled-from-listed-numbers
HP/shield/DR-bypassing-execute
near-zero-direct-damage
no-AoE/no-team-utility

abilities.name: Texas Smash
abilities.conditional_scaling: Self-damage scales with Declare Successor mark stacks: base 15 Affliction + 10 per stack (so 25 after Declare is used once). Outgoing damage benefits from United Resolve's +10/+20 damage_mod the turn after it is cast.
abilities.effects_summary: Single-target nuke. Deals 40 Piercing (skips flat + %DR) to one enemy; All Might self-inflicts 15 Affliction (25 after Declare Successor). Uncounterable.

abilities.name: United Resolve
abilities.conditional_scaling: If HP < 40 when cast: applies +10 outgoing damage_mod for next turn (dur 3 = self-facing 1 turn); a DAMAGE_RECEIVE_TRIGGER watcher upgrades that mod to +20 if All Might takes new damage during the buff window.
abilities.effects_summary: Self panic-button / setup. 1 turn: ignore_non_damage_effect (immune to Harmful non-damage effects) + immortality_effect (cannot die / survives at 1 HP). Both invisible. Below 40 HP, also primes a +10 (->+20 if hit) next-turn damage buff. No CC/heal, no damage.

abilities.name: United States of Smash
abilities.conditional_scaling: Self-damage scales with Declare Successor mark stacks: 25 Affliction + 10 per stack (35 after Declare). Outgoing damage gains United Resolve's +10/+20 the following turn.
abilities.effects_summary: Bigger single-target nuke. 60 Piercing to one enemy; self-inflicts 25 Affliction (35 after Declare). Uncounterable. Tri-color cost (one each of Blue/White/Red).

abilities.name: Declare Successor
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent, one-time. Adds a stacking Declare Successor MARK on All Might that permanently raises his own self-damage by +10 per use (used once). Also installs an ON_DEATH_TRIGGER that converts the successor's colored costs to Random when All Might dies.
abilities.effects_summary: Ally empowerment / legacy. Grants the One For All passive (allmight5) to one ally; permanently increases All Might's own skill self-damage by 10. Once-per-game (extra_usable gated on no existing mark). No damage to enemies.

abilities.name: One For All
abilities.conditional_scaling: On All Might's death, the successor's remaining colored pips (Green/Blue/White/Red) are permanently converted to Random pips, making the successor's kit fully color-flexible.
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden passive applied to the successor via Declare Successor. Reduces that ally's Random costs by 1 (economy buff); the ally takes 10 Affliction each time they use a new skill. Posthumous bonus: ally's colored costs all become Random. execute() is an intentional no-op (placeholder).

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Outgoing damage is fixed: 60 (US of Smash) + 20 (max United Resolve mod, when <40 HP and hit) = 80 single-target in one turn. He has no enemy-facing AoE and applies no DoT. His only scaling is downward/self-harmful (self-damage grows +10 per Declare Successor stack). Effective damage is high because all attacks are Piercing (bypass flat and % DR).
damage_profile.notes: Both attacks are Piercing, so effective damage vs DR/armor targets is the full 40/60. Texas Smash (40) + United Resolve setup, then United States of Smash next turn at +10/+20 = up to 80 burst. United Resolve is on a 4-turn cooldown, so the +20 window is occasional, not sustained. Self-damage (Affliction, bypasses his own barriers) is a real cost: 15/25 -> 25/35 after Declare, and the successor also bleeds 10 Affliction per skill use.

economy.color_dependency: Moderate-to-high. United States of Smash demands one each of Blue, White, Red (3 distinct colors in a single turn), and Texas Smash needs a Red. Character colors are [Blue, White, Red] (1,2,3) - notably NO Green. The two utility skills (United Resolve, Declare Successor) are 1 Random each and color-free.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast on offense: Texas Smash cd 1 (near-spammable), US of Smash cd 2, Declare Successor cd 0 (but once-per-game). United Resolve is the only long cooldown at 4. He can attack almost every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low/negative ramp. No buildup needed to function; he comes online turn 1. Declare Successor is a one-time investment that actively raises his own self-damage (anti-ramp on himself) in exchange for a permanent ally upgrade.

invuln_or_counter: United Resolve: immortality_effect for 1 turn (cannot die / survives lethal at 1 HP)
United Resolve: ignore_non_damage_effect for 1 turn (immunity to Harmful non-damage / control effects)

internal_synergies: United Resolve below 40 HP -> +10/+20 damage on next turn's Texas Smash / US of Smash; the immortality + non-damage-immunity lets him intentionally dip low and survive to cash in the bonus, turning his fragility into a damage engine

Declare Successor + One For All: hands an ally a permanent economy buff (Random cost -1) and, on All Might's death, converts that ally's colored costs to Random - All Might's death becomes a posthumous team upgrade
Self-damage is Affliction (bypasses barriers), which both fuels the <40 HP United Resolve condition and acts as a built-in clock - synergizes with his own panic-button immortality
role: single-target Piercing burst attacker with self-damage cost and a one-time ally-empowerment passive
signature_mechanic: Self-harm-fueled aggression: every attack is Piercing (bypasses all DR) but costs him Affliction HP; United Resolve weaponizes being low (<40 HP grants +10/+20 next-turn damage) while immortality + control-immunity keep him alive long enough to spend it, and Declare Successor permanently passes One For All to an ally at the cost of even more self-damage.
strengths: High effective single-target damage: 40/60 Piercing fully bypasses flat and % damage reduction, so armored/tanky targets take full hits
Excellent tempo - Texas Smash cd 1 and US of Smash cd 2 let him pressure almost every turn
Strong self-protection turn: 1-turn immortality plus immunity to Harmful non-damage (control) effects makes him very hard to lock down or burst out, and is uncounterable on attacks
Comeback scaling: the lower his HP, the harder he hits (+10/+20), so chip damage can backfire on the enemy
Provides permanent team value via Declare Successor (ally Random cost -1, plus full color flexibility for that ally if All Might dies)
weaknesses: Pays HP for everything - 15/25 (rising to 25/35 after Declare) Affliction self-damage per attack that bypasses his own barriers; he can damage-race himself to death
No sustain whatsoever: zero healing, shields, or lifesteal to offset the self-harm
No AoE and no DoT - purely single-target, easy to itemize/position against
High color dependency on US of Smash (needs Blue+White+Red in one turn); a starved color denies his big nuke
No hard CC or energy denial - cannot lock the enemy down, only burst
United Resolve's immortality/immunity is only 1 turn and on a 4-turn cooldown, leaving long vulnerable windows
Declare Successor is once-per-game and permanently worsens his own self-damage, a real opportunity cost
win_conditions: Focus-fire a key enemy down with repeated uncounterable Piercing nukes (40 then 60) before his self-damage clock runs out
Bait the enemy into chipping him below 40 HP, survive with United Resolve immortality, then land a +20-boosted 60-damage US of Smash
Use Declare Successor early to snowball an ally's economy/flexibility and play All Might as an aggressive, expendable damage dealer whose death upgrades the successor

power_assessment.reasoning: A focused single-target Piercing burst dealer with a genuinely strong defensive/comeback turn (1-turn immortality + control immunity + low-HP damage scaling) and a unique support angle (permanent One For All grant). His damage is reliable and DR-proof, his tempo is high (cd 1/2 attacks), and he is hard to remove during United Resolve. But he is a glass cannon by design: heavy self-Affliction with zero self-sustain caps his staying power, he has no AoE/DoT/CC/energy-denial, and US of Smash's tri-color cost plus United Resolve's 4-turn cooldown create real friction. Strong in a duel/focus-fire context, mediocre against multi-target or sustain comps. Above-average but not dominant.
outlier_flags: self-damage scaling is downward/anti-self (rare) - +10 self-Affliction per Declare stack, distinct from typical offensive scaling
uses immortality_effect (survive lethal) rather than invulnerability/counter - he can be hit but not killed for 1 turn
Declare Successor + One For All is a cross-character permanent buff that rewrites a teammate's energy economy and even pays out posthumously - unusual support-on-an-attacker design
all primary attacks are Piercing AND Uncounterable, giving unusually high effective damage vs DR/counter comps

role: Sustained DoT zoner / defensive bruiser who installs permanent board-wide passive damage and walls behind invuln
signature_mechanic: Digitalize of Soul installs PERMANENT effects: a self Shield that pulses 10 NORMAL to all enemies every turn, plus a per-enemy Nullify (barrier) that pulses 20 NORMAL to that enemy every turn — 30 damage/enemy/turn indefinitely once set up, action-free. Paired with AlphaBlast's Shatter (strips enemy defenses so the Normal ticks land clean), invuln, and a counter-punishing passive to protect the engine.

abilities.name: AlphaBlast
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Normal damage + applies Shatter (DEF_NEGATE, refreshes). Shatter strips the target's defensive effects (DR/Shield/Nullify protection) so Alphamon's other Normal damage lands at full value. Cost Green:1, cd 1.

abilities.name: Blade of the Dragon King
abilities.conditional_scaling: none — JSON describes a permanent mitigation-proportional ramp but the .gd does NOT implement it (pre_damage var is dead code); flat 30 Normal, 0 cooldown spammable nuke
abilities.effects_summary: Flat 30 Normal damage, single target, 0 cooldown. Reliable repeatable nuke / finisher. NOTE: described scaling mechanic is not coded. Cost Green:1+Random:1, cd 0.

abilities.name: Digitalize of Soul
abilities.conditional_scaling: Ongoing per-turn tick damage, not per-stack: 10/turn to all enemies while self Shield (30, permanent) remains + 20/turn to each enemy while its Nullify (15 barrier, permanent) remains. Ticks fire on the cast turn too. ~30 dmg/enemy/turn indefinitely.
abilities.effects_summary: Permanent self Shield 30 (pulses 10 Normal AoE/turn) + permanent 15 Nullify on every enemy (each pulses 20 Normal/turn to that enemy). One-time non-stacking install; recast only reapplies missing pieces. Coded 30/15 values (stale describe() said 40/20). Cost Green:1+Random:2, cd 2.

abilities.name: inForce Avoidance
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self Invulnerable for 1 turn (invuln dur 2). Panic button / damage-avoidance wall to keep the DoT engine alive. Cost Random:1, cd 4.

abilities.name: Alpha inForce
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden passive wired to all 4 base abilities: if one of Alphamon's skills is COUNTERED, he refunds the full energy spent on it (random for random pips, specific otherwise) and heals 15 HP. Punishes counter-based opponents.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Bounded / no true scaling. The 'ramp' is a one-time permanent install (Digitalize) running forever at 30 dmg/enemy/turn (10 AoE shield tick + 20 per-enemy nullify tick). No per-stack growth. Single-action peak nuke is 30 (Blade) or 20 (AlphaBlast). Best one-turn single-target with Digitalize up on the Blade target = 30 + 20 + 10 = 60. Best one-turn AoE vs 3 nullified enemies = 30 each = 90, all passive.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is NORMAL type, so it is fully blunted by enemy DR/Shield/Nullify — which is WHY AlphaBlast's Shatter (def-negate) matters: it strips those defenses so the ticks and nukes connect. Against a defensive enemy he can't Shatter fast enough, effective output drops sharply. The ~30/enemy/turn passive output is independent of Alphamon's action, freeing his turn for Blade nukes, re-Shatter, or invuln. 90/turn figure assumes 3 nullified enemies.

economy.color_dependency: Light mono-Green dependency: 3 of 7 visible pips are specifically Green (one each on AlphaBlast, Blade, Digitalize); the other 4 are Random. character_colors=[0]=Green. Flexible — only one Green pip needed per relevant cast.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent early tempo: Blade is 0-cd (spam 30 nuke), AlphaBlast 1-cd (near-constant Shatter), Digitalize 2-cd one-time setup, inForce 4-cd defensive. Low 1-3 pip costs keep him fluid.
economy.ramp_dependency: Front-loaded one-shot ramp: casting Digitalize once (3 pips) installs permanent damage; afterward no further investment sustains ~30/enemy/turn. Not a stacking ramp — no escalation beyond the initial install.

soft_cc: Shatter (DEF_NEGATE) — strips/negates enemy defensive effects (DR/Shield/Nullify); an offensive debuff, not a lockout
invuln_or_counter: inForce Avoidance: self Invulnerable 1 turn (cd 4)
Alpha inForce passive: counter punish — refunds energy + heals 15 if a skill is countered

win_conditions: Land Digitalize of Soul early to install permanent ~30/enemy/turn passive AoE damage, then win the long game as the enemy team bleeds out for free.
Use AlphaBlast Shatter to strip a key target's mitigation so the Normal-type ticks and Blade nukes connect at full value.
Stall/protect with inForce Avoidance invuln (and the counter-punish passive) to outlast opponents while the DoT engine grinds.
Spam 0-cooldown Blade of the Dragon King (30) to close out softened targets.
internal_synergies: AlphaBlast's Shatter (def-negate) removes enemy DR/Shield/Nullify, critical because ALL of Alphamon's damage is Normal and otherwise fully mitigable — Shatter unlocks full Digitalize and Blade value.
Digitalize's self Shield both protects Alphamon and is the trigger that fires the 10 AoE tick each turn — offense and defense from one effect.
Digitalize tick damage is action-free, so Alphamon spends every action on Blade nukes, re-Shatter, or invuln without losing DoT pressure.
inForce Avoidance invuln + Alpha inForce counter-refund keep Alphamon (and his permanent installed effects) alive long enough for the DoT to matter.
Energy-efficient Green/Random costs usually let him afford both a Shatter and a Blade, or Digitalize plus a follow-up, each turn.
strengths: Permanent, action-free board-wide DoT (~30/enemy/turn) — exceptional sustained value with no upkeep once installed.
Self-sufficient defenses: 30 permanent Shield, a 1-turn invuln every 4 turns, and a counter-punishing heal — hard to burst down.
Built-in defense-stripping (Shatter) to beat tanky/shielded comps his Normal damage would otherwise stall against.
Cheap, flexible mono-Green economy with a 0-cd repeatable 30 nuke gives strong, consistent tempo.
Strong vs counter-reliant enemies via the energy-refund + heal passive.
weaknesses: All damage is Normal type — fully reduced by enemy DR/Shield/Nullify; against defense-stacked teams he can't Shatter fast enough, effective output craters.
Low burst ceiling: best single action is 30; can't quickly delete a priority threat and relies on grinding, so burst/assassin comps can out-race him.
No hard CC (no stun/lock) and no enemy energy denial — can't stop an enemy from comboing him off.
Damage doesn't truly scale (no per-stack ramp); ceiling is fixed at ~30/enemy/turn regardless of game length.
DoT relies on installed effects persisting — cleanse/effect removal on the enemy Nullify or his Shield shuts off the pulses; the heal is purely reactive (counter-only).
Slow to close games; weak finishing pressure vs a single high-HP/high-DR target.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, durable attrition controller. Standout is Digitalize of Soul: one 3-pip cast permanently deals ~30 damage/enemy/turn for the rest of the match at zero further action cost — compounding into large totals (up to 90/turn vs a full team) and being action-economy-positive, freeing him to nuke with a 0-cd 30 Blade or re-apply Shatter. Layered defenses (permanent 30 Shield, invuln every 4 turns, counter-refund + heal) make the engine hard to remove. Held back from top tier by being entirely Normal-typed (fully mitigable; heavily dependent on landing Shatter vs defensive comps), a low burst ceiling (max single action 30, no fast kill on a key target), no hard CC or energy denial, and no true scaling. Excellent in grindy/AoE matchups, vulnerable to burst, cleanse, and DR walls. Solidly above average, not oppressive.
outlier_flags: alphamon2 Blade of the Dragon King: describe()/JSON advertises a permanent mitigation-proportional damage ramp NOT implemented in the .gd (pre_damage declared but never used) — flat 30 Normal. Likely a balance bug / unfinished feature; if implemented it would raise his rating.
alphamon3 Digitalize of Soul: stale describe() says 40 Shield / 20 Nullify, but code and split_desc use 30 Shield / 15 Nullify — profile uses the coded 30/15.
Permanent (-1 duration) installed DoT with no charge limit is a strong, unusual lever; cumulative total damage is effectively unbounded over a long match even though per-turn output is fixed.

role: Setup-gated piercing skirmisher / durable disruptor with ally-damage amplification
signature_mechanic: Transmutation Circle (slot 1) is a one-time setup activator: it gains 1 random energy, self-marks Alphonse to unlock Weapon Alchemy (slot 2) and Destruction Alchemy Strike (slot 3), and permanently swaps slot 1 into Ground Pillars (AoE). The whole kit is gated behind this single activation.

abilities.name: Transmutation Circle
abilities.effects_summary: Setup activator: gains 1 random energy, self-marks (permanent, dur -1) to unlock Weapon Alchemy + Destruction Alchemy Strike, and permanently ability-swaps slot 1 into Ground Pillars. No damage. One-time enabler for the rest of the kit.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

abilities.name: Weapon Alchemy
abilities.effects_summary: Buffs a target ally with a DAMAGE_DEALT_TRIGGER: the next time that ally deals new (non-effect) damage, Alphonse adds 20 Piercing to that ally's primary target, then the buff consumes. Persists through ally death. Cannot stack on an already-affected ally. Requires Transmutation Circle. JSON says 15; .gd base_damage=20 is ground truth.
abilities.conditional_scaling: Conditional/delayed: a +20 Piercing rider on one ally attack.

abilities.name: Destruction Alchemy Strike
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 20 Piercing (JSON/class label say Affliction, but .gd resolves DamageType.PIERCING - ground truth), strips 1 random energy from the target (energy denial), and applies a mark (~2-turn lockout) preventing re-target. Cannot be used on a target already marked by this skill; requires Transmutation Circle. Only Red-pip ability.
abilities.conditional_scaling: AI weights by missing HP (soft execute preference) but damage is flat 20.

abilities.name: Golem Armor
abilities.effects_summary: Passive: starts the game with 30 Shield (applied in startup()). Active: refreshes/sets the Golem Armor shield to 30 and grants +5 permanent, stacking damage reduction (per_stack, dur -1). Pure self-sustain/tank tool; DR stacks indefinitely but gated by 4-turn cooldown.
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent DR stacks +5 each cast (defensive ramp); over a long game DR can climb high.

abilities.name: Ground Pillars
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 15 Piercing to ALL enemies and Shatters them (def_negate dur 1 = until end of turn), negating their defenses/DR/shields for the rest of the turn so follow-up hits land clean. Becomes the slot-1 ability after Transmutation Circle; available every turn at no cooldown thereafter.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat 15 each)

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Low. Best realistic single-target burst is ~35 (Destruction Alchemy Strike 20 + Ground Pillars 15 on one enemy in a turn). True per-turn ceiling ~50 if Weapon Alchemy's +20 rider is also consumed via an ally hit on that same enemy, but that requires an ally and is delayed/conditional. AoE caps at 15 per enemy. No per-stack or DoT damage scaling; only defensive DR ramps.
damage_profile.notes: Damage is deliberately low; Alphonse is a durability/utility/enabler, not a carry. Offensive value is force-multiplication: team-wide Shatter (def_negate) makes the team's same-turn damage bypass mitigation, Weapon Alchemy adds 20 Piercing to an ally strike, and Destruction Alchemy Strike adds energy denial + Piercing chip. All damage is Piercing (skips DR), so printed numbers are close to effective damage against tanks.

economy.color_dependency: Very low. Of the visible abilities only Destruction Alchemy Strike needs a specific pip (Red:1, matching the [3]=Red identity); everything else is Random. Ground Pillars (post-swap slot 1) costs Random:2. Easy to splash onto any team.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Mostly free-flowing: Transmutation Circle, Destruction Alchemy Strike, and Ground Pillars are all 0-cooldown; Weapon Alchemy is CD 1; Golem Armor is CD 4. After the one-time setup turn he can spam Ground Pillars + Destruction Alchemy Strike every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: High setup dependency on turn 1 (Transmutation Circle gates slots 2-3 and the slot-1 swap), then mild positive ramp via Golem Armor's stacking permanent DR. No offensive ramp.

soft_cc: Shatter / def_negate (Ground Pillars): strips defenses & DR for the rest of the turn on all enemies
Destruction Alchemy Strike mark: locks Alphonse out of re-targeting that enemy for ~2 turns (anti-focus throttle, not an enemy-action control)

internal_synergies: Transmutation Circle is the linchpin: one turn-1 cast self-marks to unlock Weapon Alchemy + Destruction Alchemy Strike AND swaps slot 1 into Ground Pillars, turning a 1-button character into a 4-button kit.

Ground Pillars' Shatter (def_negate) makes ALL enemies' defenses moot until end of turn, so Destruction Alchemy Strike, Weapon Alchemy's ally rider, and any teammate damage that same turn land at full value against tanks.
All Alphonse-sourced damage is Piercing, stacking with Shatter to hard-counter high-DR / shield-stacking enemy comps.
Golem Armor's permanent stacking DR keeps him alive to keep re-applying Ground Pillars every turn - a slow attrition engine.
Destruction Alchemy Strike's energy strip plus Transmutation Circle's self energy gain create a small net energy swing in his favor each cycle.
strengths: Excellent anti-tank / anti-mitigation: 100% Piercing personal damage plus team-wide Shatter neutralizes DR, shields, and defensive stacking.
Very low color dependency (4 of 5 costs Random; only one Red pip) - splashes into almost any team.
Strong personal durability: 30 starting shield, refreshable shield, and uncapped stacking permanent damage reduction.
Good tempo after setup: three 0-cooldown abilities let him AoE-Shatter + single-target strike every turn.
Built-in energy denial (1 random energy stripped per Destruction Alchemy Strike, 0 CD) pressures enemy economies.
Force-multiplies allies via Weapon Alchemy (+20 Piercing rider) and team-wide Shatter windows.
weaknesses: Low raw damage ceiling: ~35 self single-target / 15 AoE per turn; cannot solo-carry a kill race.
Turn-1 tax: Transmutation Circle must be spent first (gains only 1 energy, no damage, no defense), so he is nearly inert on the opening turn.
No healing, no cleanse, no hard CC, no invuln/counter - purely passive durability.
Golem Armor shield and DR are bypassed by Affliction/Bleed (shield) and Piercing/True (DR), so his tankiness drops sharply into DoT / penetration comps.
Weapon Alchemy is conditional and delayed (needs a living ally to deal damage) and is dead weight in 1v1 or if allies are pacified.
Destruction Alchemy Strike's self-mark blocks re-hitting the same enemy for ~2 turns, throttling single-target focus.
Mismatched labels: Destruction Alchemy Strike is class-tagged Affliction but deals Piercing in code, so it does not get true affliction barrier-bypass behavior.
win_conditions: Outlast and attrit: stack Golem Armor DR while chipping with 0-CD Ground Pillars + Destruction Alchemy Strike until the enemy team is worn down.
Anti-tank pivot: be the answer to DR/shield-stacking comps via Piercing + team-wide Shatter so the team's damage gets through.
Enabler in a team: open Shatter windows and add Weapon Alchemy's +20 Piercing rider to a hard-hitting ally for burst turns.
Energy starvation: repeatedly strip enemy energy with Destruction Alchemy Strike to deny key abilities while he tanks.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, low-variance utility/durability character. Strengths are real and distinctive (all-Piercing damage + team-wide Shatter is a genuine anti-mitigation package, plus energy denial, splashable Random costs, and strong self-sustain via uncapped stacking DR and a refreshable shield). But raw damage is low (~35 self single-target, 15 AoE) with no offensive scaling, he has no healing/cleanse/hard-CC/invuln, and he pays a real turn-1 setup tax that makes him slow to come online. He is a solid role-player and hard counter to tanky/shield comps, but unremarkable into squishy burst or DoT comps (shield/DR bypassed by Affliction/Bleed/Piercing). Lands squarely mid: useful, balanced, not a meta threat in isolation.
outlier_flags: JSON/metadata vs code mismatch: Destruction Alchemy Strike is described/tagged as 20 Affliction but the .gd resolves DamageType.PIERCING - ground-truth damage type is Piercing.
Weapon Alchemy JSON says 15 piercing but .gd base_damage = 20 (split_desc also says 20).
Golem Armor damage reduction is permanent and unbounded-stacking (per_stack, dur -1) - potential long-game outlier if matches run long, though gated by 4-turn cooldown.

Slot 5 (Ground Pillars) swaps into visible slot 1 after setup, so the true steady-state visible kit is Ground Pillars R:2 + Weapon Alchemy R:1 + Destruction Alchemy Strike Red:1 + Golem Armor R:1 = 5 pips, not the listed slots 1-4.

role: Counter-oriented single-target duelist with a delayed self-sacrifice execute finisher
signature_mechanic: Damage-conversion economy: Plasmantle converts incoming damage on Arthur into a stored Shield, Nirvana converts a target's outgoing damage into stored Nullify, and Violet Flash then CONSUMES both stored values to add them to its hit — turning enemy aggression into a single amplified strike. At <50 HP, Star Ring grants a 1-turn damage-ignore and permanently upgrades Violet Flash into Moon Splitting Violet Flash, a 45 Affliction execute that kills Arthur after use.

abilities.name: Violet Flash
abilities.conditional_scaling: Adds the magnitude of Arthur's Plasmantle Shield (consumed) plus the target's Nirvana Nullify (consumed) to base 20. Both stored values can be arbitrarily large since they scale off enemy damage absorbed/converted in prior turns.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 base Normal damage; consumes its own setup (Plasmantle Shield on self + Nirvana Nullify on target) to spike a single hit. No cooldown, spammable.

abilities.name: Plasmantle
abilities.conditional_scaling: Shield generated scales with how much Harmful damage Arthur would have taken that turn (full conversion, no cap shown). Bigger incoming hit = bigger stored Shield = bigger future Violet Flash.
abilities.effects_summary: Self counter/defense: for 1 turn, incoming Harmful damage is fully converted into an Invisible Shield (lasts 2 turns) instead of being taken. Acts as both damage negation and Violet Flash ammo. CD 2.

abilities.name: Nirvana
abilities.conditional_scaling: Nullify magnitude scales with the damage the marked enemy would have dealt (full conversion). Bigger enemy attack = bigger stored Nullify = bigger future Violet Flash.
abilities.effects_summary: Enemy-facing soft denial: marks one enemy for 1 turn; if they would deal new damage it is converted into Nullify (BARRIER) on them instead, neutralizing their attack AND banking the value as Violet Flash fuel. CD 2.

abilities.name: Star Ring
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (binary trigger threshold at HP < 50)
abilities.effects_summary: Free permanent arming passive. Plants a HEALTH_CHANGE_TRIGGER: when Arthur's HP first drops below 50, he gains ignore-damage for the rest of that turn (1-turn invuln) and Violet Flash is permanently swapped to Moon Splitting Violet Flash (arthur5). If already <50 HP on cast, triggers immediately. One-time.

abilities.name: Moon Splitting Violet Flash
abilities.conditional_scaling: Execute: instantly kills the target if HP < 20 after the 45 Affliction hit. Affliction bypasses barriers/shields/DR, so the 45 is near-unmitigable. No stack scaling.
abilities.effects_summary: Transformed finisher (Affliction, bypasses shields/barriers/DR) that replaces Violet Flash after Star Ring triggers. 45 Uncounterable Affliction damage + execute below 20 HP. Arthur instant-kills himself immediately after use (one-shot, terminal).

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Pre-transform: Violet Flash's 20 base + (Plasmantle Shield value) + (Nirvana Nullify value). Both bonus terms equal damage Arthur absorbed / the enemy would have dealt, so a single big enemy attack can inflate one Violet Flash to 60-100+ in practice (uncapped, but requires the enemy to feed it). Post-transform: hard 45 Affliction (uncounterable, unmitigable) plus an effective execute on anyone left under 20 HP — but it is a single one-time strike that ends Arthur.
damage_profile.notes: No multi-target damage anywhere; kit is strictly single-target. Realistic burst is a counter-fueled Violet Flash spike on a turn the enemy commits a big attack into Plasmantle/Nirvana. Moon Splitting Violet Flash is the only guaranteed-magnitude burst (45 Affliction + execute<20) and is non-repeatable.

economy.color_dependency: Hard Blue/White dependency — visible kit is 2x Blue (Violet Flash, Nirvana) + 1x White (Plasmantle), Star Ring free, zero random pips. Arthur cannot function off-color and competes for Blue/White energy. Transformed Moon Splitting Violet Flash costs Blue+White.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast: Violet Flash and Star Ring are 0 CD; Plasmantle and Nirvana are short 2-turn CDs. Whole kit is cheap (3 pips for all 4 visible skills), enabling a counter and a Violet Flash nearly every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: Soft ramp: Violet Flash payoff depends on having pre-banked Plasmantle/Nirvana conversions, and the execute mode depends on Arthur dropping below 50 HP. No stack counter, but the kit wants 1-2 turns of setup and an enemy willing to attack into it.

soft_cc: Nirvana damage-nullification mark (neutralizes one enemy's outgoing damage for 1 turn)
invuln_or_counter: Plasmantle (1-turn full Harmful-damage-to-Shield conversion = damage immunity + storage)
Star Ring ignore-damage / damage-immune for 1 turn at <50 HP
Nirvana acts as a counter that converts an enemy's attack into a self-Nullify

win_conditions: Bait a big enemy attack into Plasmantle (and/or Nirvana the threat), then dump the banked Shield + Nullify into an oversized Violet Flash for a single-target spike
Survive to low HP, trigger Star Ring's 1-turn invuln, then land Moon Splitting Violet Flash (45 Affliction, uncounterable) to execute a weakened target as a final play
Use Nirvana + Plasmantle as repeated tempo denial to neutralize the enemy's best attacker each turn while chipping with Violet Flash
internal_synergies: Plasmantle Shield AND Nirvana Nullify are both consumed by Violet Flash for bonus damage — the two defensive/denial tools are simultaneously the offensive fuel, making absorbed/denied damage directly translate into burst
Star Ring's <50 HP trigger gives a free 1-turn invuln (anti-burst) at the exact moment Arthur is most threatened AND upgrades his basic attack into an execute finisher
Plasmantle/Star Ring keep Arthur alive long enough to reach the transformed execute payoff
Nirvana's denial of the enemy's attack pairs with Plasmantle's absorption to make a turn where the enemy commits a big attack net-positive for Arthur on both defense and offense
strengths: Extremely cheap, fast kit (3 pips for 4 skills, 0-CD attack and free passive) — strong tempo and energy efficiency
Doubles as a counter/sustain shell: can fully convert incoming damage to Shield (Plasmantle) and nullify an enemy attacker (Nirvana) the same turn
Banked-damage Violet Flash can spike well above its 20 base when the enemy plays aggressively into the setup
Moon Splitting Violet Flash is a 45 Uncounterable Affliction execute that bypasses shields/barriers/DR — a reliable finisher that ignores most defensive tech
Built-in anti-burst safety valve (Star Ring 1-turn damage immunity) at low HP
Self-sufficient (all self/single-target) and hard to deny offensively due to uncounterable transformed attack
weaknesses: Zero AoE — completely single-target, weak into wide boards
No healing, no cleanse, no hard CC, no allied support — selfish kit that contributes nothing to teammates
Damage is conditional/reactive: if the enemy refuses to attack into Plasmantle/Nirvana, Violet Flash stays a feeble 20 and the kit's payoff collapses
The execute payoff is self-terminal — Moon Splitting Violet Flash kills Arthur, so the strongest play removes him from the board and is one-time
Star Ring's upgrade requires Arthur to take real damage (drop below 50 HP), coupling his power spike to being in danger; a passive/turtling opponent never feeds it
Hard Blue/White color dependency with no random pips — vulnerable to energy denial and color contention
Plasmantle/Nirvana are short-window 1-turn effects on 2-turn CDs, so mistimed setup wastes the turn

power_assessment.reasoning: A clever, self-contained counter/duelist with high tempo (cheap, low-CD) and a genuinely strong uncounterable Affliction execute finisher, but with severe ceilings: strictly single-target, no team utility, and damage that is reactive — most of his offense is borrowed from the enemy attacking into Plasmantle/Nirvana. Floor is a weak 20-damage poke; realized power requires either an aggressive opponent (to inflate Violet Flash) or reaching low HP to unlock the terminal execute. The self-kill on his best ability is a real drawback that caps his sustained impact. Solid but situational; rates middle-of-pack in isolation, leaning on opponent cooperation and timing to overperform.
outlier_flags: Self-sacrifice ability — best damage tool removes the user from play (rare, swingy design)
Uncounterable + Affliction + execute stacked on one transformed skill (bypasses nearly all defensive mitigation — potential balance hotspot vs low-HP targets)
Damage scaling is uncapped but entirely opponent-dependent — wide variance, hard to balance
Free 0-cost passive (Star Ring) granting a 1-turn invuln plus a permanent attack upgrade — efficient power for no energy

role: Flex DoT/Control Toolbox (stance-swap)
signature_mechanic: Pokemon swap stance-dance. Ash's 4 visible "Pokeball" buttons (Bulbasaur/Charmander/Squirtle/Pikachu) each cost 1 random, immediately fire that Pokemon's signature move, AND overwrite Ash's entire moveset with that Pokemon's 2-skill kit plus two universal utilities: Pokedex Scan (reveal invisible skills) and Return! (recall + 1-turn invuln, which resets the bar to the 4 Pokeballs). Only ONE Pokemon's kit is usable at a time; you commit a turn to swap in, then have 4 buttons (2 mon-skills + Scan + Return!) per turn thereafter.

abilities.name: Bulbasaur
abilities.effects_summary: Send-out/stance swap: deploys Bulbasaur, auto-casts Leech Seed (ash5) on a RANDOM enemy, and replaces Ash's moveset with Bulbasaur's kit (Leech Seed, Vine Whip, Pokedex Scan, Return!). No direct damage itself.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

abilities.name: Charmander
abilities.effects_summary: Send-out/stance swap: deploys Charmander, auto-casts Flamethrower (ash7, 15 affliction) on target, replaces moveset with Charmander's kit (Flamethrower, Fire Spin, Pokedex Scan, Return!).
abilities.conditional_scaling: Flamethrower it casts ramps if reused (see ash7).

abilities.name: Squirtle
abilities.effects_summary: Send-out/stance swap: deploys Squirtle, auto-casts Bubble (ash9) on the enemy team, replaces moveset with Squirtle's kit (Bubble, Water Gun, Pokedex Scan, Return!).
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

abilities.name: Pikachu
abilities.effects_summary: Send-out/stance swap: deploys Pikachu, auto-casts Thunderbolt (ash11, 20 piercing + cooldown paralyze) on target, replaces moveset with Pikachu's kit (Thunderbolt, Volt Tackle, Pokedex Scan, Return!).
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

abilities.name: Leech Seed
abilities.effects_summary: Permanent DoT: 10 piercing/turn for the REST OF THE GAME. Each tick heals a random damaged ally 10 HP; if no ally is hurt, Ash gains 1 random energy instead. Auto-applied (randomly) by sending out Bulbasaur; bypasses flat+%DR.
abilities.conditional_scaling: Value compounds the longer the game runs (uncapped lifetime DoT + sustain engine).

abilities.name: Vine Whip
abilities.effects_summary: AoE 10 to enemy team for 3 turns. While active, can be re-activated for 1 random to counter the next harmful skill of a target enemy (invisible counter). Soft control + chip + tech.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

abilities.name: Flamethrower

abilities.conditional_scaling: Self-ramping duration; cooldown also rises each use (anti-spam tradeoff).

abilities.name: Fire Spin
abilities.effects_summary: 10 affliction/turn for 4 turns (40 total, ignores barriers/shields/DR) AND the victim cannot target their own allies for the duration - denies enemy support/redirect for 4 turns. Long 4 cooldown.

abilities.name: Bubble

abilities.conditional_scaling: Damage scales linearly with stacks; reapply each turn (cd 0) to build big punishes.

abilities.name: Water Gun

abilities.conditional_scaling: Conditional stun on a pre-debuffed target.

abilities.name: Thunderbolt
abilities.effects_summary: 20 piercing to target + paralyzes their cooldowns for 2 turns (their on-cooldown skills can't recover). Efficient 1-cost burst + cooldown lock; bypasses flat+%DR.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Leech Seed (10 piercing/turn FOR THE REST OF THE GAME, with self-heal/energy refund) plus a stacking Bubble action-tax and ramping Flamethrower give an uncapped lifetime-DoT ceiling in long games; raw burst is low. Volt Tackle is unimplemented so true ceiling is unverifiable.
damage_profile.notes: Numbers are from abilities_data.json descriptions ONLY - no .gd ground truth exists. Per-turn burst is modest: within ONE committed stance the realistic single-turn single-target is ~20-30. Affliction (Flamethrower/Fire Spin) and piercing (Leech Seed/Thunderbolt/Bubble) bypass barriers/shields/DR, making effective damage higher vs tanky targets. peak_aoe_one_turn 10 = Vine Whip team hit; Fire Spin/Bubble are spread DoT/triggers not burst. sustained_dot ~20-25 unblockable once Leech Seed + one affliction are set up.

economy.color_dependency: Visible bar is 4x Random:1 (the 4 Pokeballs) = totally colorless to deploy. Depth lives in hidden per-Pokemon kits which DO want specific colors: Bulbasaur=Green, Charmander=Red, Squirtle=Blue, Pikachu=White/Random. Color-agnostic on the surface but each committed stance leans on one specific color; a rainbow character who wants a balanced pool to pivot.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Send-outs are all 0 cd (free pivoting), but Return! (4cd) gates stance resets, Pokedex Scan (2cd), Fire Spin (4cd), Thunderbolt/Volt Tackle (1cd) add friction inside a stance. The real tempo cost is the SWAP itself: changing Pokemon spends your whole turn re-deploying and re-applying that mon's signature.
economy.ramp_dependency: Medium-high: Leech Seed, ramping Flamethrower, and stacking Bubble all want a long game to pay off; struggles to close fast.
