abilities.conditional_scaling: +20 damage (to 60) if the target is currently skill-sealed by Totsuka Blade.
abilities.effects_summary: Post-Susanoo replacement of Tsukuyomi. 40 Piercing damage (Uncounterable), +20 = 60 if the target is sealed by Totsuka Blade. JSON's '50 base' is STALE; code base is 40.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Post-Susanoo turn-pairing: Totsuka Blade (30 Piercing + seal) one turn, then Yasaka Magatama (60 Piercing into the seal) next turn = 90 Piercing over two turns on a single sealed target, all of it ignoring flat/percent DR and counters. Single-turn ceiling is 60 (sealed Yasaka). Pre-Susanoo single-turn ceiling is ~30 (Tsukuyomi 20 + Crow Clone double-trigger 20, but the latter is reactive and rarely lands the same turn).
damage_profile.notes: Itachi is not a raw damage powerhouse; his Piercing is reliable but modest. All Susanoo-phase damage is Piercing (skips flat + percent DR) and the two key nukes are Uncounterable. No AoE anywhere in the kit. No DoT in code (stale JSON Affliction tick does not exist).

economy.color_dependency: Pre-Susanoo: light, White-anchored (Tsukuyomi + Kotoamatsukami each need White:1; Susanoo needs Red:1). Post-Susanoo: shifts hard to Red (Totsuka Red:1, Yasaka Red:2). Yata Mirror + Crow Clone's discount help feed Red, and Yata directly generates Red on harm taken. Two energy colors total (White, Red).
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast/spammable early — three 1-CD actions (Crow Clone, Tsukuyomi, Kotoamatsukami) plus a 0-CD Susanoo setup. Post-Susanoo slows slightly: Totsuka 1-CD, Yasaka 2-CD, Yata 3-CD.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Two distinct ramps: (1) breadcrumb chain — Crow Clone/Kotoamatsukami must trigger one turn before Tsukuyomi can banish; (2) the entire Susanoo power spike is gated behind taking enough damage to fall below 50 HP, and the strongest burst (Totsuka -> sealed Yasaka) requires a two-turn setup. Crow Clone also provides a self-perpetuating cost-discount ramp.

hard_cc: stun (Tsukuyomi, 1 turn)
banish (Tsukuyomi conditional, 1 turn)
skill seal (Totsuka Blade, 1 turn, non-stun so bypasses stun-immunity)
soft_cc: counter (Kotoamatsukami, use or receive)
invuln_or_counter: Kotoamatsukami counter (next Harmful, ally-protect or enemy-deny)
Susanoo permanent immunity to non-damage effects (de-facto CC immunity)
Totsuka Blade and Yasaka Magatama are Uncounterable

win_conditions: Land the breadcrumb -> banish combo: trigger Crow Clone or Kotoamatsukami, then Tsukuyomi-banish a key enemy each turn to remove it from the fight on a 1-CD loop.
Survive into Susanoo, then lock a target with Totsuka Blade's skill-seal and follow up with a 60 Piercing uncounterable Yasaka Magatama to delete priority targets through DR and immunities.
Out-tempo opponents with cheap, spammable counters and cost discounts while staying personally durable behind shields + non-damage-effect immunity.
internal_synergies: Crow Clone trigger and Kotoamatsukami counter both drop the hidden breadcrumb that upgrades Tsukuyomi from stun to banish (and Tsukuyomi consumes the mark, so one trigger = one banish).
Crow Clone's cost discount (Random, +White if it targeted Itachi) cheapens Tsukuyomi/Kotoamatsukami the following turn.
Totsuka Blade's 1-turn skill seal feeds Yasaka Magatama's +20 conditional, and the seal mark is deliberately kept alive an extra turn so the combo lines up.
Yata Mirror converts incoming Harmful skills into Red energy, directly bankrolling the Red-hungry Totsuka/Yasaka rotation.
Susanoo's HP<50 gate turns incoming damage into a power spike (shield + CC immunity + uncounterable Piercing kit), so taking damage is partly self-synergistic.
strengths: Recurring 1-turn banish on a 1-CD ability is premium, repeatable hard removal that bypasses most defenses.
Flexible counter (Kotoamatsukami) protects an ally or denies an enemy and seeds the banish chain.
Post-Susanoo damage is Piercing AND Uncounterable, ignoring DR and counter/invuln tech that walls other characters.
Totsuka's skill seal is explicitly not a stun, so it bypasses stun-immunity and stops a target's whole turn.
Strong personal durability: stacked invisible shields, a 35 Shield spike, and permanent immunity to non-damage effects after transforming.
Self-sufficient economy via cost discounts (Crow Clone) and Red generation (Yata Mirror); low specific-color pip burden.
High decision density / mind-game depth (invisible marks, conditional banish, ally-or-enemy counter).
weaknesses: Zero AoE — purely single-target; weak into wide/swarm comps.
Damage output is modest in absolute terms; relies on banish/seal control rather than killing fast pre-Susanoo.
Power spike is gated behind dropping below 50 HP — against passive or slow opponents Susanoo may never activate, leaving him in his weaker early form, and it is a once-per-game irreversible swap.
Banish requires a one-turn setup (breadcrumb the prior turn), so it can be denied by killing/banishing/cleansing in between or by banish shrug-off.
Reactive triggers (Crow Clone, counters) whiff entirely if the enemy doesn't act into them.
Becomes Red-color-starved post-Susanoo without Yata Mirror uptime or Crow's discounts.
No healing and no cleanse — sustain is purely shield-based and temporary.

power_assessment.reasoning: A control-first toolbox character with a clean, repeatable 1-turn banish on a 1-CD ability (premium removal), a flexible counter, strong self-durability, and a mid-fight transformation into an uncounterable Piercing burst dealer with a seal->bonus-damage combo. Low specific-color cost and self-feeding economy make the kit smooth to pilot. Held back from top tier by no AoE, modest raw damage, multi-turn setup on his best lines, and a power spike gated behind taking damage (HP<50) that may never trigger versus passive opponents. Strong, high-skill-ceiling pick rather than an oppressive one.
outlier_flags: Repeatable 1-turn banish on a 1-CD, ~2-cost ability is unusually strong hard-removal density.
Two of his Susanoo nukes are BOTH Piercing AND Uncounterable, ignoring most defensive tech.
STALE JSON: Susanoo grants 35 Shield in code (not 50) and has NO 10 Affliction/turn self-damage downside — the code version is strictly stronger/cleaner than the listed description.
STALE JSON: Yasaka Magatama base damage is 40 in code (not 50); peak with seal is 60 (not 70).
Crow Clone grants an undocumented 10 invisible self-Shield each cast (per split_desc), adding hidden durability not in the main JSON description.

abilities.name: Maria The Ripper
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 15 Normal + 10 Affliction (25 total, 10 bypasses barriers/shields) to one enemy. Gated: can only target Isolated or Fog-of-London-marked enemies. If the target is Isolated, applies a self cost-change so Fog of London costs only 1 Random next turn.
abilities.conditional_scaling: Conditional access only (must be Isolated/Fogged); flat damage, no per-stack scaling.

abilities.name: Fog of London
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 5 Affliction immediately to all enemies plus a 5 Affliction/turn DoT (~2-3 ticks, dur 5), applies 50% reduced healing for 3 turns (dur 6), and a Fog mark (dur 5) that lets Jack treat all marked enemies as Isolated for targeting jack1/jack3/jack4. Uncounterable. Key enabler that turns one AoE press into team-wide target access.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

abilities.name: We Are Jack
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 30 pure Affliction (bypasses barriers/shields/DR) to a single enemy. Hard-gated: target must be BOTH Isolated AND Fog-marked. No cooldown, so repeatable each turn against a valid target.
abilities.conditional_scaling: Conditional access only (needs Isolated AND Fogged simultaneously).

abilities.name: Smokescreen Ambush
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 15 Normal to target enemy and makes Jack Invulnerable for 1 turn (dur 2). Cooldown -2 if target is Isolated and another -2 if Fog-marked (both can apply, up to -4), so against a set-up target it becomes near-spammable defensive tempo.
abilities.conditional_scaling: Cooldown refund scales with target state (Isolated and/or Fogged), not damage.

abilities.name: Streets of the Lost
abilities.effects_summary: Passive isolation engine: at end of any turn, any enemy who was the only character to act (or the only one not to act) becomes Isolated for 1 turn (dur 3). Uncleansable (cleansable=false). Free secondary source of the Isolated condition that gates Jack's whole kit, especially in 1v1/low-count or stalled boards.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Flat, no real scaling. One-turn ceiling on a fully set-up target (Isolated + Fogged): jack3 30 + jack1 25 (15 Normal + 10 Affliction) + jack4 15 = 70, of which ~40 is barrier/DR-bypassing Affliction. Plus the ongoing 5/turn Fog DoT. Realistic per-turn output is closer to 30-55 since the kit competes for one thin energy pool and Jack often spends a press on setup or self-peel.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is flat, no per-stack/per-kill scaling. Strength is the high Affliction fraction (jack1 10, jack3 30, jack2 5/turn) which ignores shields/barriers/DR, plus 50% anti-heal making chip sticky. AoE is tiny (5 upfront + DoT); Jack is a single-target executioner, not a wave-clearer.

economy.color_dependency: Light two-color (Green + White): jack1=Green:1, jack2=White:1, jack3/jack4=Random:1 each. Only 2 of 4 visible pips are color-locked and they sit on the two halves of the kit (enabler jack2=White, finisher jack1=Green), so Jack wants an even Green/White trickle but is otherwise flexible. Character colors [Green, White].
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast. jack1 and jack3 are 0-cooldown and pressable every turn; jack2/jack4 are 4-cd but jack4 refunds up to -4 vs a set-up target, effectively low-cooldown once Fog is out. Bottleneck is energy (four 1-pip skills competing for 1-2 pips/turn), not cooldowns.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low-to-moderate setup dependency, no stat ramp. Must first establish Isolated and/or Fog-marked (via jack2, the jack5 passive, or external isolation) before jack1/jack3/jack4-discount come online; once Fog is up the kit unlocks team-wide for ~3 turns with no further investment.

soft_cc: Isolated (jack5 passive end-of-turn; jack2 mark grants Isolated-equivalent targeting)
invuln_or_counter: Self-Invulnerable 1 turn on jack4 (Smokescreen Ambush)

win_conditions: Land Fog of London (jack2) to unlock the whole kit team-wide for 3 turns, then hammer a priority target with jack3 (30 Affliction) + jack1 (25) each turn while the 50% heal-cut prevents the enemy from undoing the chip.
Use the jack5 isolation passive plus jack4's self-invuln to grind down a single high-value target in attrition/low-count boards where enemies naturally end up 'only one to act / not act'.
Out-value a barrier/shield/regen-heavy comp by leaning on Affliction (shield-bypassing) damage and anti-heal.
internal_synergies: Fog of London (jack2) is the linchpin: its mark makes ALL enemies count as Isolated, simultaneously unlocking jack1, jack3, and the jack4 cooldown discount, and its anti-heal protects the DoT chip.
jack3 requires BOTH Isolated AND Fogged — jack5 passive supplies the Isolated half while jack2 supplies the Fog half, stacking into the 30-damage finisher.
jack1 vs an Isolated target discounts next-turn Fog of London to 1 Random, smoothing the White requirement and letting Jack re-apply Fog cheaply.
jack4's cooldown refund (-4 vs Isolated+Fogged target) gives near-free recurring self-invulnerability once setup is online, so Jack survives while ticking the enemy down.
All affliction/DoT pieces ignore barriers/shields and pair with heal-cut for sticky, hard-to-erase damage.
strengths: High proportion of barrier/shield/DR-bypassing Affliction damage (10 + 30 + 5/turn) — strong vs tank/shield comps.
50% anti-heal on jack2 hard-counters sustain/healer comps and locks in the DoT.
Extremely energy-cheap kit (every skill 1 pip, two are free-cooldown) and only lightly color-dependent.
Self-Invulnerability on jack4 with cooldown refunds gives strong self-peel/survivability for an assassin.
jack2 is Uncounterable, so the enabler can't be denied by counter abilities.
jack5 provides a free, uncleansable isolation source that keeps the kit functional even without spending on jack2.
weaknesses: Heavily gated: jack1/jack3/jack4-discount do nothing unless the target is Isolated and/or Fog-marked — a hard cold-start before setup lands.
jack3 (the 30-damage payoff) needs BOTH conditions at once, a narrow window good play can avoid.
Almost no AoE (5 upfront + 5/turn) — poor at clearing multiple targets; a single-target executioner.
No hard CC, no healing, no ally shields, no cleanse, no energy denial — contributes only damage and self-peel to the team.
Energy bottleneck: four 1-pip skills compete for a thin Green/White pool, so Jack rarely fires her full combo in one turn.
DoT can be slow vs burst-race comps that simply kill Jack or her team first; the Fog mark/damage are cleansable (only the jack5 trigger is not).
signature_mechanic: "Condition-gated affliction assassination: Jack can only attack enemies that are Isolated or marked by Fog of London. Fog of London (team-wide mark + anti-heal) and the Streets of the Lost passive (free end-of-turn Isolation) are the keys that unlock escalating single-target Affliction damage, capped by jack3 (30) which needs both conditions."
role: "single-target affliction/DoT assassin with anti-heal and self-peel; setup-then-execute"

power_assessment.reasoning: Strong, well-defined kit with clear identity: barrier/shield-bypassing Affliction damage, hard anti-heal, self-invuln, and an extremely cheap energy curve. Peak single-target ~70 in one turn on a set-up target plus an ongoing 5/turn DoT and 50% heal-cut is excellent focused-kill pressure, and the Affliction typing resists defensive comps. The big limiter is conditional access: nearly the whole kit is locked behind Isolated/Fogged, so there is a real cold-start and counterplay window, and jack3's double-condition gate plus the thin energy pool mean she rarely hits her theoretical ceiling. Zero team utility beyond damage and self-peel. Net: a high-skill, comp-dependent single-target specialist — above average against the right targets, below S-tier due to setup fragility and no AoE/team support. Rating will swing with how easily Isolation is achieved on the live roster.
outlier_flags: jack3 30 Affliction at 1 Random + 0 cooldown is a very efficient repeatable finisher if both conditions stay up
jack4 cooldown can refund to 0 (-4) giving near-permanent self-invuln uptime vs a set-up target — potential durability outlier
jack2 is Uncounterable AND applies a team-wide Isolated-equivalent mark for only 1 White pip — unusually high enabling value for the cost

role: Shield-stacking ramp/fusion bruiser-support: layer Elemental HERO buffs, then fuse into a permanent payoff (DoT, anti-shield control, mega-shield, or team cleanse)
signature_mechanic: Four 1-pip self-buffs (one per energy color) each grant a 15 Shield + a per-turn effect and swap that slot into a Fusion. Holding any TWO of the right base buffs simultaneously unlocks the matching 2-pip Fusion (slots 5-8), which consumes both bases and applies a permanent effect. Player picks which two colors to ramp to steer toward damage, anti-shield, tank, or cleanse.

abilities.name: Elemental HERO Avian
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self: 15 Shield for 3 turns. Applies a 5-turn ticking debuff causing all enemies to deal 5 less non-Affliction damage (refreshed each turn). Swaps this slot to Flame Wingman (fusion enabler).

abilities.name: Elemental HERO Burstinatrix
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self: 15 Shield for 3 turns. Immediately deals 10 Affliction (bypasses shields/DR) to ALL enemies, then repeats 10 Affliction AoE each turn for 5 turns via ticking trigger. Swaps this slot to Rampart Blaster.

abilities.name: Elemental HERO Clayman
abilities.conditional_scaling: Clayman's own Shield grows +10/turn, capped at 45 (self-reinforcing tank value)
abilities.effects_summary: Self: 15 Shield for 3 turns. Each turn (and immediately) the Clayman Shield gains +10, capped at 45, via 5-turn ticking trigger. Swaps this slot to Mudballman.

abilities.name: Elemental HERO Bubbleman
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self: 15 Shield for 3 turns. Immediately and each turn for 5 turns heals the whole team 10 HP (ticking trigger). Swaps this slot to Mariner.

abilities.name: Elemental HERO Flame Wingman
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent recurring damage (effect dur -1) — value scales with how long Jaden survives
abilities.effects_summary: Fusion (needs Avian+Burstinatrix held; consumes both). Immediately deals 35 Normal to a random enemy, then 35 Normal to a random enemy every turn PERMANENTLY (never expires). No new shield is applied in code despite the JSON text.

abilities.name: Elemental HERO Rampart Blaster
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent (dur -1) — reapplied to all enemies every turn indefinitely
abilities.effects_summary: Fusion (needs Clayman+Burstinatrix; consumes both). PERMANENTLY each turn applies Shatter (def_negate, ignores enemy DEF) AND a no-Shield lock to ALL enemies. Pure team-wide debuff/anti-tank control; deals no direct damage itself but amplifies all incoming damage on the enemy team.

abilities.name: Elemental HERO Mudballman
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Fusion (needs Clayman+Bubbleman; consumes both). Grants a single permanent 80 Shield (dur -1). Pure tank payoff. (JSON says 100; split_desc/code say 80.)

abilities.name: Elemental HERO Mariner
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent (dur -1) cleanse loop
abilities.effects_summary: Fusion (needs Avian+Bubbleman; consumes both). PERMANENTLY cleanses ALL Harmful enemy effects off the entire team every turn (and immediately). Strong anti-debuff/anti-DoT/anti-control support engine.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No per-hit number scaling — numbers are fixed (35 Normal random-target/turn from Flame Wingman; 10 Affliction AoE/turn from Burstinatrix). 'Scaling' is purely durational: Flame Wingman and Rampart Blaster are PERMANENT, so over a long game Jaden's enabled-DoT and Shatter value compounds unbounded with survival. Fusion consumes the base buffs, so steady output is ~35 single OR ~10 AoE Affliction, not both at once.
damage_profile.notes: Flame Wingman 35 is Normal (blocked by enemy shields/DR). Burstinatrix 10 is Affliction (bypasses shields/DR/barriers) and hits ALL enemies, so its effective damage is higher than its raw number in shielded matchups. Rampart Blaster deals no damage but its permanent Shatter + shield-lock massively boosts an allied damage dealer's effective output. True burst is low; Jaden wins through attrition.

economy.color_dependency: Heavy and unusually spread: the 4 visible base skills cost one pip each of a DIFFERENT color (White, Red, Green, Blue). To reach any Fusion you must afford TWO specific colors in overlapping turns. Rainbow identity (character_colors [0,1,2,3]) means he wants a balanced 4-color economy and is punished by mono-color energy droughts.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Base skills CD2, fusions CD3. Slow ramp: realistically 2 setup turns (cast two correct bases) before a fusion comes online turn 3+. Instant class = no charge-up lock, but the shield (3 turns) / trigger (5 turns) windows gate fusion timing.
economy.ramp_dependency: Very high. Jaden does almost nothing impactful turn 1 beyond a 15 shield + minor tick; his power is entirely back-loaded into surviving long enough to assemble and fire a permanent fusion. Hard ceiling if rushed down before fusing.

soft_cc: enemy non-Affliction damage -5 (Avian)
enemies cannot gain Shield (Rampart Blaster)
Shatter / DEF-negate on all enemies (Rampart Blaster)

win_conditions: Survive the early game on stacked shields, fuse into Flame Wingman for inevitable permanent 35/turn chip the enemy can never remove
Use Rampart Blaster to permanently Shatter + shield-lock the whole enemy team so an allied carry deletes them
Out-attrition via Bubbleman/Mariner sustain: permanent team cleanse (Mariner) + heals neutralize DoT/control comps
Become an unkillable wall (Mudballman 80 permanent shield + Clayman ramp) and win on the clock
internal_synergies: Each base buff is both a shield source AND a fusion key, so casting bases is never wasted tempo
Burstinatrix's Affliction AoE bypasses shields, complementing Rampart Blaster which strips enemy shields/DEF for the rest of the team
Avian's incoming-damage-reduction debuff + base shields make the ramp window survivable
Clayman self-growing shield (to 45) feeds the tank fusion (Mudballman) and buys ramp time
Mariner's permanent team cleanse protects the squishy ramp and keeps the other permanent fusion engines alive
Player chooses fusion path reactively: damage (Flame Wingman) vs anti-tank (Rampart) vs wall (Mudballman) vs anti-control (Mariner) from the same 4-card setup
strengths: Permanent, unremovable payoff effects (Flame Wingman DoT, Rampart Shatter/shield-lock, Mariner cleanse) generate runaway value the longer the game goes
Extremely flexible — one kit covers damage, hard tanking, anti-shield control, and team support depending on color path chosen mid-match
Strong shield self-sustain plus team healing makes him hard to burst and a real attrition threat
Permanent team-wide cleanse (Mariner) is a rare, very high-value answer to DoT/debuff/control comps
Affliction AoE + Rampart shield-strip give him real reach against tanky/shielded enemy teams
Every base cast advances toward a fusion, so little dead tempo once colors are available
weaknesses: Slow, back-loaded ramp: weak and low-impact for the first 2-3 turns; vulnerable to rush/burst before fusing
Severe four-color energy dependency — each fusion needs two specific colors; color screw cripples him
Low burst and low raw single-target ceiling (35 Normal, blocked by shields/DR) — can be out-DPS'd by dedicated assassins
Fusion consumes both base buffs, so he can't easily run two payoff engines at once; committing to one fusion forecloses others until re-ramped
No hard CC and no invuln/counter — relies purely on shields to live, so shield-ignoring/Affliction enemies or DEF-negate counter him
JSON descriptions are stale (claim 25/45/100 shield) vs actual 15/15/80 — true durability is lower than advertised

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-designed, high-skill flexible ramp character. In isolation his late-game is strong: PERMANENT effects (35 random-target DoT, team-wide Shatter+shield-lock, infinite team cleanse) plus heavy shield/heal sustain make him an excellent attrition and anti-meta tool that snowballs with survival. But he is balanced by a genuinely slow, color-hungry start, low burst, and the fact fusions cancel his base buffs so he can't stack payoffs. He is a strong durable utility piece, not a top-tier carry — rewards good play and color access, punished by aggro and energy screw. Rated 6.5 in isolation; could rise in slow/control metas where his permanent engines dominate, or fall in fast burst metas.
outlier_flags: 8 abilities (4 visible + 4 fusion alts) — large, more complex kit than a typical roster entry
All payoff (fusion) effects are PERMANENT/dur -1 — uncommon and potentially snowbally; watch for unbounded value in long games
Stale JSON vs code: real shields are 15/15/80 not 25/45/100 — numbers here come from the .gd ground truth
Pure rainbow 4-color identity with all specific (zero random) pips is an extreme economy requirement
Rampart Blaster and Mariner deal zero damage but provide outsized control/support — power invisible to raw damage metrics

role: single-target isolation/lockdown controller with an execute finisher and light team support
signature_mechanic: Gibbet isolation: permanently marks one enemy so it can ONLY target Jeanne or itself and cannot be targeted by Jeanne's allies, then grinds that locked-in enemy down with Skull and Knee Crushers (damage + cost-up) until it drops to <=35 HP, at which point Guillotine instantly executes it. Wrapped around the Iron Maiden toggle, which keeps Jeanne untargetable and healing 10/turn while inactive and forces permanent active mode (and a permanent isolation engine) when she is the team's last survivor.

abilities.name: Iron Maiden
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Toggle stance. While INACTIVE (Iron Maiden MARK on self): untargetable by anyone and heals 10 HP each turn, but cannot use her offensive kit; ending Iron Maiden also ends all active Gibbets. While ACTIVE: targetable and can use her other skills. Auto-starts active if she has no targetable living ally and becomes PERMANENTLY active (locked engine) when she is the only targetable survivor on her team. Watchers (ON_DEATH/TICKING triggers on every ally) flip her to active the instant her last ally is removed.

abilities.name: Gibbet
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Permanent (-1 duration) isolation mark on one enemy: that enemy can ONLY target Jeanne or itself and CANNOT be targeted by Jeanne's allies (one-sided taunt + ally-protection). Swaps in Skull and Knee Crushers while active and installs an HP watcher that swaps in Guillotine when the target falls to <=35 HP. Death watcher cleans up the swaps on target death. No damage itself.

abilities.name: Shamash Judgment
abilities.conditional_scaling: triggers per Harmful skill used on Jeanne during the window
abilities.effects_summary: HARMFUL_RECEIVE_TRIGGER counter (duration 4) on self: any enemy that uses a Harmful skill on Jeanne during the window takes 20 NORMAL damage (reflect/retaliation). Can fire multiple times if multiple enemies attack her. Pure deterrent/punish, no mitigation.

abilities.name: Shamash's Kiss
abilities.conditional_scaling: mode depends on target state (alive -> invuln, dead -> revive)
abilities.effects_summary: Targets self or any ally (including dead). If the target is alive: grants Invulnerable for 1 turn (dur 2). If the target is dead: resurrects them at 35 HP instead. Strong single-target protection / revive on a 4-turn cooldown.

abilities.name: Skull and Knee Crushers
abilities.conditional_scaling: none on damage; enables Guillotine execute once target <=35 HP
abilities.effects_summary: Replaces the Gibbet slot while a Gibbet target exists. Deals 25 NORMAL damage to the Gibbet target and applies a cost_mod_effect (+1 Random energy to the target's skill costs for 1 turn) — energy denial. Spammable (cd 0). When the target reaches <=35 HP, this slot is swapped to Guillotine.

abilities.name: Guillotine
abilities.conditional_scaling: execute threshold: any HP <=35 -> instant kill
abilities.effects_summary: Instant-kill (instant_kill) the Gibbet target if its HP is <=35. Bypasses HP as raw damage (execute / removal). 1 White pip, no cooldown. The payoff of the Gibbet -> Crushers chain.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No numeric scaling. Effective ceiling is the Guillotine execute: any enemy at <=35 HP is removed outright regardless of its max HP, and Gibbet's isolation can keep that single target locked indefinitely. Per-turn direct output caps around 45 (Skull and Knee Crushers 25 + Shamash Judgment 20 retaliation if attacked). No multi-target damage anywhere.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is Normal type (subject to DR/barriers) except the Guillotine execute, which is an instant_kill (treated here as True/raw removal). Single-target only. Skull and Knee Crushers (25) is the repeatable grind tool; Shamash Judgment adds 20 per enemy Harmful action against Jeanne. The kit deliberately trades raw numbers for control: it locks one enemy down, slowly lowers it, then deletes it under 35 HP.

economy.color_dependency: Very low. The 4 visible skills cost 1 White + 6 Random across the whole bar (Iron Maiden 1R, Gibbet 2R, Shamash Judgment 2R, Shamash's Kiss W+R). The damage/execute alt skills (Skull and Knee Crushers W+R, Guillotine W) lean on White but only 1 White pip at a time. Extremely flexible to splash into almost any team.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Mostly cooldown-free: Iron Maiden, Gibbet, Skull and Knee Crushers, and Guillotine all have cd 0, enabling turn-after-turn grinding of the isolated target. Only Shamash Judgment (cd 2) and Shamash's Kiss (cd 4) are gated.
economy.ramp_dependency: Setup-dependent rather than ramp-dependent: she must spend a turn on Gibbet (and be in active stance via Iron Maiden) before her damage engine comes online, then a few turns of Skull and Knee Crushers to reach the <=35 HP execute window. No stacking resource.

hard_cc: Guillotine instant-kill/execute (removal) on <=35 HP Gibbet target
soft_cc: Gibbet one-sided taunt: locks target to only attack Jeanne or itself
Gibbet ally-protection: target cannot be targeted by Jeanne's allies
Skull and Knee Crushers cost increase (+1 Random for 1 turn) = action/tempo denial
invuln_or_counter: Shamash's Kiss invulnerability (1 turn, self or ally)
Shamash Judgment 20-damage retaliation on any Harmful skill used on Jeanne

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, low-color-dependency control specialist with a genuinely strong toolbox: a near-permanent untargetable/self-heal stance (Iron Maiden, also a built-in last-survivor failsafe), a permanent single-target isolation lock that doubles as a one-sided taunt AND ally-protection (Gibbet), repeatable energy denial + grind damage (Skull and Knee Crushers, cd 0), an unconditional execute on <=35 HP (Guillotine), plus support in the form of single-target invulnerability and a full resurrection (Shamash's Kiss). That breadth on a 7-pip / 6-Random visible kit is excellent value. It rates short of top tier because output is strictly single-target and low (peak ~45/turn, no AoE), the execute and revive both key on a 35 HP threshold so they whiff against high-HP bricks until ground down, and the whole engine is gated behind setup turns and the active-stance requirement. Strong in 1v1 / cleanup and as a sticky disruptor; weak versus burst comps and wide boards.
outlier_flags: execute-removal: Guillotine instant-kills any enemy at <=35 HP for 1 White pip with no cooldown
near-permanent untargetability + 10 HP/turn self-heal via Iron Maiden inactive stance
permanent (-1 duration) hard isolation lock that both taunts the target onto Jeanne and shields the rest of her team from it
full resurrection (35 HP) on a 4-turn cooldown skill that otherwise grants invulnerability

strengths: Permanent single-target isolation (Gibbet): forces the locked enemy to attack only Jeanne or itself and protects all of Jeanne's allies from it, effectively neutralizing a key threat for the whole game
Unconditional execute (Guillotine) deletes any Gibbet target at <=35 HP for 1 pip, no cooldown
Cooldown-free grind engine: Iron Maiden / Gibbet / Skull and Knee Crushers / Guillotine all cd 0
Very low color dependency (1 White + 6 Random across the visible bar) makes her splashable on any team
Built-in survivability and a last-stand failsafe: untargetable + 10 HP/turn while inactive, and permanent active engine when she is the only one standing
Real support value: 1-turn invulnerability or a full resurrection (35 HP) plus energy denial and an attack-punishing counter
weaknesses: Strictly single-target; zero AoE and no help against wide/swarm boards
Low raw damage (peak ~45 in a turn, 25 sustained) means killing a high-HP target is slow and requires reaching the 35 HP execute window
Setup tax: needs active stance + a turn on Gibbet before her damage/execute chain comes online
Execute and revive both hinge on a fixed 35 HP threshold, so they are weak against very high-HP enemies until ground down and offer nothing extra against low-cap targets
While inactive she heals/hides but contributes no offense; while active she becomes targetable and is fragile (no shields, no DR, no cleanse)
Energy denial is mild (+1 Random for only 1 turn) and her retaliation/counter only triggers when enemies choose to hit her
win_conditions: Lock the enemy's primary carry or healer under Gibbet, grind it with Skull and Knee Crushers, and Guillotine it once <=35 HP, removing it permanently
Use Gibbet's taunt to soak/redirect a dangerous attacker onto an untargetable-cycling Jeanne while the rest of her team free-hits the unprotected enemies
Outlast into the late game: survive on Iron Maiden self-heal/untargetability, then leverage the permanent solo-survivor engine plus revive to flip a losing board
internal_synergies: Gibbet -> Skull and Knee Crushers -> Guillotine is the core chain: isolation enables the cd-0 grind, the grind enables the execute swap

Iron Maiden's inactive stance (untargetable + heal) lets Jeanne survive while her Gibbet lock and counters do passive work; its solo-survivor clause guarantees the engine never shuts off when she is last alive
Skull and Knee Crushers' cost-up stacks tempo pressure on the same enemy Gibbet has already cut off from the rest of the fight
Shamash Judgment punishes enemies for attacking the Jeanne that Gibbet is funneling aggression toward
Shamash's Kiss revive pairs with the team's longevity plan, turning Jeanne's stall into a comeback engine

role: Ramping stack-scaling bruiser/controller who snowballs Crystal Beasts into a single-target nuke transformation
signature_mechanic: Crystal Beasts stacking mark: a permanent (-1 duration) self-mark that accumulates via multiple skills, scales jesse1 and jesse2 damage, fuels jesse4's invuln, and at 7+ stacks permanently swaps jesse1 into the 75-Piercing Rainbow Dragon nuke.

abilities.name: Crystal Beasts
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage per existing Crystal Beasts stack on Jesse (read BEFORE adding); base 20. Then grants 2 stacks. At 7+ stacks after, permanently swaps this slot to Rainbow Dragon (jesse5).
abilities.effects_summary: Single-target Normal damage 20 + 5/stack; self-adds 2 stacks of Crystal Beasts (permanent mark); triggers permanent ability swap to Rainbow Dragon at 7+ stacks. 0 cooldown, spammable ramp engine.

abilities.name: Crystal Abundance
abilities.conditional_scaling: Stack-gated AoE: >=1 stack = 10; >=3 stacks = 20; >=7 stacks = 30 to all enemies. Requires >=1 stack to use.
abilities.effects_summary: AoE Normal damage scaling 10/20/30 by stack threshold; at >=5 stacks also stuns each target's Harmful skills for 1 turn (dur 2). Usability gated on >=1 stack. Soft CC + cheap AoE.

abilities.name: Crystal Blessing
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat); adds to ramp (+1 stack)
abilities.effects_summary: Self-heal 15 HP and +1 Crystal Beasts stack (sourced to jesse1 so it shares the mark; can itself trigger the 7-stack Rainbow Dragon swap). 0 cooldown ramp accelerator + sustain.

abilities.name: Crystal Promise
abilities.conditional_scaling: none; consumes 1 stack as fuel
abilities.effects_summary: Consumes 1 Crystal Beasts stack to grant Jesse Invulnerability for 1 turn (dur 2). Usability gated on >=1 stack. 2-turn cooldown panic button; minor anti-synergy with stack ramp.

abilities.name: Rainbow Dragon
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat 75); unlocked only after reaching 7+ stacks via jesse1/jesse3 swap
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden transformation payoff: replaces jesse1 permanently. 75 Piercing damage (skips flat+%DR), Uncounterable and Bypassing. No further stack interaction. Endgame nuke, 1 cooldown.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Pre-transformation jesse1 caps practically: it swaps to Rainbow Dragon at 7+ stacks, so the highest jesse1 hit you typically see is ~20+5*6 = 50 (at 6 stacks before the swap-triggering use). Post-transformation single-target is a flat 75 Piercing every turn (1cd). AoE caps at 30 to all enemies (7+ stacks). No DoT.
damage_profile.notes: No bleed/affliction/DoT. Burst is front-loaded into the 75 Piercing Rainbow Dragon after ramp. jesse1 reads stacks BEFORE adding its own 2, so early hits are modest (T1=20, T2=30, T3=40). Rainbow Dragon's 75 Piercing skips flat and % damage reduction, making effective damage high vs tanky targets; it is also Uncounterable/Bypassing.

economy.color_dependency: Light Green dependency: 2 specific Green pips (jesse1, jesse2), rest random. Single-color identity, easy to fit into most teams.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast: jesse1 and jesse3 are 0-cooldown ramp engines; jesse2 is 1cd, jesse4 is 2cd. Rainbow Dragon is 1cd. Can act and build stacks every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Almost everything keys off Crystal Beasts stacks. jesse2 is dead until 1 stack; jesse4 needs a stack; the payoff (Rainbow Dragon + AoE stun + triple AoE) requires 5-7 stacks. Stacks build ~2-3/turn so the kit comes online around turns 3-4.

soft_cc: Crystal Abundance (jesse2) at 5+ stacks stuns each target's Harmful skills for 1 turn (class-specific stun, not a full stun)
invuln_or_counter: Crystal Promise (jesse4): 1-turn Invulnerability (consumes 1 stack)

win_conditions: Survive the early ramp turns, hit 7+ Crystal Beasts stacks, and unlock Rainbow Dragon to nuke key targets with 75 Piercing (DR-ignoring) damage repeatedly.
Stall/control with jesse2's 5+ stack Harmful-skill stun while AoE chipping the whole enemy team for 20-30.
Use self-heal (jesse3) + invuln (jesse4) to outlast and win attrition fights once scaled.
internal_synergies: jesse1 + jesse3 both add stacks and can both trigger the Rainbow Dragon swap, so you can ramp on turns you don't want to attack (and heal while doing it).
Stacks simultaneously fuel jesse1 damage scaling, jesse2 AoE thresholds + stun, and jesse4 invuln - every stack-builder advances three payoffs at once.
jesse2's Harmful-skill stun (5+ stacks) buys survival turns to keep ramping toward the 7-stack Rainbow Dragon swap.
Rainbow Dragon being Uncounterable/Bypassing/Piercing means the late-game payoff ignores most defensive answers.
strengths: Cheap, single-color (Green) kit with 0-cooldown ramp engines - very fast tempo and easy to slot.
Strong, multi-purpose scaling: one resource (stacks) powers single-target damage, AoE damage, AoE control, and defense.
Self-sufficient survivability: built-in heal (jesse3) AND 1-turn invuln panic button (jesse4) with no ally support needed.
Excellent payoff: 75 Piercing Uncounterable/Bypassing nuke that ignores DR and most defenses, on a 1-turn cooldown.
Has both AoE damage and a class-specific stun for board control.
weaknesses: Slow start: jesse2 is unusable at 0 stacks, jesse1 reads stacks before adding so early hits are weak (T1 only 20), and the kit doesn't fully come online until ~turn 3-4.
Heavily ramp/stack dependent - anti-stack, cleanse, or mark-removal effects can cripple the entire game plan (a single mark strip resets everything).
No hard CC, no shields/barriers, no cleanse, no energy denial - limited disruption tooling.
jesse4 invuln consumes a stack, creating mild tension between defense and ramp/transformation timing.
Burst is delayed and front-loaded into one transformed skill; before Rainbow Dragon, single-target output is mediocre (~30-50).
Vulnerable to fast aggression / burst that kills him before he scales, since early-game presence is low.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, self-sufficient ramp character. The kit is cheap (5 pips), single-color, and tempo-positive with two 0-cooldown stack builders, and it converts one resource into damage, AoE, control, and defense - that breadth plus built-in heal + invuln makes him resilient and flexible. The Rainbow Dragon payoff (75 Piercing, Uncounterable, Bypassing, 1cd) is a genuinely strong DR-ignoring nuke. He's held back from top tier by a weak early game (low T1-T2 output, jesse2 dead at 0 stacks), full dependence on a single mark that cleanse/mark-removal can erase, and the absence of hard CC or energy denial. Strong in attrition/scaling matchups, soft against fast burst and anti-stack tech.
outlier_flags: Rainbow Dragon 75 Piercing + Uncounterable + Bypassing on a 1-turn cooldown for only 3 random pips is an unusually defense-proof repeatable nuke - verify against roster norms.
jesse1 and jesse3 are both 0-cooldown, allowing potentially aggressive stacking each turn; transformation-gating relies entirely on stacks surviving (single point of failure).

role: Ramping caster who builds Thunder Antenna stacks then dumps them as repeated piercing burst (single-target or AoE)
signature_mechanic: Thunder Antenna stacks: +1 stack each time she casts Supreme Thunder, and +1 each time a Sparkling Wide Pressure team shield is fully destroyed. Each stack adds +5 to Supreme Thunder; with 3+ stacks, Supreme Thunder Dragon consumes ALL stacks and repeats its piercing hit once per stack (15 piercing to main + 5 piercing to each other enemy, per stack).

abilities.name: Supreme Thunder
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage per stack of Thunder Antenna on Jupiter; each cast also grants 1 more stack (self-ramp)
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Normal damage to one enemy; stuns the target's Helpful skills for 1 turn (stun dur 2); grants Jupiter 1 stack of Thunder Antenna (stackable +5 Supreme Thunder damage_mod, infinite duration). Core ramp engine plus soft single-target lockout of support/heal skills.

abilities.name: Flower Hurricane
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Applies Shatter (def_negate, dur 3) to all enemies, deals 15 Normal damage immediately, then applies a 15 Normal damage-over-time effect (dur 3) -> roughly 30 total per enemy across the DoT window (per split_desc: '15 damage for 2 turns'). Shatter strips defenses, enabling follow-up. Pure AoE damage, no scaling.

abilities.name: Supreme Thunder Dragon
abilities.conditional_scaling: Repeats the whole hit once PER stack of Thunder Antenna. Requires 3+ stacks; consumes ALL stacks on use. So 15 Piercing x stacks to main target + 5 Piercing x stacks to each other enemy.
abilities.effects_summary: Splash AoE: 15 Piercing to main target and 5 Piercing to each other enemy, repeated once per Thunder Antenna stack (min 3). At 3 stacks = 45 Piercing main + 15 each other; at 5 stacks = 75 Piercing main + 25 each other. Consumes all stacks. Piercing skips flat and percent DR (the payoff/finisher of the ramp).

abilities.name: Sparkling Wide Pressure
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (but feeds the ramp: full shield destruction grants a Thunder Antenna stack)
abilities.effects_summary: Grants Jupiter's whole team 15 invisible Shield for 1 turn (shield dur 2, counter_timeout wrapup). If a Sparkling Wide Pressure shield is fully destroyed, Jupiter gains 1 Thunder Antenna stack (via gain_shield_break/mission trigger). Team mitigation + alternate ramp source.

abilities.name: Thunder Antenna
abilities.conditional_scaling: Stacking resource: gained on Supreme Thunder use or on Sparkling Wide Pressure shield break
abilities.effects_summary: Passive/hidden resource definition. Source of the stacking +5 Supreme Thunder damage_mod and the stacks consumed by Supreme Thunder Dragon. No direct action (PASS).

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Unbounded via Thunder Antenna stacks. Supreme Thunder Dragon scales linearly: 15 Piercing x stacks to main + 5 Piercing x stacks per other enemy. At a realistic 3-5 stacks: main 45-75 Piercing; AoE total ~75-125 across 3 enemies. Supreme Thunder itself grows +5 per stack (e.g. 20 base -> 40+ once ramped). Higher stack counts (6+) push these numbers further, but each Dragon cast fully resets the resource.
damage_profile.notes: Piercing on the Dragon makes ramped damage bypass flat and percent DR, so effective damage is higher than face value vs tanky targets. Flower Hurricane's Shatter (def_negate) also strips enemy defenses team-wide. Peak single-target 75 and peak AoE 125 assume ~5 banked stacks; floor (3-stack minimum) is 45 single / 75 AoE.

economy.color_dependency: Heavy mono-Blue dependency: 5 of 6 visible pips are Blue (Supreme Thunder 1B, Flower Hurricane 1B+1Rand, Supreme Thunder Dragon 2B, Sparkling Wide Pressure 1B). Wants steady Blue income; starved if Blue is denied.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Low cooldowns: Supreme Thunder/Flower Hurricane/Sparkling Wide Pressure all cd 1, Supreme Thunder Dragon cd 2. She can ramp every turn with no downtime and dump the Dragon roughly every other turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Real payoff requires banking Thunder Antenna stacks (3+ minimum for the Dragon). Opening turns are weak (20 + DoT); she snowballs as stacks accumulate. Sparkling Wide Pressure gives a second, indirect ramp lane through shield breaks.

soft_cc: Supreme Thunder: stuns target's Helpful skills for 1 turn (single-target lockout of support/heal/buff actions)

win_conditions: Survive/ramp the early turns with Supreme Thunder + Sparkling Wide Pressure to bank Thunder Antenna stacks, then unload Supreme Thunder Dragon for a piercing burst that ignores DR
Use Flower Hurricane's team-wide Shatter to crack enemy shields/defenses and chip AoE while the stack count grows
Lock down a key enemy healer/support with Supreme Thunder's Helpful-skill stun while ramping
internal_synergies: Supreme Thunder both buffs itself (+5/stack) AND feeds Thunder Antenna, which feeds Supreme Thunder Dragon - one button drives the whole ramp
Sparkling Wide Pressure is a second ramp lane: enemy damage that fully destroys the team shield converts into Thunder Antenna stacks, turning incoming aggression into Dragon fuel
Flower Hurricane's Shatter strips enemy defenses, increasing the effective output of the Normal-damage portions of her kit (the Dragon is already Piercing, so it least needs it)
Low cooldowns let her chain Supreme Thunder every turn to ramp while still having tempo for Flower Hurricane / Sparkling Wide Pressure
strengths: Scalable, unbounded burst via Thunder Antenna with Piercing payoff that bypasses flat and percent DR
Two independent ramp sources (offensive casts and defensive shield breaks) make the engine hard to fully shut off
Flexible target profile: the Dragon is splash AoE while still hitting a primary hard, so it punishes both clustered teams and single priority targets
Cheap, low-cooldown kit with no dead turns - she always has a productive action
Brings team mitigation (shield) and soft CC (Helpful-skill stun) on top of damage, so she is not a pure glass cannon
Team-wide Shatter is strong utility against shield/defense-heavy compositions
weaknesses: Hard ramp dependency: weak opening turns (only 20 + 15 DoT) and the Dragon needs 3+ banked stacks before it does anything
Severe mono-Blue color dependency (5/6 pips Blue) - vulnerable to Blue energy starvation and bad energy RNG
The Dragon fully consumes all stacks, so burst is feast-or-famine - after a dump she resets to a slow rebuild
No healing, no cleanse, no hard CC, no invuln/counter - thin defensive/utility toolkit beyond a small one-turn shield
Stun only blocks Helpful skills, not a full stun - limited as a lockdown tool
Shield ramp lane is conditional and partly out of her control (requires the shield to be fully destroyed, not just chipped)

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-designed ramp/scaling caster with a clean self-reinforcing loop (Supreme Thunder -> stacks -> Supreme Thunder Dragon) and a clever secondary ramp via shield breaks. Cheap costs and low cooldowns mean she ramps with no downtime, and the Dragon's Piercing payoff scales without an explicit cap, giving real burst (45 at the 3-stack floor, ~75 single / ~125 AoE at ~5 stacks). She also offers genuine utility: team-wide Shatter, a team shield, and a Helpful-skill stun, so she is more than a glass cannon. Held back from a higher rating by a slow start, feast-or-famine stack consumption that resets her after every dump, heavy mono-Blue dependency that makes her fragile to energy denial/RNG, and a thin defensive toolkit (no heal/cleanse/hard CC/invuln). Solidly above average but not oppressive in isolation.
outlier_flags: Unbounded linear scaling on Supreme Thunder Dragon (no visible stack cap) - could spike hard if a match lets her bank many stacks
Piercing burst bypasses DR, making her face damage understate her effective damage vs tanky comps

role: Ramping single-target nuker / AoE bruiser-controller who stacks a dragon for piercing scaling and unlocks a free invuln + AoE transformation
signature_mechanic: Blue-Eyes White Dragon stacking: each kaiba2 cast grants 15 stacking shield + a stacking +5 damage mod to Burst Stream and flags it Piercing/Uncounterable; at 3 stacks slot 1 swaps into Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon (invuln + 40 Piercing AoE). Enemy Controller/Crush Card Virus form a second control/reflect swap pair.

abilities.name: Burst Stream of Destruction
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage per Blue-Eyes White Dragon stack (stacking damage_mod applied by kaiba2); becomes Piercing and Uncounterable while marked by BEWD (>=1 stack)
abilities.effects_summary: Spammable single-target nuke (CD 0). 30 base Normal; 35/40/45 Piercing+Uncounterable at 1/2/3 BEWD stacks. Piercing skips flat+%DR.

abilities.name: Blue-Eyes White Dragon
abilities.cost_breakdown: Random:1 (Hold This! can drop it for a turn; still 1 Random base)
abilities.conditional_scaling: Ramp engine: each cast +15 stacking shield (stack_mag), +5 to Burst Stream, +1 BEWD mark; at 3 stacks swaps slot 1 to Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon
abilities.effects_summary: Self-buff ramp. Per cast: +15 shield (stacks to 30/45), buffs Burst Stream by +5 and makes it Piercing/Uncounterable, advances toward the 3-stack BEUD transformation. CD 0 so it can be cast every turn.

abilities.name: Enemy Controller
abilities.conditional_scaling: If stunned target uses a Helpful/Strategic skill, their Harmful skills get stunned 1 more turn (trigger)
abilities.effects_summary: Targeted soft-CC: stuns target's Harmful skills 1 turn (dur 2). Punishes utility play with +1 turn Harmful stun. Swaps slot 3 to Crush Card Virus.

abilities.name: Hold This!
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Panic button: Kaiba Invulnerable 1 turn (default_defend). Next turn Blue-Eyes White Dragon costs 1 Random (cost reduction), smoothing the ramp. Long CD 4.

abilities.name: Crush Card Virus
abilities.conditional_scaling: Delayed reflect: on expiry all enemies take Normal damage equal to total damage absorbed by the cap (uncapped, bypasses barriers); scales with how hard enemies hit during the 2 turns
abilities.effects_summary: Swap-in from Enemy Controller. For 2 turns (dur 4) caps ALL enemy damage to 15 and reveals their invisible effects. On expiry deals reflected damage = sum of damage prevented (bypasses barriers). Team-wide soft damage-denial + delayed AoE punish. Swaps back to Enemy Controller.

abilities.name: Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (fixed 40 Piercing); gated behind reaching 3 BEWD stacks via kaiba2
abilities.effects_summary: Transformation payoff (replaces Burst Stream at 3 BEWD stacks). Kaiba Invulnerable 1 turn (dur 2) AND 40 Piercing AoE to all enemies, Uncounterable. CD 1, so near-repeatable invuln+AoE once ramped.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Burst Stream caps at 45 Piercing single-target at 3 BEWD stacks (30 + 5*3), at which point slot 1 instead swaps to Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon (40 Piercing AoE + self-invuln, CD 1). Crush Card Virus's reflect is theoretically the highest ceiling: it returns the SUM of all enemy damage capped over 2 turns across all enemies (each hit reduced to 15), uncapped and barrier-bypassing on expiry — vs hard-hitting enemies this can exceed 100 AoE, but it's reactive/enemy-dependent, not Kaiba-controlled.
damage_profile.notes: Damage is modest in raw numbers but quality is high: Burst Stream and BEUD both turn Piercing (skip flat+%DR) and Uncounterable. kaiba2 itself deals no damage; it is pure ramp. Crush Card reflect is the only big number and depends entirely on enemy aggression.

economy.color_dependency: Blue+White (character_colors [1,2]). Visible kit needs exactly 1 Blue (kaiba1) and 1 White (kaiba3); rest is Random, so low/flexible color dependency. The BEUD transformation (kaiba6) demands Blue+White together, and Crush Card (kaiba5) wants White, so a White-heavy turn is needed when both control tools fire.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Two CD-0 core skills (Burst Stream nuke + BEWD ramp) mean Kaiba never idles and can stack while dealing damage. Control/defense are gated: Enemy Controller CD 2, Crush Card CD 3, Hold This! CD 4. BEUD CD 1 once unlocked. Strong turn-to-turn tempo on offense, slower on its CC/defense layer.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate-to-high. Power spikes at 3 BEWD stacks (best-case turn 3-4) unlocking BEUD invuln+AoE and 45 Piercing baseline. Early turns are low-impact (30 Normal + shield). Hold This! accelerates ramp by discounting BEWD.

soft_cc: Enemy Controller: stuns target's Harmful skills 1 turn (+1 more if they use Helpful/Strategic)
Crush Card Virus: caps all enemy damage to 15 for 2 turns (team-wide damage suppression)
invuln_or_counter: Hold This!: self-invuln 1 turn (CD 4)
Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon: self-invuln 1 turn bundled with 40 Piercing AoE (CD 1)
Crush Card Virus: hard damage cap (15) + delayed barrier-bypassing reflect (not invuln but functions as damage denial)

internal_synergies: kaiba2 -> kaiba1: every BEWD stack adds +5 and converts Burst Stream to Piercing+Uncounterable, so the spammable nuke gets better the more you ramp
kaiba2 -> kaiba6: 3 BEWD stacks swap slot 1 to Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon, trading the single-target nuke for invuln+AoE; reaching 3 stacks is the central plan
kaiba4 -> kaiba2: Hold This! discounts BEWD to 1 Random next turn while granting invuln, accelerating the stack-3 timeline safely
kaiba2 shield stacking: repeated casts pile 15->30->45 shield, letting Kaiba ramp under fire
kaiba3 -> kaiba5: Enemy Controller swaps slot 3 into Crush Card Virus, so the control button toggles between a single-target Harmful-stun and a team-wide damage cap + reflect
kaiba5 reveal: Crush Card forces enemy invisible effects visible, countering stealth/hidden-buff comps
strengths: Two CD-0 core skills give relentless tempo: ramp and nuke simultaneously every turn with no downtime
Burst Stream becomes Piercing + Uncounterable at >=1 stack, bypassing flat/%DR and counter abilities — high effective damage despite low raw numbers
Self-sufficient survivability: stacking shields (up to 45), two sources of 1-turn invuln (Hold This!, BEUD), and a team-wide damage cap make him hard to kill while ramping
Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon is an excellent payoff: invuln + 40 Piercing Uncounterable AoE on a 1-turn cooldown
Versatile control layer: single-target Harmful-stun that punishes utility play, plus a team-wide damage suppressor with a scaling barrier-bypassing reflect
Crush Card reveals invisible effects, hard-countering stealth/hidden-effect strategies
Low specific-color dependency (mostly Random pips) makes him easy to fund in most teams
weaknesses: No healing and no cleanse — survivability is shields/invuln only, so sustained chip or affliction/bleed (which bypass shields) wears him down
Ramp-dependent: first 1-2 turns are weak (30 Normal + shield) and a focus-fire kill before stack 3 denies his whole payoff
Crush Card's big reflect is reactive and enemy-controlled — passive/defensive enemies deny it, and it does nothing on its own
Damage cap (15) and the stun are only soft control: it doesn't hard-stun all actions, and DoT/affliction can still tick depending on pipeline
Transformation rigidity: hitting 3 BEWD stacks removes the single-target nuke entirely (slot 1 becomes AoE), which can be a downgrade vs a single priority target
Control tools sit behind CD 2/3/4, so he can be out-tempoed on the defensive/CC axis
BEUD and Crush Card both want White (and BEUD wants Blue+White same turn), creating a brief color crunch on his big turns
win_conditions: Reach 3 Blue-Eyes White Dragon stacks safely (using Hold This! invuln/discount and stacked shields), then loop Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon for repeated invuln + 40 Piercing Uncounterable AoE
Out-survive and out-value via stacked shields + invuln windows while chipping with Piercing Burst Stream
Land Crush Card Virus into an aggressive enemy team to suppress their damage to 15 for 2 turns and then detonate a large barrier-bypassing reflect
Use Enemy Controller to lock a key threat's Harmful skills and tempo them out while ramping

power_assessment.reasoning: Well-designed, self-sufficient ramp bruiser with multiple win axes. The CD-0 ramp+nuke pairing gives him no dead turns, and converting Burst Stream to Piercing+Uncounterable makes his modest raw numbers hit much harder in effective terms. He brings layered defense (stacking shields + two invuln sources + a team-wide damage cap) with zero healing, plus genuine utility (Harmful-stun, damage suppression, invisible-effect reveal, scaling reflect). The Blue-Eyes Ultimate Dragon payoff (invuln + 40 Piercing Uncounterable AoE on CD 1) is strong once online. He is held back from top tier by ramp dependency (weak first turns, killable before stack 3), no healing/cleanse versus affliction/bleed, and a reactive/enemy-dependent reflect that can whiff. Solidly above average but not oppressive in isolation.
outlier_flags: Crush Card Virus reflect has an effectively unbounded ceiling (sum of all damage capped over 2 turns, barrier-bypassing) — potential AoE outlier vs hyper-aggressive comps; verify intended ceiling
split_desc on kaiba1 advertises +5/stack but execute() hardcodes 30 — the +5 actually comes from kaiba2's stacking damage_mod; correct in practice but a maintenance/transparency footgun
Two CD-0 skills (ramp + nuke) on the same character is unusual; gives him no-downtime tempo that may overperform

role: Single-target disruptor/control assassin with strong team protection (counter + invuln)
signature_mechanic: Piercing single-target disruption: every offensive skill ignores DR (Piercing), pairs damage with a hard-shutdown rider (non-mental stun on kakashi1, full damage-nullify + energy drain on kakashi2), while kakashi3/kakashi4 give the team a counter and a 2-person invuln. The passive (kakashi5) makes his own skills immune to counters/reflects.

abilities.name: Lightning Blade Kunai
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 40 Piercing damage (skips flat + % DR) to one enemy and stuns their non-Mental skills for 1 turn (stun_effect dur 2, exclusion = Mental skills). Soft CC that lets them still use Mental skills.

abilities.name: Long-Range Kamui
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 30 Piercing damage; removes 1 random energy (energy denial); applies damage_null_effect(1.0, -1) so the target's NEXT skill deals 100% less damage (full nullify), persisting via an action-use trigger until they use a new skill. Mental class. Invisible debuff.

abilities.name: Lightning Release: Shadow Clone
abilities.conditional_scaling: Conditional on enemy attacking the protected target; 25 Piercing dealt only on a successful counter.
abilities.effects_summary: Self or ally counter (counter_effect, COUNTER_RECEIVE, dur 2 = 1 turn, filter ['Harmful']). The next Harmful skill used on the protected character is countered and the countered enemy takes 25 Piercing. Invisible. Deterrent / punish + soft protection.

abilities.name: Kamui Squad Ambush
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Makes Kakashi AND a selected ally invulnerable for 1 turn (invuln_effect dur 2 on both). Two-target ignore-all-damage save; long 4-turn cooldown.

abilities.name: Copy Ninja Kakashi
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Passive (hidden, not on action bar): ignore_effect_effect on COUNTER_RECEIVE and COUNTER_USE for -1 (permanent). Kakashi's own skills cannot be countered or reflected, letting him strike counter/reflect characters safely.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Flat / no ramp. Both damage skills are CD1 so he can fire kakashi1 (40) + kakashi2 (30) for 70 Piercing in a single turn if energy allows; kakashi3 adds 25 Piercing only on a reactive counter. No per-stack/transformation scaling. All offense is Piercing, so effective damage is unusually high vs DR/armor targets.
damage_profile.notes: No AoE at all (every offensive skill is SINGLE-target). No damage-over-time. Real ceiling is ~70 self-initiated Piercing/turn plus situational 25 counter Piercing. Strength is in riders (energy drain, full damage-nullify, stun), not raw numbers.

economy.color_dependency: High and spread across all four colors: kakashi1 needs Green+Blue, kakashi2 needs White+Red, kakashi3 needs Blue, kakashi4 needs 1 Random. Touching every energy color makes a full-throttle turn energy-hungry and dependent on diverse generation; off-color turns force partial kits.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Aggressive on offense (kakashi1 & kakashi2 both CD1, spammable every turn), medium on protection (kakashi3 CD2), slow on the panic button (kakashi4 invuln CD4).
economy.ramp_dependency: None — no stacking or build-up; effectiveness is immediate and consistent from turn 1.

soft_cc: kakashi1 non-Mental skill stun (1 turn)
kakashi2 full damage-nullify on target's next skill (effectively neutralizes one attack)
invuln_or_counter: kakashi3 counter next Harmful skill (self/ally, 1 turn, +25 Piercing punish)
kakashi4 invulnerability on self + 1 ally (1 turn)
kakashi5 passive: own skills cannot be countered or reflected

internal_synergies: kakashi2's energy drain + full damage-nullify softens a key threat, while kakashi1's non-Mental stun denies their physical/energy options the same turn — chaining both on one target can lock it out of meaningful action.
Piercing on all offense means kakashi1/kakashi2/kakashi3 ignore enemy DR/armor, synergizing with the disruptor identity against tanks.
kakashi5 passive guarantees kakashi1/kakashi2 land on counter/reflect enemies without being turned around.
kakashi3 (counter punish) + kakashi4 (invuln) form a protect-and-deter package for a fragile ally over a 2-turn window.
kakashi2's nullify pairs well with kakashi3: bait an attack into the counter or simply nullify the one skill they do get off.
win_conditions: Tempo/lockdown: repeatedly disrupt the enemy carry with stun (kakashi1) and damage-nullify + energy drain (kakashi2) so the team out-actions them.
Chip + protect: grind Piercing damage that ignores armor while keeping a key ally alive with invuln (kakashi4) and the counter (kakashi3).
Anti-counter sniping: use the uncounterable passive to safely kill reactive/counter-based enemies.
strengths: All offensive damage is Piercing — ignores flat and % DR, so consistent effective damage vs armored/tanky comps.
Strong, varied disruption: non-Mental stun, full single-skill damage nullify, and 1 random energy drain per cast.
Both damage/disruption skills are CD1 and cheap (2 pips each) — high uptime on control.
Excellent team-protection suite for a damage character: ally+self invuln (kakashi4) and a damaging counter (kakashi3).
Passive immunity to counters/reflects makes him a clean answer to reactive characters and removes a common counterplay.
No ramp dependency — fully online from turn 1.
weaknesses: Zero AoE — completely single-target, weak into wide/swarm comps and slow at closing multiple threats.
No healing, no shields/barriers, no cleanse — purely preventive/disruptive defense; once damage lands he can't undo it.
Heavy four-color energy dependency: a full power turn wants Green, Blue, White and Red, so off-color draws cripple his throughput.
Modest raw numbers (40/30/25) with no scaling — damage ceiling is low and stays flat all game.
Key save (kakashi4 invuln) is on a long 4-turn cooldown; protection is bursty, not sustained.
Soft CC only: kakashi1 leaves Mental skills usable and kakashi2 only nullifies one skill, so a determined caster can still operate.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, high-utility tempo/disruptor. Spammable CD1 Piercing damage with a stun and a full damage-nullify, plus energy drain, gives him strong per-turn pressure and control that ignores DR. He also brings a damaging counter and a 2-target invuln, which is a lot of protection for a damage character, and the uncounterable passive removes a whole counterplay category. He's held back from top tier by no AoE, no healing/shields/cleanse, flat low raw numbers with no scaling, a long invuln cooldown, and a demanding four-color cost spread. Effective and flexible, but not a runaway carry — a solid, slightly-above-average disruptor/support hybrid.
outlier_flags: all-Piercing offense (DR-agnostic effective damage)
100% single-skill damage nullify is a strong single-target neutralize
touches all four energy colors in a 4-skill kit (unusually high color dependency)
passive uncounterable/unreflectable is a hard counter to reactive characters

role: single-target bleed/piercing assassin with self-protection
signature_mechanic: Apply Bleed via cheap Tentacle Pierce, then make it permanent with Disembowel; Bloodthirsty Rampage turns Tentacle Pierce into a 2-target random nuke while granting non-damaging-debuff immunity.

abilities.name: Tentacle Pierce
abilities.target_type: SINGLE (becomes 2 random enemies while Bloodthirsty Rampage mark is active)
abilities.conditional_scaling: none — describe() claims +5 per use and 5 base, but the actual execute() deals a flat 5 Piercing + a fixed 15 Bleed; no stacking/escalation in code. While marked by Bloodthirsty Rampage it hits 2 random enemies (pseudo-AoE).
abilities.effects_summary: 5 Piercing immediate damage + a 15 Bleed damage_effect (last_turn_only=true, so it ticks once on the enemy's next turn). 0 cooldown, repeatable. Under Bloodthirsty Rampage mark it retargets to 2 random living non-invuln enemies. Sets up bleed for ken2 to make permanent.

abilities.name: Disembowel
abilities.conditional_scaling: Indirect: converts ANY active Bleed damage effect on the target to permanent (set_duration(-1), last_turn_only=false), turning ken1's one-shot 15 bleed into 15/turn forever — unbounded sustained DoT if stacked.
abilities.effects_summary: 30 Piercing burst (skips flat + % DR). Makes all active Bleed on the target permanent, converting Tentacle Pierce's temporary bleed into an infinite-duration 15/turn tick.

abilities.name: Bloodthirsty Rampage
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self-buff for ~3 turns: ignore_non_damage_effect (immunity to all Harmful non-damaging effects — stuns/CC/debuffs, but NOT damage) + a self mark that makes Tentacle Pierce target 2 random enemies. Combines anti-CC immunity with a pseudo-AoE bleed-application window. (describe() text about auto-counterattacking is stale; real effect is the 2-target retarget.)

abilities.name: Tentacle Block
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: default_defend — self invulnerability for 1 turn. Pure panic button / damage avoidance on a 4-turn cooldown.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No per-use escalation (the describe() +5/use is stale). Real ceiling is permanent-bleed stacking: each Tentacle Pierce applies a 15 Bleed; Disembowel makes all active bleeds permanent. Repeating Tentacle Pierce (0 CD) and converting could stack multiple 15/turn permanent bleeds → unbounded sustained DoT over a long match, but realistically ~15-30/turn permanent. Single-turn burst caps near 35 (ken2 30 Piercing + ken1 5 Piercing), all DR-bypassing.
damage_profile.notes: ken1 Piercing skips flat+%DR; ken2 Piercing skips flat+%DR; Bleed bypasses barriers/shields entirely. So Ken's effective damage vs tanky/shielded targets is high relative to the raw numbers. Burst is low (~35) but the damage is hard to mitigate. AoE figure (30) is the two-target Tentacle Pierce under Rampage = 5 Piercing + 15 Bleed each across 2 random enemies (does not include the 30 single-target on ken2).

economy.color_dependency: Low. Only 2 White pips required across the whole kit (ken1 White:1, ken2 White:1); the rest is Random. Mono-White identity but very flexible to splash.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast offensive loop: ken1 has 0 CD (spammable), ken2 only 1 CD. Defensive/setup buttons (ken3, ken4) are on long 4-turn cooldowns, so protection windows are infrequent.
economy.ramp_dependency: Mild. Damage is back-loaded into stacking permanent bleeds, but no resource/transformation ramp; comes online turn 1.

invuln_or_counter: ken4 Tentacle Block: self invulnerability 1 turn (4 CD)
ken3 Bloodthirsty Rampage: 3-turn immunity to Harmful non-damaging effects (anti-CC, not damage)

win_conditions: Spread 15 Bleed with spammable 0-CD Tentacle Pierce, then lock it in permanently with Disembowel for inevitable DoT attrition.
Use Bloodthirsty Rampage to push through CC-heavy comps (immunity to stuns/debuffs) while spreading bleed to 2 targets.
Out-attrition tanky/shielded teams using all-DR-bypassing Piercing + barrier-bypassing Bleed.
internal_synergies: ken1 -> ken2: Tentacle Pierce seeds a 15 temporary Bleed; Disembowel makes it permanent (core combo).
ken3 -> ken1: Rampage retargets Tentacle Pierce to 2 random enemies, multiplying bleed application for ken2 to lock in.
ken3 + ken4: stacked self-protection layer — non-damaging-effect immunity (anti-CC) plus an invuln turn lets Ken keep cycling Tentacle Pierce safely.
Piercing (ken1/ken2) + Bleed (ken1) both bypass mitigation, so the kit synergizes against defensive archetypes.
strengths: All offensive damage bypasses mitigation: Piercing skips flat+%DR, Bleed skips barriers/shields — strong vs tanks/shield comps.
Permanent-bleed engine creates inevitable, snowballing attrition that can be stacked over a long game.
Very low color commitment (only 2 White pips) and a cheap, spammable 0-CD primary — high tempo and easy to fit on any team.
ken3 grants a rare 3-turn blanket immunity to Harmful non-damaging effects (hard counter to stun/CC controllers).
Self invuln (ken4) gives a clean panic button against burst turns.
weaknesses: Low immediate burst (~35 peak single-target); relies on time and stacking to win, slow to close games.
No team utility whatsoever — no heals, shields for allies, cleanse, or energy denial; purely selfish.
Rampage's 2-target retargeting is RANDOM (can hit the same enemy twice / waste on low-value targets), reducing reliability.
Bleed and Piercing are exactly the damage types most countered by affliction/bleed-immunity or DoT cleanse on the enemy side.
Protective cooldowns are long (4 turns) and offer no damage mitigation against affliction; ken3 immunity explicitly does NOT block damage.
Stale describe()/JSON (claimed escalating +5/use and counterattack) overstate the kit; real numbers are modest.

power_assessment.reasoning: A solid, low-cost attrition assassin whose entire damage profile bypasses mitigation, making it a reliable check against tank/shield comps and CC controllers (via ken3's 3-turn non-damaging-effect immunity). The ken1->ken2 permanent-bleed combo gives a clean, repeatable engine, and a 0-CD primary plus only 2 White pips means excellent tempo and splashability. However, raw output is low (peak ~35 single-target, 15 sustained DoT), it has zero team support, its pseudo-AoE is random and unreliable, and its damage types are exactly what bleed/affliction-immunity counters. Good in a niche, unremarkable on balanced boards. Mid-tier.
outlier_flags: stale_description: ken1 describe()/JSON claims escalating +5-per-use and 5 base, but execute() is a flat 5 Piercing + fixed 15 Bleed with no stacking
stale_description: ken3 describe() claims an auto-counterattack on harmful skills, but execute() actually just makes Tentacle Pierce hit 2 random enemies
all-damage-bypasses-mitigation: unusually mitigation-proof for its low numbers — effective damage > nominal vs defensive targets
permanent-bleed-stacking: theoretical unbounded sustained DoT via repeated Pierce+Disembowel locks

role: Conditional single-target burst dealer with a ramping nuke and a board-wide tempo/control field
signature_mechanic: Stable Resonance: a 4-turn board-wide field that punishes enemies who skip a skill (10 dmg) and rewards allies who use skills (heal 10). Each trigger grants Kid a permanent, stacking +5 damage buff to Death Cannon (the ability Stable Resonance swaps him into), turning passive board pressure into an escalating single-target nuke.

abilities.name: Sanzu River Shot
abilities.conditional_scaling: +15 if target has exactly one living ally whose HP differs from the target; +15 if target has two living allies with mismatched HP from each other (symmetry-break bonus). Max 25 vs an asymmetric enemy team.
abilities.effects_summary: Pure single-target damage. 10 base, scales to 25 when the enemy team's HP values are not symmetrical. Spammable (0 CD, 1 Blue pip).

abilities.name: Fatal Error
abilities.conditional_scaling: Adds a 1-turn stun (stun_effect dur 2) only if the target used a counter last turn (target.was_countered). No damage scaling.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 flat damage, spammable (0 CD). Anti-counter tech: hard-stuns enemies who countered, otherwise just solid cheap chip.

abilities.name: Stable Resonance
abilities.conditional_scaling: Each end-of-turn trigger (enemy skips skill = 10 dmg; ally uses a skill = heal 10) grants Kid a permanent stacking +5 damage_mod to Death Cannon. Unbounded ramp.
abilities.effects_summary: Applies a ~4-turn field: every enemy that does NOT act takes 10 Normal dmg at end of turn; every ally that uses a skill heals 10. Every trigger stacks +5 permanent Death Cannon damage. Swaps Kid's slot-2 into Death Cannon for the duration. Strong tempo coercion + team sustain + ramp engine.

abilities.name: Death Slide
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self-Invulnerable for 1 turn (invuln_effect dur 2 via default_defend). Panic button / dodge a telegraphed nuke. 4-turn CD, flexible 1 Random pip.

abilities.name: Partners: Liz and Patty
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Passive synergy: if Kid and the Thompson Sisters (Liz & Patty) are on the same team, using either sister's Transform skill on Kid auto-activates both transforms (if the other isn't on cooldown). Pure team-comp synergy, no standalone effect (execute is a no-op PASS).

abilities.name: Death Cannon
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 per Stable Resonance trigger via stacking permanent damage_mod (applied in the damage pipeline). Ramps unbounded with field uptime. Using it also strips all 'Stable Resonance' field effects from the board (ends the field early).
abilities.effects_summary: Ramping single-target nuke that replaces Death Slide's slot only while Stable Resonance is active. 30 base + 5 per accumulated trigger. 2-turn CD. The payoff of the Resonance ramp engine.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Death Cannon is theoretically unbounded: 30 + 5 per Stable Resonance trigger. With a full enemy team skipping skills + allies acting, the field can yield 4-8+ triggers per cast, so Death Cannon realistically reaches 50-70+ damage and scales higher with repeated Resonance casts (stacks are permanent). Conditional bursts: kid1 caps at 25 vs asymmetric teams; kid2 flat 20.
damage_profile.notes: No native AoE damage output (Stable Resonance damage is conditional end-of-turn ticks of 10 per non-acting enemy, not a burst). Real peak burst comes from a ramped Death Cannon (hidden slot 6), gated behind Stable Resonance uptime. Base, un-ramped one-turn ceiling from a single visible action is 25 (kid1).

economy.color_dependency: Moderate Green/Blue dual-color dependency. Every damage tool except Death Slide needs a specific Green or Blue pip; Stable Resonance and Death Cannon both demand one of each. Cannot function mono-color.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Front-loaded spam: kid1 and kid2 are both 0-CD 1-pip filler. Stable Resonance is the only long cooldown (5). Death Slide 4 CD, Death Cannon 2 CD. Very fluid tempo outside the Resonance window.
economy.ramp_dependency: High for ceiling, low for floor. Kid plays fine as a cheap spam-damage character on turn 1, but his standout damage (ramped Death Cannon) requires investing a Stable Resonance cast and several turns of field uptime to come online.

hard_cc: 1-turn stun via Fatal Error (conditional: only vs enemies who countered last turn)
soft_cc: Stable Resonance coerces enemy tempo: enemies that skip a skill take 10 dmg, pressuring them to act
invuln_or_counter: Self-invulnerability for 1 turn (Death Slide, 4 CD)

win_conditions: Land Stable Resonance, keep the field up for multiple triggers, then unload a heavily ramped Death Cannon for a kill
Out-tempo the enemy with 0-CD spam (Sanzu River Shot + Fatal Error) while the Resonance field whittles passive/stalling enemies
Punish counter-reliant and stall/turtle compositions: Fatal Error stuns counter-users, Stable Resonance taxes any enemy who skips a turn
internal_synergies: Stable Resonance -> Death Cannon is the core engine: every field trigger permanently buffs the Death Cannon it swaps you into, and the field's heal feeds your own (and allies') skill usage
Stable Resonance heals allies who act, indirectly rewarding the same Death-Cannon-and-spam tempo Kid wants to play
Sanzu River Shot synergizes with focus-fire/uneven-HP boards (its bonus triggers on HP asymmetry), so combining it with allied AoE that leaves teams at different HP enables its +15/+15
Fatal Error pairs with counter-heavy enemies as an anti-counter stun; otherwise just cheap chip
Liz & Patty passive (kid5): on a shared team, auto-activating both Thompson transforms via one cast is a comp-specific tempo boost
strengths: Excellent energy efficiency: two 0-CD, 1-pip damage spells give relentless cheap pressure
Unbounded ramp ceiling on Death Cannon — scales hard against slow/defensive matchups
Multi-tool kit: damage, soft tempo control, a conditional hard stun, team healing, and a self-invuln panic button in only 4-5 buttons
Strong vs turtle/stall and counter comps specifically (Resonance taxes inaction, Fatal Error stuns counterers)
Self-invuln gives survivability without spending a defensive teammate
weaknesses: No native burst AoE — single-target focused; struggles to swing wide boards quickly
Headline damage is conditional and slow: kid1's bonus needs HP asymmetry, Death Cannon needs Resonance ramp turns, Fatal Error's stun needs the enemy to have countered
Dual Green/Blue color requirement; can be starved if the team's energy doesn't supply both
Stable Resonance ramp is fragile/tempo-negative early — investing the 2-pip, 5-CD field with no immediate payoff can lose initiative vs aggressive comps

kid6 split_desc claims it 'consumes all stacks' but the .gd only removes the Stable Resonance field, not the damage_mod stacks — likely a description/implementation mismatch; functionally the ramp may persist beyond intent
Low raw single-cast numbers before ramp (10/20/25) make him underwhelming in fast games

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, efficient toolkit character whose floor is solid (cheap spam + self-invuln + a stun + team heal) and whose ceiling (unbounded ramping Death Cannon) is high but gated behind multi-turn field uptime and dual-color energy. He is strong into stall/turtle and counter comps and energy-efficient, but lacks AoE burst and is tempo-negative when committing to his ramp engine. Most of his damage is conditional, which keeps him from being a top-tier reliable threat but makes him a flexible, matchup-dependent mid-to-upper-mid pick.
outlier_flags: Unbounded Death Cannon ramp (permanent +5/trigger stacks) — potential balance outlier if Stable Resonance is recast repeatedly, since stacks appear permanent and are not actually consumed by the .gd despite the description
kid6 description/code mismatch: 'Consumes all stacks and ends Stable Resonance on use' — code only strips the field, leaving damage_mod stacks intact
