abilities.conditional_scaling: +10 damage (=35) and refunds 1 Red energy if the target is Invulnerable
abilities.effects_summary: Cheap 0-CD spammable single-target nuke that bypasses Invulnerability; vs an invuln target it self-funds (net free Red) and hits for 35. Feeds Rubber Body shield.

abilities.name: Gomu Gomu No Gatling Gun
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent stacking self-buff: +5 damage to this skill each cast (per_stack, dur -1, no cap). Against any enemy who is Invulnerable, also applies a 10-damage Normal DoT that hits again next turn (dur 3).
abilities.effects_summary: AoE that ramps indefinitely (+5/cast) and bypasses invuln. Each cast stacks a permanent damage-mod buff so late-game AoE grows unbounded; invuln enemies eat an extra delayed 10 hit.

abilities.name: Gomu Gomu No Bazooka
abilities.conditional_scaling: If the target is Invulnerable: full stun for 1 turn (stun_effect dur 2). No damage increase.
abilities.effects_summary: Hard-hitting 40 single-target that bypasses invuln; punishes invuln-reliant enemies with a hard CC full stun. Biggest single shield-feed for Rubber Body.

abilities.name: Gomu Gomu No Balloon
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self invulnerability for 1 turn (invuln_effect dur 2). Panic-button defensive cooldown; AI uses it as a self panic button.

abilities.name: Rubber Body
abilities.conditional_scaling: Flat per-trigger, not damage-scaled despite stale JSON
abilities.effects_summary: Passive: on any DAMAGE_DEALT trigger, Luffy gains a flat 15 Shield for 1 turn (shield_effect 15, dur 2). NOTE: live .gd grants flat 15, not 'equal to damage' as the JSON metadata claims.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: luffy2 ramps +5 damage per cast with no cap (permanent stackable per_stack buff), so AoE per-target damage grows linearly with game length: 10/15/20/25... In a long match the AoE can exceed the 40 single-target. Single-target is fixed (25 / 35-on-invuln / 40). DoT and stun riders only proc vs Invulnerable enemies.
damage_profile.notes: peak_aoe_one_turn=10 is the BASE first cast; effective AoE is unbounded over time via luffy2 ramp. All offensive damage is Normal type (subject to DR/shields/barriers) but Bypassing Invulnerability. The invuln-conditional 10 DoT (luffy2) is the only sustained tick and only fires against invuln targets.

economy.color_dependency: Heavy mono-Red: luffy1 (R1), luffy2 (R1), luffy3 (R2) all demand Red; only luffy4 is 1 Random. Strong Red commitment, no off-color flexibility on offense.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very high tempo: luffy1 is 0-CD spammable, luffy2/luffy3 on 1-turn CD, only luffy4 (defensive) on 4-turn CD. Can act every turn on cheap Red.
economy.ramp_dependency: Mild positive ramp via luffy2's permanent +5/cast stack and luffy1's energy refund vs invuln; not required to function but rewards extended fights.

hard_cc: Full stun 1 turn (luffy3, only vs Invulnerable target)
invuln_or_counter: Self-invulnerability 1 turn (luffy4, 4-CD)

win_conditions: Out-tempo with cheap Red 0/1-CD attacks while passively stacking 15 shield/turn to outlast
Hard-counter invulnerability/dodge compositions: bypasses invuln entirely and punishes it with bonus damage, a full stun, refunds, and a DoT
Ramp luffy2 over a long match into an oppressive uncapped AoE
internal_synergies: Every offensive skill feeds Rubber Body (15 shield/turn), so aggression equals defense; he is self-sustaining without a healer
luffy1 energy refund vs invuln keeps his Red economy positive while spamming
luffy4 self-invuln buys a defensive turn while CDs reset; thematically ties into his anti-invuln identity though purely defensive
luffy3 stun vs invuln + luffy1/luffy3 spam can lock down a dodge-tank then delete it through the invuln
strengths: Premier anti-invulnerability / anti-dodge specialist — completely ignores and punishes a whole defensive mechanic
Excellent tempo and energy efficiency (0-CD spam, refunds, all cheap)
Free self-sustain via 15 shield/turn with no healer needed
Complete flexible kit: 40 single-target nuke, uncapped ramping AoE, conditional hard CC, and a self-invuln panic button
Self-invuln gives a defensive out on a reasonable 4-CD
weaknesses: All damage is Normal type — fully stopped by enemy shields/barriers and reduced by DR (no Piercing/True/Affliction to push through tanky comps)
Conditional riders (bonus damage, stun, DoT) are dead weight against enemies who never go Invulnerable — most of the roster
Heavy mono-Red dependency makes him vulnerable to Red energy denial/screw
No team utility: no heals, no team shields, no cleanse, no enemy energy denial — purely selfish
Self-shield is flat 15 (not damage-scaled), small against heavy hitters and out-traded by chip above 15
Base AoE is weak (10) and needs many turns of ramp to matter; no burst AoE

power_assessment.reasoning: A clean, efficient, self-sufficient bruiser with strong tempo (cheap, low-CD), solid single-target output (40), passive shielding, and a self-invuln out. But a large fraction of his kit's power budget is locked behind the enemy being Invulnerable — bonus damage, the full stun, and the DoT all only fire vs invuln targets, so against typical opponents he is a vanilla mono-Red beatstick: 25 spam / 40 nuke / weak 10 AoE that needs ramp. Normal damage type means shields and DR blunt him with no bypass. Solid floor, low ceiling outside his niche; swings to ~7+ specifically against invuln/dodge-heavy comps and dips toward ~4 into shield/DR walls.
outlier_flags: JSON metadata for luffy5 (Rubber Body) is STALE: claims shield 'equal to damage dealt'; live .gd grants a flat 15 shield. Rated on the .gd (flat 15).
luffy2 ramp buff has no stack cap (permanent +5/cast) — theoretically unbounded AoE in very long games, a potential balance edge case.
Damage 'class' tag is Physical but resolve_damage uses DamageType.Type.NORMAL on all hits.

role: Mark-stacking single-target controller/executioner with self-sustain and a death-save
signature_mechanic: Morphin Mark — a stackable, permanent, shared mark applied by every pendulum skill. Marks are the universal resource: at 3+ total marks Blind Pendulum (slot 2) transforms into Big Ben Wire Frame; marks scale Big Ben's delayed damage AND its execute threshold (+15 each); marks gate Blind Pendulum's stun, Halvaya's self-heal, and Mastema's mark-generation engine.

abilities.name: Homing Pendulum
abilities.target_type: SELF (random enemy first cast; SINGLE directed next turn)
abilities.conditional_scaling: none on damage; applies 1 Morphin Mark (the scaling resource for the rest of the kit)
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 20 Normal to a random enemy and applies 1 Morphin Mark. Installs a TARGET_CHANGE buff so next turn Lyserg picks the target. Installs/refreshes the Big Ben watcher that swaps slot 2 to Big Ben at 3+ total marks. Spammable (CD 0, 1 Green) so it is the core mark-stacking engine.

abilities.name: Blind Pendulum
abilities.target_type: ALL (only enemies with a Morphin Mark are affected)
abilities.conditional_scaling: scales with number of marked enemies (stuns each, one per marked enemy)
abilities.effects_summary: Stuns every enemy holding a Morphin Mark for 1 turn (stun dur 2) and strips 1 mark from each. No damage. At 3+ total active Morphin Marks this slot is swapped out for Big Ben Wire Frame (via lyserg1's watcher). Requires at least one marked enemy to be usable.

abilities.name: Mastema Dolkeen
abilities.conditional_scaling: mark-generation ramp: ~3 guaranteed marks over 3 turns + 1 mark per harmful skill aimed at Lyserg
abilities.effects_summary: For 3 turns (dur 6): auto-applies 1 Morphin Mark to a random enemy each turn, AND applies 1 Morphin Mark to any enemy that hits Lyserg with a Harmful skill (HARMFUL_RECEIVE_TRIGGER retaliation). Applies 1 mark immediately on cast. While active, Homing Pendulum (slot 1) is replaced by Halvaya (AoE self-heal) and Big Ben Wire Frame is locked out. The kit's ramp/sustain enabler.

abilities.name: Heavenly Intervention
abilities.conditional_scaling: none; one-time trigger (used flag, once per game)
abilities.effects_summary: Permanently shields one ally/self with a single fatal-damage save: lethal new damage is prevented, the target becomes Immortal until end of turn, and Lyserg deals 35 Normal to the enemy that was targeting them (counter). Once per game (used flag + per-team uniqueness check). Protective utility/anti-burst counter, not a recurring tool.

abilities.name: Big Ben Wire Frame
abilities.conditional_scaling: delayed damage = 15 + 15 per Morphin Mark on the target; execute threshold = HP below (15 + 15 per Morphin Mark) while active
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden alt that occupies slot 2 once 3+ total Morphin Marks exist. Marks the target; after 2 turns detonates for 15 +15/mark Normal damage (.gd value; JSON's 20/20 is stale). While the timer is active the target is instantly executed if HP drops below 15 +15/mark (a low-HP guillotine). Locked while Mastema Dolkeen is active. The kit's payoff/finisher.

abilities.name: Halvaya
abilities.conditional_scaling: self-heal scales with number of marked enemies hit (heal = post-mitigation damage dealt to each marked target)
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden alt that replaces Homing Pendulum (slot 1) while Mastema Dolkeen is active. Deals 15 Normal to all enemies; Lyserg heals for the damage dealt to every target carrying at least 1 Morphin Mark (up to 15 per marked enemy hit, less if mitigated). CD 0 — spammable AoE self-sustain during the Mastema window.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Big Ben Wire Frame is the ceiling: 15 + 15 per Morphin Mark on the target on detonation. With ~3-4 stacks that is 60-75 delayed Normal damage to one target; effectively unbounded as marks stack (CD0 Homing + Mastema auto-marks). The execute threshold scales identically (HP below 15+15/mark), so a heavily-marked target can be guillotined from fairly high HP. Direct on-cast damage stays modest (20 Homing, 35 Heavenly counter).
damage_profile.notes: Almost no instant burst; Lyserg is a delayed/attrition dealer. The 45 single-target figure is a realistic mid-game ~2-mark Big Ben detonation (15+15*2); higher with more marks. All damage is Normal (mitigable by DR/shields/barriers); no Affliction/Piercing/True. The 35 from Heavenly Intervention is a one-time conditional counter, not a planned nuke. Halvaya AoE is only 15 but self-heals per marked enemy hit.

economy.color_dependency: Light-moderate dual-color [Green, Red]. Visible bar wants Green:2 (Homing, Blind) + Red:1 (Mastema) + Random:2 (Heavenly) = 3 specific / 2 flex. Hidden alts add a Random pip each (Big Ben G+Rand, Halvaya R+Rand). Cheap per-skill (1-2 pips).
economy.cooldown_tempo: Engine skills are low/no cooldown: Homing CD0, Heavenly CD0, Halvaya CD0, Blind CD1. Setup/payoff are slow: Mastema CD4, Big Ben CD2 plus an inherent 2-turn fuse. Fast on mark-stacking/stun, slow on the actual kill.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Weak turn 1 (one mark, 20 damage); snowballs as Morphin Marks accumulate. Designed around reaching 3+ marks to unlock Big Ben and make detonation/execute lethal; Mastema accelerates ramp but costs a turn and locks Big Ben while running.

hard_cc: AoE 1-turn stun on all marked enemies (Blind Pendulum)
instant-kill execute below scaling HP threshold (Big Ben Wire Frame)
invuln_or_counter: Heavenly Intervention: one-time fatal-damage save granting Immortal-until-end-of-turn to self/ally + 35 Normal counter to the attacker

win_conditions: Stack Morphin Marks (CD0 Homing Pendulum + Mastema auto/retaliation marks) on a priority target, then detonate Big Ben Wire Frame for 15+15/mark delayed damage to burst or execute them.
Use the scaling execute threshold (HP below 15+15/mark while Big Ben is active) to guillotine a marked, softened target the team chips down.
Lock down the enemy team with repeated cheap AoE 1-turn stuns from Blind Pendulum on all marked enemies while marks ramp.
Outlast and grind with Halvaya self-sustain during Mastema windows while the mark engine and stuns wear the enemy down.
internal_synergies: Morphin Mark is the spine: Homing Pendulum and Mastema generate it; Blind Pendulum, Big Ben, and Halvaya all consume/scale off it.
Homing Pendulum's CD0 spam + Mastema's per-turn + retaliation marks rapidly hit the 3-mark threshold that swaps Blind Pendulum into Big Ben.
More marks simultaneously raise Big Ben's detonation damage AND its execute threshold, double-dipping the same resource.
Mastema Dolkeen reshapes the kit while active: swaps Homing->Halvaya (AoE self-sustain) and locks Big Ben, trading finisher access for ramp + survivability.
Blind Pendulum stun buys time for Big Ben's 2-turn fuse, but consumes a mark per enemy, creating tension with Big Ben's mark-scaling.
Heavenly Intervention's counter and Halvaya's sustain let Lyserg stall to reach his ramp payoff.
strengths: Strong repeatable AoE hard CC: cheap, low-cooldown 1-turn stun on every marked enemy.
Scaling single-target finisher with a built-in execute whose threshold grows with marks.
Reliable, redundant mark engine (spam, per-turn, retaliation) makes the snowball consistent.
Self-sustain (Halvaya) plus a one-time team death-save + 35 counter (Heavenly Intervention) for staying power.
Very cheap kit (5 pips visible, mostly 1-pip skills) with low cooldowns on engine pieces.
Retaliation marking punishes enemies for focusing Lyserg, turning aggression into more fuel.
weaknesses: Slow and ramp-dependent: minimal turn-1 impact (one mark, 20 damage).
All damage is Normal, fully mitigable by DR/shields/barriers; no Affliction/Piercing/True against tanky comps.
Payoff (Big Ben) is doubly gated: needs 3+ marks to appear AND has a 2-turn fuse + CD2, and is locked out while Mastema runs.
Mode conflict: Mastema (ramp/sustain) and Big Ben (kill) are mutually exclusive, forcing awkward sequencing.
Mark removal/cleanse hard-counters the whole kit; killing or cleansing marked targets resets the snowball.
No ally healing, no shields, no energy denial; Heavenly Intervention is single one-time use.
Blind's stun and Big Ben's damage both want marks, so spending marks on stuns weakens the detonation.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-designed ramp controller/executioner. Cheap repeatable AoE stun + a scaling execute + reliable multi-source mark generation + self-sustain is genuinely strong in a grind, and the scaling execute threshold can produce blowout kills. But he is back-loaded and conditional: low early impact, all-Normal damage that tanks/shields blunt, a finisher gated behind both a mark threshold and a 2-turn fuse, and a Mastema-vs-Big-Ben mode conflict that slows the close. Fast burst comps or cleanse/mark-removal can neutralize him before he ramps. Solidly above-average in the right matchup, mediocre into anti-snowball comps, so ~6.5.
outlier_flags: JSON-vs-.gd mismatch: Big Ben Wire Frame deals 15+15/mark and executes below 15+15/mark in the .gd (lyserg5), NOT the 20+20 the metadata JSON states; metadata is stale.
Dynamic slot contents: only lyserg1-4 are normally visible; Big Ben (5) appears in slot 2 at 3+ marks, Halvaya (6) replaces slot 1 during Mastema, so the action bar changes mid-game.
Scaling execute threshold (HP below 15+15/mark while Big Ben active) is a potential high-impact outlier; with many stacks it can instant-kill from surprisingly high HP.
Big Ben damage scales effectively unbounded with mark count via CD0 mark generation; practical ceiling depends on how fast marks stack on one target before detonation.

role: Taunt-locking control bruiser / draw-aggro disruptor with energy denial and a death-detonation finisher
signature_mechanic: Relentless taunt control: every harmful skill applies a Taunt, plus Infinite Hand sets a redirect field that taunts any enemy who attacks a non-Machinedramon ally, funneling the entire enemy team onto him. Backed by EMP Wave invuln and the Catastrophe Day passive that detonates for 25 to all on death.

abilities.name: Giga Cannon
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 35 Normal damage to one enemy; removes 1 random energy (energy denial); taunts target for 1 turn (dur 2).

abilities.name: Giga Destroyer
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 35 Affliction damage (bypasses barriers/shields/DR) to one enemy; taunts 1 turn (dur 2); stuns target's Physical skills for 2 turns (dur 4).

abilities.name: Infinite Hand
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Normal AoE damage to all enemies each turn for 3 turns (dur 5 ticking; ~45 total per enemy). Also places an allied trigger on each ally so any enemy that hits a non-Machinedramon ally with a harmful skill is taunted 1 turn (team-protect redirect). User carries a control_cancel to end the field early.

abilities.name: EMP Wave
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self invulnerability for 1 turn via default_defend. NOTE: JSON metadata claims it also grants +1 Blue energy, but the .gd only calls default_defend with NO energy gain — ground truth is invuln only.

abilities.name: Catastrophe Day
abilities.conditional_scaling: triggers when Machinedramon's HP is brought to 20 or below (first time only)
abilities.effects_summary: Passive death-detonation. The first time HP falls to <=20, at the end of his next turn he deals 25 Normal damage to ALL targetable characters (enemies AND allies, skipping invuln targets), then instant-kills himself. Effectively a guaranteed AoE on death.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No scaling. Hard caps: single-target ~70 in one turn (Giga Cannon 35 + Giga Destroyer 35, both 2-cost/CD2, the Affliction half bypassing shields/DR). AoE per turn ~40 if Catastrophe Day (25 to all) coincides with an Infinite Hand tick (15). Infinite Hand contributes a flat 45 per enemy spread over 3 turns. Catastrophe Day adds a one-time 25 AoE on death but also damages own allies.
damage_profile.notes: Damage is flat and modest; this is a control/disruption kit, not a damage carry. Giga Destroyer's Affliction typing is the only piercing damage and is the most reliable chunk.

economy.color_dependency: Very high. Uses ALL four colors across the visible kit (character_colors = [0,1,2,3] = Green/Blue/White/Red). Blue appears in 3 of 4 visible skills (skills 1,2,3), making Blue the backbone; Green, White, and Red each gate a specific skill. Only EMP Wave is flexible (1 Random). Rainbow energy demand is steep and a real consistency liability.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Twin nukes (Giga Cannon, Giga Destroyer) on CD 2 give steady every-other-turn taunt+disruption pressure; Infinite Hand and EMP Wave on CD 4 are cyclical cooldowns. No ramp.
economy.ramp_dependency: None — no stacks or build-up. Effectiveness is immediate but back-loaded only by the Catastrophe Day death trigger.

hard_cc: Taunt (Giga Cannon 1 turn)
Taunt (Giga Destroyer 1 turn)
Physical-skill stun 2 turns (Giga Destroyer)
Infinite Hand redirect-taunt 1 turn on offending enemies
soft_cc: Energy drain 1 (Giga Cannon)
invuln_or_counter: EMP Wave self-invulnerability 1 turn
Infinite Hand acts as a reactive counter-taunt that punishes enemies for not attacking him

power_assessment.reasoning: A strong, focused control/tank-disruptor. Every harmful action staples a Taunt, and Infinite Hand creates a team-wide redirect field that forces the enemy to either attack Machinedramon or eat a taunt — extremely oppressive to setup/burst comps and excellent ally protection. Giga Destroyer is a clean package: 35 Affliction (shield/DR-piercing) + 1-turn taunt + 2-turn Physical-class stun on a 2-cost/CD2, which is efficient and partially shuts down physical attackers. Giga Cannon adds energy denial. EMP Wave gives a panic invuln, and Catastrophe Day guarantees a 25 AoE detonation when he's killed, so even dying him is punished. Held back by: flat/modest damage with zero scaling (not a win-by-damage threat), a punishingly four-color rainbow cost that strains energy economy, no healing/shields/cleanse for true tankiness, and Catastrophe Day damaging his OWN allies. Taunt also relies on the enemy team being susceptible (multi-target). Solid niche pick around 6.5 in isolation.
outlier_flags: Uses all four energy colors in the visible kit — among the most color-greedy economies in the roster
EMP Wave: JSON description claims +1 Blue energy gain but the .gd (default_defend only) does NOT grant energy — metadata/.gd mismatch, ground truth is invuln-only
Catastrophe Day deals its 25 detonation to ALLIES as well as enemies (friendly fire on death)
Infinite Hand's allied redirect-trigger is a rare 'protect the team by taunting attackers' mechanic

strengths: Pervasive Taunt control: every harmful skill taunts, dictating enemy targeting
Infinite Hand team-protect field forces enemies onto him or eats a taunt — shuts down focus-fire and setup
Giga Destroyer pierces shields/DR (Affliction) AND stuns Physical skills 2 turns — efficient anti-physical package
Energy denial (Giga Cannon) plus on-demand 1-turn invuln (EMP Wave)
Catastrophe Day punishes killing him with a guaranteed 25 AoE detonation
Cheap, low cost-per-skill (1-2 pips) with frequent CD2 nukes
weaknesses: Flat, modest damage with no scaling — cannot carry a kill race
Four-color rainbow cost (Green/Blue/White/Red) is a severe energy-consistency strain
No healing, shields, barriers, or cleanse — fragile for a frontline taunter
Catastrophe Day damages his own allies and only fires once
Taunt value drops vs single-target or taunt-immune compositions
Infinite Hand is the only AoE and is low per-tick (15); reliant on the 3-turn field
win_conditions: Lock the enemy team with chained Taunts so they cannot execute their game plan, while allies kill freely
Use Infinite Hand to redirect all aggro onto himself and protect carries
Grind enemies down with Giga Destroyer's piercing Affliction + Physical stun while denying energy with Giga Cannon
Turn his own death into value via the Catastrophe Day detonation
internal_synergies: Taunt + EMP Wave invuln: taunt enemies onto him, then go invulnerable to waste their forced turns
Infinite Hand redirect field + single-target taunts blanket-lock the enemy's targeting
Giga Destroyer's Physical stun + taunt double-disables physical attackers
Catastrophe Day pairs with low HP — being focused down still yields a 25 AoE payoff
Giga Cannon energy drain compounds the tempo loss enemies suffer while taunted

role: Defensive support / shield-and-nullify engine with piercing AoE DoT and a one-shot self-sacrifice clutch (full heal + invuln, revive, or team silence)
signature_mechanic: Shield/Nullify economy tied to a self-destruct passive: Karmic Destiny and Rose Barrage continuously stack Shields on allies and Nullify (barrier) on enemies; Madoka1 scales off the total count of Shield/Barrier effects on her and the target; her passive (Soul Gem) ticks up each time one of her Shield/Nullify effects is fully absorbed and kills her at 15 stacks, while My Wish requires >=7 passive stacks and kills Madoka on use to deliver a massive clutch payoff.

abilities.name: Magical Arrow
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 per BARRIER and per SHIELD effect on Madoka, +5 per BARRIER and per SHIELD effect on the target. Counts effect instances, not magnitude (each stacking 5-Nullify barrier from Karmic Destiny adds +5). Self-feeding ramp off her own effect-spray.
abilities.effects_summary: Single-target nuke; base 15 Normal, scales with the number of Shield/Barrier effects on caster and target. No CC/utility. Spammable (cd 0).

abilities.name: Rose Barrage
abilities.conditional_scaling: Mode-switch, no scaling. Initial cast: 10 Piercing to whole enemy team + applies a 10-Piercing DoT (damage_effect dur 10 = ~5 turns) to each enemy. While the Rose Barrage self-mark is active, recast for FREE (cost->0) as SINGLE-target: 10 Piercing + 15 Barrier (Nullify) to one enemy until Rose Barrage ends.
abilities.effects_summary: AoE piercing DoT (bypasses barriers/shields/DR) ~5 turns; then a free repeatable single-target follow-up dealing 10 Piercing and stamping 15 Nullify on an enemy (feeds Magical Arrow scaling and Soul Gem passive). Damage is 10/tick, not the 5 the JSON claims.

abilities.name: Karmic Destiny
abilities.conditional_scaling: Ramp/snowball: for a 3-turn window (trigger dur 6), every new skill used by ANY character permanently adds 5 Shield (allies) or 5 Barrier/Nullify (enemies). Output scales with action count in the window and feeds Magical Arrow's per-effect damage.
abilities.effects_summary: Team-wide passive-grant for 3 turns: allies snowball permanent Shields, enemies snowball permanent Nullify. Pure defensive/economy engine, no damage.

abilities.name: My Wish
abilities.conditional_scaling: Gated: usable only if Soul Gem passive >= 7 stacks. Three target-based branches. Madoka ALWAYS dies on use.
abilities.effects_summary: Clutch wish. Dead ally -> revive at 50 HP. Living ally -> cleanse ALL enemy effects + heal 50 + invuln 1 turn (dur 2). Self -> permanently Silence (dur -1, survives death) every enemy. In all cases Madoka self-destructs. High-impact panic button.

abilities.name: Soul Gem: Madoka
abilities.conditional_scaling: Counter: +1 stack per fully-absorbed Shield/Nullify effect (gain_corruption). At 15 stacks Madoka instantly dies. Also the >=7 gate for My Wish.
abilities.effects_summary: Self-corruption clock. Drives the >=7 My Wish gate but is a liability: her own handed-out Shields/Nullify, when broken, push her toward 15-stack self-death. Display-magnitude mark on Madoka.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Magical Arrow is soft-unbounded: 15 base + 5 per Shield/Barrier instance on her and the target. With Karmic Destiny snowballing permanent 5-Nullify barriers onto enemies plus her own Shields, the effect count climbs mid-game (45 shown = ~6 combined effects, can exceed). AoE/DoT from Rose Barrage is fixed 10 Piercing per enemy per tick, no scaling. 30 AoE = initial 10 Piercing x3 enemies; 30 sustained = 10 Piercing/tick across 3 enemies for ~5 turns.
damage_profile.notes: Low-damage character. Offense is the cd-0 Magical Arrow (15 base Normal, ramps with effect count) plus Rose Barrage's 10/tick Piercing AoE DoT (bypasses shields/barriers/DR, ~5 turns). Sustained team-wide DoT ~30/turn across 3 enemies. Single-target peak grows over the match as her Nullify/Shield engine inflates the effect count, but baseline burst is weak; no execute, no true burst window beyond ramp.

economy.color_dependency: Light. Two White pips across the visible kit (Rose Barrage 1, Karmic Destiny 1); rest Random. Single-color (White) identity, cheap to splash. Rose Barrage goes free while its mark is active.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Two cd-0 spammable skills (Magical Arrow, Rose Barrage) give constant tempo; Karmic Destiny (cd 3) and My Wish (cd 4) are the longer utility/clutch buttons. Very low cost per turn, often 1-2 pips or free Rose Barrage recasts.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate-to-high. Magical Arrow's damage and My Wish's availability both depend on ramping (effect counts / Soul Gem stacks). Early she is a cheap chip/DoT + shield bot; she becomes more threatening and gains her clutch wish as Shields/Nullify accumulate.

hard_cc: Silence (permanent, team-wide, survives death) via My Wish self-target
invuln_or_counter: 1-turn invulnerability granted to a single ally via My Wish

win_conditions: Ramp the Shield/Nullify economy (Karmic Destiny + Rose Barrage) so Magical Arrow's per-effect scaling becomes a repeatable cd-0 nuke while allies are blanketed in permanent Shields.
Grind enemies with Rose Barrage's piercing AoE DoT (ignores barriers/shields/DR) over the long game while staying cheap and shielded.

Reach 7+ Soul Gem stacks and bank My Wish as a game-swinging clutch: full-heal+cleanse+invuln a carry, revive a dead ally, or hard-lock the enemy team with permanent team-wide Silence (at the cost of Madoka's life).
internal_synergies: Karmic Destiny -> Magical Arrow: each acting enemy gains a permanent 5-Nullify barrier, and every such barrier instance adds +5 to Magical Arrow, so the AoE shield-grant inflates her single-target nuke.
Allied Shields from Karmic Destiny also count for Magical Arrow's +5 and protect the team.
Rose Barrage free recast applies 15 Nullify to an enemy, fueling Magical Arrow scaling and (when absorbed) the Soul Gem passive toward the My Wish gate.
Soul Gem passive <-> My Wish: handing out Shields/Nullify drives passive stacks to the 7-stack gate, but the same mechanic risks the 15-stack self-kill.
Closed loop: spray Shields/Nullify -> Magical Arrow hits harder -> absorbed effects build Soul Gem stacks -> unlock My Wish payoff.
strengths: Extremely cheap and tempo-positive: two cd-0 skills, mostly Random pips, single White identity, Rose Barrage free while active.
Piercing AoE DoT (Rose Barrage) bypasses barriers/shields/DR — reliable team-wide chip that ignores defensive stacking.
Deep support package: permanent team Shields, full single-target cleanse + 50 heal + invuln, and ally revive — strong sustain and a hard save button.
Permanent team-wide Silence (My Wish self) is powerful hard-CC that persists through death (remove_on_death=false).
Self-feeding offense: her own effect-spam ramps Magical Arrow into an increasingly large repeatable nuke.
Excellent enabler in shield/effect-heavy comps.
weaknesses: Low raw burst early; offense is weak until the Shield/Nullify count ramps, and Rose Barrage's DoT is only 10/tick.
Self-destruct liabilities: the passive can KILL HER at 15 stacks as a side effect of her own kit, and My Wish always kills her on use — losing a body for value.
My Wish is gated (>=7 passive stacks) and one-shot; without ramp the clutch is unavailable.
Against effect-light enemies Magical Arrow stays near its weak 15 base — poor scaling vs targets with no Shield/Barrier.
No mobility, no stealth, no personal defense beyond shared shields; fragile if focused before ramp.
Her 'Nullify' is enemy-applied barrier, not pip removal — it doesn't disrupt enemy economy and can even absorb her own DoT/Arrow value if mis-sequenced.

power_assessment.reasoning: A versatile, very cheap support/control character with a clean closed-loop design: shield/Nullify economy + a scaling cd-0 nuke + piercing AoE DoT + a high-ceiling clutch button (revive / full save+invuln / permanent team silence). The breadth (heal, cleanse, shields, invuln, revive, hard CC, AoE DoT, scaling single-target) is well above average and the cost efficiency is excellent. Held back from top tier by genuinely weak early burst, dependence on ramp for both damage and the My Wish gate, and two built-in self-kill mechanics (15-stack passive death, mandatory death on My Wish) that cap her staying power. Strong in long games and shield-synergy comps, mediocre into fast aggression.
outlier_flags: Self-kill passive: Soul Gem can instantly kill Madoka at 15 stacks driven by her OWN Shield/Nullify spam — rare design where the core engine can suicide her; needs balance review.

My Wish always kills Madoka and delivers an outsized one-shot effect (full cleanse+heal+invuln, or revive, or PERMANENT team-wide silence that survives death) — swingy, possibly oppressive, especially the permanent silence lock.
Stale text vs .gd: Rose Barrage deals 10 Piercing per tick (not 5), DoT duration ~5 turns (dur 10) not 3-4, and My Wish JSON omits the always-die clause present in code.
Magical Arrow scaling counts effect INSTANCES (each 5-Nullify barrier = +5), so Karmic Destiny can inflate it faster than the description implies.

abilities.name: Reap
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Pure single-target poke: 25 piercing damage (skips flat+%DR). Cheap, near-spammable (1cd). Replaced by Figure-6 Hunter while Witch Hunter is active on an enemy.

abilities.name: Soul Resonance
abilities.cost_breakdown: Random:1 (free if Soul Evans on team)
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: For 3 turns (dur 6) Maka and one ally ignore harmful non-damage effects (CC/debuff immunity) and get -1 cooldown on all their skills (cooldown_mod -1, dur 5). With Soul on team it is free, unstunnable, and locks to Soul only (Partner passive). Strong tempo/anti-CC support buff.

abilities.name: Witch Hunter
abilities.conditional_scaling: per-turn DoT until cancelled; enables Figure-6 Hunter
abilities.effects_summary: Hits for 30 piercing up front, then permanent 15 piercing/turn DoT (dur -1, channeled, bypasses DR). Target's skills cost +1 random energy (soft energy denial). Swaps Maka's Reap into Figure-6 Hunter (35 true nuke). Channeled, breaks if target uses a NEW harmful skill — a quasi-disarm/lockdown that punishes the enemy for attacking. Mark-the-target win-condition engine.

abilities.name: Scythe Deflection
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: For 1 turn (dur 2) counters ALL Physical skills targeting Maka (invisible counter). Reflects/negates physical attackers. Cooldown drops to 2 turns while wielding Soul. Self-protect panic button vs physical-heavy comps.

abilities.name: Figure-6 Hunter
abilities.conditional_scaling: modifier_value=2: gains DOUBLE effect from allied damage-increase buffs
abilities.effects_summary: Replaces Reap only while Witch Hunter is active and can only target the Witch-Hunter'd enemy. 35 TRUE damage (skips all DR), 1cd so repeatable every turn. Takes double benefit from allied damage buffs, so it scales hard with support. The payoff/execute on the marked target.

abilities.name: Partner: Soul
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Passive: if Soul Evans is on the team, Soul Resonance becomes free, unstunnable, and can only target Soul. Synergy gate that makes the support buff frictionless with the intended partner.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Once Witch Hunter is up: 15 piercing/turn DoT + 35 true from Figure-6 Hunter = 50/turn effective (both bypass DR). Figure-6's modifier_value=2 means allied damage-increase buffs are doubled, so with team damage buffs the true-damage nuke climbs well past 35 each turn, repeatable at 1cd. No native self-scaling — ceiling is support-dependent.
damage_profile.notes: Pre-setup damage is low (one 25-piercing poke). Turn 1 of Witch Hunter spikes to 30+15=45 piercing. Steady-state single target is ~50/turn (15 DoT + 35 true), all DR-bypassing, which is high effective damage. No AoE whatsoever.

economy.color_dependency: Light Red dependency: only 2 of 5 visible pips are specific (Red on Reap and Witch Hunter); the rest are random. Figure-6 Hunter (hidden) adds a 3rd Red. Single-color (Red) identity, easy to fund.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Mixed: Reap (1cd) and Figure-6 Hunter (1cd) are near-spammable; Witch Hunter 4cd, Scythe Deflection 4cd (2cd with Soul), Soul Resonance 5cd. Soul Resonance's own -1 cooldown buff and the Partner synergy improve team tempo.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate. The kit is front-loaded with a setup turn: Witch Hunter must land to unlock the 35-true Figure-6 nuke and the DoT engine. Until then output is just a 25 poke. Once online it sustains without further ramp.

internal_synergies: Witch Hunter (maka3) is the kit's keystone: it applies the DoT, the +1 energy tax, AND swaps Reap into Figure-6 Hunter — so one cast turns a 25 poke into a 35 true-damage repeatable nuke locked onto the marked enemy.
Figure-6 Hunter can ONLY hit the Witch-Hunter'd target, so the two are hard-coupled; Figure-6's modifier_value=2 turns any allied damage buff into double value on the true nuke.
Witch Hunter's break-on-new-harmful-skill clause pressures the marked enemy into NOT attacking, while the +1 random cost tax further slows them — soft lockdown that protects Maka's channel.
Soul Resonance grants -1 cooldown to itself + an ally, shortening Maka's own 4-5cd utilities and accelerating a partner.

Partner: Soul passive makes Soul Resonance free + unstunnable when Soul Evans is fielded, removing all cost/CC friction from the support buff. Scythe Deflection also gains a shorter 2cd while wielding Soul — the kit is explicitly built around pairing with Soul.

power_assessment.reasoning: Solid, well-rounded single-target specialist with excellent EFFECTIVE damage because nearly all of it bypasses defenses: Reap (piercing), Witch Hunter DoT (piercing, permanent), and Figure-6 Hunter (35 true, 1cd, doubles allied buffs). Steady-state ~50 DR-ignoring damage/turn on one target is strong, and she layers real utility on top — energy taxation (+1 cost), a channel-protecting disarm-pressure clause, blanket anti-CC + cooldown reduction support (Soul Resonance), and a physical-counter panic button — all on a cheap mono-Red, mostly-random cost base. Held back from top tier by: zero AoE, a mandatory setup turn (low pre-Witch-Hunter output), reliance on the channel surviving (target using a new harmful skill cancels the whole engine), and the best parts of the buff/cooldown package being gated behind specifically running Soul Evans. Self-defense is narrow (physical-only counter). A strong supportive duelist, not a standalone carry.
outlier_flags: JSON metadata is STALE: Witch Hunter does 30 initial + 15/turn piercing (not 10/turn as the table states), and Reap's .gd has a base_damage=30 var but execute() actually deals 25.
Witch Hunter's DoT duration is -1 (permanent/channeled), not a fixed turn count — sustained until the channel breaks.
Figure-6 Hunter's modifier_value=2 is an unusual double-dip on allied damage buffs that can spike true damage well beyond the listed 35 in a buff-heavy comp.
Heavy intended dependency on a specific second character (Soul Evans) for the passive/cost discounts — combo-locked design.

role: Single-target DoT/execute duelist with energy-denial and anti-CC team support
signature_mechanic: Witch Hunter mark: a permanent piercing DoT + energy tax that swaps Reap into the Figure-6 Hunter 35-true-damage nuke, locking Maka onto one enemy while punishing them for attacking (channel breaks if they use a new harmful skill).
strengths: Very high EFFECTIVE damage — almost the entire kit bypasses defenses (Piercing on Reap + Witch Hunter DoT, True on Figure-6 Hunter), so shields/DR/barriers do little.
Repeatable true-damage execute: Figure-6 Hunter at 1cd for 35 true on the marked target, with double scaling off allied damage buffs.
Built-in soft lockdown: +1 random energy tax on the target plus a break-on-new-harmful-skill clause discourages the enemy from acting.
Cheap, low-color-dependency economy (mono-Red, mostly random pips; total visible kit only 5 pips).
Excellent team utility in Soul Resonance: 3-turn anti-CC immunity + -1 cooldown to herself and an ally.
Physical-counter panic button (Scythe Deflection) for self-protection vs melee comps.
Strong, frictionless synergy package when paired with Soul Evans (free unstunnable buff, shorter counter cooldown).
weaknesses: No AoE at all — purely single-target, weak into wide or swarm comps.
Requires a setup turn: before Witch Hunter lands, output is a single 25 poke.
The whole damage engine hinges on the channel surviving; if the marked enemy uses a new harmful skill the DoT, tax, and Figure-6 swap all end.
Self-defense is narrow — Scythe Deflection only counters Physical skills, no answer to Energy/Affliction/ranged threats.
Best buff/economy upside is gated behind specifically fielding Soul Evans (combo-locked).
No healing or shields for herself or the team; squishy if focused.
Channeled lockdown can be undone by the enemy choosing not to attack, creating a passive standoff that stalls her offense.

invuln_or_counter: Scythe Deflection: counters all Physical skills targeting Maka for 1 turn (invisible)
soft_cc: Witch Hunter: +1 random energy cost on target's skills (energy tax)
Witch Hunter: channel breaks if target uses a new harmful skill (pressures target into passivity / soft disarm)

win_conditions: Land Witch Hunter early, then sustain Figure-6 Hunter (35 true) + 15/turn piercing DoT to grind down a priority single target through any defenses.
Use the +1 energy tax and break-on-harmful clause to soft-lock a key enemy out of acting while you whittle them.
Pair with Soul Evans and/or allied damage buffers to make Soul Resonance free and double-dip Figure-6 Hunter's damage for an accelerated true-damage kill.
Provide anti-CC + cooldown support (Soul Resonance) to enable a faster ally carry while contributing DR-bypassing chip.

role: Mark/counter-punishing control-disruptor with a single-target burst finisher
signature_mechanic: Tiro Concert marks (permanent, stacking 5-dmg "punish on skill use" tags) feed into Tiro Finale, a Ribbon-Wrap-gated nuke that converts every accumulated Concert stack into +10 burst, all underpinned by a self-corruption Soul Gem clock that buffs her at 4 stacks but kills her at 8.

abilities.name: Tiro Concert
abilities.conditional_scaling: Punish damage = 5 x stacks (10 x stacks once Soul Gem >= 4); stacks accrue permanently and via Tiro Assault counters
abilities.effects_summary: Applies a permanent, stackable ACTION_USE_TRIGGER mark to ALL enemies (duration -1). Each time a marked enemy uses ANY skill, they take 5 Normal damage per stack (becomes 10/stack while Mami has 4+ Soul Gem stacks). 0 cooldown, so stacks can be piled on; foundation for Tiro Finale scaling.

abilities.name: Ribbon Wrap
abilities.conditional_scaling: When Soul Gem mag >= 2 (i.e. 3rd stack onward), self-applies an ability_swap turning this slot into Tiro Finale for 1 turn
abilities.effects_summary: Isolates target 1 turn (dur 2) and stuns their Harmful skills 1 turn (dur 2), plus a 'can be targeted by Tiro Finale' mark (dur 3). Soft-lock setup that also flags the Finale target. At 3+ Soul Gem, swaps the slot to Tiro Finale for one turn.

abilities.name: Tiro Assault
abilities.conditional_scaling: Counter engine snowballs Tiro Concert stacks (on enemy) and Soul Gem stacks (on Mami) each time it triggers; self-re-applies the counter every tick
abilities.effects_summary: Upfront 10 Normal damage. Applies a ticking DoT (dur 7 ~ 3-4 turns) dealing 5 Normal/turn, and grants Mami a counter vs the first Harmful skill each turn. On counter: the attacker gains a Tiro Concert stack and Mami gains a Soul Gem stack, then the counter is renewed each tick. Strong vs aggressive single targets; also a primary Soul Gem ramp source (accelerates the self-kill clock).

abilities.name: Ribbon Show
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Team-wide cleanse: removes ALL harmful (enemy-applied) effects from every ally via cleanse_all_enemy_effects. Strong anti-CC / anti-DoT support button on a 4-turn cooldown.

abilities.name: Tiro Finale
abilities.conditional_scaling: Damage = 40 + 10 per Tiro Concert stack on target, then all Tiro Concert stacks are consumed
abilities.effects_summary: Single-target nuke: 40 Normal + 10 per Tiro Concert stack on the target, then strips all Tiro Concert from them. Unlocked at Soul Gem 3+ and gated to the Ribbon-Wrapped target; the payoff for stacking Concert marks. Hidden alt that the Ribbon Wrap slot swaps into for 1 turn.

abilities.name: Soul Gem: Mami
abilities.conditional_scaling: Stacks ramp the kit: 3+ unlocks Tiro Finale; 4+ makes Tiro Concert deal 10/stack and gain +1 stack/turn (doubling the clock); 8 = instant death
abilities.effects_summary: Permanent passive: immune to stun, gains 1 Soul Gem stack/turn. 3+ stacks unlocks Tiro Finale; 4+ stacks doubles Tiro Concert punish damage (5->10/stack) and adds +1 stack/turn (now +2/turn); at 8 stacks Mami instantly dies. Self-imposed clock — note metadata JSON lists death at 6, but the .gd ground truth is 8.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Tiro Finale scales unbounded with Tiro Concert stacks: 40 + 10*stacks. With ~8 accumulated Concert stacks (very feasible via 0-CD Tiro Concert spam + Tiro Assault counters) a single Finale exceeds 120; theoretically only capped by how many stacks you pile before the 8-turn Soul Gem self-kill ends the game. Tiro Concert punish also passively does 5-10 per stack per enemy skill use across the whole enemy team.
damage_profile.notes: Direct on-cast damage is modest: Tiro Assault is 10 upfront + 5/turn DoT. The burst lives in Tiro Finale and in stacked Tiro Concert punish triggers (whole-team passive chip that grows). Peak single-target ~120 assumes a healthy Concert-stack pile (40 base + 80 from 8 stacks); higher with more stacks. No real AoE damage burst — Tiro Concert is AoE application but damage is reactive per-enemy, not a one-turn AoE hit.

economy.color_dependency: Light Green dependency: 2 of 4 visible skills (Tiro Concert, Tiro Assault) cost Green:1; Tiro Finale costs Green:2. Ribbon Wrap and Ribbon Show are flexible Random:1. Overall mono-Green leaning but cheap.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very cheap, fast tempo. Tiro Concert is 0-CD (spammable mark-stacker), Ribbon Wrap CD2, Tiro Assault CD3, Ribbon Show CD4, Tiro Finale CD2. Every visible skill costs only 1 pip, so she can act every turn while developing the board.
economy.ramp_dependency: High ramp dependency, but self-driving: Soul Gem auto-ramps +1/turn (then +2/turn at 4). Tiro Finale is locked until Soul Gem 3 (turn ~3). Finale damage and Concert punish both scale with stacks accrued over the game. The same clock kills her at 8, forcing a finite, accelerating game plan.

hard_cc: isolate (Ribbon Wrap, 1 turn)
soft_cc: Harmful-skill stun (Ribbon Wrap, 1 turn)
punish-on-cast discouragement (Tiro Concert)
invuln_or_counter: Tiro Assault: counters first Harmful skill on Mami each turn for ~3-4 turns (renewing)

win_conditions: Stack Tiro Concert (0-CD spam + Tiro Assault counters) and detonate a huge Tiro Finale on a Ribbon-Wrapped target before the Soul Gem clock runs out
Punish a skill-spam enemy comp: marked enemies bleed 5-10 per stack every time they act, while Mami counters and gains stacks
Lock down a key threat with Ribbon Wrap (isolate + Harmful-stun) while Ribbon Show keeps her team clean of CC/DoT, racing the opponent within her 8-turn life window
internal_synergies: Tiro Assault counters -> apply Tiro Concert stacks to enemy AND grant Soul Gem stacks to Mami: simultaneously fuels Finale damage and ramps the unlock/clock
Soul Gem 3+ -> unlocks Tiro Finale and lets Ribbon Wrap swap into it; Ribbon Wrap's Tiro-Finale mark + swap is the delivery system for the nuke
Soul Gem 4+ -> doubles Tiro Concert punish (5->10/stack) and doubles stack gain (+2/turn), sharply accelerating both Finale ceiling and the death clock
Tiro Concert (AoE mark) builds the stack pool that Ribbon Wrap+Tiro Finale convert into single-target burst
Stun immunity (Soul Gem) keeps her reliably casting Ribbon Wrap / Finale even under enemy CC
strengths: Extremely cheap kit (all visible skills 1 pip; total 4) with fast tempo and a 0-CD spammable mark
Self-driven ramp that auto-unlocks a scaling nuke without needing items/allies
Excellent vs skill-spam / multi-cast enemy comps (whole-team punish-on-cast that grows)
Personal stun immunity plus a renewing counter make her hard to lock down and punishing to attack
Team-wide full cleanse (Ribbon Show) is rare, high-value anti-CC/anti-DoT support
Unbounded single-target burst ceiling via Tiro Finale
Hard CC (isolate) + Harmful-stun lockdown bundled on a cheap CD2 skill
weaknesses: Self-kill clock: dies at 8 Soul Gem stacks (accelerating to +2/turn at 4), so she has a hard finite lifespan and must win fast — counters/Tiro Assault that ramp her also shorten her life
Low immediate/raw damage: outside Finale she only does 10 + 5/turn; Concert punish is reactive and depends on enemies casting
No self-healing, no shields, no innate sustain — pure tempo/burst with a built-in death timer
Tiro Finale is gated (needs Soul Gem 3+ AND a Ribbon-Wrapped target), so the payoff can be telegraphed/delayed and disrupted by killing/cleansing the wrap or denying tempo
Concert punish damage is passive and conditional on enemies using skills — a passive/turtling enemy starves her ramp value
Mono-Green leaning (Finale needs Green:2); color-screwed if Green is scarce
All Normal damage (no Affliction/Piercing/True), so barriers, shields, and DR blunt both Finale and punish damage

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, cheap control/punish/burst package with a genuinely scary scaling ceiling (Tiro Finale grows ~+10 per Concert stack, easily 120+ in a real game) plus rare utility in team-wide cleanse, isolate+stun lockdown, a renewing counter, and self stun-immunity. Tempo is excellent — every visible button is 1 pip and Tiro Concert is 0-CD. The main thing keeping her off the top tier is the built-in 8-stack self-kill clock that hard-caps her game and pressures her to commit, plus all-Normal damage that DR/shields blunt and a burst payoff that is gated and telegraphed. Strong but self-limiting; rates a high-mid 7 in isolation.
outlier_flags: Soul Gem self-kill threshold mismatch: metadata JSON says 6 stacks = death, but mami6.gd and mami.gd ground truth = 8 stacks (and 4+ doubles stack gain to +2/turn). Profiled per the .gd.
Tiro Concert 4+ punish: JSON/describe says '+5 more damage'; code doubles base 5->10 per stack (i.e. 2x, not +5 flat per hit) — uses base=10 multiplied by stacks.
Tiro Assault describe()/split_desc disagree on numbers (10 vs 5 DoT, 3 vs 4 turns); code = 10 upfront + 5/turn DoT for dur 7 (~3-4 turns).
Tiro Finale damage scales unbounded with stacks — a balance outlier if Concert stacks can be piled high before the death clock fires.

abilities.name: Blue Flames of Resurrection
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Heals target ally 25 HP instantly. No cooldown, spammable single-target heal.

abilities.name: Hoo-In
abilities.conditional_scaling: Buffed by marco6 passive: +5 dmg per passive activation stack the following turn
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 20 Normal damage that bypasses defensive mitigation. No cooldown, repeatable poke. AI custom_behavior models it at 25 with bypass.

abilities.name: Immortal Thistle
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: For 1 turn (dur 2), target ally reflects the FIRST harmful skill used on them back to its user (invisible counter, Harmful class only). While on cooldown, slot 4 swaps to Pineapple Stone (marco5).

abilities.name: Phoenix Wing Block
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Grants Marco or target ally Invulnerability for 1 turn (dur 2). Premier protect tool, long 4-turn cooldown.

abilities.name: Pineapple Stone
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: AoE team heal: heals all allies 15 HP instantly PLUS a 15 HP/turn regen effect for 2 turns (dur 3). Total up to 45 HP per ally over the window. Accessed via the marco3 swap (slot 4 alt while Immortal Thistle is on cooldown).

abilities.name: Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Phoenix
abilities.conditional_scaling: Scales with incoming damage: per 15 damage received Marco self-heals 5 HP and gains a stacking +5 damage mod for next turn
abilities.effects_summary: Passive self-sustain: whenever Marco takes damage, for each full 15 damage he heals 5 HP and gains a stackable/display +5 damage buff applied next turn (mods his Hoo-In). Rewards tanking; advances mission 8.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hoo-In 20 base can grow via marco6 passive: each 15 damage Marco absorbs adds +5 to next turn's damage. A few stacks pushes Hoo-In into the 30-40 range, but damage is a strictly secondary, low ceiling.
damage_profile.notes: Marco is not a damage dealer. Only marco2 (Hoo-In, 20 Normal/Bypassing) deals damage; everything else heals/protects. No AoE damage at all. Passive can incrementally raise Hoo-In but realistically caps around 30-40 in a turn after heavy tanking.

economy.color_dependency: Moderate: 1 Blue + 2 White across visible slots (Pineapple Stone swap adds Blue:1+Random:1). Built on Blue/White identity per character_colors [1,2]. Two White pips make White the limiting color; Blue needed for healing.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast on offense/single heal (marco1 and marco2 are cd0, spammable). Protective tools gated: Immortal Thistle cd2, Phoenix Wing Block cd4, Pineapple Stone cd2. Whole kit can be cycled while always having a free heal or poke.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low. Passive marco6 provides mild damage ramp the more Marco is hit, but support/heal output is fully online from turn 1 with no setup.

invuln_or_counter: marco4 Phoenix Wing Block: 1-turn Invulnerability (self or ally), cd4
marco3 Immortal Thistle: 1-turn invisible reflect of first harmful skill back to caster, cd2

signature_mechanic: Phoenix self-sustain + ally protection: a no-cooldown single-target heal and bypass-poke, backed by an invuln, a damage-reflect counter, an AoE regen (via swap), and a passive that converts incoming damage into self-healing and a growing damage buff.
internal_synergies: marco6 passive turns tanking damage into both self-healing AND a stacking +5 damage buff that amplifies marco2 Hoo-In the following turn — front-lining Marco feeds his offense
marco3 Immortal Thistle's cooldown unlocks marco5 Pineapple Stone (AoE regen) in slot 4, so casting the reflect rotates the kit into team-wide healing
marco4 Invuln + marco3 reflect let Marco protect a key ally while marco1/marco5 top the team's HP, making him a layered defensive anchor
marco1 (cd0 25 HP heal) plus marco5 regen plus marco6 self-heal stack into strong total HP throughput across a team
win_conditions: Outlast the enemy via superior healing/protection economy — keep the team topped while allies provide kill pressure
Use Invulnerability and reflect at key moments to neutralize enemy burst turns and trade favorably
Sit Marco in the front, soak damage to fuel passive self-heal, and chip with bypass Hoo-In while sustaining
strengths: Free, no-cooldown single-target heal (25 HP) gives relentless sustain with zero tempo cost
Phoenix Wing Block grants full 1-turn Invulnerability to self or ally — top-tier hard protect
Immortal Thistle reflects an enemy's first harmful skill, punishing single-target burst/assassins
Pineapple Stone (swap) is an efficient AoE team heal: 15 instant + 15/turn x2 (up to 45 per ally)
marco6 passive makes Marco extremely durable as a damage sink and quietly ramps his own damage
Cheap kit (4 pips visible) with a no-cost bypass poke that ignores DR/shields
weaknesses: Almost no damage — only one 20-dmg skill; cannot threaten kills or close games on his own
No hard CC, no stun/lock, no energy denial — purely reactive/supportive
No shields/barriers or cleanse despite being a defensive character; relies on raw heals and invuln
Reflect is single-skill, single-target, and only catches Harmful class — easily played around by AoE or waiting it out
Protect tools have real cooldowns (invuln cd4), so burst can be timed for the windows they're down
Healing can be neutralized by anti-heal/Affliction/execute mechanics in the roster
Double-White color requirement plus Blue can strain energy if the team shares those colors

power_assessment.reasoning: A clean, well-rounded dedicated support/healer-tank. The combination of a free spammable 25 HP heal, a strong AoE regen, a 1-turn ally Invulnerability, and a burst-punishing reflect makes Marco a very sticky defensive anchor, and his passive lets him eat damage almost for free while slowly ramping offense. He is genuinely hard to kill and keeps a team alive across long fights. He is held back from a higher rating by near-zero kill pressure (single 20-dmg skill), no CC, and no cleanse/shields — he enables wins rather than securing them, and his value is heavily team-dependent. Strong in a sustain composition, mediocre on a team that needs a proactive playmaker.
outlier_flags: No-cooldown 25 HP single-target heal is unusually free for its value — potential efficiency outlier
Full 1-turn Invulnerability on a 4cd is a high-impact protect that can swing burst turns
marco6 passive self-heal-on-damage plus damage ramp makes him very low-investment durable
Damage output is an extreme low outlier for the roster (effectively a non-combatant offensively)

role: Team support / healer-tank (sustain anchor with protect tools, minimal offense)

abilities.name: Blazing Mandala
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 per living character marked by Ofuda (base 10). At 2 marks=20, at 6 marks (full 3v3 board)=40. Same scaling applies to the heal mode.
abilities.effects_summary: Flexible single-target: deals scaling Normal damage to a marked enemy, OR heals a marked ally for the same scaling amount (10 + 5/mark). No cooldown, so spammable every turn.

abilities.name: Akuryo Taisen
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (fixed 20 dmg / 25 heal)
abilities.effects_summary: Flexible single-target burst+control: deals 20 Normal damage AND stuns a marked enemy for 1 turn (stun_effect(2)), OR heals a marked ally for 25 HP. Hard CC on demand against any marked enemy.

abilities.name: Snake Fire
abilities.conditional_scaling: none on the damage; the heal-trigger value (15 HP per allied harmful hit on the target) can repeat each time a marked ally hits the cursed enemy.
abilities.effects_summary: Applies 15 Affliction immediately plus a multi-turn 15-Affliction DoT (damage_effect dur 5 ~= 2-3 ticks; ~45 total affliction, bypasses shields/barriers). Also plants a HARMFUL_RECEIVE trigger: while active, any Ofuda-marked ally that lands a new Harmful skill on the cursed enemy heals 15 HP. Team-wide sustain engine.

abilities.name: Ofuda
abilities.conditional_scaling: Each cast adds the chosen target + 1 random unmarked character to the Ofuda pool; ramps mars1's scaling and expands valid targets for the whole kit.
abilities.effects_summary: Free, permanent (dur -1) MARK enabler. Marks the chosen target plus one random unmarked character (enemy or ally) for the rest of the game. Required setup: nearly the entire kit can only target Ofuda-marked characters, and mars1's damage/heal scales with total marks. 1-turn cooldown.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: mars1 caps at 10 + 5x6 = 40 once all 6 characters on a 3v3 board are Ofuda-marked; full one-turn single-target ceiling ~= mars1 (40) + mars2 (20) + mars3 initial (15) = 75, mostly Normal with 15 Affliction. Requires several turns of mars4 ramp to reach.
damage_profile.notes: No AoE in the entire kit (all abilities are SINGLE-target). Early game peak is low: at 2 marks, mars1=20 + mars2=20 = ~40 one-turn single-target. Snake Fire DoT contributes ~15/turn affliction (bypasses shields) over 2-3 turns. Damage is gated entirely behind Ofuda marks - cannot touch unmarked enemies at all.

economy.color_dependency: Moderate Red dependency: mars2 and mars3 each require 1 Red pip; mars1 is 1 Random, mars4 is free. Mono-Red (character_colors=[3]) identity, but only 2 Red pips needed across the visible kit.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast/spammable: mars1 has 0 cooldown (every turn), mars4 and mars2 are 1-turn cooldown, mars3 is 2-turn. Can fire all 4 abilities in a single turn for only 4 pips when set up.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. The whole kit is dead without Ofuda marks - mars4 (free) must be used first to enable every other ability, and mars1's output scales linearly with cumulative mark count, so power grows over several turns of marking.

hard_cc: mars2: Stun for 1 turn (marked enemy)

role: Mark-based hybrid striker/support: scaling single-target damage + on-demand stun + team-wide DoT/heal engine, gated behind Ofuda marks
signature_mechanic: Ofuda marks (mars4): a free, permanent enabler that tags target + 1 random character. Every other ability can ONLY target marked characters, and mars1 scales +5 damage/heal per total living mark - making the entire kit a ramp around accumulating marks on both teams.
internal_synergies: mars4 -> everything: marks are a hard prerequisite for mars1/mars2/mars3 to have any target; each cast also ramps mars1's scaling.
mars1 dual-mode: marking allies (mars4 hits random allies too) turns mars1/mars2 into scaling heals, so accumulated marks buff both damage and healing simultaneously.

mars3 + team harmful: the Snake Fire trigger heals any Ofuda-marked ally 15 HP whenever they land a Harmful skill on the cursed enemy - turns marked teammates into self-sustaining attackers and rewards focus-firing the marked target.
mars1 0-cooldown spam: with marks accumulated, mars1 provides reliable per-turn scaling damage or heal every single turn at 1 random pip.
win_conditions: Ramp marks across the board over the first few turns, then convert mars1 into 30-40 free scaling damage/heal every turn at 1 pip.
Lock down a key enemy with mars2's repeatable on-cooldown stun while afflicting them with Snake Fire DoT that bypasses shields.
Out-sustain the opponent: Snake Fire's heal-on-harmful trigger + dual-mode mars1/mars2 heals keep marked allies topped off while the team focus-fires the cursed enemy.
strengths: Extremely energy-efficient: full 4-ability kit costs only 4 pips with mars4 free and mars1 castable every turn for 1 random pip.
Flexible hybrid - mars1 and mars2 each pivot between damage and healing depending on whether the marked target is an enemy or ally.
On-demand hard CC: mars2 stun on a 1-turn cooldown against any marked enemy.
Affliction DoT (Snake Fire) bypasses barriers/shields/DR for guaranteed chip on a tanky meta.
Strong team-support layer: Snake Fire's trigger plus scaling heals make her a force multiplier, not just a solo carry.
Scaling damage that grows for free as marks accumulate, with no energy cost increase.
weaknesses: Hard ramp dependency - turn 1 she must spend an action on mars4 (free but tempo-costing) and her damage/heal start low (10/+5).
No AoE whatsoever; every ability is single-target, so she struggles to swing multi-target fights or clear waves.
Entirely gated behind Ofuda marks - if marks are removed/cleansed or targets die, large parts of the kit go offline.
mars4's second mark is RANDOM, so she can't precisely choose who gets marked, sometimes wasting marks on irrelevant allies/enemies.
Low burst ceiling early; peak single-target relies on full board-marking which takes several turns to set up.
No defensive tools for herself (no shields, no self-cleanse, no invuln) - fragile if focused.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, energy-efficient mark-ramp hybrid with genuine flexibility (damage OR heal on two abilities), repeatable hard CC, shield-bypassing DoT, and a team-wide sustain trigger. The 4-pip total cost with a free enabler and a 0-cooldown scaling spell is very economical, and the dual-mode damage/heal gives her relevance in almost any matchup. However she is held back by a real ramp tax (turn-1 mars4, low early numbers), zero AoE, total dependence on marks (vulnerable to cleanse/kills and the random second mark), and no self-defense. Her ceiling (~40 from mars1 + 20 stun-burst + affliction) is solid but not explosive, and arriving there takes setup. Squarely mid-tier: reliable, supportive, and efficient, but neither a burst threat nor a fight-swinging AoE force.
outlier_flags: mars1 JSON metadata understates the ability: JSON says 5/character base, but ground-truth .gd is base 10 + 5 per mark (so 20 at 2 marks, not 10).
Snake Fire DoT duration arg is 5 (damage_effect dur 5), giving ~2-3 affliction ticks rather than a clean '3 turns' - effective total ~45 affliction including the immediate hit.
mars4's second mark is random and can land on allies, which is unusual - it doubles as a way to set up dual-mode heals on teammates, not just enemy marks.
Zero AoE in the entire kit is notable for a 'magical girl' damage dealer.

role: Defensive support / tank-protector who shields and makes allies invulnerable while body-blocking reflected damage
signature_mechanic: "A Knight That Protects" vow: makes a chosen ally permanently invulnerable to non-Strategic skills and reflects all Harmful skills cast on them back onto Mash, who gains 30 Shield to absorb it. Her shield value both fuels Flying Galahad's bonus damage and gates the vow's lifetime; if an enemy breaks the shield the vow ends, that enemy is marked, and Flying Galahad transforms into the stunning Around Round Axe for 1 turn.

abilities.name: Flying Galahad
abilities.conditional_scaling: +10 damage per 20 Shield currently on Mash (integer division total_shield/20). 30 Shield = +10 (25 total); 40 Shield = +20 (35 total). Bonus = 0 if Mash's shield is broken/ignored.
abilities.effects_summary: Spammable single-target Physical nuke (no cooldown). Damage scales with Mash's own Shield. Transforms into Around Round Axe (mash5) for 1 turn after the vow ends.

abilities.name: Around Round Crash
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat). JSON metadata stale: .gd deals 25, not 15. Metadata note about costing 1 less Random after the vow ends is NOT implemented in this .gd.
abilities.effects_summary: 25 Physical AoE to all enemies + taunts the primary target for 1 turn (taunt dur 2). Provides aggro control alongside damage.

abilities.name: Lord Camelot
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Team-wide invulnerability for 2 turns (invuln dur 4 = 2 enemy-facing turns) for all of Mash's teammates. Strategic class. Massive defensive ultimate (CD 8). Also advances a mission objective on low-HP allies.

abilities.name: A Knight That Protects
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (vow lifetime gated by Mash's 30 Shield, extendable to 40 via mash6)
abilities.effects_summary: Targets one ally: permanent invulnerability to non-Strategic skills (invuln dur -1) AND reflects all Harmful skills cast on them back to Mash. Mash gains 30 Shield (dur -1) and swaps mash4 -> Shield of White Walls. Ends when the Shield is destroyed; on break the breaking enemy is marked and Flying Galahad becomes Around Round Axe for 1 turn.

abilities.name: Around Round Axe
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage (30 total) and applies a 1-turn stun if the target is marked by 'A Knight That Protects' (i.e. it broke Mash's vow shield last turn).
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden alt of Flying Galahad available for 1 turn after the vow shield is broken. 25 Physical, or 30 + 1-turn stun (stun dur 2) vs the shield-breaker. Punish/retaliation tool.

abilities.name: Shield of White Walls
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Adds 25 to the remaining Shield on A Knight That Protects, capped at 40 total. Sustains the vow shield (prolonging the protect+reflect lock) and pushes Flying Galahad's bonus from +10 to +20. Replaces mash4 while the vow is active.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Single-target caps at 35 (Flying Galahad with 40 Shield = 15 + 20). Around Round Axe peaks at 30 + stun vs the shield-breaker. No DoT. Mash is not a damage character; her single-target ceiling is shield-gated and modest, AoE is a flat 25.
damage_profile.notes: Damage is secondary. Flying Galahad needs ~40 Shield (vow + Shield of White Walls) to hit 35. Around Round Axe is a conditional 1-turn punish window. No multi-hit or stacking damage scaling.

economy.color_dependency: Blue-locked. 4 of 7 visible pips are Blue (mash1 Blue:1, mash2 Blue:1, mash3 Blue:2). Strong single-color (Blue) dependency; needs steady Blue energy to function.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Two near-free spammable tools (Flying Galahad CD0, Around Round Crash CD1). A Knight That Protects on CD3 with Shield of White Walls (CD2) to sustain it. Lord Camelot is a long-CD8 emergency ultimate. Good turn-to-turn tempo on cheap actions; the big protect tools are gated.
economy.ramp_dependency: Light ramp. Flying Galahad wants Mash to build/maintain Shield (vow + Shield of White Walls) to reach max damage, but her protective value is online from turn one via the vow and Lord Camelot.

hard_cc: 1-turn stun (Around Round Axe, conditional on marked shield-breaker)
soft_cc: 1-turn taunt on primary target (Around Round Crash)
invuln_or_counter: Team-wide invulnerability 2 turns (Lord Camelot)
Permanent invulnerability to non-Strategic skills on one ally (A Knight That Protects)
Reflect: all Harmful skills cast on the protected ally bounce to Mash (A Knight That Protects)

win_conditions: Keep a key carry alive indefinitely via A Knight That Protects (permanent invuln to non-Strategic skills) while Mash soaks the reflected damage on her 30-40 Shield.
Use Lord Camelot's 2-turn team invulnerability to neutralize an enemy burst/ultimate window and win the resulting tempo swing.
Outlast the opponent: stack Shield via Shield of White Walls, body-block with the vow, and chip with Flying Galahad / AoE Around Round Crash while the protected ally carries the kill.
internal_synergies: A Knight That Protects -> Shield of White Walls: the vow grants 30 Shield and swaps in Shield of White Walls, which tops it to 40 to extend vow lifetime AND maxes Flying Galahad's bonus (+20).
Shield value -> Flying Galahad: more Shield on Mash = more damage (15 -> 25 at 30, -> 35 at 40).

Vow break -> Around Round Axe + mark: when an enemy breaks the shield, break_vow marks that enemy and swaps Flying Galahad to Around Round Axe for 1 turn, letting Mash retaliate for 30 + a 1-turn stun on the breaker.
Around Round Crash taunt + vow/reflect: taunt pulls aggro onto Mash; combined with reflect she can redirect and punish enemy single-target attackers.
Lord Camelot + A Knight That Protects: layered defense - permanent single-ally invuln for the carry plus an on-demand 2-turn full-team invuln panic button.
strengths: Elite ally protection: permanent invulnerability (to non-Strategic skills) on one ally plus a 2-turn full-team invulnerability ultimate.
Damage redirection/reflect turns enemy single-target attackers against themselves while Mash tanks it on Shield.
Very cheap, spammable offense (Flying Galahad CD0, Around Round Crash CD1) keeps her contributing even while playing defense.
Built-in retaliation: marks and stuns the enemy that breaks her vow.
Aggro control (taunt) plus self-shielding makes her a sticky, hard-to-ignore frontline.
Strategic-class defensive skills bypass many enemy counters.
weaknesses: No healing and no cleanse - purely mitigation/prevention; once shields and invuln windows lapse she has no way to recover team HP or remove debuffs.
The vow funnels damage onto Mash; concentrated burst or Affliction/Bleed/Piercing/True damage that bypasses Shield can collapse her quickly and end the vow.
Invulnerability is non-Strategic-only - Strategic-class harmful skills still hit the protected ally, and reflect only covers Harmful skills.
Heavy Blue color dependency (4 Blue pips); Blue starvation cripples both her offense and Lord Camelot.
Low, shield-gated personal damage (35 single-target ceiling, 25 AoE); she cannot close games on her own and depends on a carry.
Lord Camelot's CD8 means the team-invuln panic button is available only sparingly.
Stun/punish from Around Round Axe is conditional on her vow being broken and lasts only a 1-turn window.

power_assessment.reasoning: Mash is a specialist defensive support whose value is entirely in keeping allies alive: permanent single-ally invulnerability with damage reflection, a 2-turn team-wide invulnerability ultimate, self-shielding, taunt, and a conditional stun. In a protect-the-carry composition she is very strong and frustrating to break through, and her offense is cheap enough that she is never a dead turn. She is held back from a higher rating by zero healing/cleanse, a modest shield-gated damage ceiling, heavy Blue dependency, and the fragility of routing all reflected/redirected damage onto her own HP+Shield against burst or barrier-bypassing damage. Rated as a high-floor, ceiling-limited enabler rather than a standalone powerhouse.
outlier_flags: JSON metadata for Around Round Crash (mash2) lists 15 damage but the .gd deals 25 - stale description, profiled from .gd ground truth.
Metadata note about Around Round Crash costing 1 less Random after the vow ends is NOT implemented in mash2.gd execute (no cost-reduction code present).

A Knight That Protects grants PERMANENT (dur -1) invulnerability and reflect with only a CD3 / 1-Random cost - very cheap for an indefinite invuln lock, gated only by Mash's 30-40 Shield being broken.
Lord Camelot grants full-team 2-turn invulnerability for 3 pips on CD8 - a swingy team-save button.
Permanent-invuln + reflect routing all damage to one character is a potential balance outlier dependent on how shield-bypass damage interacts with it.

abilities.name: Fairy Law
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat); skips enemies that are Invulnerable, skips allies that are Isolated
abilities.effects_summary: 3-turn channel (ticking trigger), resolves end of 3rd turn: all non-invuln enemies take 35 Normal dmg + 1-turn stun (AoE hard CC); all non-isolated allies heal 25 HP. Channel cancels if Mavis is stunned.

abilities.name: Bestow
abilities.conditional_scaling: indirect: grants ally access to Fairy Glitter (40 True dmg, CD1) for 2 turns
abilities.effects_summary: Replaces a chosen ally's first skill with Fairy Glitter (40 True damage, CD 1, cost White+Random) for 2 turns. Pure enabler/empowerment; the ally becomes a True-damage nuke.

abilities.name: Fairy Sphere
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Team-wide defensive cooldown: whole team ignores ALL damage for 1 turn, ignores Harmful non-damage effects for 2 turns, and gains 25 Shield for 3 turns. Massive single-turn team invuln panic button.

abilities.name: Fairy Heart
abilities.conditional_scaling: energy ramp: +1 Random energy per turn for 3 turns
abilities.effects_summary: Self goes Invulnerable for 3 turns but cannot act; gains +1 Random energy each turn (3 energy banked). Self-isolation/ramp + invuln panic button. Requires a targetable living ally. While active, exempt from Fairy Star Strategy targeting.

abilities.name: Fairy Star Strategy
abilities.conditional_scaling: ramps per Mavis stack: 1=10 shield, 2=20 heal, 3=permanent +10 non-Affliction dmg to that ally, 4+=that ally's skills are free next turn
abilities.effects_summary: Passive engine: each turn marks a random living ally (invisible). If that ally uses a new skill while marked, Mavis gains 1 permanent stack and the ally gets an escalating reward keyed to Mavis's total stacks (shield -> heal -> permanent damage buff -> free skills). Snowballs team value over time.

abilities.name: Fairy Glitter
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden skill only granted to an ally via Bestow. Deals 40 True damage (skips DR) to a target enemy, CD 1. Mavis cannot use it herself; it lives on the bestowed ally for 2 turns.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Mavis has no scaling personal damage. Her offense is fixed: 35 Normal AoE (Fairy Law, every 4 turns, delayed 3 turns) and 40 True damage granted to an ally via Bestow (40 dmg/turn for 2 turns on CD1). Indirect ceiling comes from Fairy Star Strategy stack 3 (+10 permanent non-Affliction damage per stack-3 proc, repeatable across allies) and stack 4+ free-cost turns enabling extra ally attacks. True ceiling is team-multiplicative, not Mavis-personal.
damage_profile.notes: Fairy Law's 35 damage is delayed by 3 full turns and skips invulnerable enemies, so effective burst is low and telegraphed. The only reliable damage Mavis enables is the 40 True nuke handed to an ally. No DoT in kit.

economy.color_dependency: Heavy White dependency: all four visible skills are White-based (1+1, 1, 2, 1 = 5 White pips + 1 Random across the visible bar). Mono-White identity, no off-color flexibility. Fairy Heart self-generates Random energy to refund the kit.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Slow/defensive tempo. Fairy Law CD4 (plus 3-turn channel), Fairy Sphere CD7, Fairy Heart CD5, Bestow CD3. Only the bestowed Fairy Glitter (CD1) provides fast recurring action. Mavis herself is low-frequency, setup-oriented.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate-to-high. Fairy Star Strategy must accumulate stacks over many turns to reach the strong tiers (3 = permanent damage, 4+ = free skills). Fairy Heart banks energy but costs Mavis 3 turns of action. Value compounds the longer the game runs.

hard_cc: 1-turn AoE stun on all non-invuln enemies (Fairy Law, delayed 3 turns)
invuln_or_counter: Fairy Sphere: team ignores ALL damage for 1 turn (team-wide invuln) + ignore Harmful non-damage effects 2 turns + 25 team shield 3 turns
Fairy Heart: self Invulnerable for 3 turns (cannot act)

internal_synergies: Bestow + Fairy Star Strategy: handing an ally Fairy Glitter (CD1) gives them a cheap repeatable 'new skill' to fire each turn, reliably triggering the Fairy Star mark and feeding Mavis's stack engine while dealing 40 True damage.
Fairy Heart (energy ramp) + Bestow/Fairy Sphere (White-hungry kit): the banked Random energy helps pay for the expensive White skills, but Mavis is locked out while banking, so it's a tempo trade.
Fairy Star Strategy stack 4+ (free skills) + any high-cost ally: removing ally costs for a turn enables burst turns the team could not otherwise afford.
Fairy Sphere (team ignore-damage 1 turn) + Fairy Law channel: Sphere can protect the team while Fairy Law's 3-turn channel resolves, and protects Mavis so the channel isn't cancelled by a stun.
Fairy Heart invuln + 'cannot act' lockout cleanly disables her own Fairy Star Strategy self-targeting (she is exempted while sealed), avoiding wasted marks.
role: team support / protector enabler — AoE control + shields/heals, ally empowerment, and a scaling team buff engine
signature_mechanic: Fairy Star Strategy: each turn a random ally is invisibly marked; when that ally acts, Mavis gains a permanent stack and the ally receives an escalating reward (10 shield -> 20 heal -> permanent +10 non-Affliction damage -> free skills next turn). A whole-team snowball engine driven by Mavis enabling her allies to act, amplified by Bestow handing out a cheap CD1 Fairy Glitter to keep the marks triggering.
strengths: Excellent team protection: Fairy Sphere is a near-Aegis (team ignores ALL damage 1 turn + ignore harmful non-damage 2 turns + 25 team shield 3 turns) on CD7, plus self-invuln on Fairy Heart.
Strong delayed AoE control: Fairy Law hits every non-invuln enemy for 35 + 1-turn stun, a full-team lockout.
Compounding team value: Fairy Star Strategy permanently buffs ally damage (stack 3) and grants free-skill turns (stack 4+), getting stronger the longer she survives.
Bestow grants an ally 40 True damage (bypasses all DR/shields) on a 1-turn cooldown — reliable, undeniable damage routed through a teammate.
Self-sufficient energy via Fairy Heart, and a clean panic-button suite (two forms of invuln) make her very hard to kill.
Provides both healing and shielding, covering team sustain without a dedicated healer.
weaknesses: Almost no personal proactive damage: her only direct damage is a delayed, telegraphed 35 AoE that whiffs on invuln targets; she relies entirely on allies to deal damage.
Slow ramp and slow tempo: the strong Fairy Star tiers (3, 4+) require many turns of allies acting while marked; early game she contributes little offense.
Mono-White color dependency with 5 White pips across the visible bar — vulnerable to White energy denial/drain and inflexible.
Fairy Heart trades 3 full turns of inaction for invuln+energy, a big tempo sacrifice that can be a liability if the team is losing tempo.
Heavily dependent on having living allies: Bestow, Fairy Heart, and Fairy Star Strategy all require/are far weaker without teammates — poor in 1v1 or as last unit standing.
Control is conditional (skips invulnerable enemies) and her heal (skips Isolated allies) can be denied by status effects.
No cleanse, no energy denial, no way to break enemy ramp — purely a protect-and-enable kit.
