win_conditions: Outlast and snowball: survive with Fairy Sphere/Fairy Heart while Fairy Star Strategy stacks accrue, permanently buffing ally damage and granting free-skill burst turns until the team overwhelms.
Enable a carry: Bestow + free-cost turns turn an ally into the primary damage dealer (especially via repeatable 40 True Fairy Glitter and stacked +10 damage buffs).
Tempo denial via protection: chain Fairy Sphere (team ignore-damage) and Fairy Law (AoE stun) to neutralize enemy offensive turns while allies act safely.

power_assessment.reasoning: A high-ceiling, low-floor team-support engine. Her protection layer (team-wide ignore-all-damage + shields, plus self and team invuln) is genuinely excellent in isolation, and Fairy Star Strategy provides compounding, permanent team value (permanent +10 damage stacks and free-skill turns) that can snowball a game. Bestow grants reliable 40 True damage routed through an ally. However she has near-zero personal offense, a slow telegraphed AoE, heavy White color dependency, a steep ramp, and is strongly team-dependent (multiple skills are dead in 1v1). She is a strong piece in a coordinated team comp but a weak solo unit, which caps her at the upper-mid tier in isolation. Numbers verified against the .gd ground truth: 35 Normal AoE + 1-turn stun (delayed 3 turns), 40 True via Bestow/Fairy Glitter, 25 team shield + 25/20 heals.
outlier_flags: Fairy Sphere (CD7) is a very strong team-wide ignore-ALL-damage panic button — borderline overstatted for a 2-cost skill; flag for cross-roster recalibration vs other invuln cooldowns.

Fairy Star Strategy stack 3 grants PERMANENT, repeatable +10 non-Affliction damage to allies (remove_on_death=false) and stack 4+ grants free skills — uncapped compounding team value that may be an outlier in long games.
Bestow gives an ally repeatable 40 True damage (DR/shield-bypassing) on CD1 — a lot of guaranteed damage outsourced to a teammate.
Personal proactive damage is an outlier on the LOW side: Mavis's own single-target burst is effectively 0 (the True nuke lives on an ally).

role: single-target class-locking control/disruptor with mark-payoff burst
signature_mechanic: Shikigami Summoning passive rolls a random skill class (Physical/Energy/Mental/Affliction) each turn; Bottomless Well, Great Serpent, and Rabbit Escape all reference that rolled class to selectively stun the enemy's matching skill type or make Megumi invulnerable to it. Bottomless Well / Great Serpent also apply named marks that Nue consumes for a Piercing damage upgrade or a damage debuff.

abilities.name: Bottomless Well
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (damage fixed); stun target-class is dynamic from Shikigami roll, default Physical
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Normal damage; class-stun (dur 2 = 1 turn) on the currently-rolled skill class (default Physical); applies 'Bottomless Well' mark for 3 turns (dur 7) that Nue consumes for Piercing upgrade

abilities.name: Great Serpent
abilities.conditional_scaling: stun target-class is dynamic from Shikigami roll (default Physical)
abilities.effects_summary: No damage; class-stun (dur 2 = 1 turn) on the currently-rolled skill class (default Physical); applies 'Great Serpent' mark for 3 turns (dur 7) that Nue consumes to inflict a -5 damage debuff on the target

abilities.name: Nue
abilities.conditional_scaling: on-mark: if target marked by Bottomless Well -> 30 Piercing (skips flat+%DR) instead of 25 Normal; if marked by Great Serpent -> additionally applies -5 damage debuff (dur 2 = 1 turn)
abilities.effects_summary: 25 Normal damage, no cooldown (spammable); upgrades to 30 Piercing vs Bottomless Well mark; applies -5 damage-mod debuff vs Great Serpent mark

abilities.name: Rabbit Escape
abilities.conditional_scaling: invuln class is dynamic from Shikigami roll (default Physical)
abilities.effects_summary: Self becomes Invulnerable to the currently-rolled skill class (default Physical) for ~1 turn (constructor dur 2); selective class-based panic button, not full invuln

abilities.name: Shikigami Summoning
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Permanent passive (dur -1). Each turn rolls 1-4 to pick a random class (Physical/Energy/Mental/Affliction), stored as the effect's mag; Bottomless Well, Great Serpent, and Rabbit Escape read this to decide which skill class to stun/become invulnerable to. Initializes to Physical.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hard-capped low. Best one-turn line: Nue on a pre-existing Bottomless Well mark (30 Piercing) + Bottomless Well (20 Normal) = 50 to one target, requiring the mark set up a prior turn. Without setup, a turn is ~45 (Nue 25 + Bottomless Well 20). No AoE, no DoT, no per-stack growth; damage is fixed numbers.
damage_profile.notes: Nue's only upgrade is 25->30 and Normal->Piercing when the Bottomless Well mark is present (DR-bypass matters vs tanky/DR targets). Megumi is a control character, not a damage dealer; total damage output is modest and front-loaded around marks.

economy.color_dependency: Light. 2 Red pips (Bottomless Well, Nue) + 2 Random pips (Great Serpent, Rabbit Escape). Mono-Red identity but cheap; everything is 1 pip.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast. Nue CD 0 (spammable every turn), Bottomless Well & Great Serpent CD 1, Rabbit Escape CD 2. Can act meaningfully every turn with minimal downtime.
economy.ramp_dependency: None for resources; mild setup dependency - Nue's Piercing payoff and Great Serpent's debuff payoff want a mark applied the prior turn.

hard_cc: class-specific stun (Bottomless Well, Great Serpent) - stuns only the rolled skill class, not a full stun
soft_cc: -5 damage debuff (Nue vs Great Serpent mark)
invuln_or_counter: class-specific invulnerability to one skill class for 1 turn (Rabbit Escape)

win_conditions: Lock down a key enemy's threatening skill class with repeated class-stuns so they can't use their core abilities
Maintain marks and chip with no-cooldown Nue (Piercing vs DR targets) while denying responses
Use Rabbit Escape selectively to dodge the enemy's primary damage class on a critical turn
Grind out attrition matchups where acting every turn and shutting off one enemy skill class wins tempo
internal_synergies: Shikigami Summoning's rolled class drives Bottomless Well, Great Serpent, and Rabbit Escape, but the roll is random so the class-lock is opportunistic rather than reliable
Bottomless Well mark -> Nue upgrades to 30 Piercing (DR bypass)
Great Serpent mark -> Nue applies -5 damage debuff
Both marks last 3 turns while Nue has 0 cooldown, so marks reliably stay live to feed Nue
Rabbit Escape and the stuns share the same rolled class, so a good roll makes both defense and offense land on the same threat
strengths: Extremely cheap kit (all 1-pip, total 4) with fast cooldowns; can act every turn
Nue has no cooldown and gains Piercing to punch through DR/armor stacking
Class-specific stun can fully shut off an enemy's key skill type when the roll matches
Selective invulnerability (Rabbit Escape) is a flexible defensive tool
Marks are long (3 turns) and easy to keep feeding the payoff skill
Mono-Red but light, with 2 flexible Random pips for easy splashing
weaknesses: Whole identity hinges on a RANDOM class roll each turn - the stun/invuln frequently target a class the enemy isn't using that turn, wasting the effect
Class-specific stun is conditional CC, not a true stun; against off-class skills it does nothing
Low total damage, no AoE, no DoT - cannot threaten teams or burst down a target
No healing, shields, cleanse, or energy denial - pure single-target disruption with no team support
Great Serpent does no damage and Rabbit Escape only defends one class, so two of four buttons are low-impact on bad rolls
Rabbit Escape invuln is short (dur 2 = 1 turn) and class-gated, can whiff entirely on a wrong roll
Heavy reliance on the opponent actually using the rolled skill class makes performance swingy and matchup-dependent

power_assessment.reasoning: A cheap, fast, every-turn disruptor with a genuinely good payoff in Nue (0 CD, Piercing on-mark) and a flexible class-gated invuln. But its core control is gated behind a per-turn RANDOM class roll, so the class-stuns and invuln only matter when the roll happens to match the enemy's active skill class, making the kit unreliable and swingy. Damage is low (peak ~50 single-target with setup, no AoE, no DoT) and there is zero team utility (no heal/shield/cleanse/energy denial). It can excel in a specific 1v1 attrition matchup or against a DR-stacker (Nue Piercing), but underperforms when rolls do not cooperate. Net: a below-average-to-fair control specialist whose ceiling is capped by RNG and whose floor is low.
outlier_flags: RNG-dependent core mechanic (random class roll governs whether CC/invuln lands)
Nue has 0 cooldown - fully spammable single-target with conditional Piercing
Two of four visible skills (Great Serpent, Rabbit Escape) deal no damage and can whiff on a bad roll
Conditional/class-gated stun is much weaker than the 'stun' wording implies

role: One-shot single-target Piercing nuke with heavy self-lockout (glass-cannon mage)
signature_mechanic: Explosion: a single big Piercing nuke set up via a stacking cost-reduction skill (Crimson Incantation, -2 Random per use) and an invuln/counter-bypass mark, but after firing leaves Megumin locked into only her recovery skill for 3 turns ("depleted").

abilities.name: Waga wa Megumin! (Invuln/Counter Bypass Setup)
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Free permanent setup. First use: permanent self-mark so Explosion bypasses Invulnerability. Second use (if already marked by 'Waga wa Megumin!'): permanent ignore_counter effect so Explosion ignores Counter and Reflect. Pure enabler; each use one-time (extra_usable gates re-use).

abilities.name: Crimson Incantation (Explosion Cost Ramp)
abilities.conditional_scaling: Stacking cost reduction: each cast adds -2 Random to Explosion's cost (stackable, displayed). Consumed when the damage skill fires. 2 casts can fully zero out the 4-Random Explosion.
abilities.effects_summary: Applies a stacking COST_MOD (-2 Random, infinite duration) to Explosion until next used. Ramps the nuke from 4-cost to 2 (1 cast) or 0 (2 casts). Gated by extra_usable: not while marked_by('Explosion') lockout.

abilities.name: Explosion
abilities.cost_breakdown: Random:4 (reducible by Crimson Incantation to 2 or 0)
abilities.conditional_scaling: Effective cost scales down with Crimson Incantation stacks; mission-advance bonus when fired after >=2 stacks (mag <= -4). Damage flat 65. With megumin1 marks the hit bypasses Invulnerability and ignores Counter/Reflect. AI weights it at 300.
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 65 Piercing (skips flat + % DR) to one enemy. Consumes Crimson Incantation cost-mod stacks. Then self-applies a 3-turn lockout mark 'Megumin can only use Face-first Slide' (mark dur 7), disabling skills 1-3 until cleared. Big swing followed by forced downtime.

abilities.name: Face-first Slide (Self-Cleanse / Recovery)
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self-recovery: fully cleanses ALL enemy-applied effects on Megumin (cleanse_all_enemy_effects) and removes the post-Explosion lockout mark, ending depletion early. Only skill usable during lockout; her escape hatch. Note: metadata SINGLE/Physical but execute() resolves on self.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hard-capped at 65 Piercing per Explosion. No per-stack/per-kill damage scaling — the only 'scaling' is cost efficiency (down to free) and bypass utility (invuln/counter/reflect). Effective DPS is low because Explosion forces a 3-turn self-lockout after each fire (escapable in 1 turn via Face-first Slide), so practical cadence is one 65 nuke every ~2-4 turns.
damage_profile.notes: 65 Piercing is moderate raw damage but high effective damage vs DR/tank comps since Piercing skips flat and % DR. Bypass-invuln and ignore-counter/reflect (from megumin1) make it reliable against defensive/counter targets. Number and type taken from megumin3.gd (resolve_damage 65 PIERCING).

economy.color_dependency: Light. Only 1 specific Red pip (Crimson Incantation); everything else Random. Single-color [Red] identity but the kit is almost entirely Random-funded, so she splashes into any team with minimal energy strain.
economy.cooldown_tempo: All offense/setup skills are cooldown 0; only Face-first Slide has cd 2. Tempo is gated NOT by cooldowns but by the self-imposed 3-turn lockout after Explosion and the 2-cast ramp to discount it.
economy.ramp_dependency: High self-ramp dependency for efficiency: Explosion base 4 Random is steep; Crimson Incantation must be cast 1-2x to make it affordable (2 casts -> free). Also relies on pre-casting both megumin1 setups to make the nuke bypass invuln/counter. Setup-heavy and self-depleting after firing.

invuln_or_counter: Explosion bypasses enemy Invulnerability (via megumin1 first use)
Explosion ignores enemy Counter and Reflect (via megumin1 second use)

win_conditions: Pre-stack Crimson Incantation (1-2x) and the two Waga wa Megumin! setups, then land a discounted/free 65 Piercing Explosion on a key target, ignoring DR/invuln/counter.
Punch through tank/defensive/counter-reliant comps where Piercing + bypass utility is disproportionately effective.
Win the surrounding turns with allies while she is in self-lockout — she is explicitly designed to need allied support during depletion windows.
internal_synergies: Crimson Incantation (slot 2) -> Explosion (slot 3): stacking -2 Random cost-mod makes the 4-cost nuke affordable or free; firing consumes the stacks and grants a mission bonus at >=2 stacks.

Waga wa Megumin! (slot 1) -> Explosion: first use makes it bypass Invulnerability, second use makes it ignore Counter/Reflect — turning a one-shot into a guaranteed-connect nuke; also relaxes Explosion targeting state (bypass_state).
Face-first Slide (slot 4) -> removes the post-Explosion lockout mark and full-cleanses enemy debuffs, shortening forced downtime from 3 turns to 1 and acting as her only emergency action.
strengths: High effective single-target damage: 65 Piercing skips flat and percentage DR, strong into tanks/bruisers.
Reliable connect: can bypass Invulnerability and ignore Counter/Reflect, beating defensive/counter archetypes that wall most nukers.
Very low color tax (1 Red, rest Random) — easy to slot into any team energy-wise.
Self-sufficient cleanse + lockout-removal in one button (Face-first Slide).
Cost ramp can make the nuke free, freeing energy for allies on the firing turn.
weaknesses: Crippling self-lockout: after Explosion she can only use Face-first Slide for 3 turns; spending the cleanse to escape costs a full action and tempo.
No AoE, no CC, no healing, no shields, no energy denial — purely a single-target one-trick.
Heavy setup tax: needs 1-2 Incantation casts plus two Waga setups to reach peak, so the first Explosion is slow to come online.
Damage hard-capped at 65 with zero damage scaling — output does not grow over a long game.
Extremely dependent on allies to carry the lockout windows; alone she is feast-or-famine.
Wasted setup risk: if the target dies or is True-immune, the entire ramp investment is spent.

power_assessment.reasoning: A deliberately swingy glass-cannon. Her one nuke (65 Piercing, invuln/counter-bypass) is genuinely strong against defensive comps and cheap to fund, but the 3-turn self-lockout, lack of any AoE/CC/sustain, hard damage cap, and multi-skill setup tax keep practical throughput low. She is a support-dependent specialist rather than a self-sufficient threat — below-average-to-average in isolation. Note a metadata/wiring quirk: the .gd files do not match metadata ability names (megumin3.gd is the 65-Piercing + lockout skill while metadata labels slot 3 'Explosion'/Energy/Harmful, and megumin4.gd is a self-cleanse despite SINGLE/Physical metadata) — mechanics rated from the .gd ground truth.
outlier_flags: self-lockout-mechanic
metadata-vs-gd-name-mismatch
no-damage-scaling-hard-cap-65
explicitly-support-dependent-by-design
cost-can-reach-zero-via-ramp

role: Counter-based punisher / reactive bruiser who turns enemy aggression into Piercing burst
signature_mechanic: Full Counter + Revenge Counter loop: punishes enemies for using Harmful skills, and Revenge Counter charges a scaling Piercing nuke (+30 per Harmful skill absorbed) while Meliodas is effect-immune and skill-locked.

abilities.name: Hellblaze
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Affliction immediate + a 5 Affliction tick (~1 turn) = 20 Affliction total; applies ignore_healing for 1 turn (target cannot be healed). Affliction bypasses barriers/shields/DR. Cheap heal-denial + chip. describe()/JSON text is stale (mentions equipping Dragon Hilt); split_desc/execute are accurate.

abilities.name: Full Counter
abilities.conditional_scaling: binary trigger: 25 on counter (enemy uses new Harmful skill), 10 on timeout if not triggered
abilities.effects_summary: Invisible counter on target for 1 turn (dur 2). If target uses a new Harmful skill they take 25 Normal; if they don't, timeout deals 10 Normal. .gd resolves DamageType.Type.NORMAL for both (JSON/describe incorrectly say Piercing). Discourages enemy aggression on the counter'd target.

abilities.name: Revenge Counter
abilities.target_type: SELF (then SINGLE on the charged follow-up)
abilities.conditional_scaling: base 30 Piercing (mag starts at 1), +30 Piercing per Harmful skill received during the 2-turn charge window; no upper bound
abilities.effects_summary: Self: ignore_non_damage_effect (2 turns) + self skill-lock mark (2 turns), both invisible — Meliodas is immune to harmful non-damage effects but cannot act. Counts Harmful skills received via HARMFUL_RECEIVE_TRIGGER. On expiry converts into a free-cost single-target follow-up dealing 30 * mag Piercing. Skips flat+%DR. Panic-button/charge that rewards being focused while locked.

abilities.name: Jitsuzo Bunshin
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Normal to all enemies + self invuln_effect restricted to Physical skills for 1 turn (dur 2). Cheap AoE that also self-protects vs physical attackers. JSON says generic Invulnerable; .gd limits invuln to the 'Physical' class only.

abilities.name: Dragon's Sin of Wrath
abilities.conditional_scaling: triggers once per qualifying enemy action; scales with how often allies are attacked
abilities.effects_summary: Permanent (dur -1) passive applied to all allies: whenever an enemy uses a Harmful non-Strategic skill on a Meliodas ally, Meliodas deals 10 Normal retaliation to that enemy (Strategic skills excluded). Hidden passive slot (not on action bar). Reinforces the anti-aggression theme; passive team-wide thorns.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Revenge Counter is theoretically unbounded: 30 Piercing base + 30 per Harmful skill absorbed over 2 turns. Realistically ~90-150 Piercing if focused by multiple enemies; in practice 60-90. Single-turn peak combining a fired Revenge Counter (60 typical) is the spike; everything else is low, chip-level damage.
damage_profile.notes: Most of Meliodas's damage is reactive/conditional, not proactive. Hellblaze gives 20 Affliction (bypasses shields) + heal-denial. Full Counter is binary (25 or 10 Normal). Jitsuzo Bunshin is the only true AoE at a flat 15 Normal. The passive adds 10 Normal per enemy aggression instance. Real output depends heavily on the enemy choosing to attack into counters.

economy.color_dependency: Light Red dependency: 3 of 5 visible pips are Red (Hellblaze, Full Counter, Jitsuzo Bunshin each Red:1); Revenge Counter is 2 Random and flexible. Mono-Red identity (character_colors = [3]) but very cheap overall.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast: Hellblaze and Full Counter on 1cd, Revenge Counter on 0cd (gated by its charge state), Jitsuzo Bunshin on 2cd. Can act meaningfully every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low ramp but high situational dependency. No stacking/ramp resource; Revenge Counter 'ramps' only within its 2-turn window and only if enemies attack Meliodas. Power is gated by enemy behavior, not by time.

invuln_or_counter: Full Counter (counter: 25 Normal on Harmful-skill trigger, 10 on timeout, invisible)
Revenge Counter (effect-immunity to harmful non-damage effects for 2 turns + scaling Piercing payoff, invisible)
Jitsuzo Bunshin (self invuln vs Physical skills, 1 turn)
Dragon's Sin of Wrath passive (team-wide 10 Normal thorns on enemy aggression)

win_conditions: Bait enemies into attacking, then cash out Full Counter + Revenge Counter for heavy Piercing burst.
Use Revenge Counter as a panic button to ignore disables/control for 2 turns and punish focus-fire with an unbounded Piercing nuke.
Grind down healers/regen comps with Hellblaze's heal-denial + Affliction chip (bypasses shields).
Protect a fragile carry: passive thorns + counters tax any enemy that attacks Meliodas's allies.
internal_synergies: Full Counter + Dragon's Sin passive both punish enemy Harmful skills, stacking retaliation on aggressive enemies.
Revenge Counter's effect-immunity protects Meliodas from CC while he's the natural focus target, and the more he's attacked the bigger the payoff — being focused is rewarded.
Hellblaze's heal-denial makes all chip/counter damage (and Affliction tick) stick against sustain comps.
Jitsuzo Bunshin's Physical-invuln pairs with melee-heavy enemy comps to deny their turn while the passive/counters still tax them.
All damage is cheap (mostly Red:1), so the kit is energy-efficient and lets Meliodas always have a play.
strengths: Extremely cheap kit (5 total pips, mostly 1-cost) with fast cooldowns — high tempo, low energy footprint.
Strong reactive package: two counters plus a permanent team-wide thorns passive heavily tax enemy aggression.
Revenge Counter is a rare combined CC-immunity + skill-lock + scaling Piercing payoff that can hit very hard if focused.
Hellblaze provides shield-piercing Affliction damage AND heal-denial, a strong anti-sustain tool.
Piercing/Affliction damage in the kit bypasses DR/shields, so effective damage is higher than raw numbers suggest.
Built-in defensive layers (Physical invuln, effect-immunity window) make him durable for his cost.
weaknesses: Damage is heavily reactive/conditional — a passive or kiting enemy denies Full Counter, the passive, and most of Revenge Counter's scaling, leaving only ~15-20 Affliction + chip.
Revenge Counter locks Meliodas out of acting for 2 full turns; if enemies simply don't attack him, he loses tempo for a small payoff (30 Piercing).
No healing, no hard CC, no shields, no energy denial — purely a damage/punish profile.
Only one real AoE (flat 15) and modest proactive single-target damage; struggles to close games on his own initiative.
Jitsuzo Bunshin's invuln only covers Physical skills — Energy/Affliction/True attackers ignore it.
Several JSON/describe texts are stale/wrong (counter type, invuln scope), a design-clarity weakness rather than a mechanical bug.

power_assessment.reasoning: A cheap, well-rounded reactive bruiser. Floor is solid: every turn he can play something for 1 pip, he has shield-piercing chip + heal-denial, a permanent thorns passive, and two defensive counters. Ceiling (a multi-stacked Revenge Counter for 90-150 Piercing while immune to control) is genuinely strong but requires the enemy to cooperate by attacking him. Against passive/avoidant or pure-control comps his output collapses to chip damage and he idles 2 turns on a mistimed Revenge Counter. Lacks the proactive burst, AoE, or utility (heal/hard-CC/energy-denial) of top-tier picks, so he lands as a solid, matchup-dependent mid-tier rather than a carry.
outlier_flags: Revenge Counter has no coded damage cap (30 * mag Piercing) — theoretically unbounded if repeatedly focused; potential balance outlier in heavy-focus scenarios.
JSON metadata mislabels Full Counter as Piercing (actually Normal in .gd) and Jitsuzo Bunshin's invuln as full (actually Physical-only) — data/description drift, not a power bug.
Hellblaze damage_effect uses an odd duration (3) and an unusually cheap 1-cost shield-piercing + heal-deny package — strong for its cost.

abilities.name: Shabon Spray
abilities.conditional_scaling: Deals 25 instead of 15 if Mercury is already marked by 'Shabon Spray' (i.e. used it last turn) — chaining the basic ramps damage by +10. Also applies a self 'Empowered' mark (dur 3 = 1 self-turn) that upgrades mercury2/3/4, and reduces Shine Aqua Illusion's cooldown by 3 via a cooldown_mod.
abilities.effects_summary: 15 dmg (25 when self-marked/chained); self-applies 'Empowered' mark for 1 turn enabling upgraded versions of the other 3 skills; auto-refreshes Shine Aqua Illusion cooldown by -3.

abilities.name: Shabon Spray Freeze
abilities.conditional_scaling: While Empowered (self-marked by Shabon Spray): additionally increases target's cooldowns by 1 (cooldown_mod mag +1, dur 4). No damage scaling.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 dmg + Paralyze for 2 turns (locks target's cooldowns from ticking). If Empowered, also adds +1 to the target's current cooldowns (cooldown denial/tempo stall).

abilities.name: Mercury Aqua Mirage
abilities.conditional_scaling: While Empowered: can be cast on any ally instead of only self (extends the counter protection to a teammate). Counter damage is fixed at 15.
abilities.effects_summary: Invisible 1-turn counter: the first enemy to use a Harmful skill on the protected character is countered for 15 dmg and the counter triggers (interrupts/stops their action via default_counter_trigger). Self-only by default; any ally while Empowered.

abilities.name: Shine Aqua Illusion
abilities.conditional_scaling: While Empowered, effective cooldown is reduced by 3 (delivered through mercury1's auto cooldown_mod), turning the 4-CD invuln into a roughly 1-CD panic button as long as the basic is being chained.
abilities.effects_summary: Self Invulnerable for 1 turn (default_defend — blocks all damage/effects). Pure defensive panic button; cooldown collapses to ~1 when Mercury keeps her Empower loop running.

role: Defensive disruptor / tempo controller — low-damage chip with paralyze + cooldown denial, self-protection counters, and a near-spammable invuln
signature_mechanic: 'Empowered' self-mark loop: using Shabon Spray (slot 1, 0-CD) marks Mercury for 1 turn, which (a) upgrades the next Freeze/Mirage/Illusion into stronger versions, (b) auto-discounts Shine Aqua Illusion's cooldown by 3, and (c) lets a repeated basic deal 25 instead of 15. Keeping the loop active every turn is the engine of her whole kit.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hard-capped: max single-target output is 25 (chained Shabon Spray). She has no AoE and no DoT. Counter adds 15 reactively but is not on-demand burst. Realistic per-turn damage is 15-25.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is Normal type (mitigated by DR/barriers/shields). No execute, no per-stack/per-kill scaling beyond the flat 15->25 chain bonus. Damage is incidental; her value is control, not killing.

economy.color_dependency: Light Blue dependency: 2 of 4 visible skills (Freeze, Mirage) require a specific Blue pip; the basic and the invuln take 1 Random each. Single-color identity (character_colors=[1] Blue), easy to fund.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent. Basic is 0-CD and spammable; Freeze and Mirage are 2-CD; Shine Aqua Illusion is nominally 4-CD but auto-reduced by 3 (to ~1) whenever the Empower loop is running. Very few dead turns.
economy.ramp_dependency: Light ramp — only a 1-turn self-mark that must be re-applied each turn by recasting the 0-cost basic. No multi-turn stacking; the loop resets instantly if she skips the basic.

hard_cc: Paralyze (Shabon Spray Freeze) — 2-turn cooldown lock
soft_cc: Cooldown increase +1 on Empowered Freeze
Paralyze prevents cooldowns from advancing
invuln_or_counter: Invulnerable 1 turn (Shine Aqua Illusion, ~1-CD when looped)
Invisible 15-dmg counter vs first Harmful skill (Mercury Aqua Mirage, extendable to allies)

win_conditions: Stall the enemy out of tempo: paralyze + cooldown padding to keep a key threat's abilities offline while teammates win
Outlast via near-permanent self-invuln and reactive counters, acting as an unkillable disruptor that the enemy must overcommit into
Protect a carry with ally-targeted counters (while Empowered) and chip damage until allies close the game
internal_synergies: Shabon Spray's self-mark is the keystone: it simultaneously enables Freeze's cooldown bump, Mirage's ally-targeting, Illusion's -3 CD, and its own 25-dmg upgrade — one 0-cost cast lights up the entire kit
Illusion's auto -3 CD from the basic means as long as she keeps spamming Shabon Spray she has invuln available nearly every turn
Paralyze (Freeze) + Empowered cooldown +1 stack into a heavy single-target tempo lock
strengths: Extremely cheap, single-color, easy to fund kit (1 pip per skill, 2 Random)
Near-spammable 1-turn invulnerability — outstanding personal survivability / panic button
Strong single-target cooldown denial (Paralyze 2 turns + Empowered cooldown padding) disrupts cooldown-reliant enemies
Self loop is self-contained and reliable — no setup turns, no external dependencies, no ramp to lose on a bad draw
Counter can be projected onto an ally when Empowered, giving light team protection
weaknesses: Very low damage ceiling (25 single-target, no AoE, no DoT) — cannot close games on her own
No healing, shields, cleanse, or true energy (pip) denial — purely cooldown-side control
All damage is Normal type, fully mitigated by DR/barriers/shields
Control is single-target only; struggles vs wide enemy boards
Empower loop demands she spend her basic almost every turn, constraining her action economy and limiting how often she can branch into Freeze/Mirage in the same turn
Counter and invuln are reactive/defensive — passive playstyle that can be ignored if the enemy targets her teammates instead

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-designed, internally coherent defensive control unit but a clear low-damage specialist. Her standout traits are near-infinite 1-turn invulnerability (Illusion auto-discounted to ~1-CD by the basic) and solid single-target cooldown denial (2-turn Paralyze + Empowered cooldown padding), all on a dirt-cheap single-Blue economy with no dead turns. However she brings no AoE, no DoT, no healing/shields/cleanse, no pip denial, and tops out at 25 damage — she literally cannot win a game by herself and is a tempo/support piece that needs damage dealers around her. Reactive, passive counters can be played around by ignoring her. Mid-tier: high floor and very survivable, low ceiling. Useful as an annoyance/protector in the right comp, unimpactful in a vacuum.
outlier_flags: near-permanent self-invuln (Illusion effective CD ~1 while looping) is a survivability outlier
0-cost 0-CD basic that both deals damage and powers the entire kit is unusually efficient action economy
damage ceiling (25 max, no AoE/DoT) is a low-end outlier for an offensive-tagged character

role: single-target control bruiser with ramping self-buff and execute-priced burst
signature_mechanic: One For All ramp: a permanent stacking self-buff (+5 DR, +5 damage, ignore-stun per stack) paid for with escalating self-damage (5 HP per stack per new skill use), gated behind a transformation chain (St. Louis Smash swaps in the hidden Faux 100%, which permanently grants self-invuln-on-skill-use + bypass invulnerability).

abilities.name: Blackwhip
abilities.conditional_scaling: Applies vulnerability_effect(mag 10) tagged to Blackwhip/St. Louis Smash/Detroit Smash/Faux 100% (dur 3) - target takes +10 damage from any of Midoriya's named follow-up skills next turn. A damage-amp mark, not unconditional bonus damage.
abilities.effects_summary: 10 Normal dmg; stuns target's Helpful skills for 1 turn (partial CC); applies a +10 vulnerability mark vs Midoriya's named skills. AI references this mark to boost Smash/Detroit priority (+75).

abilities.name: St. Louis Smash
abilities.conditional_scaling: none on own damage; benefits from Blackwhip mark (+10 taken). Enables the kit: swaps slot 1 (Blackwhip) for Faux 100% (slot 5) for 1 turn.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Normal dmg; FULL stun for 1 turn (hard CC); swaps in the hidden Faux 100% ability for 1 turn (transformation enabler).

abilities.name: Detroit Smash
abilities.conditional_scaling: none on own damage; benefits from Blackwhip mark (+10 taken).
abilities.effects_summary: 30 Normal dmg; FULL silence for 1 turn (hard CC - locks all target skills). Highest base damage of the standard kit.

abilities.name: One For All
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent stacking buff: per cast adds +5 damage_mod, +5 damage_reduction, and ignore-STUN (rest of game). Self-cost scales: trigger deals stack_count*5 HP to self every time Midoriya uses a NEW skill; each cast adds another stackable trigger, so HP drain compounds.
abilities.effects_summary: No damage. Permanent self-buff: +5 damage, +5 DR, ignores enemy stun. Stacks. Downside: loses 5 HP per stack each skill use, so the buff is self-damaging ramp. Provides the kit's only damage scaling and stun immunity.

abilities.name: Faux 100%
abilities.conditional_scaling: Benefits from Blackwhip +10 mark (mark fires vs Faux 100%). Permanently installs trigger: every subsequent Midoriya skill use grants self Invulnerable 1 turn, and all his skills Bypass Invulnerability (one-time install on first cast).
abilities.effects_summary: 45 PIERCING dmg (skips flat + %DR) - the kit's burst nuke; only reachable via St. Louis Smash swap. Permanently grants: invuln-for-1-turn on every skill use + bypass-invuln on all his skills. Turns Midoriya into a slippery, unblockable attacker.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Per-hit damage grows by +5 for every One For All stack (no cap, rest-of-game). Faux 100% nuke 45 Piercing + Blackwhip +10 mark = 55 effective in one turn before stacks; with stacked OFA the Faux cast climbs indefinitely (e.g. 4 stacks => ~45+20+10 = ~75 piercing). No AoE and no DoT; ceiling is bounded by self-HP attrition from One For All rather than energy.
damage_profile.notes: All standard hits are Normal (subject to DR/shields/barriers); only Faux 100% is Piercing (skips flat+%DR). The +10 Blackwhip mark applies only to Midoriya's four named skills, so 'burst' is a 2-turn setup (Blackwhip -> mark -> Smash/Faux). True one-turn single-target peak from a single action is Faux 100% at 45 Piercing (55 with an active mark).

economy.color_dependency: Heavy Green dependency - mono-Green identity (character_colors=[0]). Visible kit: Blackwhip Green:1, St. Louis Smash Green:1, Detroit Smash Green:1+Random:1, One For All Random:1. Hidden Faux 100% is Green:2. Cheap overall but Green-locked.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast: three of four visible skills are cooldown 1 (spammable each turn); only One For All is cooldown 4. Faux 100% is cooldown 1 once swapped in. Excellent tempo - Midoriya rarely idles.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate-to-high. Damage scaling and stun-immunity live entirely in One For All, which must be ramped over multiple casts while paying escalating self-HP. The burst nuke (Faux 100%) requires the St. Louis Smash swap each cycle, so the kit ramps into power rather than starting strong.

hard_cc: full stun 1 turn (St. Louis Smash)
full silence 1 turn (Detroit Smash)
soft_cc: Helpful-skill stun 1 turn (Blackwhip) - locks only the target's Helpful abilities
invuln_or_counter: self Invulnerable 1 turn on every skill use (Faux 100% passive)
Bypass Invulnerability on all his skills (Faux 100% passive)

win_conditions: Lock down a key enemy with the stun/silence chain (Blackwhip Helpful-stun -> St. Louis Smash full stun -> Detroit Smash silence) while ramping One For All in the background.

Transform via St. Louis Smash into Faux 100% and snowball: permanent invuln-on-action + bypass-invuln makes him nearly unkillable and uncounterable, then chip with 45 Piercing nukes scaled by One For All.
Out-value durably: cheap mono-Green CC every turn neutralizes a priority threat while +5/+5 stacks turn him into an unstoppable bruiser, racing the enemy before self-HP attrition catches up.
internal_synergies: Blackwhip's +10 vulnerability mark is keyed to his own three follow-up skills + Faux 100%, so it amplifies every other damage source and the AI prioritizes Smash/Detroit/Faux against marked targets (+75 weight).
St. Louis Smash is the gatekeeper: its full stun buys a safe turn AND swaps in Faux 100%, the only access to the 45 Piercing nuke and the invuln/bypass-invuln passive.
One For All's ignore-stun stacks with Faux 100%'s self-invuln-on-action to make Midoriya extremely sticky; +5 damage/stack scales Faux 100%'s Piercing nuke that ignores DR.
Faux 100% bypass-invuln lets all his skills (and AI targeting, which passes bypassing=true) punch through invuln defenders, solving a common counter.
strengths: Dense, cheap CC: full stun, full silence, and a Helpful-skill lockout for ~1 pip each at cooldown 1 - exceptional control density and tempo.
Permanent, uncapped scaling via One For All (+5 dmg/+5 DR/stun-immune per stack) that also grants stun immunity, a strong anti-control trait.
Faux 100% end-state is oppressive: self-invuln on every action + bypass-invuln on all skills + 45 Piercing (ignores flat+%DR), making him both untargetable and unblockable.
Mono-Green and ultra-cheap (5 visible pips total), trivial to fit into any Green-leaning team and never energy-starved.
weaknesses: Self-damaging ramp: One For All's stack_count*5 HP cost per skill use compounds dangerously - over-ramping can kill him, and the drain fires on EVERY skill use, so an active Midoriya bleeds constantly.
No defensive sustain at all - zero healing, shields, barriers, or cleanse to offset the self-attrition; pure glass-cannon ramp.
Strictly single-target with no AoE and no DoT; weak into wide/swarm comps and slow to close out multiple threats.
Power is back-loaded: real burst (Faux 100%) is locked behind the St. Louis Smash swap each cycle and meaningful damage needs several One For All stacks, so he is mediocre in the opening turns.
Standard Smashes deal Normal damage (eaten by DR/shields/barriers); only the gated Faux nuke is Piercing, so shield/DR comps blunt most of his output until he transforms.

power_assessment.reasoning: Elite control density (full stun + full silence + helpful-lockout, all ~1 pip, cooldown 1) on a mono-Green, ultra-cheap chassis, plus an uncapped permanent scaling buff and a genuinely oppressive Faux 100% end-state (self-invuln-on-action, bypass-invuln, 45 Piercing). That combination is strong and hard to interact with. Held back from S-tier by real costs: no sustain/defense beyond stacked DR, a self-HP attrition mechanic that punishes the very spam his tempo encourages, strictly single-target output, and front-loaded weakness (burst is gated behind the swap and several ramp turns). He wins drawn-out single-target duels and snowballs once transformed, but is exploitable by burst, swarm, and shield/DR comps before he comes online.
outlier_flags: One For All self-damage scales as stack_count*5 per skill use AND each cast adds a new stackable trigger - HP drain compounds; likely a balance/bug edge case worth flagging.
Permanent, uncapped +5 dmg/+5 DR/ignore-stun with no listed cap could become oppressive in long games.
Faux 100% grants BOTH self-invuln-on-every-action and bypass-invuln permanently from one Green:2 cast - a very strong, low-cost defensive+offensive package on a hidden ability.
Three 1-cost cooldown-1 hard/soft CC skills is unusually high control-per-pip versus typical roster economy.

role: Anti-strategic disruptor / single-target piercing duelist with a team anti-kill panic button
signature_mechanic: Strategic-skill lockdown: nearly every harmful ability stuns the target's Strategic (and non-Strategic) skills, while Rallying Call grants whole-team immortality that ramps +1 turn per use. Maneuvering Gear swaps her free utility into the harder-hitting Thunder Spear.

abilities.name: Titan Takedown
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage if target is currently stunned (25 total); flat otherwise
abilities.effects_summary: Spammable (cd 0) single-target nuke. 20 Piercing (skips flat+% DR). Cannot be countered or reflected. Synergizes with her own stun-applying skills for the +5 bonus.

abilities.name: Rallying Call
abilities.conditional_scaling: Ramps: applies immortality for 2 + 2*stacks duration; each cast adds a stackable self mark, so each subsequent cast lasts +1 turn longer
abilities.effects_summary: Team-wide IMMORTALITY (cannot be killed) for 1 turn base, extended by 1 turn per prior use via a stacking self mark. A team-saving panic button vs lethal turns; does not prevent damage, only death.

abilities.name: Maneuvering Gear
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Free utility. Mikasa + selected ally IGNORE harmful non-damage effects for 1 turn (invisible cleanse/immunity vs stuns/CC/debuffs). Also swaps her own slot 3 to 'Thunder Spear' (mikasa5) for the duration, enabling the stronger attack.

abilities.name: Unlikely Savior
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self-INVULNERABILITY until end of her next turn (~1 turn) AND stuns target enemy's NON-Strategic skills for the same window. Defensive + offensive lock: shields Mikasa while denying the enemy's damage/utility actions (leaving only their Strategic skills usable).

abilities.name: Thunder Spear
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden swap-in (replaces slot 3 while Maneuvering Gear is active). Shatters the target's Shield, deals 25 Piercing, then stuns their STRATEGIC skills for 1 turn. Anti-shield + anti-strategic-engine attack.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Low and flat. Titan Takedown caps at 25 (20 + 5 vs a stunned target); Thunder Spear is a fixed 25. No multi-hit, no AoE, no DoT, no per-stack/per-kill damage growth. Realistic best turn is one attack (~25 Piercing) since her economy and cooldowns don't enable double-attacking.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is Piercing (bypasses flat + % DR), so effective damage holds up against tanky/DR targets, but absolute numbers are very low. She is a control/utility character, not a damage threat.

economy.color_dependency: Light Red dependency: only Titan Takedown (and the hidden Thunder Spear) require a specific Red pip. Rallying Call and Unlikely Savior cost 1 Random each; Maneuvering Gear is free. Very easy to fund on almost any team.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Cheap and high-uptime: a 0-cd spammable attack and a free 3-cd utility give constant pressure, while the two strongest control/protect tools (Rallying Call, Unlikely Savior) sit on 4-cd. Tempo is steady rather than bursty.
economy.ramp_dependency: Only Rallying Call ramps (immortality duration +1 turn per prior cast); the rest of the kit is fully online from turn 1. Low ramp dependency overall.

Unlikely Savior: stuns non-Strategic skills ~1 turn

invuln_or_counter: Unlikely Savior: self invulnerability ~1 turn
Rallying Call: team-wide immortality (cannot be killed) 1+ turns
Maneuvering Gear: ignore harmful non-damage effects 1 turn (self+ally, effective CC immunity)

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded control/protection support with low damage. Strengths: Piercing damage that ignores DR, a 0-cost free utility, light color requirements, two layers of self-protection (invuln + non-damage-effect immunity), a team-wide anti-lethal panic button that ramps, and strong class-selective stun pressure (especially Thunder Spear shattering shields + locking Strategic skills, plus Unlikely Savior locking non-Strategic skills). The Titan Takedown -> stun-bonus loop and Maneuvering Gear -> Thunder Spear swap give nice internal synergy. Weaknesses keep her mid: damage is very low (~25 peak/turn, no AoE, no DoT, no scaling), so she rarely closes games on her own; her stuns are partial (class-restricted), not full lockouts; Rallying Call only prevents death (not damage) and needs multiple casts to be long; and several effects are duration ~1 turn. She enables a team rather than carrying. Rated around average in isolation: very durable and disruptive, but no win-by-herself ceiling.

role: Low-HP-scaling ranged burst sniper (single-target + piercing AoE) with self-counterplay

Genius Sniper layers a 3-turn mark making her two damage skills Uncounterable + Bypassing (ignore taunt/protection) and dealing +10 to the marked enemy.

abilities.name: Roman Artillery - Pumpkin
abilities.cost_breakdown: 1 Blue (reduced to 1 Random if Mine HP < 40)
abilities.conditional_scaling: If Mine HP<70: +10 damage (30 total) AND damage becomes Piercing. If Mine HP<40: cost drops to 1 Random. With Genius Sniper mark on target: +10 vs marked enemy (and uncounterable/bypassing). Peak vs marked low-HP: 40 Piercing for 1 Random, 0 CD.

abilities.name: High Output Blast Blade

abilities.effects_summary: Piercing AoE that always ignores DR; below 60 HP adds a team-wide 1-turn soft-lock (non-Strategic skills stunned, Strategic still usable) and scales up at low HP.

abilities.name: Genius Sniper
abilities.conditional_scaling: Applies +10 vulnerability vs the marked target specifically for Roman Artillery and High Output Blast Blade (3 turns). Effect is a flat setup buff, not damage itself.
abilities.effects_summary: 3-turn setup: self-mark + ignore_counter makes Mine's skills Uncounterable and Bypassing (ignore taunt/protect/redirect on the targeting side), and applies a +10 vulnerability on the chosen enemy to her two damage skills. Targets through cover (bypassing=true).

abilities.name: Narrow Dodge
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: default_defend: Mine becomes Invulnerable for 1 turn. Panic button / survives a turn; also lets her safely sit near low-HP thresholds without dying.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Single-target same-turn ceiling ~90 vs a Genius-Sniper-marked enemy while Mine HP<30: Roman Artillery 40 Piercing (20 base +10 low-HP +10 mark) + High Output Blast Blade 50 Piercing to that target (25 base +15 low-HP +10 mark). Both Piercing so they skip flat+% DR; ~90 effective on one target. AoE ceiling is High Output Blast Blade alone at 50 Piercing on the marked enemy (40 on the rest) plus a team-wide non-Strategic stun. No DoT.
damage_profile.notes: All burst is front-loaded and Piercing once Mine is hurt; zero damage-over-time. Roman Artillery has 0 cooldown so single-target pressure repeats every turn (40 Piercing/turn marked at low HP), while the big AoE+stun is on a 2-turn cooldown. Damage is gated on Mine being LOW on HP, which is also when she is closest to dying.

economy.color_dependency: Light. Only 2 Blue pips total across the kit (1 on each damage skill); mine3/mine4 are pure Random. Below 40 HP even Roman Artillery's Blue requirement disappears (becomes 1 Random), so color reliance shrinks as she ramps.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Strong tempo: Roman Artillery 0 CD (spammable every turn), High Output Blast Blade 2 CD, Genius Sniper 3 CD, Narrow Dodge 4 CD. Sustained pressure leans on the free 0-CD nuke.
economy.ramp_dependency: Inverse-HP ramp rather than stack/turn ramp: power scales with how much damage Mine has TAKEN. No stack/energy buildup; thresholds activate instantly when HP crosses 70/60/40/30. Genius Sniper is a 3-turn setup window boosting both damage skills.

invuln_or_counter: Narrow Dodge: self-Invulnerable 1 turn
Genius Sniper grants Uncounterable (ignore_counter) on Mine's skills for 3 turns
soft_cc: High Output Blast Blade: AoE stun of all enemies' non-Strategic skills for 1 turn while Mine HP<60 (Strategic skills remain usable)

internal_synergies: Genius Sniper + Roman Artillery/High Output: the mark grants Uncounterable + Bypassing (skips taunt/protect/redirect) and +10 vulnerability, so both damage skills hit harder, hit the intended target through cover, and can't be punished by counters for 3 turns.

Low-HP thresholds + Narrow Dodge: Pumpkin gets stronger as Mine is cornered; the 1-turn invuln lets her survive at the dangerous sub-40/sub-30 band where her damage, Piercing conversion, and free recast all come online.
Sub-40 HP cost reduction makes Roman Artillery a 1-Random, 0-CD, 30 Piercing nuke (40 vs marked) — extremely cheap repeatable single-target pressure once cornered.
Piercing conversion (mine1 <70 HP) + mine2 always-Piercing makes the whole damage kit ignore flat and % DR exactly in the window where she most needs to close games.
strengths: Excellent armor/DR penetration: Piercing on demand (mine1 <70 HP, mine2 always) bypasses flat and % damage reduction.
Cheap, repeatable single-target burst: 0-cooldown Roman Artillery that gets free (1 Random) and stronger as she takes damage.
Built-in counterplay against defensive comps: Genius Sniper makes her uncounterable and bypassing (ignores taunt/protect) for 3 turns.
Has a hard survival button (1-turn invuln) and a team-wide soft stun, so she is not purely a one-note nuker.
Very low color commitment (only 2 Blue pips), easy to fit into mixed-energy teams; tempo-positive cooldowns.
weaknesses: Glass cannon with anti-synergistic scaling: best damage requires being low HP, exactly when she is easiest to kill; one burst can end her before thresholds pay off.
Zero self-healing, shields, barriers, or cleanse — survivability is just one 4-CD invuln turn and dodging focus fire.
At full/high HP she is weak: 20 Normal single-target and 25 Piercing AoE with no stun, no scaling active.
No hard CC, no energy denial, no sustained DoT — limited disruption beyond a single 1-turn non-Strategic stun.
AoE stun and +damage thresholds are conditional on her own HP, so healing/over-shielding her actually turns OFF parts of her kit; awkward to support.
Genius Sniper's value is single-target (vulnerability + mark on one enemy), so against wide teams the boost is narrow and costs a turn of setup.

power_assessment.reasoning: A focused, well-designed glass-cannon assassin. Her ceiling is high and relevant: ~90 effective single-target burst in one turn that is Piercing (ignores DR) and uncounterable/bypassing via Genius Sniper, plus a 0-cooldown 1-Random recast nuke once cornered and a team-wide soft stun on a 2-CD Piercing AoE. Color cost is trivial. What holds her back from top-tier carry is the anti-synergistic risk profile: peak output is gated on her own low HP with no innate sustain, only a single 4-CD invuln to protect the cornered window. Played from full HP she is mediocre (20 Normal / 25 Piercing AoE, no stun). Strong for a pilot who can ride the HP knife-edge and against defensive/armored comps, but fragile and swingy otherwise — squarely upper-mid tier.
outlier_flags: 0-cooldown single-target damage skill (Roman Artillery) — uncommon and strong for repeatable pressure
Cost-reduction-to-1-Random at low HP makes a 30-40 Piercing nuke nearly free
Reverse scaling (stronger as own HP drops) is mechanically unusual and creates support anti-synergy (healing her can disable her stun/bonus damage)
Uncounterable + bypassing (ignore taunt/protect) for 3 turns is a strong defensive-comp counter on a 3-CD 1-cost setup

role: Bypassing single-target nuker with a self-ramp and two mutually-exclusive late-game transformation paths (AoE-conversion vs. double-power)
signature_mechanic: Combo-swap system: using Railgun marks/swaps it to Ultra Railgun for 1 turn (and Iron Sand to Iron Colossus), while Overcharge converts incoming damage into PERMANENT +5 Railgun damage / +5 Iron Sand shield per stack. Committing the alt form (Iron Colossus = permanent AoE + team invuln, or Ultra Railgun = permanent doubled base effects at +1 cost) locks her out of all further switching for the game.

abilities.name: Iron Sand
abilities.effects_summary: Grants one ally a 20 Shield for 1 turn (dur 2). +5 Shield per Overcharge stack; x2 (40 base) while marked by Ultra Railgun. After use, swaps self to Iron Colossus (alt form) for 1 turn unless already locked. Becomes AoE permanently after Iron Colossus; base doubled to 40 permanently after Ultra Railgun.
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 shield per Overcharge stack (permanent ramp); x2 base if Ultra Railgun mark active; doubled base permanently after Ultra Railgun commit

abilities.name: Railgun
abilities.effects_summary: 25 Normal damage to one enemy. Bypasses invulnerability, cannot be countered or reflected. x2 (50) while marked by Ultra Railgun. Base damage permanently increased +5 per Overcharge stack. After use, swaps self to Ultra Railgun (alt form) for 1 turn unless locked. Note: JSON lists 20; .gd ground truth is 25.
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 base damage per Overcharge stack (permanent, unbounded ramp); x2 if Ultra Railgun mark active; doubled base permanently after Ultra Railgun commit

abilities.name: Overcharge
abilities.effects_summary: For 1 turn (dur 2), each time Misaka takes NEW damage she gains a permanent (dur -1) stack: +5 Railgun damage AND +5 Iron Sand shield. 2 stacks per trigger after Ultra Railgun committed. Applies the trigger to the whole team after Iron Colossus committed. Triggers can stack multiple times within the turn if hit repeatedly.
abilities.conditional_scaling: scales with incoming hits taken during the window; permanent per-stack ramp; double rate after Ultra Railgun

abilities.name: Electric Deflection
abilities.effects_summary: Misaka becomes invulnerable for 1 turn (default_defend). Long 4-turn cooldown panic button / self-protection.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

abilities.name: Iron Colossus
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden alt form of Iron Sand (available 1 turn after Iron Sand is used). Makes the entire team invulnerable for 1 turn (invuln dur 2). PERMANENTLY converts Iron Sand and Railgun (and Overcharge) to hit ALL valid targets. Removes all her ability-swap effects and applies a permanent lockout mark preventing any future form switching.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (commitment effect — converts kit to AoE for rest of game)

abilities.name: Ultra Railgun
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden alt form of Railgun (available 1 turn after Railgun used). Deals 40 Normal damage to one enemy, Bypasses invulnerability, uncounterable/unreflectable. PERMANENTLY doubles the base effects of Iron Sand and Railgun (25->50 dmg, 20->40 shield base) but adds +1 random energy to each cost. Removes her swap effects and applies permanent lockout preventing future switching.
abilities.conditional_scaling: fixed 40 on cast; commitment effect doubles base of Iron Sand/Railgun for rest of game

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Unbounded via Overcharge: Railgun base = 25 + 5*N (N = total damage-instances absorbed across all Overcharge windows, doubled rate after Ultra Railgun). With Ultra Railgun mark doubling on top, a ramped Railgun hits (25+5N)*2. Practical mid-game peak ~90 in one turn (ramped Railgun ~50 + Ultra Railgun 40, or doubled-base 50 Railgun + 40 Ultra). Theoretical ceiling grows each turn she is hit while Overcharge is active.
damage_profile.notes: All her damage is Normal but flagged Bypassing+Uncounterable, so it ignores invulnerability and reflect/counter (still subject to standard DR/shields since it is Normal, not Piercing/True). Peak single-target counts a swap-window turn: use Railgun (25, swaps to Ultra), or once Ultra is available cast Ultra Railgun 40 + a ramped/doubled regular Railgun. Sustained per-turn damage is just one Railgun cast (25 base, scaling with ramp). No DoT in kit.

economy.color_dependency: Light: visible kit is Blue:1 (Iron Sand) + White:1 (Railgun) + Random:1 (Overcharge) + Random:1 (Electric Deflection) = 4 pips, only 2 color-locked (1 Blue, 1 White). Transformations (Iron Colossus / Ultra Railgun) cost Blue:1+White:1 each. After Ultra Railgun commit, Iron Sand & Railgun each gain +1 random pip.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent — Iron Sand, Railgun, and the transformations are all 0 cooldown (spammable every turn); Overcharge cd 1; only Electric Deflection is gated at cd 4.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate-to-high for damage ceiling: needs Overcharge stacks (built by absorbing damage) to scale, and benefits from committing to Ultra Railgun. Baseline kit is fully functional un-ramped (1-cost 25 bypass nuke + 1-cost 20 shield every turn).

invuln_or_counter: Electric Deflection: self-invuln 1 turn (cd 4)
Iron Colossus: team-wide invuln 1 turn
Railgun/Ultra Railgun pierce invulnerability on offense

win_conditions: Grind down a single key target with un-counterable, invuln-piercing Railgun/Ultra Railgun damage that no defensive cooldown can stop
Snowball Overcharge by tanking hits, permanently inflating Railgun damage and Iron Sand shields, then commit to a transformation to lock in the advantage
Stall/protect with rotating invulnerability (self every 4 turns, whole team once via Iron Colossus) to outlast burst and reach ramp
Late-game pivot: Iron Colossus to flip the entire kit to AoE (team shields + AoE Railgun) for board control, or Ultra Railgun to double her single-target output
internal_synergies: Overcharge + being focused: incoming damage is converted into permanent Railgun/Iron Sand scaling, so she is rewarded for tanking
Electric Deflection / Iron Colossus invuln keeps her alive long enough for Overcharge stacks to matter
Railgun's free swap to Ultra Railgun each turn, plus the Ultra Railgun mark, lets the standard Railgun and Iron Sand double their effect in the combo window
Ultra Railgun commit doubles Iron Sand/Railgun base AND Overcharge grants 2 stacks/trigger — ramp and base-doubling compound
Iron Colossus makes Overcharge apply team-wide and Iron Sand/Railgun AoE, turning a solo carry into a team buffer/AoE threat
strengths: Bypassing + Uncounterable damage cleanly ignores invulnerability, counters, and reflects — extremely reliable against defensive/counter compositions
Outstanding tempo: 1-cost, 0-cooldown nuke and 1-cost, 0-cooldown shield usable every single turn
Cheap, mostly-flexible cost (only 2 color-locked pips in the visible kit)
Permanent, theoretically unbounded damage/shield ramp via Overcharge that converts enemy aggression into power
Two layers of invulnerability (self on cd 4, team-wide once) for survivability and tempo denial
Flexible late-game identity via two distinct transformation paths (AoE conversion or double-power)
weaknesses: Damage is type Normal — still mitigated by flat/% DR and shields (only invuln/counter are bypassed), so high-DR or shield-stacking foes blunt her
No CC, no healing, no cleanse, no energy denial — purely a damage/shield/invuln package with limited disruption
Overcharge ramp requires her to actually take damage; against avoidance or if she is ignored she scales slowly, and Overcharge windows are short (1 turn each)
Transformations are one-way commitments that permanently lock out all further switching, so a mistimed choice is irreversible
Ultra Railgun's permanent +1 random cost on Iron Sand/Railgun raises her per-turn energy load after committing
Modest un-ramped baseline numbers (25 / 20) — needs setup or commitment to reach high output

power_assessment.reasoning: A very well-rounded, high-floor carry. The combination of cheap (1-cost) 0-cooldown abilities, invulnerability/counter-piercing damage, a permanent scaling engine, and two layers of invuln makes her flexible and hard to shut down defensively. Her bypassing/uncounterable tag is a strong meta tool against defensive comps. She is held back from top tier by Normal damage type (still eaten by DR/shields), zero CC/control, ramp that is conditional on absorbing damage in short windows, and irreversible transformation commitments. Strong, reliable, but not a runaway outlier in isolation.
outlier_flags: JSON metadata understates Railgun base (20) vs .gd ground truth (25); descriptions are stale, used .gd values
Overcharge ramp is permanent (dur -1) and per-stack with no visible cap — potential unbounded scaling outlier if she can repeatedly tank hits during the window
All offensive damage ignores invulnerability AND cannot be countered/reflected — unusually strong defensive-counterplay denial

role: single-target/AoE blind-execute assassin with team evasion and counter support
signature_mechanic: Unexpected Beheading (passive): any damage Muichiro deals to a Blinded enemy is banked as invisible stacks instead of HP loss; when stacks >= the target's CURRENT HP they are instantly executed. His own kit blinds (muichiro1) and pumps Piercing damage (muichiro1 20 + muichiro5 10+30 DoT) into the same target, and allies can feed stacks too via the Fourth Form mark.

abilities.name: Third Form: Scattering Mist Splash
abilities.conditional_scaling: Blind duration scales: 2 turns (dur 4) base, +1 turn (dur 6) if target already Blinded. JSON 'AoE/3-stack/15' description is stale.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Piercing to one enemy + applies Blind (1 turn, longer if already Blinded). Blind both reduces enemy accuracy AND is the precondition for converting his damage into Unexpected Beheading execute stacks. Core combo enabler.

abilities.name: Fourth Form: Shifting Flow Slash
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Invisible counter on an ally or self for 1 turn: first enemy to use a Harmful skill on the protected character is countered (negated), then Blinded (1 turn) and Marked. The Mark makes damage dealt to that enemy count as dealt by Muichiro, so teammates can feed Unexpected Beheading stacks. Counter + protect + setup.

abilities.name: Seventh Form: Obscuring Clouds
abilities.conditional_scaling: Team dodge chance starts 5%, increases +5% each turn for 4 turns (5/10/15/20%); DOUBLED against attackers that are Blinded. muichiro5's mark doubles Tokito's own dodge from this further.
abilities.effects_summary: AoE team buff: growing dodge/evasion for the whole team for 4 turns, scaling per turn and doubled vs Blinded enemies. Also swaps slot 4 (Sixth Form) into Fifth Form: Sea of Clouds and Haze; ends if Tokito dies. cd0 = spammable team evasion engine.

abilities.name: Sixth Form: Lunar Dispersing Mist
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self Invulnerable for 1 turn (default_defend panic button). Long 5-turn cooldown. This slot is replaced by Fifth Form (muichiro5) after muichiro3 is cast.

abilities.name: Fifth Form: Sea of Clouds and Haze
abilities.conditional_scaling: DoT: 10 Piercing immediate to all enemies + 10 Piercing/turn for 3 turns (dur 5). vs Blinded targets all of this banks as Unexpected Beheading execute stacks (bypasses healing/shields entirely).
abilities.effects_summary: AoE Piercing nuke + 3-turn AoE Piercing DoT to all enemies; self-mark that doubles Tokito's Seventh Form dodge. Hidden alt swapped into slot 4 by muichiro3. His AoE pressure + execute-fuel against a blinded team.

abilities.name: Unexpected Beheading
abilities.conditional_scaling: Stacks equal the raw damage value that would have been dealt to a Blinded target; execute fires when accumulated stacks >= the target's CURRENT HP. Effectively unbounded scaling that strengthens as enemies are damaged/lowered by any source.
abilities.effects_summary: Passive: damage Muichiro deals to a Blinded enemy is converted into invisible, stackable Unexpected Beheading marks instead of HP loss (engine: receive_ability_damage / receive_effect_damage -> receive_beheading). When stacks >= current HP -> instant kill, bypassing barriers/shields/healing. Also triggers for damage dealt by allies to a Fourth-Form-marked target.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Unbounded via execute: banked Beheading stacks ignore healing/shields and kill once they reach the target's CURRENT HP, so the more the target (or anyone) erodes HP, the easier the execute. A realistic full combo on one blinded target: muichiro1 20 + muichiro5 10 hit + 10x3 DoT = 60 banked stacks over ~4 turns, plus ally contributions via the Fourth Form mark, then instant kill regardless of remaining shields/heals.
damage_profile.notes: Raw hit numbers are low (20 single / 10 AoE per Piercing tick). All real damage is Piercing (skips flat+%DR) and, against Blinded targets, becomes True-effect execute fuel that bypasses shields/barriers/heals. Damage profile is execute-pressure, not burst.

economy.color_dependency: Heavy Blue/White (his colors are [Blue, White]). Visible bar wants 2 Blue + 2 White + 1 Random across the four slots (m1 Blue, m2 White, m3 Blue+White, m4 Random); m5 post-swap adds Blue+Random. Dual-color but well within identity; cheap per-ability (1-2 pips).
economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent. m3 is cd0 (spam team dodge / set up the swap), m1 cd1 (re-blind almost every turn), m2 cd2. Only m4 (cd5) and m5 (cd3) are slow. He can blind+feed nearly every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate. Execute payoff ramps over turns as Beheading stacks accumulate and target HP drops; Seventh Form dodge ramps +5%/turn. Not a hard transformation gate, but he wants 3-4 turns to convert setup into kills.

soft_cc: Blind (accuracy denial) on muichiro1 and via muichiro2 counter
invuln_or_counter: Self Invulnerable 1 turn (muichiro4)
Counter first Harmful skill on ally/self for 1 turn: negate + Blind + Mark the attacker (muichiro2)

internal_synergies: muichiro1 Blind is the gate for muichiro6: once a target is Blinded, ALL of Muichiro's Piercing damage (m1 hit, m5 hit + DoT) converts to Unexpected Beheading execute stacks instead of HP.
muichiro5's per-turn AoE Piercing DoT continuously banks stacks on every Blinded enemy, turning a team-wide blind into a team-wide execute clock.
muichiro2's counter Blinds AND Marks the attacker, so the punished enemy both feeds execute stacks and lets allies' damage count as Muichiro's (allied feeding into the passive).
muichiro3 doubles team dodge vs Blinded attackers - the same Blind that enables executes also makes the whole team evasive against those enemies, and m3 unlocks m5 (the AoE DoT engine).
muichiro5's self-mark doubles Muichiro's own Seventh Form dodge, stacking his personal survivability while he ramps.
strengths: Execute that bypasses healing, shields, and barriers - banked Beheading stacks ignore all mitigation and kill at current HP, hard-countering tanks, sustain, and overheal comps.
All damage is Piercing (skips flat + % DR), so even his non-execute pressure is hard to mitigate.
Strong, low-cost team support: cd0 ramping team-wide dodge (m3), a counter that negates+blinds+marks an enemy (m2), and a self-invuln panic button (m4).
Excellent tempo and cheap costs - re-blinds almost every turn (m1 cd1) and can keep the dodge engine up perpetually.
AoE execute potential: m5's team-wide Piercing DoT banks stacks on every blinded enemy simultaneously, so a wide blind can snowball into multiple kills.
weaknesses: Very low raw damage (20 single / 10 AoE ticks) - if he cannot Blind or the target shrugs off Blind, the passive does nothing and he is a weak chip-dealer.
Hard dependency on the Blind condition: blind immunity, cleanse, or 'shrug off Blind' (blind_check) completely neutralizes his win condition.
Slow kill clock vs high-HP targets - executes only fire when stacks reach CURRENT HP, so against full-HP bricks he needs many turns or external HP erosion.
No healing, no shields, no hard CC, no energy denial - purely Blind + evasion + execute; squishier than dedicated tanks/supports.
Dodge defense is RNG and can fail; m4 invuln is on a long 5-turn cooldown, so a focused burst between cooldowns can drop him before stacks pay off.
Slot-swap quirk: must cast m3 to access m5 (his main damage), so the AoE DoT isn't available turn 1.
win_conditions: Blind one or more enemies, then pile Muichiro's Piercing damage (and m5's DoT, plus marked-target ally damage) into Unexpected Beheading stacks until they exceed current HP for unmitigatable executes.
Use the team-wide ramping dodge + counter + self-invuln to outlast burst while the execute clock ticks, especially against shield/heal-reliant comps that his stacks ignore.
Against multi-target comps, spread Blind + m5's AoE DoT to set up simultaneous executes across the enemy team.

power_assessment.reasoning: A specialist with a genuinely powerful, mitigation-proof win condition (execute that ignores heal/shield/barrier and uses Piercing chip), wrapped in a cheap, high-tempo support shell (cd0 ramping team dodge, counter, self-invuln). Ceiling is high against tank/sustain/overheal comps where most damage dealers struggle. Floor is meaningfully lower: raw damage is tiny, everything hinges on landing and keeping Blind, and the execute is slow against full-HP bricks or anyone with blind immunity/cleanse. The blend of a hard counter-archetype niche plus solid team utility lands him clearly above average but short of a top-tier generalist; conditional and team-dependent enough to keep him at 7.
outlier_flags: Execute bypasses ALL mitigation (heal/shield/barrier) - a hard counter to entire defensive archetypes; potential balance outlier vs sustain comps.
JSON metadata is badly stale for muichiro1 (says AoE team / 3-stack / 15 dmg; actual is single-target 20 Piercing + Blind) - flagged for data cleanup; split_desc + .gd are ground truth.
Passive can be fed by ALLIES via the Fourth Form mark and counter (cross-character execute attribution) - synergy that can spike his effective power in coordinated teams beyond his solo numbers.

role: single-target anti-healing assassin / support-denial controller
signature_mechanic: Grisly Wing's "mark" gates the rest of the kit: marked targets get permanent heal-immunity from Crimson Lightning and a longer (2-turn) banish from Disintegrate's Helpful-skill counter. Win path is mark-then-punish: shut off a key healer/support's sustain and out-DPS them.

abilities.name: Grisly Wing
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat). Damage repeats: 10 Piercing on cast + 10 Piercing/turn DoT for 2 displayed turns (~30 total over mark lifetime)
abilities.effects_summary: 10 Piercing immediate (heals Myotismon 10 via ability.health_drain) + applies a 10 Piercing/turn damage-over-time effect for 2 turns (DoT does NOT heal him - its own health_drain flag is unset) + applies Grisly Wing MARK for 3 turns. The mark enables myotismon2/myotismon3 bonuses.

abilities.name: Crimson Lightning
abilities.conditional_scaling: on-mark rider: no extra damage, but if target marked by Grisly Wing it applies PERMANENT ignore-healing (heal immunity, duration -1)
abilities.effects_summary: 40 Normal damage (.gd base_damage=40; JSON says 35 - .gd is ground truth at 40). If target is marked by Grisly Wing, applies a permanent Ignore-Healing effect (target can no longer be healed for the rest of the match). Primary burst + the kit's hard anti-heal payoff.

abilities.name: Disintegrate
abilities.conditional_scaling: on-mark: banish duration 1 turn -> 2 turns if target marked by Grisly Wing
abilities.effects_summary: No damage. Places an invisible 1-turn conditional COUNTER on the target keyed to the 'Helpful' class: if the target uses a NEW Helpful skill that turn it is countered (skill fails) and the target is banished for 1 turn (2 turns if marked by Grisly Wing). Anti-support/anti-buff tech and a soft removal/tempo tool; only triggers if the enemy actually casts a Helpful skill.

abilities.name: Myotismon Protect
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self Invulnerable for 1 turn (default_defend -> invuln_effect dur 2 = 1 displayed turn). Panic button / damage-avoidance on a long 4-turn cooldown.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Flat, no real scaling. Crimson Lightning 40 (Normal) is the burst ceiling; a Crimson Lightning turn while a prior Grisly Wing DoT ticks reaches ~50. Grisly Wing total over its lifetime is ~30 Piercing (10 cast + 10 + 10 DoT). No per-stack/per-kill growth - the 'payoff' is utility (heal-lock + banish), not damage scaling.
damage_profile.notes: Single-target only, no AoE anywhere. Grisly Wing damage is doubled-up vs its JSON text: it deals an immediate 10 Piercing AND a 10/turn Piercing DoT for 2 turns, but only the immediate 10 lifesteals (the DoT effect's health_drain flag is never set). Crimson Lightning is 40 in the .gd vs 35 in JSON - .gd ground truth = 40. Piercing skips flat+%DR so Grisly Wing damage is reliable into tanks; Crimson Lightning is Normal and fully mitigable by DR/shields/barriers.

economy.color_dependency: Heavy on Red (slots 1-2) and White (slots 2-3); identity colors [White, Red]. Crimson Lightning needs both White+Red. Only Protect is flexible (1 Random). Two-color dependent but cheap.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast: two 1-cooldown spam abilities (Grisly Wing, Crimson Lightning) form a near-every-turn rotation; Disintegrate cd2 utility; Protect cd4 defensive. Very high uptime on the core damage/mark loop.
economy.ramp_dependency: None - no stacking/ramp. Effective from turn 1; only 'ramp' is the one-turn setup of applying the mark before Crimson Lightning/Disintegrate land their bonus.

hard_cc: banish (1 turn, 2 if marked, conditional on enemy casting a Helpful skill)
soft_cc: mark (enables payoffs)
invuln_or_counter: self invulnerability 1 turn (cd4)
conditional counter on enemy Helpful skills (Disintegrate)

internal_synergies: Grisly Wing mark is the linchpin: it upgrades Crimson Lightning into a permanent heal-lock and Disintegrate's banish from 1 to 2 turns.
Grisly Wing cd1 + mark dur 3 turns means the mark stays up nearly permanently, so the marked-target bonuses are reliably online.
Self-lifesteal (Grisly Wing immediate) + self-invuln (Protect) give modest self-sustain/survivability to out-attrition a heal-locked target.
Crimson Lightning heal-immunity + chip DoT is an attrition engine: once a key enemy can't be healed, frequent small damage and DoT grind them down.
strengths: Best-in-slot anti-heal: Crimson Lightning's permanent ignore-healing hard-counters healer/sustain/regen comps and lifesteal bruisers.
Cheap, fast rotation - two 1-cooldown abilities, total 5-pip visible kit, no ramp needed.
Piercing DoT + Piercing chip ignores flat and % damage reduction, so it stays relevant into tanks.
Strong anti-support tech: Disintegrate counters and banishes enemies trying to buff/cleanse/heal via Helpful skills (mark extends the banish).
Self-sustain (lifesteal) plus a 1-turn invuln panic button for survivability.
weaknesses: Entirely single-target with no AoE - poor in multi-target / swarm situations and weak teamfight presence.
Low raw burst ceiling (~40-50 in a turn); cannot quickly delete high-HP threats, relies on attrition.
Disintegrate is purely reactive - whiffs entirely if the enemy doesn't cast a Helpful skill that turn; dead weight vs non-support targets.
Heavy two-color (White+Red) dependency on the core combo (Crimson Lightning needs both); awkward in off-color energy droughts.
Anti-heal/anti-support value is heavily matchup-dependent - vs comps with no healing or buffs, half the kit does little, leaving only modest chip damage.
No team support, no ally shields, no energy denial - a purely selfish single-target duelist.
win_conditions: Mark and heal-lock the enemy's primary healer/sustain carry, then grind the team down through attrition once they can't recover.
Use Disintegrate to deny and banish enemy support plays (heals/buffs/cleanses), creating tempo windows.
Out-duel a single priority target with lifesteal + DoT + invuln, especially after stripping their healing.

power_assessment.reasoning: A focused, well-costed single-target specialist that is excellent in its niche (anti-heal / anti-support) but mediocre as a generalist. The kit is cheap (5 pips), low-cooldown, and reliable thanks to Piercing and a near-permanent mark, and permanent ignore-healing is a genuinely powerful, swingy effect against sustain comps. But raw output is low (peak ~40-50/turn, ~30 over a Grisly Wing lifetime, no AoE), Disintegrate is conditional/reactive, and a large chunk of the kit's value evaporates against comps with no healing or buffs. Solid B-tier duelist/tech pick: high ceiling into the right matchup, low floor into the wrong one. Rated in isolation; cross-roster anti-heal demand will shift this either way.
outlier_flags: JSON vs .gd damage mismatch: Crimson Lightning is 40 in myotismon2.gd but 35 in the metadata/JSON - .gd (40) is ground truth.
Grisly Wing applies BOTH an immediate 10 Piercing AND a separate 10/turn Piercing DoT for 2 turns (~30 total), not the single 10 the JSON implies.

split_desc claims Myotismon 'heals for any damage dealt by this skill,' but only the immediate hit lifesteals - the DoT effect's health_drain flag is never set, so DoT ticks do not heal him (likely a bug or stale description).
Permanent (duration -1) ignore-healing is an unusually strong, irreversible debuff - high balance-impact effect for a 2-pip ability.

role: single-target affliction assassin with silence-lock and self-protection (counter/invuln)
signature_mechanic: Killing Intent: a cheap (1 random, CD1) Affliction DoT + Silence that is repeatedly buffed — Bloody Knife adds lifesteal and +5 damage, Friendly Smile stacks extend its duration by a turn each, letting Nagisa permanently silence-lock a single target while draining health through barriers.

abilities.name: Killing Intent
abilities.conditional_scaling: Immediate 10 Affliction hit PLUS an Affliction DoT of 10/turn. Base DoT/Silence duration = 3 (ticks ~1 enemy turn); each consumed Friendly Smile stack adds +2 duration (one extra turn of DoT+Silence per stack). When marked by Bloody Knife: the hit deals +5 and both the immediate damage and the DoT gain health_drain (lifesteal).
abilities.effects_summary: 10 immediate Affliction (bypasses barriers/shields/DR) + 10/turn Affliction DoT + Silence, both ~1 turn base, extended by Friendly Smile stacks; lifesteals while Bloody-Knife-marked; consumes and is empowered by Friendly Smile stacks.

abilities.name: Bloody Knife
abilities.conditional_scaling: none on the hit itself; enables Killing Intent lifesteal + Killing Intent +5 damage for ~2 turns (mark dur 5 / damage_mod dur 5 on self).
abilities.effects_summary: 25 Physical (skips flat+%DR) burst; applies self-mark 'Killing Intent will steal HP' and a damage_mod giving +5 to Killing Intent for ~2 turns. The setup/empower button.

abilities.name: Don't Test Me
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: For ~1 turn ignores ALL incoming damage and all harmful (non-damage) effects (full harmful invuln). Counter trigger: any character who uses a Harmful skill on Nagisa during this window is Silenced for ~2 turns. Long CD5 anti-burst/anti-focus panic button with punish.

abilities.name: Friendly Smile
abilities.conditional_scaling: stackable: each cast adds 1 stack that extends the next Killing Intent's DoT+Silence by 1 turn (consumed on next Killing Intent).
abilities.effects_summary: Invulnerable for 1 turn (default_defend) + stacking self-mark that lengthens the next Killing Intent's DoT/Silence. Dual purpose: survival cooldown and ramp for the silence-lock.

abilities.name: Natural Assassin
abilities.conditional_scaling: flat -5 damage taken from Silenced attackers (permanent, duration -1).
abilities.effects_summary: Passive permanent 5 flat damage reduction from Silenced characters. Synergizes with his own kit, which silences targets, turning his control into defensive value.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No burst ceiling growth — single action per turn caps a turn at Bloody Knife's 25 Physical or a Bloody-Knife-buffed Killing Intent (15 immediate + lifesteal). The real ceiling is DURATION: Friendly Smile stacks each add a full turn to Killing Intent's Affliction DoT (10, or 15 with Bloody Knife) AND its Silence.
