Stacking 2-3 Friendly Smiles before a Killing Intent yields a 3-4 turn unbreakable Affliction DoT + Silence lock on one target, all lifestealing through barriers. Total damage scales with lock length, not per-hit numbers.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is single-target. Affliction DoT bypasses barriers/shields/DR; Bloody Knife's 25 is Physical (skips flat+%DR). 'Sustained 15/turn' assumes Killing Intent DoT (10) +5 from active Bloody Knife buff; 10/turn without the knife buff. Health drain converts that DoT into self-healing.

economy.color_dependency: Moderate Blue/White dependency. Visible kit needs Blue x2 (Bloody Knife, Don't Test Me) and White x1 (Don't Test Me); core loop (Killing Intent + Friendly Smile) is all random pips, so the silence-lock engine itself is nearly color-agnostic. Don't Test Me is the only ability gated on the harder Blue+White combo.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast core: Killing Intent CD1 (spam every turn), Friendly Smile CD3, Bloody Knife CD2 — the offensive/ramp loop has almost no downtime. Defensive Don't Test Me is the only long cooldown (CD5).
economy.ramp_dependency: Medium. Functional turn 1 (Killing Intent alone is a self-sufficient DoT+Silence), but reaches full power only after layering Bloody Knife (lifesteal/+5) and stacking Friendly Smile for extended locks. Reward scales smoothly rather than requiring a hard transformation.

hard_cc: Silence (1 turn base, extendable to 3-4+ turns via Friendly Smile stacks; repeatable every turn via CD1 Killing Intent)
invuln_or_counter: Friendly Smile: Invulnerable 1 turn (CD3)
Don't Test Me: ignore all damage + all harmful effects 1 turn AND silence any harmful attacker for 2 turns (CD5)

win_conditions: Pin and silence-lock a key enemy (healer/control/carry) indefinitely with chained Killing Intent + Friendly Smile stacks, removing them from the game while chipping with Affliction DoT.
Outlast focus-fire using Friendly Smile invuln (CD3) and Don't Test Me (full harmful invuln + counter-silence) to survive while the lock and lifesteal grind the enemy down.
Self-sustain to attrition victory: lifesteal Affliction DoT through barriers keeps Nagisa topped up while he denies an enemy's actions.
internal_synergies: Bloody Knife -> Killing Intent: enables lifesteal and +5 on the CD1 DoT, turning chip into sustain.
Friendly Smile -> Killing Intent: each stack extends the DoT+Silence by a turn; stack up, then unleash a multi-turn lock.
Friendly Smile also = invuln, so ramping the lock and surviving are the same button.
Natural Assassin passive feeds off his own kit: every target he Silences deals 5 less to him, converting his primary control into layered defense.
Don't Test Me's counter Silence also triggers Natural Assassin's DR against the punished attacker.
strengths: Best-in-class single-target silence-lock: CD1 reapplication + stackable duration extension can fully disable one enemy for many turns.
Two strong, on-demand defensive layers on short/medium cooldowns (invuln CD3, full harmful-invuln + counter CD5) make him extremely hard to kill or focus.
Affliction DoT bypasses all barriers/shields/DR; Bloody Knife is Physical (skips flat+%DR) — his damage ignores most mitigation.
Lifesteal gives self-sustain without needing a healer.
Cheap, mostly-random core loop with near-zero downtime; passive DR scales off his own control.
Counter-silence punishes anyone who tries to interrupt him.
weaknesses: Zero AoE — completely single-target; can only meaningfully control/kill one enemy at a time, weak into wide teams or swarms.
Low raw damage numbers (10/25 base); kills come slowly through DoT duration, not burst — poor at racing or finishing.
Silence-lock ceiling requires setup turns (stacking Friendly Smile) and a target that doesn't cleanse/dodge; cleanse or invuln on the enemy unwinds his whole plan.
Don't Test Me's counter only fires on Harmful skills and is a long CD5; non-harmful disruption or simply ignoring him bypasses it.
Lifesteal/DR are conditional (need Bloody Knife active / enemy Silenced) — without the loop running he is a fragile, low-damage chipper.
No team support, shields, or cleanse for allies — purely selfish kit.

power_assessment.reasoning: A specialist single-target lockdown/sustain character with an unusually clean, low-downtime engine. The combination of a CD1 repeatable Silence, stackable duration extension, barrier-piercing Affliction, lifesteal, and two reliable defensive cooldowns makes him a frustrating, durable threat that can effectively delete one priority enemy (healer/control) from a match. He rates above-average in 1v1 or focus scenarios. He's held back from top tier by total lack of AoE, low raw/burst damage (wins are slow), reliance on multi-turn setup for the big locks, and full vulnerability to cleanse/dodge/non-harmful counters. Strong, swingy specialist rather than an all-rounder.
outlier_flags: CD1 hard-CC (Silence) reapplied every turn is unusually low for a control effect and is the main balance pressure point.
Friendly Smile stacking has no visible cap on extension duration in the .gd, so a long ramp could produce an extremely long silence-lock (multi-turn near-permanent disable on one target).
Killing Intent applies BOTH an immediate 10 Affliction hit AND a 10 Affliction DoT, effectively double-dipping on a 1-cost CD1 ability.
Don't Test Me grants total immunity to both damage and all harmful effects for a turn plus a 2-turn counter-silence for only a 2-pip cost (CD5).

role: single-target disruptor/bruiser with self-sustain and an invuln panic button
signature_mechanic: Two reliable single-target damage strikes paired with disruption (energy-cost tax on Toad Kumite, non-Strategic skill stun on Rasenshuriken), backed by a self-heal + energy-gen that locks itself until he uses a damage skill, and a 1-turn invuln defend. JSON descriptions advertise Shadow Clone stacking, a 45-HP transformation, and alt-ability swaps, but the live .gd code implements NONE of that — the actual kit is flat-value and much simpler.

abilities.name: Toad Kumite
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (live code is flat 35; JSON 'Shadow Clone stack' scaling and custom_behavior=25 are stale/legacy bot hints, not executed)
abilities.effects_summary: 35 Normal damage to one enemy + applies cost_mod_effect(+1 Random) to the target's skills for 2 turns (dur 4 enemy-facing). Consumes the self 'Sage Chakra Gather' mark if present (unlocking naruto3). Low 1-turn cooldown spammable energy-tax.

abilities.name: Rasenshuriken
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (live code is flat 40; describe()/split_desc/custom_behavior=50 stacking text is stale, not executed)
abilities.effects_summary: 40 Normal damage to one enemy + stun_effect targeting all non-Strategic skills for 1 turn (dur 2 enemy-facing, excludes Strategic). Strong soft-lock: target can still use Strategic skills but loses offense/most actions for a turn. Consumes the 'Sage Chakra Gather' mark if present.

abilities.name: Sage Chakra Gather
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self: heals 25 HP and gains 1 bonus Green energy. Gated by extra_usable: cannot be used while marked by 'Sage Chakra Gather' (self-lock) — must use Toad Kumite or Rasenshuriken to consume that mark before reusing. Net result: sustain + ramp toward his Green-heavy damage skills, on a soft once-per-damage-cycle cadence.

abilities.name: Naruto Block
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self: invuln_effect for 1 turn (dur 2) via default_defend — full invulnerability, blocks all damage/effects for the turn. The describe() text about a 45-HP auto-trigger, removing all enemy effects, and swapping Uzumaki Barrage/Rasengan to alternate abilities is STALE and NOT implemented; live code is a plain 1-turn defend on a 4-turn cooldown.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No real scaling in live code. Per-turn output is one strike: 40 (Rasenshuriken, every other turn) or 35 (Toad Kumite, every turn). Over a 2-turn window he does ~75 single-target (40 + 35). No DoT, no AoE, no stacking despite stale JSON claims.
damage_profile.notes: Flat-value bruiser. Rasenshuriken (40) is the hardest single hit; Toad Kumite (35) is the low-CD filler. Both Normal damage, fully blocked by barriers/shields/DR. Effective damage drops sharply vs tanky/DR targets since nothing pierces.

economy.color_dependency: Green-centric (Green appears in both damage skills: naruto1 Green+White, naruto2 Green+Blue), plus one White and one Blue. Sage Chakra Gather refunds 1 Green, partially self-financing his Green dependence. Moderate color dependency across 3 colors (Green/Blue/White) matching character_colors [0,1,2].
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast. Toad Kumite CD1 (near-spammable), Rasenshuriken CD2, Sage Chakra Gather CD2 (further soft-gated by self-mark), Naruto Block CD4. He can act with a damage skill nearly every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low. Sage Chakra Gather provides minor energy ramp (+1 Green) and sustain but no power ramp; kit is flat from turn 1.

soft_cc: Rasenshuriken: stuns all non-Strategic skills for 1 turn (target can still use Strategic skills)
invuln_or_counter: Naruto Block: 1-turn full invulnerability (self, CD4)

win_conditions: Grind down a single priority target with reliable 35-40 strikes while taxing/stunning it to deny counterplay
Outlast opposing burst via Naruto Block invuln + Sage Chakra Gather self-heal, winning attrition
Lock down an enemy carry's offense each cycle (Rasenshuriken stun + Toad Kumite cost tax) so allies can clean up
internal_synergies: Sage Chakra Gather refunds 1 Green, directly funding the Green pip in both Toad Kumite and Rasenshuriken, and the self-lock is cleared by using either damage skill — creating a natural heal -> strike -> heal cadence
Toad Kumite's +1 Random cost tax and Rasenshuriken's non-Strategic stun stack as a tempo-denial combo to soft-lock a single threat (tax their economy, then deny their actions)
Naruto Block (1-turn invuln) buys a turn to outlast burst while Sage Chakra Gather sustains him back up
strengths: Cheap, low-cooldown reliable single-target damage (35 on CD1, 40 on CD2) with no setup
Built-in disruption on both damage skills: energy cost tax (Toad Kumite) and non-Strategic stun (Rasenshuriken)
Self-sufficient: heals 25 HP + refunds Green energy, partially self-financing his color needs
1-turn full invuln as a panic button against burst
Low ramp dependency — fully online turn 1
weaknesses: No AoE whatsoever — purely single-target, weak into wide/multi-threat comps
All damage is Normal type — fully stopped by barriers, shields, and DR; no piercing/affliction/true damage for effective damage
No hard CC (no full stun/lock); Rasenshuriken stun leaves Strategic skills usable and is only 1 turn
No cleanse, no team support, no shields for allies — entirely selfish kit
Flat damage ceiling (~40/turn) that doesn't scale; falls off against high-HP/high-DR targets
Sage Chakra Gather self-locks until a damage skill is used, slightly throttling sustain cadence

power_assessment.reasoning: A clean, self-contained single-target bruiser: reliable flat damage (35 CD1 / 40 CD2), per-strike disruption (cost tax + non-Strategic stun), self-heal + energy refund, and a 1-turn invuln. Everything is honest and online from turn 1, making him a solid, low-variance pick — but nothing is exceptional. Damage is all Normal (no piercing/affliction), so DR and barriers gut his effective output; he has zero AoE and zero team utility; his CC is soft and short. He is a middle-of-the-roster value bruiser: dependable but capped, with no win-more scaling or game-breaking tool. Rated 5/10 in isolation.
outlier_flags: JSON/describe() text is heavily STALE — advertises Shadow Clone stacking (+5/stack), a 45-HP auto-trigger transformation, removal of all enemy effects, alt-ability swaps (Uzumaki Barrage/Rasengan), and instant-cast Rasengan; NONE of this exists in the live .gd execute code, which is flat-value and only 4 abilities (no hidden slot 5+ alts).
metadata cooldowns and bot-hint custom_behavior damage values (25, 50) do not match true execute damage (35, 40).

role: Single-target Affliction bruiser/duelist with self-cleanse and ramping fire stacks
signature_mechanic: "I'm all fired up!" ramp: every time Natsu deals new Affliction damage OR is hit by a new harmful Strategic skill, he gains a stacking +5 Affliction damage to ALL his skills. Stacks compound because his own kit deals Affliction every turn, and his cleanse (Consume Flame) grants extra stacks per harmful effect removed.

abilities.name: Fire Dragon's Iron Fist
abilities.conditional_scaling: The 10 Affliction portion scales +5 per I'm all fired up! stack, and dealing it triggers a new fired-up stack
abilities.effects_summary: Damage spam: 10 Normal + 10 Affliction to one enemy (GROUND TRUTH per .gd and split_desc; describe()/JSON stale at 15/5). No cost beyond 1 Red, no cooldown, repeatable every turn and feeds the ramp each cast.

abilities.name: Fire Dragon's Wing Attack
abilities.conditional_scaling: If the marked target does NOT use a new skill, the whole enemy team takes 15 Normal + 5 Affliction (the 5 Affliction scales with fired-up stacks). Lose-lose pressure.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Normal to one enemy + a delay effect: for 1 turn, if the target uses a NEW skill it is delayed 2 turns (soft tempo denial). If they refrain, on wrapup Natsu deals 15 Normal + 5 Affliction to the ENTIRE enemy team (conditional AoE).

abilities.name: Fire Dragon's Roar
abilities.conditional_scaling: 35 Affliction scales +5 per fired-up stack and triggers another stack. Self-discounts: for ~1 turn after first cast it costs only 1 Random and deals 15 Affliction but can ONLY hit the previously-marked target (cheap finisher).
abilities.effects_summary: Premier nuke: 35 Affliction (bypasses all DR/shields/barriers) to one enemy. Applies -15 to that target's NON-Affliction damage for 1 turn (dur 2 = 1 enemy turn). Marks target+self to enable the discounted 15-Aff/1-Random follow-up.

abilities.name: Consume Flame
abilities.conditional_scaling: +10 healing AND +1 fired-up stack (+5 Affliction to all skills) per qualifying cleansable harmful Strategic-type effect removed. Punishes enemy debuff/control comps.
abilities.effects_summary: Self panic button + ramp engine: cleanses ALL enemy effects from Natsu, heals 15 HP base +10 per harmful effect removed, and grants 1 fired-up stack per effect. NOTE: the .gd does NOT implement the JSON-described 'swap to Fire Dragon's Roar' line; only heal + stacks are coded. 2-turn cooldown.

abilities.name: I'm all fired up!
abilities.conditional_scaling: Each trigger adds +5 Affliction to ALL Natsu's skills; stacks with no cap, self-feeding since nearly every Natsu skill deals Affliction.
abilities.effects_summary: Battle-start passive with two triggers: (1) Natsu is targeted by a new harmful STRATEGIC skill, (2) Natsu deals new Affliction damage. Each fires a +5 Affliction damage_mod (duration arg 5 -> ~2 self-turns; description claims 3 turns). Stacks compound.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Unbounded via I'm all fired up! stacks (+5 Affliction each, no cap). Mid-game with ~3-5 stacks: Roar 35->50-60 Affliction, Iron Fist Affliction 10->25-35. No true DoT; all damage is on-cast.
damage_profile.notes: Affliction is the bulk of his output and fully bypasses DR/shields/barriers, so effective damage is far higher than face value vs tanky/shielded targets. peak_single_target ~45 turn-1 (Roar 35 Aff plus chip, ramping past 60+ as stacks accrue). peak_aoe is the Wing Attack team-punish 15 Normal + 5 Affliction = 20, conditional on the enemy using a new skill. Numbers use ground-truth .gd values, not the inflated 15/5 JSON for natsu1.

economy.color_dependency: Light-moderate Red: only 3 of 7 visible pips are specific (all Red), the other 4 are Random. natsu1/2/3 each need exactly 1 Red; natsu4 is pure Random. Easy to fuel in a Red or mixed team.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent tempo: two 0-cooldown spammable damage skills (Iron Fist, Roar). Wing Attack 1cd, Consume Flame 2cd. Can output damage every turn with no downtime; Roar re-casts cheaply next turn (1 Random, 15 Aff).
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate. Functional from turn 1 (cheap 0-cd Iron Fist, strong 35-Aff Roar) but his ceiling is gated by accumulating I'm all fired up! stacks. Ramp is self-sustaining (Affliction every turn) and accelerated by enemy debuff comps via Consume Flame, so it is reliable rather than fragile.

soft_cc: Wing Attack delay: if the target uses a new skill it is delayed 2 turns (skill-delay / tempo denial)

win_conditions: Out-duel a single target with ramping Affliction that ignores their defenses (DR/shields/barriers).
Snowball I'm all fired up! stacks across a long fight until Roar/Iron Fist hit for unblockable big numbers.
Hard-counter enemy debuff/control comps: every harmful Strategic skill thrown at him fuels his ramp, and Consume Flame turns their stacked debuffs into massive heals plus free stacks.
Use Roar's cheap discounted follow-up to repeatedly nuke a focused target while feeding the ramp.
internal_synergies: I'm all fired up! (natsu5) + every Affliction skill: each Affliction hit grants a stack that boosts all future Affliction, a self-reinforcing loop.
Consume Flame (natsu4) + I'm all fired up!: cleansing enemy debuffs converts incoming control into both healing and permanent damage ramp (anti-debuff payoff).
Roar self-mark + cost_change: enables a 1-Random, 15-Affliction follow-up Roar so he can nuke a focused target two turns running for minimal energy.
Roar's -15 non-Affliction damage debuff softens the marked target while Natsu keeps hammering it with Affliction.
Wing Attack delay + 0-cd Iron Fist/Roar: punish enemy action economy while never losing his own tempo.
strengths: All-bypass damage: most output is Affliction (Roar 35, Iron Fist 10, plus ramp) that ignores DR, shields, and barriers - excellent vs tanks and shield comps.
Open-ended, self-sustaining scaling with no hard cap that ramps every turn.
Outstanding tempo: two 0-cooldown damage skills, cheap Red-only color cost, acts meaningfully every turn from turn 1.
Strong self-sufficiency: cleanse + scaling self-heal (15 +10/effect) on a 2-turn cooldown makes him resilient and a natural hard-counter to debuff/control teams.
Soft tempo denial via Wing Attack's skill-delay creates a lose-lose for the targeted enemy.
weaknesses: Almost entirely single-target - only one conditional, low (20-total) AoE option, so weak at clearing or pressuring multiple enemies.
No hard CC, no stun, no invuln, no counter, no shields - purely an offense+self-sustain duelist with no team protection or lockdown.
Front-loaded damage is modest (Roar 35 turn 1); needs time to ramp, so fast burst comps can race him before stacks matter.
Provides nothing for allies - no team heal, no team buff, no enemy energy denial; entirely selfish kit.
Ramp-on-receive trigger only fires on harmful STRATEGIC skills, so vs pure-damage enemies he ramps solely off his own Affliction (slower).
Stale/unimplemented data: natsu1 actually deals 10/10 not the advertised 15/5, and Consume Flame's described 'swap to Roar' is not coded, so the real kit is slightly weaker than the text implies.

power_assessment.reasoning: A clean, well-rounded Affliction duelist. His mostly-unblockable Affliction damage gives high effective DPS against the tanky/shielded targets that wall normal attackers, and his scaling has no cap. Excellent tempo and cheap color cost let him act every turn, and his cleanse + scaling self-heal make him a genuine hard-counter to debuff/control comps. He is held back from top tier by being almost purely single-target with no hard CC, no team utility, and modest turn-1 burst - he wins long 1v1 attrition and punishes control, but contributes little in AoE-clear or protect-the-carry roles. Solidly above-average, not oppressive.
outlier_flags: JSON_vs_GD_mismatch: natsu1 advertised 15 Normal + 5 Affliction but .gd deals 10 Normal + 10 Affliction (split_desc confirms 10/10).
UNIMPLEMENTED_DESCRIPTION: Consume Flame's 'swaps to Fire Dragon's Roar per harmful effect removed' is in describe()/JSON but absent from the .gd execute(); only heal + fired-up stacks are coded.
DURATION_MISMATCH: I'm all fired up! described as a 3-turn buff but the damage_mod_effect duration arg is 5 (~2 self-turns).
UNCAPPED_SCALING: I'm all fired up! stacks have no cap; in long games Affliction output can balloon well beyond listed numbers.

abilities.name: Doctor Blythe
abilities.conditional_scaling: Heal scales 10 HP per stack of Doctor Blythe consumed; stacks accrue 1/turn permanently, so heal grows the longer the mark sits unconsumed
abilities.effects_summary: Applies a permanent ticking mark (Doctor Blythe) on an ally that gains 1 stack each turn for the rest of the game. Re-casting on an already-marked ally consumes all stacks to heal that ally 10 HP per stack. Pure ramping heal-bank; no damage.

abilities.name: Puppeteering
abilities.conditional_scaling: Execute on target at/below 20 HP. Self-stacking ticking effect: end of each turn deals 10 Piercing to a random enemy PER stack of Puppeteering. Each cast adds +1 stack and an immediate 10 Piercing, so end-of-turn random Piercing output ramps 10/stack indefinitely
abilities.effects_summary: Executes any character at or below 20 HP (instant kill; works on dead chars too for mission purposes). On cast deals an immediate 10 Piercing to a random enemy and adds 1 permanent self-stack. At end of EVERY turn, deals 10 Piercing (bypasses shields/DR) to a random enemy once per stack. Ramping random Piercing DoT engine.

abilities.name: Terpsichora
abilities.conditional_scaling: Active damage = 20 + 5 per Terpsichora stack (+5 damage mod, stacking, stack_mag). Each cast (setup or attack) adds +1 stack, so single-target damage ramps +5 per use. Shield refreshes to 10 each turn permanently
abilities.target_type: SELF to toggle on, then SINGLE enemy
abilities.effects_summary: First cast: permanent self target-change toggle + a ticking effect that refreshes up to 10 Shield each turn for the rest of the game + first +5 damage-mod stack. While active, recast deals 20 Normal damage to target enemy and adds another +5 damage stack. CD0 so spammable; combines a self-sustaining 10-shield-per-turn defense with a ramping nuke.

abilities.name: Cat Reflexes
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self becomes Invulnerable for 1 turn (invuln_effect dur 2). Pure panic button / defensive cooldown.

abilities.name: Post-Mortem Nen
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Passive applied at battle start. The first time each game Neferpitou would die, they instead become Immortal until the end of their next turn — a guaranteed one-time death-save that also keeps her ramping engines (Puppeteering/Terpsichora/Doctor Blythe) alive one extra turn.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Effectively unbounded. Terpsichora active = 20 + 5/stack and gains +1 stack per cast (CD0), so single-target ramps indefinitely. Puppeteering end-of-turn random Piercing = 10/stack with no stack cap and permanent duration, so passive random Piercing output climbs 10 per Puppeteering cast every turn for the rest of the game. Doctor Blythe heal = 10/stack with no cap. All three are game-long ramps with no decay.
damage_profile.notes: Early single-target is modest: Terpsichora opener costs a turn (setup, deals 0), then ~25 (20+5 from first stack) per cast climbing +5 each use. peak_single_target ~50 reflects a Terpsichora hit after several stacks accrued (~20+30) in one turn; with CD0 plus damage mod it scales far higher mid/late. Peak AoE is incidental — Puppeteering's per-stack random-target Piercing ticks spread across the enemy team (e.g. 3 stacks = 30 Piercing distributed each turn end, plus immediate 10, plus a Terpsichora hit). All Puppeteering damage is Piercing (skips flat+%DR), making effective damage high vs tanky comps. sustained_dot_per_turn=30 assumes ~3 Puppeteering stacks mid-game; uncapped so this grows.

economy.color_dependency: Light/split. Identity colors Green+Red. Only Doctor Blythe (Green:1) and Terpsichora (Red:1) demand specific colors; Puppeteering and Cat Reflexes are Random:1. Very low color tax for a two-color character.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent. All four visible skills cost only 1 pip each. Terpsichora is CD0 (spam every turn), Doctor Blythe CD1, Puppeteering CD2, Cat Reflexes CD4. Can act every turn while the ramps tick passively.
economy.ramp_dependency: High — power is almost entirely back-loaded. Turn 1 Terpsichora and first Puppeteering deal little; value compounds each turn. Weak burst, strong if allowed to snowball. Post-Mortem Nen and Cat Reflexes exist mainly to buy the extra turns the ramp needs.

invuln_or_counter: Cat Reflexes: self Invulnerable 1 turn (CD4)
Post-Mortem Nen passive: first lethal hit converts to Immortal until end of next turn
Terpsichora: permanent up-to-10 Shield refreshed every turn

win_conditions: Survive long enough for the ramps to snowball: Puppeteering passive random Piercing (10/stack/turn, uncapped) and Terpsichora's +5/stack scaling nuke eventually out-damage anything
Use the 1-pip-each, low-cooldown kit to act every turn while passive DoT chips the whole enemy team through DR/shields (Piercing)
Bank Doctor Blythe stacks on a key ally and dump a huge burst heal at a critical moment to keep the team alive into the late game
Cleanup executions via Puppeteering on anything dropped to <=20 HP
internal_synergies: Cat Reflexes (invuln) + Post-Mortem Nen (death-save Immortal) buy survival turns, which is exactly what every Neferpitou engine needs since they all ramp over time
Terpsichora's self target-change toggle pairs its permanent 10-shield-per-turn with its own ramping nuke — one skill is both her defense and her scaling offense
Puppeteering's execute closes out enemies that the chip DoT and Terpsichora soften, and the same skill's stacks keep ticking even on turns she does other things
Post-Mortem Nen preserving her one extra turn lets her get a final Puppeteering tick / Terpsichora cast / Doctor Blythe dump off after lethal
Doctor Blythe lets her self-sustain or sustain an ally without spending offense tempo, since it's CD1 and 1 Green pip
strengths: Extremely cheap kit — every visible skill is 1 pip, two of them Random; near-zero color tax and great tempo (can act every turn)
Multiple compounding, uncapped, permanent ramps (Puppeteering Piercing DoT, Terpsichora damage mod, Doctor Blythe heal-bank) that have no decay
Piercing DoT bypasses flat and %DR and shields — strong, reliable chip vs tanky/defensive comps and spread across the whole enemy team
Self-sufficient survivability stack: permanent 10 shield/turn + 1-turn invuln (CD4) + a guaranteed one-time death-save (Immortal)
Provides both team healing (Doctor Blythe) and offense, so she flexes between support and carry
Built-in execute for cleanup and tempo finishes
weaknesses: Very weak burst and slow start — turn-1 setup (Terpsichora toggle, first Puppeteering) deals minimal damage; loses hard races against fast burst comps
All power is back-loaded and ramp-dependent; if she's focused down before stacks accumulate, the kit underperforms drastically
Puppeteering's end-of-turn damage targets a RANDOM enemy, so it can't be aimed to finish a specific threat or focus-fire
Almost no real CC — no stun/silence/disable; cannot disrupt enemy combos, only out-attrition them
Death-save and invuln are one-and-done / long-CD; once spent she's fragile if she hasn't ramped enough
No energy denial or cleanse — vulnerable to her ramp effects being removed/ignored and to enemy resource pressure
Heal is locked to Doctor Blythe stacking up over many turns; no fast reactive heal for spike damage
role: Ramping attrition carry/support hybrid: scaling Piercing DoT + self-sustain + bankable team heal
signature_mechanic: Permanent uncapped ramps with no decay: Puppeteering stacks deal 10 Piercing to a random enemy per stack at every turn's end, Terpsichora's nuke gains +5 damage per stack each cast (CD0), and Doctor Blythe banks a heal of 10 HP per stack — all compounding for the rest of the game while a self-shield and a one-time death-save keep her alive to scale.

power_assessment.reasoning: Exceptional economy (all 4 visible skills 1 pip, mostly Random; Terpsichora CD0; light Green/Red color tax) lets her execute her game plan every single turn. Her ceiling is genuinely strong: three uncapped, permanent, no-decay ramps, one of them Piercing (ignores DR/shields) spread across the enemy team, plus self 10-shield/turn, a CD4 invuln, and a guaranteed one-time Immortal death-save make her very hard to kill and very hard to out-attrition in long games. The drag on her rating is a slow, low-burst start and total ramp dependency — she has essentially no early tempo, no hard CC, and Puppeteering's DoT is randomly targeted so she can't reliably focus or close on a specific threat. Against fast burst or disruption comps she can be put behind before she snowballs. Net: a high-ceiling, slow, self-sufficient attrition unit that's strong in grindy fights and mediocre in fast ones — a solid 7 in isolation with a higher effective ceiling if games go long.
outlier_flags: uncapped-permanent-ramp (Puppeteering 10 Piercing/stack/turn and Terpsichora +5/stack have no stack cap or decay — late-game scaling can exceed normal damage budgets)
Terpsichora cooldown 0 — spammable scaling nuke
guaranteed one-time death-save passive (Post-Mortem Nen Immortal) plus permanent self-shield plus invuln stacks unusually high survivability
all-1-pip kit with 2 Random pips is unusually cheap for a two-color carry/support hybrid

role: Defensive team support / protector with a counter-and-heal engine
signature_mechanic: Protector's Reiatsu passive heals/shields every ally each time Nel spends energy (5 HP per pip, doubled to 10 under Declare Gamuza), so her whole kit doubles as team sustain; Gamuza transformation converts ally stuns into invulnerability and punishes enemy invulnerability with Shatter (def-negate).

abilities.name: Lanzador Verde
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage (to 40) while Declare, Gamuza mark is active on Nel
abilities.effects_summary: Pure single-target nuke, Uncounterable. Spammable (0 CD). Each cast also triggers the nel5 heal/shield passive on allies (10 HP/ally under Gamuza for this 2-pip cast).

abilities.name: Cero Doble
abilities.conditional_scaling: Follow-up damage doubles 15 -> 30 if the marked enemy actually used a Harmful skill and was countered
abilities.effects_summary: Setup/counter: applies an invisible COUNTER_USE effect on target for 1 turn (dur 2) that counters their next Harmful skill and resets this CD. Arms a free-reuse mark on Nel; next turn Nel reuses for 0 cost to deal 15 (or 30 if countered) Energy. Tempo/energy denial vs an enemy aggressor. The free follow-up is excluded from the nel5 passive.

abilities.name: Declare, Gamuza
abilities.conditional_scaling: Transformation buff window: doubles nel5 passive (5->10/pip), +5 nel1 damage; reactive triggers scale with how often allies are stunned / enemies go invulnerable
abilities.effects_summary: Self transformation for 4 turns (dur 9 self). Grants every living ally a STUN_RECEIVED trigger: if Stunned they become Invulnerable 1 turn instead. Grants every living enemy an ON_INVULN trigger: if they become Invulnerable they are Shattered (def-negate) for 1 turn. Buffs Lanzador Verde +5 and doubles Protector's Reiatsu. Portrait swap. Strong anti-stun protection + anti-invuln tech.

abilities.name: Nel Block
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (its 1 pip still feeds the nel5 passive: 5 HP/ally, 10 under Gamuza)
abilities.effects_summary: Self Invulnerable for 1 turn (default_defend). Panic/self-protect button on a 4 CD; also a cheap way to tick the heal passive.

abilities.name: Protector's Reiatsu
abilities.conditional_scaling: 5 HP per energy pip spent, doubled to 10/pip while Declare Gamuza is active; scales with Nel's total pip expenditure each turn
abilities.effects_summary: Core engine: whenever Nel spends energy on a skill, each other living ally is healed 5 HP per pip spent (10 under Gamuza). Allies at full HP instead gain that as Shield (5/pip, dur 2). Cero Doble's free reuse does not trigger it. Turns every Nel action into team sustain.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Offense is low and flat: nel1 caps at 40 (Gamuza), nel2 follow-up caps at 30. The 70 single-target peak requires the same turn to land a Gamuza-buffed Lanzador Verde (40) plus a primed Cero Doble follow-up that countered a Harmful skill (30) — situational. No AoE, no DoT. The real 'scaling' is team HP throughput: a 2-pip skill heals each ally 20 HP under Gamuza, so 4-team uptime can mean ~60 ally HP/turn restored.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is Normal/Energy (no Affliction/Bleed/Piercing/True), so it is fully blocked by enemy shields and DR. She is a support, not a damage threat.

economy.color_dependency: Light: only 2 fixed-color pips across the visible kit (1 Green on nel1, 1 White on nel2); nel3/nel4 are pure Random. Splashable into Green/White cores but otherwise flexible.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Two 0-CD spammable skills (nel1 nuke, nel2 counter-setup) drive the heal engine every turn; defensive/transform tools on moderate 4-5 CDs. Smooth turn-to-turn tempo, no dead turns.
economy.ramp_dependency: Soft ramp: kit is functional turn 1 but roughly doubles in value once Declare Gamuza is up (4-turn window, 5 CD). Counter payoff (nel2 30 dmg) also depends on baiting an enemy Harmful skill.

invuln_or_counter: Self Invulnerable 1 turn (nel4)
Cero Doble counters next enemy Harmful skill (nel2)
Allies who would be Stunned become Invulnerable instead under Gamuza (nel3)
Enemies who become Invulnerable are Shattered/def-negated under Gamuza (nel3)

strengths: Near-free team sustain: every energy pip Nel spends heals all allies, and her two 0-CD skills let her spend reliably every turn (10-20 ally HP/skill under Gamuza)
Overheal converts to Shield, so sustain is never wasted
Strong reactive protection: Gamuza turns ally stuns into invulnerability, a hard counter to stun-lock comps
Anti-invuln tech: enemies that go invulnerable under Gamuza get Shattered (def-negate), punishing defensive/invuln-reliant enemies
Cero Doble is flexible tempo control that counters an enemy Harmful skill and resets its own CD, with a damage payoff
Two self-protect layers (nel4 invuln, nel2 counter) make Nel hard to focus
Very low color commitment (only 2 fixed pips) — easy to slot into many cores
weaknesses: Very low personal damage (40 peak nuke, all Normal/Energy that shields/DR fully block) — cannot threaten kills alone
No AoE and no DoT — single-target everything, weak into wide boards
No hard CC, no cleanse, no energy denial, no team-wide invuln/barrier on demand
Healing is conditional on Nel spending energy: if energy-starved or forced to PASS, the engine stops and allies get nothing
Best protection (anti-stun, doubled heal, +dmg) is gated behind Declare Gamuza's 4-turn / 5-CD window, leaving gaps
Cero Doble counter is reactive and whiffs entirely if the marked enemy doesn't use a Harmful skill; the free follow-up deliberately does NOT feed the heal passive
nel3 anti-invuln/anti-stun triggers are dead weight against comps that never stun or never go invulnerable
win_conditions: Outlast: keep a 4-ally frontline topped off and shielded while damage dealers grind the enemy down
Maintain Declare Gamuza uptime to double the heal engine and lock down enemy stun/invuln plans
Bait enemy aggressors into Cero Doble counters to deny key Harmful skills and chip 30 damage
Be the durable anchor that never dies (invuln + counter) so the team always has its support online
internal_synergies: Declare Gamuza (nel3) doubles Protector's Reiatsu (nel5) AND buffs Lanzador Verde (nel1) — the central power spike that ties offense and sustain together
Two 0-CD skills (nel1, nel2 setup) guarantee Nel spends energy every turn to keep the heal/shield passive ticking
Gamuza's enemy-invuln -> Shatter trigger combos with allies who force enemy invulnerability, opening them for the team's burst
Gamuza's ally-stun -> invuln conversion pairs with stun-heavy enemies to flip their CC into a defensive boon
nel4 / nel2 cost pips still feed nel5, so even her defensive turns produce team healing

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded defensive support whose value is in low-cost, ever-present team sustain plus situational hard counters, not in damage. The energy-spend heal engine is efficient and hard to interrupt thanks to two 0-CD skills, and Declare Gamuza gives a meaningful double-sustain + anti-stun + anti-invuln spike. But her ceiling is capped: trivial personal damage that shields fully block, no AoE/DoT, no hard CC or cleanse, and her best tools are conditional (Gamuza window, enemy must use Harmful for the counter, enemy must stun/go-invuln for Gamuza's reactive triggers). She is a strong glue/anchor support in the right comp and mediocre as a standalone threat — landing solidly mid-tier.
outlier_flags: no AoE at all
two 0-cooldown skills enabling every-turn passive procs
heal output scales with own energy expenditure rather than a fixed value
reactive-trigger abilities (nel3) can be fully dead vs certain comps

abilities.name: Blood Demon Art
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat 20 either mode)
abilities.effects_summary: Dual-mode, free-to-spam (1 White, no CD): on an enemy deals 20 Normal dmg; on an ally heals 20 HP and cleanses ALL hostile afflictions. Either way applies a permanent MARK ('Blood Demon Art', duration -1). Mark is the engine feeding Demonic Frenzy (nezuko2) and the Pyrokinesis (nezuko3) bonus. Won't re-mark an already-marked target.

abilities.name: Demonic Frenzy
abilities.conditional_scaling: scales with number of marked characters: 20 dmg/heal per mark + 15 self-heal per affected character
abilities.effects_summary: Re-casts Blood Demon Art on every marked character at once: 20 Normal dmg to each marked enemy, 20 heal + full affliction cleanse to each marked ally. Bypasses invulnerability. Nezuko self-heals 15 HP per character affected. CD 4. With 3+ marked, advances a mission counter. Pure mark-count payoff button.

abilities.name: Pyrokinesis
abilities.conditional_scaling: on-mark: +5 immediate (35 total) plus a 5 Affliction DoT for the next 2 turns
abilities.effects_summary: 30 Affliction damage (bypasses barriers/shields/DR) to one enemy, no cooldown. If target is marked by Blood Demon Art: +5 immediate (35 total) and applies a 5 Affliction/turn damage_effect for 2 turns (dur arg 5). Spammable affliction nuke; the mark from nezuko1 upgrades it into a DoT.

abilities.name: Little Nezuko!
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self invulnerability for 1 turn via default_defend. Cheap (1 Random) panic button on CD 4. AI tags it as a self panic-button. Note: her own Demonic Frenzy bypasses invuln, but enemy invuln-piercers are the relevant threat.

abilities.name: Demon Blood
abilities.conditional_scaling: one-time trigger at HP<=50
abilities.effects_summary: Passive self-sustain. The first time Nezuko's HP falls to 50 or below, she gains a regen of 10 HP/turn for 5 turns (50 HP total over the window). One-shot trigger; removes itself after firing. Adds resilience but no offense/utility for the team.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Demonic Frenzy scales 20 dmg per marked enemy (up to ~60 across a 3-enemy team if all are marked) plus 15 self-heal per affected; but marks are applied one-per-turn by nezuko1, so multi-mark setups take several turns. Single-target ceiling is Pyrokinesis at 35 Affliction + a 5/turn DoT for 2 turns (45 total over the window).
damage_profile.notes: Damage is low and slow. nezuko1=20 Normal, nezuko3=30 Affliction (35 on mark), nezuko2=20 Normal per marked enemy. Best one-turn enemy focus = Pyrokinesis on a marked target: 35 immediate Affliction (bypasses shields/DR) plus 5x2 DoT. AoE 'peak' is per-target 20 and requires pre-marking, so realistic burst is modest. Affliction on nezuko3 is the only DR-bypassing damage in the kit.

economy.color_dependency: Mono-White, low strain: 3 White pips total (one each in nezuko1/2/3), single-color identity so easy to fuel; 3 Random pips give flexibility. No multi-color tension.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent tempo on her two core buttons: nezuko1 (mark/heal/poke) and nezuko3 (affliction nuke) are both 0-cooldown and spammable every turn. Only the payoff (nezuko2) and the defensive (nezuko4) sit on CD 4.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate: nezuko1 must be spent to seed marks before nezuko2 pays off and before nezuko3 upgrades to a DoT, so her ceiling builds over 2-3 turns rather than landing immediately.

invuln_or_counter: self invulnerability 1 turn (nezuko4, CD4)

power_assessment.reasoning: A flexible, low-cost hybrid support/off-DoT with no dead buttons but no standout power spike. Strengths: two spammable 0-CD buttons (mark+20 dmg/heal, and a 30/35 Affliction nuke that bypasses shields/DR), genuine team utility via cleanse (removes ALL afflictions on heal), scaling AoE heal/damage through marks, self-sustain via 15/affected self-heal and a passive 10/turn x5 regen, and a cheap self-invuln panic button. Demonic Frenzy bypassing invulnerability is a nice anti-defensive niche. Weaknesses: damage numbers are low and the kit has zero hard CC, no shields, no energy denial, and no offensive burst — her AoE and DoT both require spending turns pre-marking with nezuko1, so the payoff is slow and telegraphed. She can't close games on her own and leans on teammates to convert her chip + sustain into wins. Net: a solid, fair role-player slightly below midline — useful glue character, not a carry.
outlier_flags: nezuko1 is 0-cooldown, 1-pip, and does dual heal+cleanse OR damage AND a permanent mark — unusually efficient for 1 White; arguably over-loaded utility for the cost
nezuko3 is a spammable 0-cooldown 30 Affliction nuke (35 on mark) that bypasses shields/DR — high uptime affliction with no CD is a notable efficiency point
Demonic Frenzy explicitly bypasses invulnerability, a strong anti-defensive clause

role: Hybrid off-healer / mark-based affliction support with light sustain and team cleanse
signature_mechanic: 'Blood Demon Art' permanent MARK economy: nezuko1 (spammable, 1-pip) seeds marks on allies (heal+cleanse) or enemies (damage); marks then power Demonic Frenzy's AoE re-cast + self-heal and upgrade Pyrokinesis into a damage-over-time.
internal_synergies: nezuko1 seeds the permanent mark that everything keys off — it's the hub of the kit
Marked enemies turn Pyrokinesis (nezuko3) from a 30 nuke into 35 + 5/turn DoT for 2 turns
Marked characters are all hit by Demonic Frenzy (nezuko2), which scales 20 dmg/heal per mark and self-heals 15 per affected — reward for spreading marks over multiple turns
nezuko2 + nezuko1 cleanse stacking lets her strip afflictions off the whole marked allied side at once
nezuko4 self-invuln + nezuko5 passive regen give her a survivability layer to keep spamming her 0-CD buttons
Self-heal from nezuko2 (15/affected) plus passive regen keeps her topped to stay in marking range
strengths: Two spammable 0-cooldown core buttons (mark/heal/poke + affliction nuke) for excellent turn-to-turn tempo
Mono-White, low-cost kit (6 pips across 4 skills, half flexible Random) — easy to fuel, fits many teams
Strong anti-affliction tech: heal+full cleanse on nezuko1 and AoE cleanse on nezuko2
Affliction damage on Pyrokinesis bypasses shields/DR; Demonic Frenzy bypasses invulnerability
Layered self-sustain: per-affected self-heal + passive 10/turn x5 regen + on-demand self-invuln
Scaling AoE heal/damage through accumulating marks — flexible offense or support depending on where marks land
weaknesses: Low raw damage — peak single-target is 35 and AoE is only 20/target; can't burst or close games alone
No hard or soft CC whatsoever — zero stuns/silences/stagger
No shields/barriers, no energy denial, no teammate protection beyond cleanse
Payoff is slow and telegraphed: marks are applied one-per-turn by nezuko1, so AoE/DoT ceilings need 2-3 turns of setup
Passive sustain (nezuko5) is a one-time trigger and self-only — easily outpaced by real burst
Reliant on teammates to convert her chip + sustain into actual kills
win_conditions: Grind out attrition: spread marks, then chain Demonic Frenzy + spammable Pyrokinesis DoTs to out-sustain the enemy team
Act as the team's anti-affliction/heal anchor while damage dealers close, using cleanse + heals + self-invuln to stay alive
Punish defensive comps via invuln-bypassing Demonic Frenzy and shield/DR-bypassing Pyrokinesis affliction

abilities.name: Unblockable Strike
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 True damage per prior use of this skill this battle (self-stacking MARK counter, unbounded); +5 more True per Sheath Dodger vulnerability stack on target
abilities.effects_summary: Single-target True damage that ramps every cast; Bypassing (ignores Invulnerability), True skips all DR; each use adds a permanent self stack so damage scales without limit; 0 cooldown makes it the spammable win condition

abilities.name: Sheath Dodger
abilities.conditional_scaling: Applies a vulnerability that makes target take +5 from Unblockable Strike for the duration
abilities.effects_summary: 5 True on hit + 5 True/turn DoT (dur 7, ~4 turns, Bypassing) + Unblockable Strike vulnerability (+5) on target; grants Oetsu invulnerability to Strategic-class skills for the duration (self-protection vs strategic CC/buffs)

abilities.name: God of the Sword
abilities.conditional_scaling: Escalating permanent buff per use on the same ally (3 tiers)
abilities.effects_summary: Ally-targeted permanent forge buff: 1st use = permanently ignore Counter & Reflect; 2nd = permanent -1 cooldown to that ally's skills; 3rd = permanent -1 Random cost to that ally's skills. No self-target. 0 cooldown but each tier requires a separate turn

abilities.name: Perfect Stance
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Panic button: for 1 turn (dur 2) Oetsu ignores ALL harmful effects (ignore_damage + ignore_non_damage) = full invulnerability, plus becomes Invisible. Defensive only

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Unbounded. Unblockable Strike = 10 + 5*(prior uses) + 5*(Sheath Dodger vuln). 0-cooldown spam means stacks grow every turn: ~15 (2nd cast), ~25 (4th), ~40-50 by mid-game, climbing indefinitely. All True+Bypassing so DR/shields/invuln never reduce it.
damage_profile.notes: No native AoE at all. Real damage is the ramping single-target True nuke plus a 5/turn True DoT from Sheath Dodger. Early turns are weak (10-15); the threat is the late-game stack count. The custom_behavior AI hint of 50 reflects intended mid-fight single-target output.

economy.color_dependency: Minimal. Identity is White (character_colors=[2]) but only Sheath Dodger requires a specific pip (White:1). The other three skills each cost 1 Random, so the kit is almost color-agnostic and easy to splash on any team.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Two 0-cooldown skills (Unblockable Strike, God of the Sword) = spammable every turn; Sheath Dodger on cd 3; Perfect Stance panic on cd 4. Very high tempo on the core damage/support loop.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Both win conditions are ramps: Unblockable Strike's per-use stack scaling and God of the Sword's 3-tier permanent ally forge. Needs uninterrupted turns to come online; weak in short fights or when forced off-tempo.

invuln_or_counter: Perfect Stance: 1-turn full invulnerability (ignores all harmful, damage + non-damage) + Invisible
Sheath Dodger: self invulnerability to Strategic-class skills for ~4 turns

role: Ramping single-target True-damage carry with a permanent ally-buff support package
signature_mechanic: Unblockable Strike: a 0-cooldown, Bypassing, True-damage strike that gains a permanent +5 stack every time it is used this battle, so single-target output snowballs without limit and cannot be reduced by DR, shields, or invulnerability.
internal_synergies: Sheath Dodger applies a +5 vulnerability specifically to Unblockable Strike AND grants Oetsu Strategic-immunity, so it both boosts the nuke and shields him while he ramps.
Unblockable Strike checks for the Sheath Dodger INVULN to advance a mission (manually_advance_mission), tying the two together.
God of the Sword's 3rd tier (-1 Random cost) directly refunds the Random pips that Unblockable Strike, God of the Sword, and Perfect Stance all spend, accelerating his and allies' economy.
God of the Sword tier 1 (ignore Counter/Reflect) protects allied attackers; tier 2 (-1 cd) speeds the whole team.
Perfect Stance covers the vulnerable ramp window with full invuln + stealth.
win_conditions: Survive early turns and accumulate Unblockable Strike stacks until the True+Bypassing nuke one-shots through any defense.
Forge an ally with all 3 God of the Sword tiers to create a cooldown/cost-reduced, counter-immune second carry while Oetsu chips with True damage.
strengths: Unblockable damage: True + Bypassing means DR, shields, barriers, and invulnerability never reduce his core output.
Unbounded single-target scaling from 0-cooldown stacking — late-game he reliably deletes any single target.
Strong, near-color-agnostic economy (3 of 4 skills are 1 Random) makes him easy to fit on any roster.
Excellent self-protection for a damage carry: a 1-turn total invuln + stealth panic button plus a 4-turn Strategic-immunity window.
Doubles as a powerful support: permanent counter/reflect immunity, cooldown reduction, and cost reduction handed to an ally.
weaknesses: No AoE whatsoever — useless for board clears or multi-target pressure.
Very weak early game: opening casts deal only 10-15 and the support buffs take 3 separate turns to fully pay off.
Entirely ramp-dependent; if rushed down, stunned, or denied turns before stacks build, he contributes little.
No healing, no shields, no hard CC — purely timed invuln windows for defense, so sustained focus between cooldowns kills him.
God of the Sword cannot target self and does nothing without a living ally, so on certain comps a whole skill is wasted.

power_assessment.reasoning: The unblockable, unbounded-scaling True nuke is a genuine top-tier win condition: nothing in the damage pipeline can mitigate it and 0 cooldown lets it grow every single turn, so given enough time he kills anyone through anything. He also pairs that carry threat with a real support kit (permanent counter-immunity, cd and cost reduction) and two solid defensive escape buttons, all on a cheap, near-color-free economy. He is held back from elite status by zero AoE, a genuinely weak early game, and total reliance on getting uninterrupted turns to ramp — a fast aggressive or CC-heavy comp can close the game before his stacks matter. Strong but exploitable: rate 7 in isolation.
outlier_flags: unbounded-scaling: Unblockable Strike has no cap on the per-use +5 stack, so theoretical single-target damage is infinite in long games
fully-unmitigable: all his direct damage is True + Bypassing, ignoring DR, shields, barriers, AND invulnerability simultaneously
permanent-economy-buff: God of the Sword permanently reduces an ally's cooldowns and energy cost, an effect that persists all battle
zero-AoE: complete absence of multi-target damage is an extreme profile outlier

role: single-target lockdown controller / anti-execute counter-bruiser
signature_mechanic: Straw Doll Technique permanently Isolates a chosen enemy and "links the doll": that linked target is the payoff for everything else — Hairpin upgrades from execute-counter to a 2-turn 20-damage counter against it, and (per JSON) Resonance stuns are meant to last longer on it. Hammer Swing self-ramps via a permanent stacking +5-damage mark, and Resonance temporarily converts Hammer Swing into a rotating class-stun engine while swapping the bar to the hidden Hairpin counter.

abilities.name: Hammer Swing
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent stacking mark: each prior Hammer Swing on the target adds +5 damage to all future Hammer Swings on that target (base 20, then 25, 30, 35...). Unbounded ramp on a single target. Note: .gd base is 20 (JSON says 15 - stale).
abilities.effects_summary: Deals scaling Normal damage and applies a permanent stackable 'Hammer Swing' damage-up mark (+5 per stack). While Resonance is active, ALSO applies a 1-turn stun to one not-yet-used skill class drawn from the Resonance pool (Physical/Energy/Mental/Affliction), consuming that class from the pool; if the target also has Straw Doll Technique it advances a mission counter (per-Straw-Doll synergy hook).

abilities.name: Straw Doll Technique
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (sets up conditional payoffs on other skills rather than scaling itself)
abilities.effects_summary: Re-castable single-target 'link': removes any existing Straw Doll mark, then permanently Isolates the new target (duration -1, ends only on Nobara's death or re-use) and applies an enabler MARK. Isolate cuts the target off from allied effects/healing routing. NOTE: the JSON-promised -10 healing-received debuff is NOT implemented in the .gd (only Isolate + the link mark are applied). The link is the precondition for Hairpin's upgraded counter and Resonance's extended stun behavior.

abilities.name: Resonance
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self-buff for 4 turns (dur 9): each Hammer Swing now also stuns one skill class for 1 turn, drawn without replacement from {Physical, Energy, Mental, Affliction} (max 4 distinct class-stuns over the window). Simultaneously swaps action-bar slot 3 (Resonance) to the hidden Hairpin counter for 4 turns. Per .gd split_desc/swap args it swaps to HAIRPIN (JSON saying 'Embrace Pain' is stale).

abilities.name: Embrace Pain
abilities.conditional_scaling: Conditional sustain: triggers only while affected by an enemy harmful NON-damaging effect (stun, CC, debuffs, isolate, taunt, vuln, cost/cooldown mods, etc.).
abilities.effects_summary: For 2 turns Nobara ignores instant-kill and execute effects (hard anti-execute self-protection). Usable while stunned. On cast and at the end of each of her turns during the window, if she is under any enemy harmful non-damaging effect she heals 15 HP and gains 10 Damage Reduction. Turns being CC'd into self-healing + mitigation.

abilities.name: Hairpin
abilities.conditional_scaling: Execute threshold: countered enemy is executed if HP <= 30 (execute_attempt at 30). Against a Straw-Doll-linked target it instead becomes a longer (2-turn) counter dealing 20 Normal damage per trigger rather than executing.
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden ability (swapped onto the bar by Resonance). Places an invisible counter on the first Harmful skill the target uses (default dur 2 = 1 turn). On trigger: if target is Straw-Doll-linked, deal 20 Normal damage (and counter window is 2 turns/dur 4); otherwise attempt to execute the attacker if their HP <= 30. Counters/negates the triggering harmful skill via default_counter_trigger.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hammer Swing ramps unbounded on one target: +5 per permanent stack (20 -> 25 -> 30 -> ...). Realistically reaches 35-50 per swing after several casts on the same foe. No AoE and no DoT; Hairpin adds 20 burst per counter trigger against a linked target. True per-turn output is modest single-target Normal damage; the kit's 'damage' ceiling is gated by ramp time, not raw numbers.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is Normal type (subject to barriers/shields and DR) - no Piercing/True/Affliction/Bleed bypass. Peak listed (20) is the first Hammer Swing or a Hairpin counter; effective single-turn damage rises only as Hammer Swing stacks accumulate. The kit is control-and-lockdown first, damage second.

economy.color_dependency: Light: visible kit needs exactly 1 Green (Hammer Swing) and 1 Blue (Resonance); Straw Doll and Embrace Pain are Random:1. Dual Green/Blue identity but only one pip of each is hard-required, so easy to fund.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very cheap and spammy core: Hammer Swing and Straw Doll are 1 pip with 0 cooldown (usable every turn). Resonance CD3, Embrace Pain CD2, Hairpin CD3 - the control/defense tools are gated but the damage/ramp engine is not.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate-to-high. Damage relevance depends on stacking Hammer Swing over multiple turns on one target, and the full lockdown payoff (rotating class-stuns) only exists during the 4-turn Resonance window. Slow to come online; strongest in long fights.

hard_cc: 1-turn class-targeted stuns via Hammer Swing during Resonance (up to 4 distinct classes over the window)
soft_cc: permanent Isolate on the linked target (Straw Doll Technique)
invuln_or_counter: Hairpin: invisible counter on first Harmful skill (negate + execute<=30HP, or 20 dmg vs linked target)
Embrace Pain: 2-turn immunity to instant-kill/execute effects

win_conditions: Lock one priority threat down: permanently Isolate it with Straw Doll, then use Resonance so Hammer Swing chain-stuns its skill classes (Physical/Energy/Mental/Affliction) one per turn, denying its actions while ramping damage.
Grind a single target with stacking Hammer Swing until each swing hits for 35-50+, finishing in a war of attrition.
Bait an enemy carry into a Hairpin counter to negate their key Harmful skill and execute them at <=30 HP, or chip with 20-damage counters against a linked target.
Outlast execute/burst comps using Embrace Pain (anti-execute + CC-fed self-heal and DR).
internal_synergies: Straw Doll Technique is the hub: its linked target enables Hairpin's upgraded 2-turn/20-damage counter and (per intended design) extended Resonance stuns; Hammer Swing on a linked target also advances Nobara's mission counter.
Resonance + Hammer Swing: Resonance converts every cheap 0-CD Hammer Swing into a class-stun, so Nobara can lock a different skill class each turn while still ramping the damage mark.
Resonance also swaps in Hairpin, layering a counter threat on top of the stun-lock during the same window.
Embrace Pain turns enemy CC against them: the more the opponent stuns/debuffs Nobara, the more she heals and mitigates, complementing her slow grind playstyle.
0-cooldown 1-pip core (Hammer Swing / Straw Doll) keeps energy free for Blue Resonance and Random defensive casts.
strengths: Persistent single-target lockdown: permanent Isolate plus a 4-turn rotating multi-class stun engine can fully shut down one key enemy.
Extremely cheap, spammable core (two 1-pip, 0-CD skills) with light color requirements.
Strong anti-execute / anti-burst resilience (Embrace Pain immunity + CC-fueled heal/DR) that punishes assassin and execute comps.
Built-in counter with execute and skill-negation upside (Hairpin) that swings tempo against enemy carries.
Unbounded single-target damage ramp rewards long fights.
weaknesses: No AoE whatsoever and no DoT - useless at spreading pressure; hard-countered by wide/swarm comps.
Low and slow raw damage: all Normal type (blocked by shields/barriers/DR), starts at just 20 and needs many turns to ramp.
Payoff is heavily conditional and RNG-tinged: Resonance class-stun draws are random, and the full kit only shines during the 4-turn Resonance window with a linked target.
Implementation gaps weaken the on-paper kit: Straw Doll's -10 healing debuff is not coded, so its only real effect is Isolate.
Defensive tools are reactive and conditional - Embrace Pain heals nothing if the enemy doesn't apply non-damaging harmful effects; Hairpin does nothing if the target avoids Harmful skills.
Very strong vs single targets but contributes little to team fights or burst races; no shields, no cleanse, no allied support.

power_assessment.reasoning: A specialist single-target lockdown/anti-execute controller, not a damage dealer. Her ceiling - permanent Isolate plus a rotating class-stun chain off cheap 0-CD Hammer Swings during Resonance, backed by a counter that can negate-and-execute - is genuinely oppressive against one priority target and against execute/assassin comps. But the floor is low: no AoE/DoT, only Normal damage starting at 20, slow ramp, and payoff gated behind a 3-CD window plus RNG stun draws. The not-implemented Straw Doll healing debuff further trims her on-paper value. Solid, well-designed single-target toolbox that lands around the middle of the roster in isolation - oppressive in its niche, weak outside it.
outlier_flags: JSON metadata stale: Hammer Swing base is 20 in .gd not 15; Resonance swaps to Hairpin not Embrace Pain
Straw Doll Technique's -10 healing-received debuff described in JSON is NOT implemented in nobara2.gd (only Isolate + enabler mark applied)
Unbounded permanent damage-stack mark on Hammer Swing (no cap) - potential late-game outlier in very long single-target fights
Hairpin is a hidden slot-5 ability only reachable via Resonance's swap, so the 'visible' 4-skill bar understates her real action options during Resonance

role: Single-target piercing burst + energy-denial controller with strong self-defense
signature_mechanic: "Sea Dragon's Cradle" is a dual-purpose name: as a debuff it raises an enemy's skill costs by +1 random for 2 turns (removed on their next action); as a payoff token Roar consumes it to stun, and Point-Blank Roar consumes it for +15 piercing. Saint Valkyrie Dress is the transformation core — it gives DR, doubles/extends Cradle durations, makes Cradle no longer consumed by Roar (so Roar can stun repeatedly), and swaps Roar into 30-45 piercing Point-Blank Roar.

abilities.name: Sea Dragon's Roar
abilities.conditional_scaling: If target has Sea Dragon's Cradle, consumes it to stun for 1 turn (stun_effect(2)). Under Saint Valkyrie Dress mark, Cradle is NOT consumed, enabling repeated stuns.
abilities.effects_summary: Cheap spammable 15 normal damage + conditional 1-turn stun on Cradle'd targets; with Valkyrie Dress can chain-stun without spending the Cradle.

abilities.name: Sea Dragon's Cradle
abilities.conditional_scaling: Duration doubles from 2 turns (dur 4) to 4 turns (dur 8) if Noelle is marked by Valkyrie Dress.
abilities.effects_summary: AoE energy denial: all enemies' skills cost +1 random energy for 2 turns; effect removed by the next skill each enemy uses. Also applies the Cradle token that Roar/Point-Blank Roar consume for stun/bonus damage.

abilities.name: Saint Valkyrie Dress
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (state-enabling transformation)
abilities.effects_summary: Self 10 damage reduction for 3 turns (dur 6); marks self for 3 turns so Cradle lasts +2 turns and is no longer consumed by Roar; extends all currently-active Cradles by +2 turns; swaps Roar -> Point-Blank Sea Dragon's Roar for 2 turns. Core defensive + transformation enabler.

abilities.name: Sea Dragon's Nest
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self invulnerability for 1 turn (default_defend) — panic button / damage immunity.

abilities.name: Point-Blank Sea Dragon's Roar
abilities.conditional_scaling: Consumes Sea Dragon's Cradle on target for +15 damage (45 total piercing). Note: this version always consumes the Cradle even under Valkyrie Dress (does not respect the no-consume mark).
abilities.effects_summary: Swap-in upgraded Roar: 30 piercing (skips flat+%DR), or 45 piercing if it consumes a Cradle. Noelle's main burst payoff during the Dress window.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hard-capped. Single best hit is Point-Blank Roar consuming a Cradle = 45 piercing. No stacking/ramping damage; damage ceiling is fixed by flat numbers. Real value comes from piercing reliability + repeated cheap 1-cd hits, not raw scaling.
damage_profile.notes: Base Roar 15 normal. Point-Blank Roar 30 piercing base, 45 with Cradle consumed. Cradle (noelle2) and both defensive skills deal zero damage. Per-turn output is limited to one Roar (1 cd) so theoretical sustained ~15-45/turn against a single target; no AoE damage at all (custom_behavior AoE/single-target weights are AI scoring hints, not actual damage).

economy.color_dependency: Light. Only 2 Blue pips across the 4 visible skills (noelle2 and noelle3 each need 1 Blue); the rest is random. Point-Blank Roar also costs Blue:1. Mono-Blue identity but very cheap.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Aggressive on offense, gated on utility. Roar/Point-Blank Roar are 1-cd spammable; Cradle is 3-cd; both defensive buttons (Valkyrie Dress, Nest) are 4-cd. Strong round-to-round pressure, but the protective tools are not always available.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low/medium. No resource ramp, but the kit has a clear setup->payoff loop: land Cradle, then consume it with Roar (stun) or Point-Blank Roar (+15). Valkyrie Dress greatly amplifies the loop (longer Cradles, no-consume stun-lock, piercing swap) but is not strictly required to function.

hard_cc: 1-turn stun via Roar consuming Sea Dragon's Cradle (repeatable under Valkyrie Dress)
soft_cc: AoE +1 random cost increase on all enemy skills (energy tax) for 2 turns, removed on their next action
invuln_or_counter: 1-turn invulnerability (Sea Dragon's Nest)

internal_synergies: Cradle (noelle2) feeds both Roar (stun) and Point-Blank Roar (+15 piercing) — it is the hub token of the entire kit.

Valkyrie Dress (noelle3) is a force multiplier on Cradle: doubles its base duration (cast after Dress), extends existing Cradles +2, and makes Roar stop consuming it — enabling a repeated 1-turn stun lock on a single target.
Valkyrie Dress simultaneously swaps Roar into Point-Blank Roar (30/45 piercing), so the Dress window is both Noelle's tank phase (10 DR) and her burst phase.
Mono-Blue + cheap random costs keep the rotation castable nearly every turn (Roar 1-cd) while Cradle taxes the enemy's own energy.
win_conditions: Out-tempo opponents with energy denial: Cradle taxes the whole enemy team while Noelle chips and stun-locks the priority target.
Enter Valkyrie Dress, then chain Roar to keep a key enemy permastunned (Cradle not consumed) and/or land repeated Point-Blank piercing bursts that ignore DR/shields.
Survive to the late game using DR + 1-turn invuln to outlast burst comps, winning attrition through piercing reliability.
strengths: Piercing burst (Point-Blank Roar) ignores flat and % damage reduction — reliable against tanks/DR stackers.
Excellent self-preservation: 10 flat DR for 3 turns plus an on-demand 1-turn invulnerability, on a 1-cost frame.
Genuine energy denial — AoE +1 random cost on all enemy skills disrupts expensive-kit opponents.
Repeatable 1-turn stun that under Valkyrie Dress no longer spends the Cradle, enabling a single-target stun lock.
Very cheap, low color dependency (mostly random pips, only 2 Blue in the visible kit); 1-cd main attack gives consistent tempo.
Clean setup->payoff design with a transformation that amplifies the whole loop.
weaknesses: No team support whatsoever — no healing, no shields for allies, no cleanse, purely selfish.
Zero real AoE damage; all output funnels into one target per turn.
Hard damage ceiling (45) with no scaling/ramp — can be out-damaged by scaling carries in long games.
The strong burst is locked behind Valkyrie Dress (cd 4) and behind landing/holding a Cradle; raw output without the loop is just 15/turn.
Cradle's energy tax is removed by the enemy's very next skill, so against active opponents it is a single-turn tax, not a lockout.
Inconsistency: Point-Blank Roar still consumes the Cradle even under the no-consume mark, breaking the intended stun-lock + burst overlap on the same target.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, self-sufficient duelist/disruptor. Her strength is reliability rather than raw numbers: piercing burst that bypasses DR/shields, a flexible 1-cost transformation that doubles as a tank window and a burst window, on-demand invulnerability, and a 1-turn stun that becomes a near-lock under Valkyrie Dress. Energy denial adds real disruption against expensive comps. She is held back from a higher rating by a hard 45 damage ceiling with no scaling, total absence of team support/AoE, and the fact that her best pattern depends on a 4-cd transformation plus holding a Cradle. Strong in 1v1 / focus situations, mediocre as a team-fight contributor. Lands solidly above average as a flexible, low-cost control-bruiser.
