abilities.name: Flute Missile
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat 10); applies a vulnerability that amplifies later hits
abilities.effects_summary: 10 Piercing to one enemy; applies vulnerability_effect(+5, dur4 = 2 enemy turns) increasing ALL non-Affliction damage taken by 5. Pure setup/amp + chip. Bypasses flat+%DR (Piercing).

abilities.name: Overture Barrage
abilities.conditional_scaling: none, but lays the 'Overture Barrage' mark that Unstoppable Performance and Concentrated Climax key off of
abilities.effects_summary: 5 Piercing instant to ALL enemies + applies a 5 Piercing/turn DoT (damage_effect dur5) and an 'Overture Barrage' mark (dur5) to all. Mark auto-targets them with Unstoppable Performance and lets Concentrated Climax bypass invuln. Swaps this slot to Concentrated Climax while active. Note: .gd base_damage=5 (instant 5 + DoT 5/turn), not the '10' in the stale JSON.

abilities.name: Concentrated Climax
abilities.conditional_scaling: bypasses invulnerability if target carries the Overture Barrage mark
abilities.effects_summary: 10 Normal instant + 10 Normal/turn DoT (damage_effect dur5) + 'Concentrated Climax' auto-target mark to one enemy. Bypasses invuln when target is Overture-marked. Becomes Unstoppable Performance (slot5) while active. control_cancel: the whole channel is cancelled if Nonon is stunned. Damage here is Normal (NOT Piercing), so subject to DR/shields.

abilities.name: Sound Negation
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: default_defend: Nonon becomes invulnerable for 1 turn. Panic button / survivability tool, cd4.

abilities.name: Unstoppable Performance
abilities.conditional_scaling: stacks per mark on the target: 10 to main target + 10 per Overture-marked enemy + 10 per Climax-marked enemy (a single enemy carrying both marks eats up to 30)
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden alt unlocked by Concentrated Climax (cd0, repeatable). Deals 10 Piercing to the main target, an additional 10 Piercing to every enemy with the Overture Barrage mark, and 10 Piercing to every enemy with the Concentrated Climax mark. Effectively a free re-fireable nuke that converts Nonon's marks into burst. Piercing = ignores flat+%DR.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: On a fully set-up single target carrying both Overture + Climax marks under Flute Missile's +5 vuln: Unstoppable Performance = (10+10+10)=30 Piercing, each instance +5 vuln = 45; plus that turn's DoT ticks (Overture 5 + Climax 10 = 15, +vuln ~25). One-turn focus on a primed target lands ~45 burst and ~70 including amplified DoTs. AoE ceiling scales with marked enemies: Overture marks the whole team, so UP adds 10 to each marked enemy team-wide each cast.
damage_profile.notes: Damage is split across Piercing (nonon1/2/5, bypasses flat+%DR) and Normal (nonon3 instant+DoT, blocked by DR/shields). No raw burst on turn 1 (~20-25); power comes from 2-3 turns of mark+DoT ramp, then repeatable cd0 Unstoppable Performance. Flute Missile's +5 non-Affliction vuln multiplies every later Piercing/Normal hit.

economy.color_dependency: Moderate Red dependency: nonon2/nonon3 (and the hidden nonon5) each cost Red:1. The two visible setup attacks need Red; nonon1 and nonon4 are Random. So to ramp she needs reliable Red income, but total spend is cheap (1 pip per ability).
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast / spammy. nonon1 cd1, nonon3 cd1, nonon5 cd0 (repeatable), nonon2 cd2; only the nonon4 invuln is on a long cd4. She can act every turn and re-fire Unstoppable Performance continuously once Climax is active.
economy.ramp_dependency: High — kit is near-worthless on turn 1 and snowballs once Overture Barrage + Concentrated Climax marks are applied and the swap chain reaches Unstoppable Performance.

invuln_or_counter: Sound Negation: self invulnerability for 1 turn (cd4)
Concentrated Climax bypasses enemy invulnerability when target is Overture-marked

role: AoE DoT / mark-stacking ramp attacker with an anti-invuln finisher
signature_mechanic: Mark-and-detonate ability-swap chain: Overture Barrage (AoE mark+DoT) -> Concentrated Climax (single-target mark+DoT, swaps in) -> Unstoppable Performance (cd0 repeatable nuke that deals bonus 10 Piercing per Overture and per Climax mark on the targets). Flute Missile's +5 universal vulnerability amplifies the whole chain, and Climax bypasses enemy invulnerability on Overture-marked targets."
internal_synergies: Flute Missile's +5 non-Affliction vulnerability amplifies EVERY subsequent Piercing/Normal hit and DoT tick on that target
Overture Barrage marks the whole team; Unstoppable Performance then deals +10 Piercing to each marked enemy, turning the AoE mark into team-wide burst
Concentrated Climax's mark stacks with the Overture mark so Unstoppable Performance can hit one target for 10 (main) + 10 (Overture) + 10 (Climax) = 30
Overture mark enables Concentrated Climax to bypass enemy invulnerability, defeating defensive opponents
Sound Negation covers Nonon's fragility while her DoTs/marks do the work; control_cancel on Climax means she wants to avoid stuns to keep the chain alive
win_conditions: Land Overture Barrage + Concentrated Climax marks, then spam cd0 Unstoppable Performance for escalating Piercing burst
Stack Flute Missile vulnerability on a key target and detonate amplified marks/DoTs
Grind enemy team down with team-wide Piercing DoTs that bypass flat+%DR while staying alive behind Sound Negation
Use Climax's invuln-bypass to punish defensive/invulnerability-reliant compositions
strengths: Piercing on 3 of 5 abilities ignores flat and % damage reduction, making her damage hard to mitigate
Anti-invulnerability tech (Climax bypass on Overture-marked targets) is a rare and valuable counter to defensive teams
Extremely cheap (1 pip per ability) and fast (cd0/cd1 spam) once ramped
Team-wide DoT pressure plus a repeatable mark-detonation finisher
Self-invulnerability panic button covers her squishiness
Universal +5 vulnerability is a strong force-multiplier for herself and potentially allies' damage
weaknesses: No real turn-1 output (~20-25); heavily ramp-dependent and slow to come online
No hard CC, no healing, no shields, no cleanse, no energy denial, no ally support beyond the vulnerability debuff
Stun-vulnerable: Concentrated Climax's control_cancel wipes the channel/swap chain if she is stunned, collapsing her whole engine
Concentrated Climax instant + DoT are Normal damage, so blocked by DR and shields (only the Overture/UP/Flute portions pierce)
Red color dependency on her two main ramp attacks (and the finisher) can be choked by energy denial
Fragile body with only a single cd4 defensive cooldown; if marks are removed or she is locked down she contributes little

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-designed conditional snowball DPS. Once her Overture/Climax marks land and she swaps into the cd0 Unstoppable Performance loop, she puts out efficient, hard-to-mitigate Piercing damage (~45 burst + 15-25/turn DoT) on a 1-pip-per-ability economy, and her invuln-bypass is genuinely strong counter-tech. But she is gated by a multi-turn ramp, has near-zero turn-1 impact, brings no team utility (no heal/shield/cleanse/hard CC), and her entire engine is fragile to a single stun via Climax's control_cancel. Strong in a vacuum against greedy/defensive comps, mediocre into fast aggro or any control. Lands as solidly above-average but not oppressive.
outlier_flags: JSON description for nonon2 (Overture Barrage) is stale: says '10 damage' but .gd base_damage=5 (5 instant + 5/turn DoT)
Unstoppable Performance (nonon5) is cd0 and can stack 3x10 Piercing on a single double-marked target -> verify it isn't unintentionally re-castable for unbounded burst within a turn
Climax instant+DoT are Normal damage despite the Piercing-heavy theme; possible inconsistency vs. the kit's Piercing identity
control_cancel makes the whole kit binary against stun — high-variance design

role: single-target piercing bruiser / counter-ramp duelist
signature_mechanic: Permanent stacking damage ramp from multiple sources (passive +5 per hit taken, +5 per successful counter) paired with a Taunt that grants him Bypass Invulnerability, turning him into an unkillable scaling duelist that also strips enemy damage via stacking -5 piercing debuffs.

abilities.name: Omni-Headbutt
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 15 Physical to one enemy and stuns their HARMFUL skills for 1 turn (soft CC; only blocks offensive actions, leaves helpful/strategic usable). Cheap CD1 repeatable poke; benefits from passive/counter ramp bonuses.
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 per Omni-Rage stack (hit taken) and +5 per Omni-Counter stack are added to his outgoing damage globally, so this hit grows beyond 15 as stacks accrue

abilities.name: Omni-Bisect
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 30 PIERCING damage to one enemy (skips flat + percent DR) and permanently reduces that enemy's damage by 5 (stacks). Primary nuke + repeatable offensive-denial debuff that compounds across the match.
abilities.conditional_scaling: Permanent -5 enemy damage per cast (stacks, no listed cap); own outgoing damage also grows with Omni-Rage / Omni-Counter ramp stacks

abilities.name: Omni-Flight
abilities.effects_summary: No damage. Taunts one enemy for ~2 turns (forces that enemy to target Omni-Man) and, while active, his skills Bypass Invulnerability. Sets up forced single-target duels and counters defensive invuln walls.
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (utility/enabler); enables his nukes to ignore invulnerable targets

abilities.name: Omni-Counter
abilities.effects_summary: Targets himself or an ally and counters the first enemy skill used on them for 1 turn (Invisible). On a successful counter, Omni-Man permanently deals +5 damage (stacks). Defensive protection + second permanent ramp source.
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 permanent outgoing damage per successful counter (stacks); ramp conditional on the enemy actually striking the protected target

abilities.name: Omni-Rage
abilities.effects_summary: Passive: 25% Damage Reduction at all times, and permanently gains +5 outgoing damage every time he takes damage (stacks). Core survivability + main ramp engine; rewards trading hits and pairs with the self-Taunt that funnels damage onto him.
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 permanent damage per instance of damage taken (stacks, no listed cap); the more he is hit the harder he hits, synergizing with Omni-Flight's Taunt

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Open-ended/unbounded. Base same-turn burst is ~45 (Omni-Headbutt 15 + Omni-Bisect 30, both CD1, 4 pips). Every hit he takes (+5 via Omni-Rage) and every successful counter (+5 via Omni-Counter) permanently raises ALL outgoing damage with no listed cap, and his self-Taunt funnels incoming damage onto him to feed the passive. Late-game a 2-skill turn can climb from 45 toward 70-100+ in a long match. Enemy offense simultaneously decays via stacking -5 piercing debuffs.
damage_profile.notes: No AoE and no DoT anywhere - pure single-target threat. 30 of his base 45 is PIERCING (bypasses flat+%DR), so effective damage vs tanky/shielded targets is higher than raw. Headbutt portion is non-piercing. WARNING: source .gd files (abilities/omniman1-5.gd) and character/omniman.gd are MISSING from the repo; only compiled .res exports + omniman.tscn + abilities_data.json exist. All damage numbers, Physical/Piercing typing, durations, and stack caps come from JSON descriptions and could NOT be verified against ground-truth GDScript.

economy.color_dependency: Moderate Red-leaning. Of 6 visible pips: 3 specific (White:1 + Red:2) and 3 Random. Red is required for both his nuke (Omni-Bisect) and his Taunt enabler (Omni-Flight), with one White for Bisect. Energy identity (White/Red) inferred from costs since character/omniman.gd is missing.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast/aggressive. Two damage skills (Headbutt, Bisect) are both CD1 and can be cast nearly every turn; Taunt is CD2; Counter is the only long cooldown at CD4. Pressures every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: High but passive/low-effort. Damage scaling accrues automatically by taking hits (Omni-Rage) and via counters; he needn't spend turns setting up ramp - tanking fuels it. Weak in very short fights before stacks accumulate.

hard_cc: Taunt (Omni-Flight, ~2 turns, forces enemy to target Omni-Man)
soft_cc: Harmful-skill stun (Omni-Headbutt, 1 turn - blocks only the target's offensive skills)
invuln_or_counter: Omni-Counter (counters first enemy skill on self/ally for 1 turn, Invisible)
Omni-Flight grants Omni-Man Bypass Invulnerability vs the taunted enemy
25% passive Damage Reduction (Omni-Rage)

internal_synergies: Omni-Flight (Taunt) + Omni-Rage: forcing an enemy to attack him feeds the passive's +5-per-hit-taken ramp while 25% DR keeps him alive, turning focus-fire into a snowball.
Omni-Flight (Bypass Invulnerability) + Omni-Bisect/Headbutt: lets his nukes punch through invuln defensive cooldowns that would otherwise wall a single-target attacker.
Omni-Counter + Omni-Rage: two independent permanent +5 damage ramp sources stack onto the same pool, compounding single-target output.
Omni-Bisect debuff + survival kit: stacking -5 enemy damage lowers incoming damage over time, complementing 25% DR so the longer the fight runs the safer he gets while he hits harder.
Piercing on Omni-Bisect + Taunt invuln-bypass: combined defensive-stat penetration makes him a reliable answer to tanks/DR-stackers/invuln characters.
win_conditions: Win a long single-target attrition fight: out-survive (25% DR + counter + enemy damage-debuffs) while permanent +5 ramp stacks snowball his nukes toward one-shot territory.
Lock down and delete one priority target each turn via CD1 Bisect + Headbutt, using Taunt to deny escape and Bypass Invulnerability to ignore defensive cooldowns.
Use himself as Taunt-bait tank: soak focus fire to fuel Omni-Rage stacks, protecting squishier allies while becoming the late-game finisher.
strengths: Unbounded permanent damage ramp from two passive-ish sources (hits taken + counters) with no listed cap - very strong in drawn-out games.
30 Piercing on a CD1 nuke ignores flat and percent DR; with Taunt's Bypass Invulnerability he hard-counters tanks, DR stackers, and invuln defensive kits.
Very tanky for a damage dealer: always-on 25% DR, a self/ally counter, and stacking enemy damage-down debuffs make him hard to kill.
Excellent tempo: two damage skills on CD1 mean pressure every turn at low, partly-flexible cost (3 of 6 pips Random).
Built-in control suite (Taunt + harmful-skill stun) lets him dictate the duel and protect allies.
weaknesses: Zero AoE and zero DoT - purely single-target; poor into wide/multi-threat comps and easily outvalued by AoE teams.
Ramp-dependent: in fast games or burst-down comps his stacks never come online and he is just a ~45-burst bruiser.
No healing, shields, cleanse, energy denial, or stealth - can be kited, energy-starved, or out-sustained by dedicated counters.
Self-Taunt synergy is double-edged: funneling damage onto himself relies on 25% DR + debuffs holding; heavy Piercing/Affliction/True burst punishes it.
Red-leaning color dependency (needs Red for both nuke and Taunt) can be choked in Red-contested economies.
CD4 on his only defensive counter leaves coverage gaps.

role: single-target lockdown/control specialist with counter and skill-denial escalation
signature_mechanic: A counter-into-stun escalation chain: Relinquished (pegasus2) counters the target's Harmful skill, granting a permanent shield that locks both that skill and Relinquished itself. While that shield is up, resolving Dark-Eyes Illusionist (pegasus3, mark-punish for not acting) permanently upgrades Relinquished into Thousand-Eyes Restrict (pegasus5), which hard-stuns ALL of the target's Harmful skills for 4 turns and grants a 40 shield. The lock persists until the shield is broken.

abilities.name: Toon Assault
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

abilities.name: Relinquished
abilities.conditional_scaling: none

On counter, Pegasus gains a permanent (dur -1) 30 Shield, and the target is skill-locked from re-using the countered ability for as long as that shield exists. Relinquished itself becomes unusable while the shield is up. Shield breaking removes the target's skill-lock. Energy/tempo denial + self-protection; the key enabler of the upgrade chain.

abilities.name: Dark-Eyes Illusionist
abilities.conditional_scaling: Conditional payoff: deals 25 only if target does NOT use a new skill that turn (mark punish). If it resolves while Pegasus holds the Relinquished Shield, it permanently swaps Relinquished -> Thousand-Eyes Restrict (a 4-turn class stun). No numeric damage scaling, but a large state-upgrade payoff.

If the target stays passive, 25 Normal damage hits at end of turn. On that damage resolving with the Relinquished Shield active, Pegasus gains an ability-swap effect upgrading Relinquished into Thousand-Eyes Restrict. Tension/mind-game tool: punishes inaction and gates the transformation.

abilities.name: Thousand-Eyes Restrict
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden upgrade form of Relinquished, unlocked via the pegasus2->pegasus3 chain. Stuns all of the target's 'Harmful' class skills for dur 8 (= 4 enemy turns) and grants Pegasus a permanent 40 Shield. If the shield is destroyed, the stun ends and the skill reverts to Relinquished. Unusable while its own shield is active. Heavy, near-total offensive lockdown of a single target.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Low and flat. No stacking or scaling damage. Best-case offensive turn is roughly Toon Assault's 20 immediate + 25 from a resolved Dark-Eyes mark = 45 in one turn, plus the lingering 20/turn DoT tick. There is no damage growth ceiling; the kit caps out around 60 total from one Toon Assault over its 2-turn window. Pegasus wins through denial, not damage.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is Normal type (subject to DR/shields), except Toon Assault bypasses Invulnerability only (not DR). Dark-Eyes' 25 is conditional on the target staying passive, so reliable per-turn output is closer to 20 (Toon Assault tick) on average.

Character colors are Green+Blue. The hidden Thousand-Eyes Restrict costs Green+Blue. Cheap, low-commitment energy profile.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Cheap and spammable on the control half: Relinquished CD2, Dark-Eyes CD1, Toon Assault CD1. Thousand-Eyes Restrict is CD0 (re-castable). The only slow piece is Millennium Eye at CD4. Overall fast, low-energy tempo built for repeated disruption.
economy.ramp_dependency: Moderate state-ramp, not energy-ramp. The payoff transformation requires a 2-step setup: land Relinquished and have it counter a Harmful skill (target-dependent), then resolve Dark-Eyes' mark punish while the shield holds. Gated by enemy behavior; against passive or non-Harmful enemies the chain stalls.

power_assessment.reasoning: A specialist control/denial character that trades damage for the ability to neutralize a single threatening enemy. The escalation chain is genuinely strong on payoff: Thousand-Eyes Restrict locks ALL of a target's Harmful skills for 4 turns while Pegasus sits behind a 40 shield, which can completely take a single damage-dealer out of the game. Cheap costs (5 total visible, mostly flexible pips), low cooldowns, a 1-turn invuln panic button, and a 60-damage bypassing DoT round it out. However, its power is conditional and target-dependent: Relinquished only triggers if the enemy uses a Harmful skill within 1 turn, and the upgrade additionally requires the Dark-Eyes mark to resolve (enemy staying passive) while the shield is up — a multi-step, behavior-gated combo. It offers no team support, no healing for allies, no AoE, and low, flat damage, so it cannot close games on its own and is weak into burst/affliction comps that ignore shields or kill before the lock lands. Solid in single-target lockdown duels, mediocre as a generalist.

No DoT and no AoE; all damage bypasses flat and %DR (Piercing).

economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast offensive tempo: Thundershock (CD 0) and Thunder (CD 0) are both spammable, so Pikachu can chain damage + control every turn if energy permits. Volt Tackle is CD 1. Only Agility is slow (CD 4).

Static is applied reactively (enemy must attack Pikachu) or refreshed by Thunder once a mark exists. Until a target is marked, Volt Tackle deals no damage and the upgraded control modes are unavailable.

role: Single-target cooldown-denial controller with piercing burst and self-protection
signature_mechanic: 'Passive: Static' mark — applied reactively when an enemy targets Pikachu (5 Piercing + 1-turn mark) and refreshable by Thunder. The mark unlocks/upgrades every skill: Thundershock's 2-turn cooldown paralysis, Volt Tackle's actual 35 damage + 4-turn cooldown-increase punish, and Thunder's non-strategic stun + mark refresh, forming a cooldown soft-lock loop on a single high-value target.
internal_synergies: Thundershock cost-reduces Thunder (1 Blue + 1 Random) the same turn, enabling a 20+45 = 65 piercing burst on a tight energy budget
Static seeds the mark that powers all three offensive skills; Thunder re-casts Static on a marked target, sustaining the loop without needing the enemy to attack again
Cooldown paralysis (Thundershock) + cooldown-increase punish (Volt Tackle) + non-strategic stun (Thunder) stack into a near-total tempo lock on one target
Agility provides a defensive reset; combined with Static's reactive punish, attacking Pikachu is costly and sometimes wasted into invulnerability
strengths: Pure Piercing damage bypasses flat and percentage DR, making the 65/turn burst reliable against tanky/armored targets
Excellent single-target cooldown/tempo denial: can paralyze, increase, and stun a key enemy's skills nearly every turn
Two CD-0 damage skills give relentless turn-by-turn pressure and control
Cheap kit (5 pips for 4 skills) with 2 flexible Random pips
Agility gives a strong invulnerability panic button vs burst or to dodge a telegraphed hit
Static makes Pikachu annoying to focus and self-seeds its own mark
weaknesses: No AoE whatsoever — useless for board-wide pressure or clearing multiple threats
No healing, no shields, no cleanse — survivability is just one 4-CD invulnerability plus its base HP, and Volt Tackle self-damages 15 HP
Heavily mark-dependent: against an enemy who never attacks Pikachu, Static may never apply, gating Volt Tackle's damage and all upgraded control modes
Piercing does NOT bypass barriers/shields (only Affliction/Bleed do), so shielded targets blunt the burst
Blue-color reliant for its biggest hit (Thunder, 2 Blue)
Single-target focus means it can be kited or outscaled by AoE/sustain comps; contributes little to team fights
Reactive Static and recoil on Volt Tackle make the damage ceiling situational
win_conditions: Lock down one high-priority enemy (carry/healer) with chained cooldown paralysis + increase + stun while chipping it down with 65 piercing/turn
Use Static + Agility to make Pikachu a frustrating, low-value target that enemies waste turns into, while it dismantles their tempo
Win the energy/tempo war: deny a key target enough cooldowns that the opposing team falls behind on rotations

power_assessment.reasoning: Strong, focused single-target controller: reliable Piercing damage (65/turn, ~100 ceiling) that ignores DR, plus a deep cooldown-denial suite (paralysis + CD increase + stun) and a 1-turn invulnerability. The Static mark gives good internal synergy and a self-protecting identity. Held back from top tier by zero AoE, no healing/shields/cleanse, fragile survivability (single 4-CD invuln + recoil), and a real setup dependency — Volt Tackle and all upgraded control modes need the Static mark, which is applied reactively. It is a high-impact single-target disruptor but low-utility in team fights, landing around mid-high. Rated in isolation.

strengths: Two 0-cooldown nukes give relentless single-target pressure with no tempo gaps.
Ideal Strike is Piercing AND uncounterable AND ignores invulnerability — bypasses DR, counters, and invuln defenses simultaneously, a rare triple-bypass.
Cheap, mostly-random energy cost makes the kit easy to fund and splash into many teams.

weaknesses: Zero AoE — fully single-target, contributes nothing to multi-target swings.
No utility whatsoever: no CC, healing, shields, cleanse, energy denial, or team support.
Best burst (Ideal Strike) is self-gated behind being below 50 HP, a risky/awkward condition that often means you're already losing.
Magic Sword ramp is a tempo loss and permanently raises Knight's Sword's cost and cooldown, eroding its spam value.
Highly predictable, low-complexity kit; opponents can play around the < 50 HP execute window and the 4-CD invuln.
No way to proactively self-damage to enter the Ideal Strike window — dependent on enemy chip.

power_assessment.reasoning: A clean, low-complexity single-target duelist. Strong raw points: two 0-cooldown nukes, an exceptional triple-bypass execute (Piercing + uncounterable + ignores invuln), cheap mostly-random energy, and a self-invuln defensive button. But it is one-dimensional — no AoE, no CC, no healing/support, and its best damage is conditionally locked behind a self-detrimental < 50 HP gate that you can't reliably trigger on your own. The Magic Sword ramp is a net-neutral-to-mild payoff that costs tempo and raises the basic's cost/CD. Solid as a focused assassin/finisher in 1v1 trades, mediocre in team/AoE-heavy contexts. Lands slightly below average for a roster where most kits bring utility on top of damage.

role: single-target Bleed/Piercing sniper with anti-Strategic counter and self-protection
signature_mechanic: Bleed-stacking: apply Bleed via Bleeding Shot, then fire Close-Range Rifle whose Piercing damage scales +5 per Bleed effect on the target. Wave Tracking (passive) is supposed to mirror each new Bleed into a Shatter that makes Close-Range Rifle free — but that observer is unwired (no-op), so the Shatter/free-cast synergy does not actually function in the shipped build.

abilities.name: Bleeding Shot

Installs an ACTION_USE_TRIGGER on every living enemy: when an enemy uses a NEW Strategic skill they take 5 Bleed immediately + 5 Bleed next turn. Soft strategy/tempo denial + anti-control self-protection.

abilities.effects_summary: Full Invulnerability for 1 turn (dur 2, no class filter). Standard panic-button defend on a 4-turn cooldown.

power_assessment.reasoning: As shipped, Rakko is a below-average single-target attacker. Her damage is defense-piercing (a real edge vs tanks/shields) and she carries strong, cheap self-protection plus a nice anti-Strategic counter, but her numbers are low (peak ~30 in a turn, sustained ~10/turn DoT), she has zero AoE, and zero team utility. The kit's intended high-end (Wave Tracking mirroring Bleeds into Shatters to enable a free, spammable, Bleed-scaling Close-Range Rifle) is the whole point of her economy and is completely non-functional because rakko5 is an explicit no-op stub and no other code produces a 'Wave Tracking' Shatter. That makes rakko2's free-cast a permanently-false condition. With that synergy working she'd be a solid ~5.5-6 anti-tank zoner; broken, she lands around 4. Rated in isolation.

abilities.name: Digivolve: Kyubimon
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (fixed). Strategic, so it does NOT fire the non-Strategic passive triggers.
abilities.effects_summary: Self panic button: cleanse all harmful effects on Renamon, heal 40 HP, deal 10 Affliction to a random enemy now, then install a TICKING_TRIGGER dealing 10 Affliction to a random enemy each turn for ~3 turns. Also queues 4 ticking copies of Foxtail Inferno and a portrait-change effect — swaps Renamon's whole action bar to Foxtail Inferno while Kyubimon form is active.

abilities.name: High Speed Leap
abilities.conditional_scaling: Installs permanent passive (once): become Invulnerable to Strategic skills for 1 turn on every non-Strategic skill use. If all three triggers (Korenkyaku, Diamond Storm, High Speed Leap) are online, advances a mission counter.
abilities.effects_summary: 10 Normal on hit + self Invulnerable to non-Strategic skills for 1 turn (invuln_effect dur 2). First use permanently installs a passive: gain Invulnerable-to-Strategic for 1 turn on every non-Strategic use. 2-turn cooldown.

abilities.name: Foxtail Inferno
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden Kyubimon-form skill (the digivolve swap target). Deals 5 Affliction x3 = 15 Affliction to one enemy (bypasses barriers/shields). Free cost. Also auto-fired 4 times as ticking copies by Digivolve: Kyubimon.

role: Self-buffing ramp bruiser/skirmisher: installs permanent passive triggers that stack on-action bonus damage + invuln, with a digivolve panic button into a free Affliction DoT form
signature_mechanic: Permanent ACTION_USE_TRIGGER stacking: Korenkyaku (+10 Normal to primary), Diamond Storm (+5 Piercing to all Diamond-Storm-marked enemies), and High Speed Leap (invuln vs Strategic) each install a one-time, permanent passive that fires on EVERY non-Strategic skill use. After a 3-turn setup the kit auto-escalates every basic into multi-source damage + automatic invulnerability. Digivolve: Kyubimon is an off-ramp panic button (cleanse + heal 40 + recurring Affliction) that swaps the bar to the free Foxtail Inferno.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Ramp-capped, not stack-infinite. The three passive triggers each install exactly once, so the per-action bonus tops out at +10 Normal (primary) +5 Piercing (per Diamond-Storm-marked enemy). Fully ramped, one Korenkyaku on a marked primary = 15 base +10 trigger +5 Piercing = 30. AoE ceiling grows with number of Diamond-Storm-marked enemies: each non-Strategic action does base + (5 Piercing x marked enemies); with 3 marked that's effectively ~15 Piercing spread + DoTs. Sustained: 10 Diamond Storm DoT + ~10 Kyubimon Affliction tick + Foxtail copies in form.
damage_profile.notes: All trigger bonuses fire only on NON-Strategic skills, so the digivolve itself does not pump them. Diamond Storm DoT (10/turn) and Foxtail Inferno (15 Affliction) bypass shields/barriers; Diamond Storm passive (+5) is Piercing (skips flat+%DR). Peak single-target 30 assumes target is Diamond-Storm-marked and all triggers online. Foxtail-form burst: 4 auto ticks of Foxtail Inferno (10 Affliction each via renamon_trigger, plus manual 15) layered on the Kyubimon ticking trigger.

economy.color_dependency: High and rigid: every visible skill is a specific color and there are zero random pips. Korenkyaku=Green, Diamond Storm=Blue, High Speed Leap=White, Digivolve=Green+Blue+White. Needs all three of its colors (G/B/W) to fully ramp the trigger suite, making it color-greedy and easy to starve.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast: three of four visible skills are 0-cooldown 1-pip spammables; only High Speed Leap has a 2-turn CD. Cheap actions mean the on-action passives fire almost every turn once installed.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Effective power requires ~3 turns of setup to install all three permanent triggers (one each of Korenkyaku, Diamond Storm, High Speed Leap). Pre-ramp it is a weak 1-pip chip character; post-ramp every cheap action multiplies.

invuln_or_counter: High Speed Leap grants self Invulnerable to non-Strategic skills for 1 turn on use
Permanent passive: Invulnerable to Strategic skills for 1 turn on every non-Strategic skill use (after install) — combined, near-continuous selective invulnerability

internal_synergies: All three damage skills install permanent triggers that compound: once online, a single cheap non-Strategic action resolves base hit + Korenkyaku +10 + Diamond Storm +5 Piercing (x marked) + High Speed Leap invuln, turning 1-pip spam into multi-source value.
Diamond Storm's DoT + its passive synergize: keep enemies marked, then every non-Strategic action adds 5 Piercing to each marked target (snowballs vs multiple marked enemies).

High Speed Leap invuln (vs non-Strategic on use) + its passive (vs Strategic on every non-Strategic action) cover both damage classes — after ramp Renamon is almost always invulnerable to something while continuing to attack.
Digivolve: Kyubimon is the bail-out: cleanse + heal 40 resets a pressured Renamon, then the free Foxtail Inferno form supplies barrier-bypassing Affliction while the action-bar is locked to it.
Color trio G/B/W is exactly the digivolve cost, so a hand that can fuel the ramp can also fuel the panic button.
strengths: Self-sufficient survivability: 40 heal + full self-cleanse + frequent selective invulnerability with no team support needed
Excellent tempo/economy after ramp — 0-cooldown 1-pip actions that each trigger stacked bonus damage and invuln
Multiple defense-bypass vectors: Diamond Storm DoT + Foxtail Inferno are Affliction (ignore shields/barriers); Diamond Storm passive is Piercing (ignores DR)
Built-in answer to Strategic-skill comps via the permanent Strategic-invuln passive
Snowballs into a soft-AoE engine when several enemies are Diamond-Storm-marked
weaknesses: Slow, fragile start: needs ~3 turns to install all three triggers; pre-ramp it is just 1-pip chip damage
Rigid color dependency (G+B+W, zero random pips) — easily energy-starved or denied a color
No hard CC and no energy denial — cannot proactively stop a faster combo or interrupt setup
Low base numbers everywhere (10-15); ceiling is ramp-gated, not explosive, and capped (triggers install once, don't multi-stack)
Digivolve is Strategic, so it doesn't advance the trigger ramp and locks the bar to a single free skill; commitment cost while in Kyubimon form
Invuln is conditional/selective (only one damage class at a time per source) — true/unconditional damage and well-timed Strategic+non-Strategic mixes can punch through
win_conditions: Survive the opening, install all three permanent triggers, then grind out enemies with stacked cheap actions while staying selectively invulnerable
Spread Diamond Storm marks across the enemy team and convert every non-Strategic action into multi-target Piercing AoE
Use Digivolve: Kyubimon to reset under pressure (cleanse+heal) and out-attrition with barrier-ignoring Affliction from the Foxtail form

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-designed ramp/attrition character with strong sustain (heal+cleanse), repeated selective invulnerability, and multiple defense-bypass damage types, all on a cheap fast-tempo kit. Its power is real but back-loaded: numbers are low (10-15 base, 30 peak single-target, 20/turn sustained) and the payoff is gated behind ~3 turns of trigger installation with no CC or energy denial to protect that setup. Rigid G/B/W color needs and zero random pips make it deniable. In isolation it lands as a solid B-tier scaling skirmisher: hard to kill and oppressive if left to ramp, but beatable by fast burst, energy starvation, true damage, and comps that race it before the triggers come online.
outlier_flags: Permanent (-1 duration) passive triggers that never expire — unusually persistent self-buff engine
Stacking on-action triggers mean a single 1-pip 0-CD skill resolves 3+ damage/effect sources at once
Diamond Storm passive is uncapped-target AoE Piercing scaling with number of marked enemies
Digivolve swaps the entire action bar to a single free 0-cost Affliction skill (Foxtail Inferno), an unusual transformation that trades flexibility for free barrier-bypassing damage
DoT effect duration arg (7) vs split_desc '4 turns' is a likely description/code mismatch worth flagging

role: single-target Shatter-enabled burst duelist with Bleed DoT and a team counter
signature_mechanic: Shatter (DEF_NEGATE) loop: Rengoku applies Shatter to strip the target's damage reduction AND invulnerability, then his Bleed/swap abilities deal extra duration/magnitude against Shattered foes. His whole Piercing kit already bypasses DR, and Shatter further opens the target up for himself and his allies.

abilities.name: Second Form: Rising Scorching Sun
abilities.conditional_scaling: If target already Shattered, Shatter duration extends by +2 (an extra turn). No damage scaling.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Piercing (skips flat+%DR). Applies Shatter/DEF_NEGATE dur 3 (until end of Rengoku's next turn); +2 dur if target already Shattered. Shatter removes the target's DR and invuln, enabling allied follow-up.

abilities.name: Swift Sword Slash
abilities.conditional_scaling: Bleed 5/turn normally; doubled to 10/turn if target is Shattered (on-Shatter scaling).
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Piercing instant + Bleed DoT 5/turn for 2 turns (Bleed bypasses barriers/shields/DR). If target Shattered, Bleed becomes 10/turn. No cooldown - spammable filler.

abilities.name: Fourth Form: Blooming Flame Undulation
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Team-wide (all allies) invisible counter for 1 turn: first harmful skill used on any ally is countered. On trigger, the ENTIRE enemy team is Shattered (DEF_NEGATE) for 1 turn - mass armor-strip + invuln-strip enabling team follow-up. Counter then clears from all allies.

abilities.name: Esoteric Art
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self utility: full-removes all DAMAGE-type effects from Rengoku (cleanses DoTs/Bleeds/poisons on himself), grants Stun-ignore for 1 turn (stays uncontrolled), and swaps slot 4 into Ninth Form: Rengoku (rengoku5) - his transformation/finisher. Panic-button + setup.

abilities.name: Ninth Form: Rengoku
abilities.conditional_scaling: Bleed duration extends by +1 turn if target is Shattered. Damage flat 40.
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden alt unlocked via rengoku4 swap. 40 Normal damage (subject to DR/shields, unlike his Piercing skills) + Bleed 5/turn for 2 turns (+1 turn if Shattered). Uncounterable. No cooldown but gated behind the swap. Main burst finisher.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No multiplicative ramp. Pre-transform on a Shattered target: rengoku1 (20 Piercing) + rengoku2 (15 Piercing, applies 10/turn Bleed) = 35 instant plus stacking Bleeds. Post-swap: rengoku5 (40 Normal) + rengoku2 (15 Piercing) = 55 instant in one turn on a Shattered foe, plus 5-10/turn Bleed ticks. True ceiling is incremental DoT stacking, not one big number.
damage_profile.notes: Instant damage is modest (15-40 per hit). rengoku1/rengoku2 are Piercing (ignore flat+%DR); rengoku5 is plain Normal (mitigable). Peak single-target ~55 = post-swap rengoku5(40)+rengoku2(15) on a Shattered target. Bleed bypasses barriers/shields/DR, making sustained DoT (up to ~20/turn with both bleeds rolling and Shatter doubling r2) his most reliable damage. Zero AoE damage (rengoku3 is counter/utility, deals 0).

economy.color_dependency: Moderate. Visible kit is Red:2 (r1, r3) + Green:1 (r2) + Random:1 (r4) - leans Red with a Green splash. Transformation (rengoku5) costs Green:1+Red:1, exactly his dual-color identity. Two-color (Green/Red) but very cheap per skill.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Fast on damage, slow on utility. rengoku2 is 0-CD spammable filler; rengoku1 is 1-CD; rengoku5 is 0-CD (but swap-gated). Utility is locked behind long cooldowns: rengoku3 at 3-CD, rengoku4 at 4-CD.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low-to-moderate. No stack/ramp economy. The only ramp is the Shatter->Bleed/swap conditional: he wants to land Shatter first (via r1 or r3) to unlock 10/turn Bleed and extended durations, and to spend a turn on rengoku4 to access his 40-damage finisher.

soft_cc: Shatter/DEF_NEGATE single-target (rengoku1)
Shatter whole enemy team on counter trigger (rengoku3)
invuln_or_counter: Team-wide single-instance counter for 1 turn (rengoku3)
Stun-ignore self for 1 turn (rengoku4)

win_conditions: Land Shatter (r1 or r3) then grind the target down with doubled (10/turn) Bleed from r2 and Piercing instants that ignore DR.
Use rengoku4 to access Ninth Form (rengoku5, 40 + extended Bleed, Uncounterable) for a burst-and-bleed kill on a Shattered, defense-broken target.
Enable allies: Shatter strips enemy DR AND invuln, so Rengoku acts as a setup piece for a burst teammate to delete a Shattered foe.
Bait a harmful skill into rengoku3's team counter, then Shatter the whole enemy team for a coordinated follow-up window.
internal_synergies: Shatter (r1/r3) -> Swift Sword Slash (r2): Shatter doubles r2 Bleed from 5 to 10/turn.
Shatter (r1/r3) -> r1 again: re-Shatter on an already-Shattered target extends Shatter by +2 dur, sustaining the defense-break window.
Shatter -> Ninth Form (r5): Shatter extends r5 Bleed by +1 turn.
rengoku4 cleanses his own DoTs/damage effects AND grants Stun-ignore the same turn it sets up the finisher swap - defensive pivot into offense.
rengoku3 counter trigger applies team-wide Shatter, multiplying the value of any allied (or his own) follow-up burst.
Piercing on r1/r2 means his pressure works even before Shatter lands, and Shatter additionally opens the target's invuln for the whole team.
strengths: Excellent defense-counterplay: Piercing instants ignore DR; Bleed ignores shields/barriers/DR; Shatter strips DR AND invuln for himself and allies.
Very cheap, spammable pressure (rengoku2 is 1-cost, 0-CD with a DoT rider).
Self-sufficient survivability tools: self-cleanse of damage effects + Stun-ignore via rengoku4.
A rare team-wide counter (rengoku3) that doubles as a mass armor/invuln-strip setup.
Uncounterable finisher (rengoku5) that bypasses defensive counter strategies.
Strong enabler/support-adjacent role despite being a damage dealer - Shatter makes him valuable in any composition.
weaknesses: Low raw instant numbers (15-40); no single nuke and zero AoE damage - slow to close games alone.
Best burst (rengoku5) is gated behind spending a full turn on rengoku4 (4-CD) to transform.
rengoku5 is plain Normal damage, so it is fully mitigated by DR/shields unless he first Shatters the target - adds a sequencing tax.
Utility (counter, transform/cleanse) sits on long 3- and 4-turn cooldowns; once spent he is just cheap pokes.
No healing, no shields, no hard CC, no energy denial - limited disruptive ceiling.
rengoku3's counter is a single-instance, telegraph-dependent effect that expires in 1 turn if unused; a patient opponent can play around it.
Damage is heavily back-loaded into DoT, so he underperforms against cleanse-heavy or fast-kill enemy teams.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, technically rich enabler-duelist rather than a raw-power outlier. His standout value is defense counterplay: a kit of Piercing + Bleed damage that ignores DR/shields, plus Shatter that strips DR AND invuln for himself and his whole team - extremely valuable against tanks, shield/DR comps, and invuln-pivot characters. Economy is excellent (4-pip visible kit, a 0-CD spammable, dual Green/Red identity). However, raw output is modest: ~55 single-target burst under ideal Shattered conditions, ~20/turn sustained Bleed, and zero AoE damage. His best burst and his cleanse/transform are gated behind a turn investment and long cooldowns, and rengoku5's Normal damage needs Shatter to land properly. He grades as a solid, flexible mid-tier: high utility/enabler value, capped damage ceiling.
outlier_flags: defense-strip (Shatter removes invuln + DR) is high-leverage utility that can over/under-value him depending on enemy DR/invuln density across the roster
team-wide counter is an uncommon effect worth comparing against other counter-providers in Phase 2

universe: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
role: Affliction-DoT control mage with a one-shot power spike (Megiddo) that transforms his whole kit into AoE/counter mode; secondary self-sustain panic button
signature_mechanic: Megiddo: a once-per-game AoE that plants a permanent, unremovable, non-cleansable 5 Affliction-per-turn DoT on every enemy and irreversibly upgrades his first three skills into stronger alternate versions (AoE piercing stun, cost-free harmful counter-copy, and a cleanse/heal-or-shatter flex tool). A separate Slime Transformation panic state locks him into self-heal + effect-immunity then a single-target nuke.

abilities.name: Black Flame
abilities.conditional_scaling: After Megiddo, target_change makes it hit ALL enemies for +1 Random cost (still 15 Affliction each); also swaps to alt rimuru5 (Black Flame Thunder, 20 Piercing AoE) under Demon Lord Awakening
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Affliction (bypasses shields/barriers/DR) to one enemy + stuns their non-Strategic skills for 1 turn (stun_effect dur 2). Cheap repeatable poke + soft lockout of a target's offensive/utility skills.

abilities.name: Gluttony
abilities.conditional_scaling: After Megiddo, swaps to a counter variant (Beezlebuth/rimuru6): counters + copies the next harmful skill cost-free for 1 turn instead of paralyzing
abilities.effects_summary: Invisible action-use trigger mark for 1 turn: if the marked enemy uses a new skill, that skill is copied to Rimuru (copy_effect slot 1, 2 turns) and the enemy's cooldowns are Paralyzed (paralyze_effect 3 = ~1 turn). Skill theft + cooldown denial; punishes the enemy's tempo.

abilities.name: Megiddo
abilities.conditional_scaling: Once-per-game power spike (extra_usable gated by not already marked). Permanently swaps slots 1-3 to alternates (rimuru1 AoE mode, Gluttony->counter, Megiddo->cost-increased Black Flame AoE)
abilities.effects_summary: 25 Normal damage to the whole enemy team (DamageType.NORMAL in .gd, not Affliction as JSON claims), PLUS plants a permanent (dur -1) 5 Affliction/turn DoT on every enemy that is remove_on_death=false and cleansable=false (unremovable, ignores death-cleanup). Then self-marks, makes Black Flame AoE (+1 Random), and converts Gluttony to a counter. The defining ramp button.

abilities.name: Slime Transformation
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self panic button: heals 15 immediately + 15/turn for 2 turns (healing_effect 15 dur 3) and ignores all harmful NON-DAMAGE effects for 2 turns (ignore_non_damage_effect dur 4) = stun/cc/debuff immunity. Locks Rimuru into Demon Summon (rimuru8) as the only usable skill while active.

abilities.name: Black Flame Thunder (alt of slot 1, Demon Lord Awakening)
abilities.conditional_scaling: Only usable while NOT in Slime Transformation
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Piercing AoE (skips flat + %DR) to all enemies + stuns their non-Strategic skills for 1 turn. Post-awakening upgrade of Black Flame.

abilities.name: Beezlebuth (alt of slot 2)
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Invisible counter for 1 turn: if target uses a new Harmful skill, it is countered (negated) and copied to Rimuru cost-free for 1 turn. Upgrade of Gluttony into a denial+theft counter.

abilities.name: Demon Summon flex / alt slot 3 (any-target)
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Flex tool: on an ally, cleanses ALL hostile Affliction effects + heals 15; on an enemy, Shatters (def_negate, removes their defensive negation) and -15 damage (damage_mod) for 1 turn. Cleanse + heal or anti-tank debuff.

abilities.name: Demon Summon (Slime Transformation lock)
abilities.conditional_scaling: Only skill usable while Slime Transformation is active
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Normal single-target damage. The lone action available during the Slime Transformation immune/heal window.

abilities.name: Passive: Demon Lord Awakening
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Awakening payload: cleanses all enemy effects from Rimuru, heals his entire TEAM 20 HP, grants himself permanent +5 HP/turn (healing_effect dur -1, non-cleansable), and permanently swaps slots 1-3 to alternates (rimuru5/6/7). Strong team-heal + self-regen + kit upgrade.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Permanent 5 Affliction/turn per enemy from Megiddo is unremovable and uncleansable, so vs a full 3-enemy team it compounds to 15 unavoidable Affliction/turn for the rest of the game (bypasses shields/DR). Single-turn peak is modest: pre-Megiddo ~15 Affliction single-target; Megiddo turn = 25 AoE Normal + 5 Affliction tick; post-awakening Black Flame Thunder = 20 Piercing AoE + the 5/turn DoT. No multiplicative or per-stack burst; value is in inevitability and lockdown, not nukes.
damage_profile.notes: rimuru1 base_damage is 15 Affliction in the .gd (JSON/describe text claiming 20 is stale). Megiddo deals DamageType.NORMAL (25), not Affliction, despite the Affliction class tag and JSON. Affliction/Piercing routing means most of his damage ignores defensive layers, raising effective damage above the raw numbers.

economy.color_dependency: High and three-color (Green+White+Red). Megiddo alone demands one of each of his three colors (G/W/R) in a single turn, and Black Flame needs White while Gluttony needs Green, so he wants all three colors flowing every turn. Only Slime Transformation is flexible (Random). Heavy specific-color dependency makes him awkward to fuel on a multi-color team.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Low/repeatable on the poke tools (Black Flame CD 1, Gluttony CD 2, Megiddo CD 0) so he can apply pressure every turn; the panic/transform button is slow (Slime Transformation CD 4). Megiddo is once-per-game rather than cooldown-gated.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. The kit is built around the Megiddo / Demon Lord Awakening spike: pre-spike he is a low-damage poke+control unit, post-spike he gains permanent team-wide DoT, AoE piercing stun, a cost-free counter, and team sustain. Power is heavily back-loaded behind landing that single button.

hard_cc: full cooldown Paralyze on Gluttony trigger
soft_cc: non-Strategic skill stun (Black Flame / Black Flame Thunder)
Megiddo permanent DoT pressure
invuln_or_counter: Slime Transformation: immune to all harmful non-damage effects for 2 turns
Gluttony/Beezlebuth: copy + counter of enemy skills
Demon Summon flex: Shatter (def_negate) enemy defenses

win_conditions: Land Megiddo early to stamp permanent uncleansable 5/turn Affliction on the whole enemy team, then run out the clock as the inevitable DoT outpaces their sustain
Use Black Flame / Black Flame Thunder stuns to lock down the enemy's key non-Strategic skills while the DoT and counters grind them down
Steal the enemy's strongest skill via Gluttony/Beezlebuth copy and paralyze/counter their action economy, winning the tempo war
Survive burst with Slime Transformation's heal + effect immunity and Demon Lord Awakening's team heal + permanent regen, outlasting opponents
internal_synergies: Megiddo is the lynchpin: it both applies the permanent DoT AND irreversibly upgrades slots 1-3 (Black Flame -> AoE, Gluttony -> cost-free counter), so a single button multiplies the whole kit's value
Black Flame's non-Strategic stun pairs with Gluttony's copy/paralyze to deny enemies both their offense (stun) and their tempo (paralyze) at once
Permanent Affliction DoT (bypasses shields/DR) synergizes with the stuns to make enemy defensive turns wasted; they can't cleanse it and can't easily out-heal it
Slime Transformation's effect immunity protects the ramp window; Demon Lord Awakening's team heal + self-regen lets him stall until the DoT closes the game
Demon Summon flex (post-awakening) can cleanse the very Affliction type he specializes in off allies, covering his own team's weakness to enemy DoT
strengths: Permanent, unremovable, uncleansable team-wide Affliction DoT (remove_on_death=false, cleansable=false), a rare inevitability engine that bypasses shields/barriers/DR
Strong, repeatable control: cheap non-Strategic stun (CD 1) plus a full cooldown Paralyze and skill-copy on Gluttony
Excellent self/team survivability: Slime Transformation (15 + 15/turn heal + harmful-non-damage immunity) and Demon Lord Awakening (team 20 heal + permanent self-regen + cleanse)
Skill theft + counter denies enemy carries their best tools and refunds Rimuru cost-free copies
Damage routes through Affliction/Piercing, so effective damage is higher than the raw numbers against defensive comps
Megiddo has CD 0 and the awakening upgrades are permanent, so his power spike is sticky once achieved
weaknesses: Very low burst; peak single-turn output is ~20-25 and he cannot quickly close out a low-HP target, losing races against burst assassins
Heavily ramp/spike dependent: pre-Megiddo he is a weak poke+control unit, and Megiddo is once-per-game so a mistimed or interrupted spike is costly
Three-color specific cost (G+W+R), with Megiddo wanting one of each in a single turn, makes him hard to fuel and vulnerable to energy starvation
Slime Transformation locks him into Demon Summon only (20 single-target), a defensive turn that surrenders his control/AoE while active
DoT-centric win condition is slow; against teams with strong lifesteal/sustain or heavy burst he can still be out-tempo'd before the DoT matters
Gluttony's value is conditional on the enemy choosing to act into the mark; passive/skip turns blank it

power_assessment.reasoning: Rimuru is a high-ceiling inevitability/control unit rather than a damage dealer. His standout is Megiddo's permanent, uncleansable, death-persisting team-wide Affliction DoT (15/turn vs a full team) combined with a permanent kit upgrade and strong sustain; that is a genuine long-game win condition that bypasses most defensive answers. Repeatable cheap stuns, a full Paralyze, skill-copy/counter, cc-immunity, cleanse, and team healing give him an unusually deep toolkit across control, denial, and sustain. He is held back from top-tier by anemic burst (peak ~20-25 in a turn), heavy back-loading behind a once-per-game button, and a punishing three-specific-color cost that makes consistent fueling hard. He should reliably grind down most teams given time but is exploitable by fast burst and energy pressure before the spike lands. Mid-7 in isolation; could swing higher if the permanent DoT proves oppressive across the roster.
outlier_flags: Permanent uncleansable + remove_on_death=false Affliction DoT from Megiddo is a strong outlier mechanic and a potential balance flag for long matches

Stale-data mismatch: rimuru1 .gd base_damage=15 Affliction but describe()/JSON say 20; Megiddo is DamageType.NORMAL in .gd despite Affliction class/JSON, so engine ground truth differs from displayed text
Once-per-game irreversible kit transformation (Megiddo/Awakening) is unusual and makes balance non-linear over a match

universe: Original / Anime Arena (water-elemental spirit; not from a referenced licensed anime — same "elemental" family as Gaia/Pyrrha)
role: AoE chip-damage controller / mark-and-stun setup mage with a self-protect and a counter
signature_mechanic: "Current" stacks: an invisible mark applied by Current/River Clone that turns Undertow into a single-target stun (consuming a stack). Ripple temporarily makes Undertow hit the whole team, enabling a team-wide stun if Current has been spread; Dive (self damage-immunity) can double Ripple's AoE-Undertow window. Each Current cast also grants Elemental Essence energy ramp.

abilities.name: Current
abilities.damage_type: Normal (assumed; no .gd on disk to confirm a special type)
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (flat); engine ramp via Elemental Essence gain
abilities.effects_summary: 10 AoE to enemy team; applies 1 invisible stack of Current to the primary target (sets up Undertow stun); grants River Daughter Elemental Essence (energy ramp). 0 cooldown spammable.

abilities.name: Undertow
abilities.cost_breakdown: 1 Red/Water pip (Element idx 3 = WATER; specific color)
abilities.target_type: SINGLE (becomes ALL while Ripple is active)
abilities.conditional_scaling: Conditional control payload, not damage scaling: stun + stack-consume only if target has Current
abilities.effects_summary: 20 to one enemy. If target has Current: stun 1 turn and consume one Current stack. Becomes team-wide (20 to all + AoE stun on all Current-marked) for 1 turn after Ripple. 0 cooldown.

abilities.name: Ripple
abilities.conditional_scaling: none; enables the AoE-Undertow combo window
abilities.effects_summary: 10 AoE to enemy team and, for 1 turn, Undertow targets all enemies (turning the next Undertow into a 20 AoE + team-wide stun on Current-marked enemies). 1-turn cooldown. Window can be doubled to 2 turns if Dive was used the prior turn.

abilities.name: Dive
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Self-protect: River Daughter ignores all damaging effects for 1 turn (damage invulnerability). The following turn, Ripple gains double duration (its AoE-Undertow window lasts 2 turns instead of 1). 0 cooldown. No cleanse implied — only blocks incoming damage.

abilities.name: River Clone
abilities.conditional_scaling: If the counter actually triggers, target gains a 2nd Current stack (on-counter bonus)
abilities.effects_summary: Counter: negates the first harmful skill the target enemy uses for 1 turn, and applies 1 stack of Current to them. If the enemy is actually countered, they gain a 2nd Current stack — stacking Undertow stun fuel. Listed in slot 5 per index, though it reads as a normal usable skill.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No real damage scaling. Power scales horizontally through control: spreading Current (Current AoE primary-mark + River Clone +1/+2 stacks) then Ripple→AoE Undertow to convert marks into a team-wide stun. Ceiling is how many enemies you can stun-lock per turn, not damage.
damage_profile.notes: All numbers flat and small. Single-target ceiling in one turn = Current 10 (AoE incl. target) + Ripple 10 (AoE) + Undertow 20 = 40 on the primary target, plus a 1-turn stun. AoE ceiling = with Ripple's window active, Current 10 + Ripple 10 + AoE-Undertow 20 = 40 to EVERY enemy in one turn, plus team-wide stun on all Current-marked enemies (the real payoff is the control, not the chip). Damage type/scaling unverified — referenced .gd scripts (res://abilities/scripts/river_daughter_*.gd) do not exist on disk; numbers from abilities_data.json descriptions.

economy.color_dependency: Light. Only Undertow and Ripple need the specific Red/Water pip; Current and Dive cost a flexible Generic/Random pip. Across the 4 visible skills: 2 specific (Red) + 2 generic/random. Easy to slot into most teams.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Extremely fast. Current, Undertow, and Dive are all 0-cooldown; only Ripple has a 1-turn cooldown. Can fire 2-3 abilities per turn for ~1-2 pips each (Current+Undertow mark→stun, or Current+Ripple AoE, every turn).
economy.ramp_dependency: Self-feeds via Elemental Essence on every Current cast (helps pay the rest of the kit/team), but the kit is cheap and works without ramp. Mild positive ramp, not gated on it.

team-wide 1-turn stun via Ripple→AoE Undertow on all Current-marked enemies
soft_cc: invisible Current mark (setup debuff, no direct effect until Undertow)
invuln_or_counter: Dive: 1-turn self damage-immunity (ignores all damaging effects)
River Clone: counters the first harmful skill an enemy uses for 1 turn

win_conditions: Spread Current marks (Current AoE primary-mark + River Clone) onto the enemy team, then use Ripple to make Undertow AoE and stun every marked enemy for a turn — chaining into a team-wide stun-lock
Grind enemies down with cheap 0-cooldown AoE chip (Current + Ripple = 20 AoE/turn) while denying enemy turns via stuns
Outlast a key threat with Dive (damage immunity) + River Clone (counter) to nullify a big enemy skill, then convert the tempo into stun setup
internal_synergies: Current applies the mark + ramps energy; Undertow converts the mark into a stun and consumes it — the core 0-cd combo
Ripple turns Undertow into a team-wide stun engine, multiplying the value of every Current/River Clone mark
Dive both protects River Daughter for a turn AND doubles Ripple's AoE-Undertow window next turn — a defensive turn that pays off offensively
River Clone seeds Current on a target (and a 2nd stack if it actually counters), feeding Undertow/AoE-Undertow stuns even on enemies Current's primary-mark didn't hit

strengths: Cheap, fast kit: multiple 0-cooldown skills, low and partly-flexible pip costs, can act 2-3 times per turn
Strong stun control that scales to the whole enemy team via the Ripple→AoE-Undertow combo

Built-in energy ramp (Elemental Essence) that benefits the whole team
Low color dependency — easy to fit into many drafts
weaknesses: Very low raw damage (10/10/20 flat, ~40 ceiling per turn even comboed) — poor at killing; relies on teammates to convert stuns
Control is conditional and setup-heavy: Undertow only stuns if Current was applied, and the AoE stun needs Ripple pre-cast + marks already spread — multi-turn telegraph
Dive only blocks damage (no cleanse) and lasts a single turn; vulnerable to afflictions/debuffs and to being focused before the immunity turn
River Clone counters only the FIRST harmful skill and only for 1 turn — easily baited with a throwaway ability
No healing, no ally shields, no stealth — purely a controller; weak solo carry
Implementation risk: the referenced ability .gd scripts do not exist on disk, so exact damage types/durations/interactions are unverified

power_assessment.reasoning: In isolation, a solid disruption controller. The standout is the Ripple→AoE-Undertow combo: a potential team-wide 1-turn stun (extendable to 2 turns via Dive) for very little energy — high-value tempo denial. Backed by genuine survivability (a full damage-immunity turn + a skill counter) and self-ramp, it is hard to punish and pays into a team. However raw output is tiny (~40/turn ceiling, no scaling, no DoT, no execute), so it cannot close games alone and depends entirely on allied damage to capitalize on stuns. The control is also conditional and telegraphed (needs marks pre-spread and Ripple pre-cast), giving counterplay windows. Net: above-average utility, below-average kill power — a 6, leaning support-controller. Confidence is held down because the actual .gd scripts are missing; if hidden mechanics (longer stuns, stack-scaling damage, bigger Current payoffs) exist in the unimplemented scripts, this could be a 7+.

role: Piercing single-target assassin with a condition-based execute and barrier/buff punisher (swap-form burst)

His whole kit is Piercing/affliction-flavored anti-defense, climaxing in a no-damage instant-kill (rob7).

abilities.name: Neko Neko no Mi, Model: Leopard
abilities.conditional_scaling: Refreshes to ~2 turns each time an Alternate skill is used
abilities.effects_summary: Passive: using any Alternate skill (rob5-8) grants Leopard form for ~2 turns -> Rob IGNORES all non-damage effects (full CC/debuff/control immunity) and his Alternate skills cost 1 less Red energy. Self-sustaining once entered; portrait/profile change.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: No conventional damage scaling. Hard ceiling on raw numbers is 35 Piercing single-target (rob5) or 30 Piercing AoE (rob6; rob2 can also reach 30 per enemy vs DR-stacked targets). The real ceiling is rob7's instant-kill: any HP target dies if it meets 2 of {Shield, DR, <60 HP}, effectively unbounded effective damage on the right target. No per-stack/per-turn ramp.
damage_profile.notes: All offense is Piercing (skips flat+%DR), Affliction-vs-shields (bypasses barriers/shields/DR), or a flat execute, so effective damage far exceeds raw numbers against defensive targets; rob5 also bypasses Invulnerability. No DoT. He uses one skill per turn, so peak-one-turn equals the single best skill, not a combo.

economy.color_dependency: Primarily Red (every visible offensive skill needs Red), with White:1 appearing on Alternate forms rob5/rob7. Identity colors White+Red. Moderate-to-high Red dependency, eased once Leopard refunds 1 Red on Alternate skills.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Very fast on the visible bar: rob1 and rob4 cooldown 0, rob2/rob3 cooldown 1. Alternates are heavier (rob7/rob8 cooldown 2). Visible kit totals only 5 pips for all 4 skills, making him very energy-efficient turn to turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low/medium. No stacking ramp, but he must prime by using a base skill to expose the stronger Alternate, and ideally enter Leopard form for CC-immunity + Red discount; once in Leopard he refreshes it by continuing to use Alternates.

power_assessment.reasoning: Rob is a specialist anti-defense/execute assassin with an excellent toolkit but a deliberately low raw-damage ceiling. The standout is rob7's conditional instant-kill plus a stack of defense-piercing tools (bypass invuln, strip counters, affliction-vs-shield, piercing everywhere) and full CC-immunity via Leopard. Against tank/shield/counter/invuln comps he can be oppressive (near-free target removal at ~3 pips). Against squishy aggro lacking Shield/DR he drops to a slightly-below-average bruiser whose marquee skill is dead weight. That conditionality, plus no healing/support and Red dependence, keeps him from top-tier generalist status. High skill expression and clear hard counters place him at a solid 7 -- a strong matchup-dependent pick, not a safe blind pick.

rob6 wipes ALL enemy Counter+Reflect team-wide and is itself uncounterable -- very strong vs an entire archetype
rob9 Leopard grants total non-damage-effect immunity, neutering most CC/debuff characters against him

power_assessment.reasoning: As designed, Ruler is a low-damage utility/control specialist: a 1-for-1 mutual stun, a protective single-target counter, a self-invuln, and a flexible chip/shield filler. Strengths are excellent color flexibility (only 1 specific pip), cheap costs, and strong single-target defensive disruption (counter + invuln + barrier). But the payoffs are weak and heavily constrained: ruler1's self-stun and rising cooldown make her stun a poor trade and unrepeatable; her only reliable damage is 20 Physical; the 35 Piercing is reactive and out of her control; she has no AoE, no DoT, no healing, no energy denial, and no scaling. She is a passive, reactive support that contributes little proactively and can be ignored, making her low-impact in isolation. Floored further by the fact she currently does nothing (stub execute). Rated 3.5/10 on intended design.

Self-preservation stack (destructible defense + invuln) makes the squishy utility piece hard to remove.
Piercing on the counter bypasses flat and % DR, so the punish lands cleanly on tanky attackers.

role: Mono-Red damage-fueled bruiser/scaler: a tanky single-target nuker who converts damage taken into escalating burst, with built-in team healing/sustain
signature_mechanic: To the Extreme!! stacks — Ryohei gains a stack every 20 total damage he RECEIVES (and 1/turn during Vongola Headgear); each stack adds +15 to Maximum Cannon and +1 random cost, consumed all-at-once on use. The more punishment he absorbs, the bigger his nuke / longer his heal.

abilities.name: Maximum Cannon
abilities.cost_breakdown: Red:1 (+1 Random per To the Extreme!! stack consumed)
abilities.effects_summary: Single-target nuke, 25 base damage. +15 damage per To the Extreme!! stack and consumes ALL stacks on use. Becomes Piercing (skips flat+%DR) while Vongola Headgear is active. No CC or debuff attached. 0 cooldown spammable.
abilities.conditional_scaling: +15 damage per To the Extreme!! stack (consumes all stacks); Headgear converts damage to Piercing

abilities.name: Kangaryu
abilities.cost_breakdown: Red:1 (+1 Random per To the Extreme!! stack consumed)
abilities.effects_summary: Instant team heal for 10. With a To the Extreme!! stack active, ALSO applies a 10/turn heal-over-time for duration = 1+stacks*2 turns and consumes all stacks. With Vongola Headgear active, additionally grants every ally 10 damage reduction for (duration-1) turns. AoE sustain + DR support.
abilities.conditional_scaling: HoT duration scales +2 turns per To the Extreme!! stack; Headgear adds 10 DR to all allies

abilities.name: Vongola Headgear
abilities.effects_summary: Self setup for 3 turns: ignores harmful Stun effects (stun immunity) and harmful Cost-Mod effects (energy/cost-tamper immunity). While active Maximum Cannon becomes Piercing, Kangaryu grants allies 10 DR, and Ryohei gains 1 To the Extreme!! stack each turn via a ticking trigger (~3 free stacks over the window, independent of damage taken).
abilities.conditional_scaling: Generates 1 To the Extreme!! stack per turn for 3 turns (guaranteed ramp without needing to take damage)

abilities.name: To the Extreme!!
abilities.effects_summary: Free activator. Immediately grants 1 To the Extreme!! stack and installs a permanent passive: for the rest of the game, every 20 total damage Ryohei RECEIVES grants another stack (counter rolls over). Each stack adds +15 to Maximum Cannon and +1 random cost. One-time use (cannot recast once marked).
abilities.conditional_scaling: Open-ended: stacks accrue 1 per 20 damage received with no cap — scaling ceiling is determined by how much damage Ryohei soaks

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Uncapped. Maximum Cannon = 25 + 15*stacks. Realistic mid-game with ~3 stacks from Headgear ticks = 70 (piercing). Tanky games where Ryohei soaks 100+ damage yield 5-7 stacks = 100-130+ piercing in a single hit, but each stack also adds +1 random cost, so a 7-stack cannon costs ~8 energy. Self-throttling: bigger nuke = bigger price.
damage_profile.notes: Listed peak_single_target ~130 assumes ~7 accrued stacks (140 damage soaked + Headgear) at very high energy cost; this is an extreme upper bound, not typical. No native AoE damage and no DoT — peak_aoe and sustained_dot are 0. Base 25/turn at 0 stacks. Damage type is Normal (full DR applies) unless Headgear is up, which makes it Piercing.

economy.color_dependency: Mono-Red: two of three active abilities (Maximum Cannon, Kangaryu) require exactly 1 Red each; Headgear takes 1 Random. Narrow Red commitment. Scaling makes the kit progressively more energy-hungry — every consumed stack adds +1 Random to the next Cannon/Kangaryu cast, so a fully-stacked nuke or long heal can balloon to 5-8 total pips.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Maximum Cannon and To the Extreme!! are 0-CD (Cannon fully spammable). Kangaryu CD 2 (every other turn). Headgear CD 4 (windowed setup). Fast on offense, throttled on sustain/setup.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Power is gated behind To the Extreme!! stacks, which require either taking ~20 damage per stack or running Headgear for free 1/turn ticks. Cold-opens at a weak 25-damage nuke; needs a few turns (or to be focused) before payoff. Stack-consume design makes burst bursty, not sustained.

Single-target only on offense — no AoE damage and zero pressure on multiple threats

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-designed self-balancing scaler. The damage-taken stack engine plus Headgear's free ramp gives a real piercing-burst ceiling (70-130+) that punishes focus-fire and turtle comps, and the Kangaryu heal/HoT + DR plus stun/cost-mod immunity give him strong survivability and team value for a damage character. Held back from top-tier by a weak early game (25-damage opener, no CC), all-or-nothing stack consumption that makes burst spiky and self-throttling (+1 cost per stack can price out the big hits), and a complete lack of hard control or shields. Effective in attrition/tank-heavy matchups, mediocre against fast burst/assassin comps that kill him before he ramps. Solidly above average but not oppressive — a 6.

abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Standard default_defend: Ryuko becomes invulnerable for 1 turn. Pure panic button / survivability tool on a 4-turn cooldown.

damage_profile.notes: Fiber Lost is the only damage source: 20 base Normal, single-target. Under Decapitation Mode it hits ALL enemies for the same per-target value (20 -> AoE), so 'AoE one turn' is 20 per enemy (60 across a 3-enemy team) but each instance is still 20. Permanent +10-per-kill snowball raises the per-hit number indefinitely (30/40/50...) given successful executes — so the listed 20 is the FLOOR, not the ceiling. No CD means it repeats every turn. damage_cap(20) on target is defensive, not damage.
damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Unbounded in theory: each kill with Fiber Lost adds a permanent +10 flat damage (and +10 HP heal). Late game a fed Ryuko can land 40-60+ per Fiber Lost hit. Realistic ceiling is gated by needing actual kills with the move and enemy HP/barriers; Normal damage is fully blocked by barriers/shields/DR.

economy.color_dependency: Light/moderate: 1 Green (Fiber Lost) + 1 Red (Life Fiber Sync) — two-color identity (Green/Red) but only 1 pip each; Block is 1 random. Decapitation Mode adds +1 random per affected skill, raising effective cost when in AoE mode.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent: main nuke (Fiber Lost) and the AoE toggle are both 0 cooldown — Ryuko can attack every single turn. Support (CD3) and invuln (CD4) are the only gated tools.
economy.ramp_dependency: High for damage ceiling: kit is cheap and functional turn 1, but its standout power (the +10/kill snowball) requires landing kills with Fiber Lost over the game. Without kills she is a flat 20-per-turn poke with utility.

Decapitation Mode + Life Fiber Synchronization: converts the single-ally heal trigger into a team-wide reactive sustain buff for +1 random energy.
Fiber Lost kill -> permanent +10 damage + 10 heal: self-reinforcing loop; more kills make future Fiber Losts more lethal AND keep Ryuko healthy, accelerating further kills.
Fiber Lost damage_cap pairs defensively with Life Fiber Synchronization: capping enemy hits to 20 while allies heal half of received damage softens incoming bursts.
Ryuko Block + Life Fiber Synchronization: invuln saves Ryuko on the dangerous turn; the heal-on-damage trigger sustains her/allies on the rest.

AoE pressure: under Decapitation Mode, spread 20 Normal across the whole enemy team every turn to break low-HP comps and chain multi-target executes.
Attrition/support: use Life Fiber Synchronization team-wide + Ryuko Block to outlast the enemy while the snowball builds.
strengths: Extremely low cost, 0-cooldown primary nuke — guaranteed damage and tempo every turn for just 1 Green.
Permanent, stacking +10-per-kill damage snowball that also self-heals — strong scaling and lategame inevitability.
Flexible AoE toggle (free) lets one kit pivot between single-target finishing and team-wide AoE/support.
Self-sustain (kill heals + half-damage heal trigger) plus a 1-turn invuln panic button make her durable for a striker.
Built-in soft anti-burst (damage_cap 20 on the target she hits) gives passive defensive value.
Low, only-2-color pip dependency (Green/Red, 1 each) — easy to field in most energy economies.

Flat 20 base damage is mediocre before the snowball; she needs actual kills to come online, so anti-snowball/sustain comps starve her.
Zero hard CC, no energy denial, no cleanse — purely a damage+self-sustain package with limited disruptive ceiling.
damage_cap is only 20 per single hit (soft) — does little against multi-hit or DoT-based threats.
Decapitation Mode AoE raises real cost (+1 random per skill) and spreads damage thin (still 20 each), diluting execute reliability vs higher-HP enemies.
Support heal is only HALF the damage received (code, not the advertised full amount) and delayed over 2 turns — weaker reactive healing than it reads; description is stale/misleading.
Invuln (CD4) and support (CD3) are her only gated tools; no escape/mobility if focused between Block windows.

power_assessment.reasoning: A clean, well-rounded beginner bruiser with a genuinely dangerous scaling engine. The 0-CD, 1-Green, 20-damage Fiber Lost with permanent +10/kill snowball and self-heal is an excellent value/tempo package, and the free AoE toggle plus reactive team heal and 1-turn invuln give real flexibility and survivability. She is held back from top-tier by being entirely Normal damage (no barrier/DR bypass, no hard CC, no energy denial) and by needing kills to unlock her ceiling — against shielded/sustain comps she's a flat 20-per-turn poke. Solid, flexible, snowball-dependent mid-high pick.

Unbounded permanent damage stacking via on-kill +10 (damage_mod_effect dur -1) — snowball has no listed cap; potential balance outlier if kills come easily.
0-cooldown primary damage that becomes full AoE via a FREE toggle is unusually efficient tempo for a beginner character.

Best single-turn output is Excalibur (45 Piercing) + Wind Blade Combat (20 Normal) = 65 to one target, on the turns Excalibur is off cooldown (every 2nd turn). Off-Excalibur turns are just 20 from Wind Blade. Avalon adds 10 HP/turn of healing (negative damage), not offense.
damage_profile.notes: Strictly single-target; zero AoE. Excalibur's 45 is Piercing so it skips flat and %DR, making it reliable burst against tanks. Wind Blade's 20 is plain Normal damage and fully mitigatable. No conditional/stack scaling anywhere in the kit; output is fixed.

invuln_or_counter: Invulnerability (1 turn, Providence, self or Avalon target)
Reflect (Avalon reactivation: bounces new harmful effects from the Avalon-bearer to Saber for 1 turn)

Out-attrition the enemy with a protected, regenerating frontline: Avalon's permanent 10 HP/turn on a carry plus Providence invuln to dodge lethal turns
Use Wind Blade Combat's free-cast loop to maintain energy advantage and keep Excalibur/Providence online while staying stun-immune

Avalon designates a protected ally that Providence can then make invulnerable, and whose harmful effects Saber can soak via Avalon's reflect
Wind Blade Combat's stun-ignore keeps Saber action-reliable so she can guarantee Excalibur/Providence/Avalon timing
Excalibur's Silence + uncounterable/unreflectable tag reliably shuts off a counter-reliant or skill-reliant enemy
strengths: Excalibur is high-value: 45 Piercing (ignores DR) + 1-turn Silence, and is uncounterable AND unreflectable, so it punches through counter/reflect-based defenses
Strong personal/ally survivability: 1-turn invulnerability (Providence), permanent ally regen (Avalon), reflect option, and self stun-immunity
Excellent energy economy — Wind Blade Combat costs nothing on a loop and discounts Providence, so protection is nearly free
Wind Blade Combat has no cooldown, giving guaranteed click-every-turn pressure plus stun-ignore
Flexible protection target: Avalon + Providence can be aimed at the team's carry, not just Saber
weaknesses: Zero AoE — completely single-target; falls off hard in multi-enemy / cleave matchups

Excalibur starts on cooldown, so her signature play is unavailable for the first ~2 turns
No cleanse, no energy denial, no stealth, no real hard CC beyond a single 1-turn silence
Avalon's payoff (regen + reflect) is slow and requires investing a cast/target before it matters; reflect only catches NEW harmful effects
Two-color (Green+Blue) requirement on a small kit can pinch in mono-color energy draws

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, hard-to-kill single-target duelist/protector rather than a damage outlier. Excalibur is a genuinely strong button — DR-ignoring Piercing burst plus a silence, and being both uncounterable and unreflectable bypasses an entire category of defensive characters. Her defensive suite (1-turn invuln on a CD4 that can be cheapened to free, permanent ally regen, a reflect, and stun-immunity) makes her and a protected ally very sticky, and her energy economy via the Wind Blade free-loop is excellent. She is held back from top tier by no AoE, modest sustained DPS (~20/turn between Excalibur windows), Excalibur opening on cooldown, and the lack of cleanse/energy-denial/stealth. Solid mid-to-upper-mid pick; shines in 1v1-ish attrition and against counter/reflect comps, weak into multi-target burst races.

signature_mechanic: Shield/defense negation tied to a counter -> mark -> guaranteed instant-kill chain, plus a permanent one-time Table-Flip team reset.
