On a successful counter: gain 1 Green energy, MARK the attacker, and swap Side-Hops -> 'Serious Series: Serious Punch' for 1 turn. Invisible ability. (Implemented in saitama3.gd.)

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Effective single-target ceiling is a guaranteed instant-kill (full HP removal) via the Side-Hops counter -> Serious Punch chain - functionally unbounded regardless of enemy HP. Raw print damage caps at 45 single-target (Normal Punch) / 30 AoE (Consecutive). No DoT, no per-stack ramp.
damage_profile.notes: Both basic punches shatter shields before dealing damage, so their effective damage ignores shields entirely. The kill condition is conditional (enemy must attack Saitama while Side-Hops is up), not on-demand. peak_single_target encoded as 9999 to represent the instant-kill (true HP removal); raw damage number is 45.

economy.color_dependency: Light Green dependency: 2 fixed Green on Normal Punch + 1 Green on Consecutive (hidden Serious Punch wants 3 Green). Most costs are Random, and Side-Hops refunds 1 Green on a successful counter, easing the Serious Punch payment. Single-color identity (mono-Green) so no multi-color strain.

economy.ramp_dependency: Low/none - no stacking or transformation buildup; power is gated by a reactive condition (enemy attacking Saitama), not by ramp.

shield shatter on both punches
invuln_or_counter: Team Invulnerable 1 turn (Table-Flip)
Single-skill Counter for 1 turn (Side-Hops, leads to mark + instant-kill)

win_conditions: Bait an enemy into attacking Saitama during the Side-Hops counter window, mark them, then delete them with the uncounterable Serious Punch instant-kill.
Use Table-Flip as a mid-game reset: cleanse the team, go Invulnerable for a turn, and Shatter the enemy team's defenses to set up clean follow-up damage from allies and his own punches.
Grind through shielded/defensive comps with shield-shattering punches that other characters struggle against.
internal_synergies: Side-Hops (counter -> mark + 1 Green refund) directly funds and unlocks Serious Punch (Green:3 instant-kill).
Table-Flip's enemy-team Shattered (DEF_NEGATE for 2 turns) amplifies Normal/Consecutive Punch and any allied damage during the window, while team Invuln + cleanse buys safe tempo.
Both punches pre-shatter shields, making them reliable against the same defensive targets Table-Flip Shatters.
Normal Punch <-> Consecutive Normal Punches swap lets him flex between single-target pressure and AoE each turn.
strengths: Guaranteed, uncounterable/unreflectable instant-kill that ignores enemy HP entirely - a true win-button against any single target.
Hard counter to shields and defensive stats: every punch shatters shields, and Table-Flip Shatters the whole enemy team for 2 turns.
Strong defensive/utility burst: full-team cleanse + team Invulnerable in one button.
Cheap, flexible costs (mostly Random, mono-Green) with self-sustaining energy via the counter refund.
Flexible single-target / AoE punch swap with no real downtime.
weaknesses: The instant-kill is fully reactive - it only triggers if an enemy uses a Harmful, non-Strategic skill on Saitama while Side-Hops is up; a careful opponent can simply not attack him and deny the kill.
Raw damage is mediocre (45 / 30) and never scales; outside the kill chain he is a low-DPS bruiser.
Table-Flip is essentially once-per-match (cd 6 + permanent swap), so the big reset must be timed well.
No healing, no hard CC, no energy denial, no stealth; team protection is limited to a single 1-turn Invuln.
Instant-kill can be hard-blocked by specific anti-execute mechanics (Embrace Pain, Sealed Nightmare), and the counter can be played around with Strategic-class or AoE skills.

power_assessment.reasoning: A guaranteed, uncounterable instant-kill is one of the strongest effects a kit can have, and Saitama pairs it with a full-team cleanse + invuln + enemy-team Shatter and universal shield-shredding - a very high ceiling and excellent against defensive/shield comps. He is held back from S-tier because the kill is reactive and deniable (the opponent controls whether they attack him), his standalone damage is low and non-scaling, and his big reset is effectively once per match. High floor of utility, conditional but devastating ceiling.

win_conditions: Neutralize an enemy tank/DR-stacker by stripping their Damage Reduction every turn so the team's damage lands clean.
Keep a carry ally alive and effect-free indefinitely with Medical Ninjutsu's repeating cleanse + heal channel while chipping with cd-0 Fist.
Pop Rampage Gloves to unlock Cherry Blossom Crash and apply sustained team-wide AoE DR-strip + 30 damage, grinding the whole enemy team down.

power_assessment.reasoning: Sakura is a specialist value/utility character rather than a raw powerhouse. Her DR-strip-on-every-hit is a genuinely strong, hard-counter mechanic against DR/tank metas and makes her flat 20-30 damage punch above its weight as 'effective' damage. The cd-0 single-target plus cd-1 team AoE (via swap) give her excellent, low-cost, low-color-dependency tempo, and Medical Ninjutsu is a top-tier cleanse+sustain tool (full enemy-effect wipe + Bleed/Affliction strip + 20/turn channel). She also has two self-protection layers (1-turn invuln, 3-turn stun-immunity). What holds her at a 6 rather than higher is a low damage ceiling with zero scaling, all-Normal damage (stopped by invuln, no bypass), no hard CC/stun/energy-denial, and single-target-only sustain. She is matchup-dependent: excellent into DR/tank/DoT comps, mediocre into evasion/invuln-heavy or pure-burst comps. Solid B-tier flex support/anti-tank.

power_assessment.reasoning: A focused, well-rounded single-target assassin with a strong, uncounterable execute finisher and inevitable DoT pressure, plus enough self-protection (invuln + counter + cleanse) to survive setting up. He is balanced by all-Normal mitigable damage, modest non-Kirin numbers, a one-time/slow execute, and zero team utility. Strong into squishy/aggressive comps, mediocre into DR tanks and passive defensive teams. Mid-to-upper-mid power in isolation.

satsuki4 invulnerability blocks a turn of damage, helping preserve the full-HP state that powers the rest of the kit; at full HP its own cooldown halves, so defending keeps you defending
satsuki3's full-HP bypass cleanly punishes invuln/defend enemies, while satsuki2's full-HP stun shuts off enemy offense to reduce incoming damage and keep her at full HP

power_assessment.reasoning: A clean, well-designed conditional duelist. At full HP she is genuinely strong: 25 Piercing every turn, a 1-turn offensive stun, a 50-damage invuln-bypassing finisher, and frequent self-invuln — all for trivial energy. Her tempo and anti-mitigation coverage are very good and she is online immediately with no ramp. But her power is a binary switch tied to a single fragile condition (HP >= 100), and the meta is full of chip, DoT, Affliction, and Bleed that flip that switch off and bypass her invuln defensively. Off full HP she becomes a vanilla low-rate single-target attacker with no AoE and no team utility. The self-heal is too slow (5/turn) to reliably re-arm the condition mid-fight. Strong in a vacuum / against burst-only opponents, distinctly exploitable against any sustained-damage or DoT comp — nets out as a solid-but-swingy mid-tier.

role: Execute-payoff support/control with damage-redirection tankiness
signature_mechanic: Death Reborn Revolution: places a 3-turn delayed mark that on expiry instant-KILLS a marked enemy (true execute, ignores HP/barriers) or restores a marked ally to full HP. Backed by a web of damage-redirection passives (Saturn Crystal / Silence Wall) and a self-referential "Saturn Crystal" toggle that the other skills flip between healing allies and damaging enemies.

abilities.name: Ruinous Scythe
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Deals 15 Normal damage to one enemy. Also marks Saturn herself (dur 2 = until her next turn) so that the Saturn Crystal passive heals allies instead of damaging enemies. Spammable filler / passive-mode toggle.

abilities.name: Silence Glaive Surprise
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Heals one ally 15 HP. Clears any prior Silence-Glaive mark, then permanently marks the new target as the sole ally that Saturn Crystal will heal (while Crystal is in ally-targeting mode). Cheap spammable heal + heal-focus toggle.

abilities.name: Death Reborn Revolution
abilities.conditional_scaling: Effect is binary and unconditional once mark survives 3 turns: enemy = instant death regardless of HP; ally = restored to full max HP regardless of damage taken.
abilities.effects_summary: Places a delayed mark (dur 7 = ~3 turns, self/player-facing). On expiry: an enemy target is instant-killed via instant_kill()/die() — a true execute that ignores current HP, barriers, shields and DR (blocked only by specific immunity effects like Embrace Pain / Sealed Nightmare); an ally target is set to full max HP. Huge payoff but telegraphed and removable if the mark is cleansed before expiry.

abilities.name: Silence Wall
abilities.conditional_scaling: Redirected damage scales with incoming enemy damage (50% of damage each ally takes that turn is bounced to a random enemy).
abilities.effects_summary: Invisible 1-turn mark (dur 2) on every ally: half of all damage each ally takes this turn is redirected to a random enemy. Team-wide damage-halving + reflect; strongest against burst turns. Cheap (1 pip) on a 3-turn cooldown.

abilities.name: Saturn Crystal
abilities.conditional_scaling: Scales with incoming damage on Saturn (50% redirected).

Effectively a personal damage-sharing tank passive. The split_desc text on saturn1/saturn2 implies an engine-level 'Saturn Crystal' that toggles between damaging enemies and healing allies, but the saturn5.gd itself only implements the self-damage-redirect mark.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Direct damage is trivial (15 Normal/turn from Ruinous Scythe). The real 'damage' is the Death Reborn Revolution execute: an uncapped instant-kill on a single enemy every ~3 turns of delay (8-turn cooldown), functionally infinite single-target value regardless of target HP. Silence Wall / Saturn Crystal convert incoming damage into reflected damage but that is reactive and uncontrolled (random enemy).
damage_profile.notes: No burst, no AoE, no DoT. Her offense is entirely the binary execute payoff plus opportunistic damage reflection, not damage numbers.

economy.color_dependency: Moderate White dependency: 3 of 6 visible pips are White (2 concentrated on Death Reborn Revolution). character_colors = [2] (White). Filler skills (Scythe, Silence Wall) take only random pips, so she can function on minimal White, but her payoff skill needs 2 White.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Two 0-cooldown spammable 1-pip skills (Scythe heal-toggle, Glaive heal) give constant cheap actions. Silence Wall on a short 3-turn cooldown for team defense. The win-condition Death Reborn Revolution is on a long 8-turn cooldown plus a 3-turn arming delay, so the execute lands roughly once per ~11 turns.
economy.ramp_dependency: Low ramp; no stacking. The only 'ramp' is waiting out the 3-turn execute mark. Otherwise immediately functional from turn 1 with cheap repeatable utility.

invuln_or_counter: Silence Wall (team-wide 50% damage redirect/reflect to random enemy for 1 turn, 3cd)
Saturn Crystal passive (permanent 50% self-damage redirect to a random ally, bypassing)

win_conditions: Land Death Reborn Revolution on a key enemy and protect the mark for 3 turns to instant-kill it regardless of HP/defenses (true execute).
Use Silence Wall + Saturn Crystal to make the team functionally hard to burst, surviving until the execute resolves and grinding out the matchup.
Keep a star ally alive with cheap heals + the Death Reborn full-restore safety net while the rest of the team carries damage.
internal_synergies: Ruinous Scythe (slot1) and Silence Glaive Surprise (slot2) are toggles for the Saturn Crystal passive's mode (damage enemies vs heal allies / focus a single ally), letting her flip the passive between offense and support each turn.
Saturn Crystal (self-damage redirect to ally) + Silence Wall (team damage redirect to enemy) layer to blunt incoming burst while she stalls toward the execute.
Death Reborn Revolution's dual mode (enemy execute / ally full-heal) lets the same long-cooldown button act as either a removal threat or an emergency revive-tier heal depending on the board.
Long 8cd + 3-turn delay on the execute pairs naturally with her defensive redirect package, which is built to survive long enough for the payoff.
strengths: Uncapped single-target instant-kill (true execute) that ignores HP, barriers, shields and DR — answers tanks, high-HP threats and immortality-stack characters that normal damage can't.
Very cheap, flexible economy: two 0-cooldown 1-pip actions and mostly random pips keep her active every turn.
Strong layered damage mitigation for the whole team (Silence Wall) plus personal damage-sharing (Saturn Crystal) for little energy.
Flexible payoff button: Death Reborn can save an ally to full HP instead of killing, giving a clutch defensive option.
Solid repeatable healing supports a stall/attrition game plan.
weaknesses: The win-condition execute is heavily telegraphed (3-turn visible mark) and presumably removable by cleanse/mark-removal, so it can be denied entirely by counterplay.
Extremely low direct damage (15/turn) and zero AoE — she cannot close games on her own and depends on teammates to deal damage.
Saturn Crystal redirects half of HER damage to a random ally — actively chip-damaging her own team, which can backfire against AoE or sustained pressure.
Damage reflection (Silence Wall) hits a RANDOM enemy, so it is uncontrolled and may waste value on the wrong target.
Long 8cd + 3-turn arm means the execute lands only ~once per ~11 turns; if rushed down before then she provides little.
No hard CC, no energy denial, no cleanse, no stealth — purely reactive/defensive outside the execute.

power_assessment.reasoning: A specialist support/control unit defined by one very high-ceiling tool: an uncapped true-execute that ignores all defensive layers and can erase any single enemy every ~11 turns, plus a flexible full-heal mode on the same button. That uncounterable-by-defense quality is genuinely powerful against tanks and immortality builds. She is propped up by cheap spammable utility and a layered team+self damage-redirect package that makes her hard to burst. However her direct output is near-zero, she has no AoE/CC/energy-denial, the execute is telegraphed and likely cleanseable, and her Saturn Crystal passive can hurt her own team. She is strongly team-dependent and matchup-swingy — devastating where the execute matters, mediocre in a damage race. Net slightly above average as a niche enabler/insurance piece.

role: Self-sustaining bruiser/duelist with heal-fueled scaling damage and a counter
signature_mechanic: Heal-to-damage conversion: all HP Sayaka heals (self + allies, including HoTs and the Soul Gem passive) is tracked and grants Hero Slash +5 damage per 20 HP healed, while the Soul Gem passive ramps stacks each turn (huge missing-HP self-heal at 6+ stacks) on a death clock that kills her at 10 stacks.

abilities.name: Enraged Slash
abilities.conditional_scaling: Minimum-damage floor of 20 (cannot be reduced below 20 by DR/effects). Piercing skips flat + % DR. Does NOT scale with heal counter.

Self-stuns Sayaka's Strategic skills for 1 turn (stun_effect dur 3, classes=['Strategic'] -> Azure Healing & Hero Counter locked). Grants 1 stack of Soul Gem: Sayaka (advances ramp AND death clock). Cheapest-color (Random) reliable damage.

abilities.name: Soul Gem: Sayaka
abilities.conditional_scaling: Stacks +1/turn (plus +1 per Enraged Slash). At 6+ stacks: heals 5 HP/turn per 20 HP missing (e.g. at 60/100 HP that is 10/turn; near death up to ~25/turn). Self-heal ignores anti-heal and feeds Hero Slash's damage counter.
abilities.effects_summary: Free passive engine: ramps a MARK stack each turn, granting escalating missing-HP self-heal at 6+ stacks and ignoring heal-prevention. DEATH CLOCK: code kills Sayaka at mag >= 10 (gain_corruption + corruption_trigger both check >=10); describe()/JSON saying 12 is STALE. Hard time limit on the build; Enraged Slash accelerates it.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hero Slash is theoretically unbounded: +5 per 20 HP healed. With Azure Healing (~60 HP/cast), the passive self-heal (up to ~25/turn), and reversed-heal credit, Sayaka can realistically push Hero Slash to ~45-70 over a match before the 10-stack death clock ends the run. Practical one-turn burst is a ramped Hero Slash (~45+) plus Enraged Slash (25); no multi-hit or AoE multiplier.
damage_profile.notes: Single-target only, zero AoE. Enraged Slash (25 Piercing, floored at 20) is reliable bypass damage that ignores DR/invuln. Hero Slash carries all the scaling but is Normal damage (blockable by barriers/DR/invuln). No DoT in kit. Peak listed assumes a mid/late-game Hero Slash (~45) + Enraged Slash (25) in one turn if energy/actions allow.

economy.cooldown_tempo: Excellent. Two 0-cooldown damage skills (Hero Slash, Enraged Slash) for spam; Hero Counter every 2 turns; Azure Healing every 4. She can act every turn cheaply.
economy.ramp_dependency: High but self-sufficient. Hero Slash starts weak (20) and needs accumulated healing to scale; the free Soul Gem passive guarantees ramp without spending energy, but the same passive imposes a hard ~10-turn death timer she must win inside of.

invuln_or_counter: Hero Counter (damage-reverse: target's next damaging skill heals instead, 1 turn, invisible)

win_conditions: Out-sustain opponents: stack Azure Healing + Soul Gem self-heal to stay topped while Hero Slash ramps, then close before the 10-stack death clock.
Snowball Hero Slash damage via accumulated healing into a single-target kill on the priority enemy.
Use Enraged Slash's uncounterable/bypassing Piercing + Hero Counter to punch through tanks, invuln, and counter-heavy enemies.
internal_synergies: Soul Gem passive self-heal -> Hero Slash damage: free missing-HP healing each turn directly inflates Hero Slash's +5/20HP counter, so taking damage and healing back up makes her hit harder.
Azure Healing -> Hero Slash: ~60 HP per cast is the fastest way to load the damage counter (+~15 Hero Slash damage per cast) while also being team sustain.
Hero Counter -> Hero Slash: reversed enemy damage becomes Sayaka-credited healing, further feeding the damage counter while negating a hit.

Enraged Slash <-> Soul Gem: each Enraged Slash adds a Soul Gem stack (faster 6-stack self-heal threshold) but also pushes the 10-stack death clock — a deliberate risk/reward lever; it also self-stuns her Strategic skills (Azure Healing/Hero Counter) for a turn.
strengths: Extremely cheap, high-tempo kit (4 total pips, two 0-cd damage skills) — acts meaningfully every turn.
Strong, energy-free self-sustain that ignores anti-heal and scales with missing HP, making her very hard to burn down in the mid-game.
Enraged Slash is reliable bypass damage: Piercing, uncounterable, bypassing, with a 20-damage floor — great vs DR/invuln/counter comps.
Doubles as a team healer (Azure Healing ~60 HP) and a soft counter (Hero Counter) — flexible support-bruiser.
Damage scales without spending resources, snowballing if the game goes long.
weaknesses: Hard self-kill death clock at 10 Soul Gem stacks: passive ramps 1/turn and Enraged Slash accelerates it, so she has a strict ~10-turn window and can be stalled/timed out.
Single-target only with ZERO AoE — weak into wide/swarm comps.
Front-loaded weakness: starts at 20 damage and must invest turns healing before Hero Slash matters.
Hero Slash (her scaling carry) is Normal damage — fully stoppable by barriers, %/flat DR, and invuln; only Enraged Slash bypasses.
Heavy Blue color dependency (3 Blue pips) — vulnerable to Blue energy denial/screw.
No hard CC, no stun, no energy denial, no cleanse, no shields — purely a damage+sustain duelist.
Enraged Slash self-stuns her own Strategic skills, creating awkward turns where she can't heal or counter.

power_assessment.reasoning: A well-rounded, cheap, high-tempo sustain bruiser that is genuinely hard to kill in the mid-game and offers team healing + a counter on the side. Her damage scales for free via her own healing, an elegant snowball engine. But she is held back by single-target-only output (no AoE), a slow start, a Normal-damage main attack that is fully blockable, heavy Blue dependence, and especially a self-imposed ~10-turn death clock that hands patient/stall opponents a clean answer. Solid B-tier duelist/support hybrid rather than a top-tier carry.
outlier_flags: Self-kill mechanic: Soul Gem death threshold is mag >= 10 in code (gain_corruption and corruption_trigger), but describe()/JSON say 12 and the split_desc says 10 — GROUND TRUTH is 10. Documentation is internally inconsistent, likely a balance/clarity bug.
Hero Slash heal value mismatch: describe() text says heals 5 HP, but split_desc and execute() both use 10 — stale describe() string.
Unbounded scaling: Hero Slash damage has no cap on the heal-to-damage counter; in a long game it can grow large, though the death clock limits realized value.
Enraged Slash min-damage floor (20) makes it immune to most damage reduction, a quietly strong anti-tank property.

role: AoE Affliction DoT controller / anti-defense poisoner
signature_mechanic: Pure Affliction poison stacking that bypasses defenses, anchored by Arrogant King's Poison converting every enemy Shield/Invuln/heal-over-time effect into additional permanent 5-damage Affliction stacks. Enters via a delayed 2-turn banish and returns with a permanent 25 Shield + free energy.

abilities.name: Chains of the First Poisoner
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Affliction damage to one enemy and stuns that enemy's Helpful and Strategic skills for 1 turn (stun dur 2). Soft single-target support/strategic denial; does not lock damage abilities. Cheap 1-CD spam tool.

abilities.name: Mystical Beast - Hydra
abilities.conditional_scaling: fixed DoT, ~3 ticks per enemy
abilities.effects_summary: 10 Affliction immediate to all enemies plus a 10 Affliction-per-turn DoT (~3 turns). If the DoT expires naturally it stuns that target for 1 turn (delayed AoE stun). Enemies can cleanse the DoT by ending their turn while Invulnerable. Heavy DoT pressure that punishes both action and inaction.

abilities.name: Arrogant King's Poison
abilities.conditional_scaling: per converted defensive effect: each enemy Shield, Invuln, and heal-over-time effect becomes +5 immediate damage AND a permanent stacking 5-damage/turn Affliction DoT (dur -1, remove_on_death=false)
abilities.effects_summary: Applies a permanent stacking 5 Affliction/turn DoT to all enemies, then shatters all shields, strips all invuln effects and all heal-over-time effects, converting each stripped effect into +5 immediate Affliction and an extra permanent 5/turn poison stack. Bypasses defenses. Anti-defensive nuke + scaling permanent poison engine.

abilities.name: Scales of the Sacred Fish
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: default_defend: Semiramis becomes invulnerable for 1 turn. Panic button / survivability cooldown to let DoTs tick while she is untouchable. 4-turn cooldown.

abilities.name: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Passive entrance: Semiramis begins the match banished for 2 turns (untargetable, off-board), then rejoins with a permanent 25 Shield and gains 1 random energy. Trades early-game tempo (effectively 2-on-3 for two turns) for a durable shielded entrance and ramp toward her energy-hungry kit.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Permanent, uncapped AoE Affliction stacking. Each Arrogant King's Poison cast adds a permanent 5/turn poison to all enemies, plus +5/turn permanent per enemy Shield/Invuln/HoT stripped. Against defensive teams a single cast can apply 3-5 permanent stacks per enemy (15-25/turn AoE) on top of prior casts; recast every 3 turns it ramps to lethal Affliction (bypasses all barriers/shields/DR), so the late-game ceiling is very high vs shield/heal comps.
damage_profile.notes: All output is Affliction, so effective damage equals listed damage against virtually any defense (ignores barriers, shields, %DR, flat DR). Burst is low; the threat is permanent, compounding poison plus a single-cast value that scales off how much defense the enemy team stacked. Peak single-target is 20 (semiramis1), or higher if semiramis3 hits one heavily defended target (5 + 5*stacks). Peak AoE ~30 per enemy combining semiramis2 (10) + semiramis3 (5 base); semiramis3 immediate jumps to 20-40 per enemy vs defensive teams via converted stacks. semiramis2's ~3-tick 10/turn DoT and semiramis3's permanent 5/turn-per-stack DoTs sum to ~25/turn sustained early, climbing as stacks accrue.

economy.color_dependency: Light White dependency: 3 of 7 visible pips are White (1 each on skills 1/2/3); only one White pip per cast required, the rest random, so she splashes into most teams with a single White source. semiramis4 is pure random.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Slow-to-medium. Spammable 1-CD poke (semiramis1) every turn, but both AoE engines (semiramis2, semiramis3) sit on 3-turn cooldowns and the defensive button (semiramis4) on 4-turn. Damage is delivered over time, not in bursts.
economy.ramp_dependency: High early-game ramp dependency: banished the first 2 turns (passive), contributing nothing while teammates fight outnumbered, then must repeatedly land semiramis3 to build permanent stacks. Power is back-loaded and snowballs over time.

hard_cc: 1-turn full stun on all enemies whose Hydra DoT expires naturally (delayed AoE stun, semiramis2)
soft_cc: Helpful + Strategic skill stun for 1 turn, single target (semiramis1)
invuln_or_counter: Self invuln 1 turn on 4-CD (semiramis4)
Self untargetable banish for first 2 turns (semiramis5)

win_conditions: Outlast the enemy team with permanent, compounding AoE Affliction stacks from repeated Arrogant King's Poison casts until the whole team bleeds out through their defenses.
Hard-counter shield/heal/invuln-reliant comps: strip their defenses with semiramis3 and convert that defense into extra poison, denying their survival tools.
Survive the early banish and her own fragility (self invuln + 25 shield) long enough for the poison to outscale enemy healing/burst.
internal_synergies: semiramis3 + semiramis2: Hydra forces enemies to either eat the DoT or end-turn-while-invuln to cleanse it; semiramis3 punishes that defensive play by converting Invuln/shields/HoT into more permanent poison, so defenses become a liability.
semiramis5 grants a permanent 25 Shield + free energy that seeds her survival plan and helps pay the White/random costs of her opening rotation.
semiramis4 + semiramis5 invuln/banish windows let her ignore incoming damage while her permanent poisons keep ticking the enemy team down.
semiramis1 stuns enemy Helpful/Strategic skills, suppressing enemy cleanses/shields/heals around her big poison conversion to protect her stacks.
strengths: All damage is Affliction, ignoring shields, barriers, %DR and flat DR; effective damage equals listed damage against any defense.
Permanent, stackable, recurring AoE poison that snowballs and is hard to remove (remove_on_death=false, dur -1).
Premier anti-defense tech: shatters shields, removes invuln effects and strips heal-over-time, then turns all of it into more damage, devastating vs tank/support/heal comps.
Self-sufficient survivability: permanent 25 shield on entry plus two invuln windows (1-turn button + 2-turn banish) let her tick enemies down while untouchable.
Low color commitment (one White pip per cast) and a cheap 1-CD poke make her easy to fit and always action-positive.
Built-in CC layers: delayed AoE stun (Hydra) and single-target support/strategic lockout.
weaknesses: Starts banished for 2 turns, so her team fights effectively 2-on-3 early, a serious tempo deficit and the single biggest design risk.
Very low burst: reliable single-target is only 20 and AoE damage is delivered over many turns; she cannot close a game quickly or punish low-HP targets on demand.
Damage is heavily back-loaded and ramp-dependent; fast aggressive/burst comps can kill her or wipe her team before stacks matter.
Anti-defense conversion is dead value vs teams that run no shields/invuln/HoT, where semiramis3 falls back to a tiny 5 base AoE.
No healing and no cleanse for allies; offers the team almost no protection beyond her own survival tools.
Hydra's DoT can be self-cleansed by enemies ending their turn while invulnerable, and her invuln windows are on long cooldowns, leaving exploitable gaps.

power_assessment.reasoning: A specialist scaling DoT controller with a near-unblockable damage type (pure Affliction bypasses all defenses) and best-in-class anti-defense disruption (shatter shields + strip invuln + strip HoT, converted into permanent poison). Her permanent stacking poison gives a very high late-game ceiling, especially as a hard counter to shield/heal/tank comps. She is held back from top tier by a punishing 2-turn opening banish (team plays a man down early), low/no burst, strong ramp dependency, and matchups where defensive conversion whiffs (no shields/heals to strip). She offers no team support beyond her own survival. Net: strong in attrition and against defensive metas, weak vs fast burst and into low-defense comps, a high-variance specialist around mid-high power.
outlier_flags: Opens the game banished for 2 turns (forced early 2v3), an unusual tempo handicap that swings her viability hard by matchup and is a balance red flag.

Permanent, uncapped, stacking AoE Affliction that bypasses all defenses and persists through death-immunity (remove_on_death=false), potentially oppressive vs defensive comps and a scaling ceiling worth monitoring.
semiramis3 effective value scales off ENEMY defensive stacking (more shields/invuln/heals = more damage she deals), making her power swing wildly with opponent composition.

abilities.name: Hell Breaker
abilities.conditional_scaling: Applies (1 + RANDOM-pips-in-cost) stacks of a permanent 5 Affliction/turn DoT. RANDOM pips come from the passive ramp, so each ramp stack = +5 permanent Affliction/turn; at the 2-stack window it lands ~3 stacks = 15 permanent Affliction/turn per cast.
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Affliction burst (bypasses shields/barriers/DR) + stacks a permanent 5/turn Affliction DoT whose stack count scales with the ramp. Unconditional damage + escalating DoT.

abilities.name: Photon Flash
abilities.conditional_scaling: Hits one additional distinct random enemy per RANDOM pip in its cost (ramp stacks). Converts to multi-target as the passive ramps; at 2 stacks it strikes 3 enemies for 20 Piercing each (~60 spread).
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Piercing to primary target, bypasses invulnerability and skips flat+%DR; spreads to extra random enemies as the passive ramps (free soft-AoE conversion).

abilities.name: Android Assault
abilities.conditional_scaling: Cost-tax duration = 2 + 2*(RANDOM pips): base 1 enemy turn, +1 turn per ramp stack.
abilities.effects_summary: 10 Normal damage + COST_MOD tax: target's skills cost +1 Random energy for 1+ turns (longer as the passive ramps). Energy-denial / tempo tax.

abilities.name: Barrier
abilities.conditional_scaling: Shield = 20 + 10*(RANDOM pips); duration = 4 + 2*(RANDOM pips) i.e. 2 turns base +1 turn per ramp stack. At 2 stacks = 40 shield / 4 turns.
abilities.effects_summary: Self shield, 20 for 2 turns base, scaling up to ~40/4t with ramp. Pure self-protection panic button.

abilities.name: Infinite Energy Cycling
abilities.conditional_scaling: Self-ramp engine: every skill use grants +1 random energy AND adds a permanent stacking +1 Random COST_MOD to ALL of seventeen's skills. cost()[RANDOM] = current stack count, which every other ability scales off. Using any skill whose resolved total cost reaches 3 wipes all stacks, so the ramp self-caps around 2 stacks (1 base + 2 random = 3 -> reset).
abilities.effects_summary: Engine/ramp passive: free energy generation + escalating random-energy cost that powers all four abilities' bonuses; self-resets when a cast resolves to total cost 3.

role: Self-ramping energy-engine skirmisher: cheap unconditional Affliction/Piercing chip + escalating DoT/AoE/energy-tax that grows with a random-energy ramp
signature_mechanic: Infinite Energy Cycling passive: each cast both generates a random pip and permanently adds +1 random energy to the cost of every skill; that growing random-pip count is what every ability scales its bonus off (extra DoT stacks, extra AoE targets, longer tax, bigger/longer shield). Casting a skill that resolves to total cost 3 wipes the ramp, so it runs in a self-capping 0->1->2-stack rhythm.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Payoff is in permanent Affliction DoT, not burst. Realistic per-cast scaling caps at +2 random pips (the 2-stack window, since the cast that consumes 2 stacks resolves at cost 3 and wipes the ramp). At that window: Hell Breaker stacks ~3 (15) permanent Affliction/turn per cast and can be re-stacked indefinitely, so sustained Affliction DoT grows unboundedly over a long game (15 -> 30 -> 45+/turn across casts); Photon Flash hits up to 3 enemies for 20 Piercing each (~60 AoE). Burst single-target stays low (~20).
damage_profile.notes: Burst is weak; the threat is cumulative permanent Affliction DoT (bypasses shields/barriers/DR) plus Piercing that skips DR -- both inevitable damage. Numbers assume a 2-stack ramp window per cast; at 0 ramp it is 15 Affliction + 5/turn, or 20 Piercing single.

economy.color_dependency: Four-color: one each of Red (seventeen1), White (seventeen2), Green (seventeen3), Blue (seventeen4); character_colors = [0,1,2,3]. Base cost is all specific pips with zero base random, but the passive piles RANDOM pips onto every skill, so real-game costs become 1 specific + N random and grow random-heavy as it ramps.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Two of four skills are 0-cooldown spammable (Hell Breaker, Photon Flash); Android Assault CD1, Barrier CD2. High tempo; the passive rewards casting every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: High but soft. The kit's whole upside is gated on the self-ramp, yet the ramp self-resets at cost 3, so it never snowballs out of control -- a steady-rhythm engine, not exponential. All four abilities still function at 0 stacks (floor values), so it is not bricked without ramp.

power_assessment.reasoning: A clean, well-designed 'engine' character with no hard CC, no healing, no team support and unremarkable burst, but several pieces of inevitable damage that are hard to interact with: permanent stacking Affliction DoT (ignores shields/barriers/DR), Piercing (skips flat+%DR), and a cost tax for tempo denial. Strong in long, grindy fights where the permanent DoT accumulates and Photon Flash fans into multiple targets; self-shield gives personal sustain. Held back by low immediate burst, no protection for allies, no CC to close games, and a ramp that intentionally self-caps at ~2 stacks so it can't truly snowball. Solidly mid: durable, annoying, inevitable, but not a win-condition on its own.
outlier_flags: permanent (-1 duration) Affliction DoT that can be re-stacked every turn -> unbounded sustained damage over very long games
Photon Flash silently converts from single-target to multi-target as the passive ramps -- effectively free AoE with no AoE cost
entire kit routes through Affliction/Piercing, so enemy shields/barriers/DR are largely worthless against it

strengths: Inevitable damage: Affliction DoT bypasses shields/barriers/DR, Piercing skips flat and %DR -- defenses barely matter
Permanent re-stackable DoT scales unboundedly in long games
Two 0-cooldown spammable skills feed a high-tempo, every-turn playstyle
Self-sufficient: scaling self-shield + free energy generation, low color-greed at base (1 pip each)
Built-in soft AoE (Photon Flash) and energy/tempo denial (Android Assault) at no extra cost
Functional at zero ramp -- floor values are still usable, so it isn't bricked
weaknesses: No hard CC, no stuns, no swaps -- cannot lock down or close out a game
No ally support: shield is self-only, zero healing/cleanse for the team
Low upfront burst (~15-20); relies on time and accumulation to threaten
Ramp self-resets at cost 3, capping per-cast scaling at ~+2 and preventing a true snowball
Energy economy gets random-heavy/awkward as it ramps; rising costs can strain the team pool
Vulnerable to burst/assassins -- slow accumulating damage loses the race to fast killers
DoT-dependent, so enemy effect-cleanse / DoT removal neutralizes its main payoff
win_conditions: Grind out long fights where permanent Affliction DoT accumulates across many casts into lethal totals
Stack-and-spread chip with Photon Flash hitting the whole enemy team while DoT ticks bypass their defenses
Use Android Assault's cost tax to choke a key threat's tempo while your inevitable damage outlasts them, surviving on the self-shield
internal_synergies: Infinite Energy Cycling powers EVERY other skill -- the random pips it adds are read by each ability's cost()[RANDOM] to scale DoT stacks, AoE targets, tax duration, and shield size
Spamming the 0-CD skills (Hell Breaker / Photon Flash) both builds ramp and generates the energy to pay the rising costs
Hell Breaker + ramp = compounding permanent Affliction DoT each turn
Photon Flash + ramp = free single-to-multi-target conversion
Barrier's scaling lets seventeen tank through the time his DoT needs to win

role: Anti-defensive single-target piercing assassin with a team-protection panic button
signature_mechanic: Piercing damage that punishes defensive setups: bonus damage vs Shield/DR, AoE Shatter (DEF_NEGATE) that strips defenses while granting her two allies guaranteed unkillability for 2 turns.

abilities.name: Extase - Bisector of Creation
abilities.conditional_scaling: +10 if target has Damage Reduction, +10 if target has Shield (both can stack); base 20 -> up to 40 vs a shielded, DR'd target. Piercing already skips flat+%DR, so the bonus is pure punish-value.
abilities.effects_summary: Pure damage spam tool: 20 Piercing (40 vs full defenses), 0 cooldown, 1 White pip. No status applied.

abilities.name: Savior Strike
abilities.conditional_scaling: none on the damage; flat 35 Piercing
abilities.effects_summary: 35 Piercing damage + target.check_cancels(true), ending all of that enemy's cancellable effects (channels/control effects etc.). A damage + effect-strip tool, AI-weighted heavily (+150 each) vs targets carrying CHANNEL_CANCEL / CONTROL_CANCEL.

abilities.name: Trump Card - Blinding Light
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (fixed effect)
abilities.effects_summary: Applies Shattered (DEF_NEGATE, def_negate(3)) to ALL enemies, stripping/negating their defenses & invuln for the 2-turn window; simultaneously grants Immortality (immortality_effect(4) = 2 turns) to Sheele's allies so they cannot be killed. Team-wide teamwipe-prevention + offensive defense-strip combined.

abilities.name: Extase Block
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Standard self-defend (default_defend): Sheele becomes Invulnerable for 1 turn. Personal panic button, AI-weighted as a defensive reaction.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hard-capped, no ramp. Single best hit is sheele1 = 40 Piercing (only vs a target carrying BOTH Shield and DR). Vs undefended target it is 20 (sheele1) or 35 (sheele2). Firing both in one turn ~75 Piercing (sheele1 40 + sheele2 35) but sheele2 is 2cd. No DoT, no transformation, no stacking, so the ceiling never grows across a match.
damage_profile.notes: All offensive damage is Piercing (skips flat + %DR), so effective damage stays high vs tanks. The kit's premise is that defensive enemies make her hit HARDER, not softer; but absolute numbers are low.

economy.color_dependency: Moderate two-color White/Red dependency. sheele3 needs one White AND one Red simultaneously; sheele1 needs White, sheele2 needs Red; sheele4 is fully flexible (Random). Best in a White/Red core.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Spam-friendly front end (sheele1 cd 0, every turn) plus two long-CD utility buttons (sheele3 cd 5, sheele4 cd 4) and a mid sheele2 (cd 2). Sustained pressure is almost entirely sheele1.
economy.ramp_dependency: None. No stacking, transformation, or scaling resource; power is flat from turn 1.

soft_cc: Shattered/DEF_NEGATE (AoE, sheele3 - negates enemy defenses & invuln rather than disabling actions)
invuln_or_counter: Self-invuln 1 turn (sheele4)
Ally Immortality / cannot-be-killed for 2 turns on both allies (sheele3)

win_conditions: Out-trade defensive/tanky comps: Piercing + Shield/DR bonus damage means turtle teams feed her damage instead of mitigating it.
Survive a burst/alpha-strike window: sheele3 grants both allies 2 turns of unkillability (Immortality) while shattering the enemy team's defenses.
Enable allied burst: AoE Shatter strips enemy invuln/defenses so allies' damage lands during the same window.
Pick off a key target by stripping its protective channel/control buffs with sheele2 then finishing with piercing damage.
internal_synergies: sheele3 Shatter -> removes enemy invuln so sheele1/sheele2 always connect; note mild anti-synergy in that Shatter strips the Shield/DR that sheele1 wants present for its bonus damage on the same target.
sheele3 Immortality window + sheele4 self-invuln make Sheele's whole side near-unkillable for one decisive turn.
sheele2 effect-strip + sheele1 piercing both punish set-up-heavy enemies, reinforcing the anti-defense theme.
Low flexible costs (1+2+2+1=6) let her fire two skills a turn without monopolizing team energy.
strengths: All offensive damage is Piercing - reliable vs DR/tank/shield comps where most attackers fall off.
Anti-defense bonus: enemies who shield or stack DR make sheele1 hit for up to 40.
sheele3 is a rare, powerful team-save: 2 turns where BOTH allies cannot be killed, plus an AoE defense-strip - high-value anti-burst / anti-execute counter.
Cheap and fast: sheele1 is a 0-cooldown 1-pip piercing nuke usable every turn.
Targeted effect-strip (sheele2) answers channels/buffs.
Two independent invuln-style buttons (self sheele4, allies sheele3) give strong defensive utility for a damage character.
weaknesses: Very low damage ceiling: 40 best-case single hit, no AoE damage, no DoT, no scaling/ramp - out-damaged by any dedicated DPS late.
No hard CC (no stun/lock), no energy denial, no healing, no real shields - utility is binary and infrequent.
Two-color White+Red requirement on sheele3 plus split White/Red attacks create deck-color tension.
sheele3 is a 5-cooldown one-shot; outside its window her kit is modest piercing pokes.
sheele1's bonus is conditional on the enemy keeping Shield/DR - vs undefended targets she's a vanilla 20/35 dealer.
Beginner-flagged character (beginner = true) - intentionally simple, low-ceiling kit.
abilities_data.json sheele1 description lists +5 for DR, but .gd ground truth grants +10 DR and +10 Shield (max 40); JSON is stale.

power_assessment.reasoning: A focused niche pick rather than a generalist. Her damage is low and flat (peak 40 single-target, no AoE damage, no DoT, no ramp), capping her raw DPS well below dedicated carries. What lifts her above a vanilla beginner unit is the quality of two defensive/utility buttons: Piercing on every attack hard-counters DR/shield/tank comps (a whole matchup class many attackers struggle with), and sheele3 is a genuinely strong, cheap team-protection + AoE defense-strip that can blank an enemy alpha strike for 2 turns. That utility is matchup-dependent and on a 5-turn cooldown, so she swings between excellent counter and low-impact poke. Cheap flexible costs and a 0-CD piercing spam keep her always-useful. Net: a solid, situational support-bruiser near the middle of the curve.
outlier_flags: JSON/.gd description mismatch on sheele1 (JSON +5 DR vs code +10 DR / +10 Shield, max 40).

sheele3 'allies cannot be killed for 2 turns' (Immortality) paired with AoE Shatter is an unusually strong unconditional team-protection effect for a 2-pip 5cd - potential high-value outlier depending on roster norms.
Beginner-flagged (intentionally simple kit) - isolation rating may misstate vs a roster of complex kits.
Mild internal anti-synergy: sheele3's Shatter strips the very Shield/DR sheele1 wants present for its bonus damage.

role: Mark-based control assassin: builds Four Scythe Child marks, then converts them into Shatter (defense-strip), AoE stun, and sustained Affliction DoT
signature_mechanic: Four Scythe Child mark economy: shinoa1 passively auto-marks one random enemy per turn (permanent mark). Her damage skills consume those marks for upgraded effects — shinoa2 consumes a mark to Shatter (strip all defenses) the target, shinoa3 consumes a mark to Stun. Doji Manifestation (shinoa5, swapped into slot 1) flips the economy: while active her skills do NOT consume marks AND all marked enemies take 10 Affliction/turn — letting her stockpile marks and repeatedly re-trigger Shatter/Stun on the same targets.

abilities.name: Four Scythe Child
abilities.conditional_scaling: none (marks scale value of other abilities, not damage here)
abilities.effects_summary: Setup engine. Adds a self END_OF_TURN_TRIGGER (dur 8 = ~4 self-turns): each turn marks one random unmarked living enemy with a PERMANENT (dur -1) 'Four Scythe Child' mark. Also swaps this slot with Doji Manifestation (shinoa5) for dur 9 (~4 self-turns). extra_usable blocks re-cast while the marking trigger is active.

abilities.name: Doji Slash
abilities.conditional_scaling: on-mark: if target is marked by Four Scythe Child, applies Shatter (def_negate). No bonus damage number, but Shatter strips the target's defenses (DR/barriers) for follow-ups.
abilities.effects_summary: 20 Normal single-target, CD0 (spammable). If target marked, applies Shatter/DEF_NEGATE for dur 2 (=1 turn) and consumes the mark — UNLESS Doji Manifestation is active, in which case the mark is NOT consumed (can Shatter the same target every turn).

abilities.name: Doji Sweep
abilities.conditional_scaling: on-mark: every marked enemy hit is also stunned. Effective value scales with number of marks built up.
abilities.effects_summary: 25 Normal to ALL enemies, CD1. Each marked enemy is Stunned for dur 2 (=1 turn) and the mark is consumed — UNLESS Doji Manifestation is active (marks persist, enabling repeated AoE stun-lock).

abilities.name: Shinoa Deflection
abilities.conditional_scaling: none
abilities.effects_summary: Panic button: Shinoa becomes fully Invulnerable for 1 turn (default_defend). CD4.

abilities.name: Doji Manifestation
abilities.conditional_scaling: per-mark DoT: 10 Affliction/turn to EACH marked enemy. With marks on all 3 enemies = 30 Affliction/turn AoE, ignoring barriers/shields.
abilities.effects_summary: Hidden alt swapped into slot 1 by shinoa1 (~4-turn window). Self Invuln to non-Strategic skills for dur 4 (=2 turns). Marks self ('Doji Manifestation') so her skills do NOT consume Four Scythe Child marks while active. Adds self END_OF_TURN_TRIGGER (dur 4) dealing 10 Affliction to every enemy still marked by Four Scythe Child each turn.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Direct damage is low and fixed (20 ST, 25-per-target AoE). The real ceiling is control + DoT: with marks on all 3 enemies and Doji Manifestation active, she does 30 Affliction/turn (bypasses shields/barriers) PLUS 75 AoE + 3-enemy stun via Doji Sweep, repeatable because marks aren't consumed. Shatter from Doji Slash also amplifies any ally's follow-up by stripping target defenses.
damage_profile.notes: Peak ST 45 = Doji Slash (20) in a turn she also lands Sweep on that target (25); standalone Doji Slash is only 20 + Shatter. Peak AoE 75 = Doji Sweep 25 x3 enemies (plus stuns on any marked). Sustained DoT 30 = 10 Affliction x3 marked enemies/turn from Doji Manifestation. Numbers assume a full 3-enemy team fully marked; against 1 marked enemy the DoT is only 10/turn.

economy.color_dependency: Light. Visible kit (slots 1-4) needs only Red:2 specific (Doji Slash 1 Red, Doji Sweep 1 Red) plus 3 Random; setup/defense skills are pure Random. Doji Manifestation adds Red:2. Mono-Red identity but very few hard color requirements, so easy to splash.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Mixed. Doji Slash is CD0 (spammable each turn), Doji Sweep CD1, but both setup/defense cooldowns are long (CD4) and the transformation is CD5. Core damage loop is low-CD; the engine pieces are infrequent.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. She is weak turn 1: shinoa1 only marks 1 random enemy per turn, so it takes 2-3 turns to mark a full team, and her best effects (Shatter, Stun, Affliction DoT) all require pre-placed marks. Random targeting of the marker reduces reliability.

hard_cc: AoE Stun (Doji Sweep, on marked enemies, 1 turn each)
soft_cc: Shatter / defense-negate (Doji Slash, on marked target, 1 turn)
permanent Four Scythe Child mark (setup, no direct CC)

Invuln to non-Strategic skills 2 turns (Doji Manifestation)

internal_synergies: shinoa1 is the engine for everything: it lays the permanent Four Scythe Child marks that Doji Slash (Shatter), Doji Sweep (Stun), and Doji Manifestation (Affliction DoT) all consume/exploit.

Doji Manifestation is the keystone: it stops marks from being consumed, so Doji Slash can Shatter and Doji Sweep can AoE-stun the SAME enemies every turn while marks tick 10 Affliction each — turning a one-shot mark economy into a recurring lockdown.
Shatter from Doji Slash strips defenses, amplifying her own (and allies') subsequent damage into that target.
Two invuln layers (Deflection CD4 + Manifestation's non-Strategic invuln) let her survive the slow ramp and protect the mark engine.
All her damage skills are non-Strategic; Manifestation's 'non-Strategic invuln' still lets her keep acting offensively while protected from most enemy actions.
win_conditions: Reach a fully-marked enemy team (2-3 turns of shinoa1), then activate Doji Manifestation to lock the marks in and stack 10/enemy Affliction DoT plus repeatable AoE Stun (Doji Sweep) and repeatable Shatter (Doji Slash).
Use AoE stun-lock from Doji Sweep on multiple marked enemies to neutralize an enemy turn while DoT and ally damage close out the game.
Attrition via shield/barrier-bypassing Affliction against defensive comps that other characters can't crack.
strengths: Bypass damage: Affliction DoT from Doji Manifestation ignores barriers/shields/DR — strong vs tanky/shield comps.
Strong multi-target control: cheap CD0 Shatter + CD1 AoE stun, both upgraded by marks, give reliable lockdown once ramped.
Excellent survivability for a control piece: two invuln windows (one full, one non-Strategic) and low color commitment.
Defense-strip (Shatter) acts as a team-wide damage amplifier on priority targets.
Very low energy cost (5 pips across visible kit, mostly Random) makes her easy to fit into any team.
weaknesses: Slow, ramp-dependent: near-useless turn 1; marks accrue only 1/turn and the marker picks a RANDOM enemy, so she can't reliably mark a specific priority target.
Very low raw damage (20 ST / 25-per-target AoE); without marks she contributes little and can't burst.
Whole kit collapses without marks — counters that cleanse marks, banish, or deny her marker uptime gut her.
No healing, no team shields, no energy denial — purely self-protective defensively; offers nothing to allies except Shatter amplification.
Mark consumption outside Doji Manifestation means her best effects are one-shot per mark; before the transform she spends marks faster than she places them.
Doji Manifestation has a finite window (~2-turn invuln, ~4-turn swap) and long CD5 — control uptime is gated by it.

power_assessment.reasoning: A control/DoT specialist whose ceiling (repeatable AoE stun + Shatter + shield-ignoring 30/turn Affliction under Doji Manifestation) is genuinely strong against tanky and stall comps, and whose self-survivability (two invuln windows) lets her reach that ceiling. But the floor is low: she's passive turn 1, ramps slowly via 1-random-mark-per-turn, deals trivial raw damage, and the entire payoff is gated behind a CD5 transformation and pre-placed marks. Random mark targeting hurts reliability against single-priority-kill races. Solid B-tier enabler/controller rather than a carry — rewards a team that can stall to her power spike and capitalize on Shatter/stun windows.

Affliction DoT bypasses shields/barriers — strong vs defensive comps
extreme front-load weakness: contributes almost nothing turns 1-2

role: Single-target physical bruiser with ramping permanent affliction DoT and self-protection
signature_mechanic: Ignition: Shinra is a free self-buff (mark, self-facing 1 turn) that makes Rapid Kick and Tora Hishigi cost 1 less Green AND stamp a PERMANENT, stackable, per-stack 5 Affliction/turn DoT on the hit enemy. Each marked hit adds another permanent +5 affliction/turn stack on that target (remove_on_death=false, dur -1), so DoT pressure ramps every turn you pre-cast Ignition. The shinra5 passive (at <=40 HP) turns this into an auto-engine: he becomes Isolated and Ignition auto-reapplies on every Harmful skill, removing the need to manually pre-cast.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Direct-hit damage is fixed (25 / 40 Normal). True ceiling is the permanent affliction DoT, which adds +5/turn per marked hit and NEVER expires or clears on death-mark (dur -1, remove_on_death=false). With Ignition pre-cast (or auto via passive), every turn adds a stack: turn-by-turn DoT grows 5,10,15,20... bypassing barriers/shields. Over a long game on one target this is effectively unbounded affliction pressure, though it is slow (5 per hit) and split if targets are spread.
damage_profile.notes: Burst is modest (40 single-target, no AoE). Real damage is the ramping permanent affliction. Best-case single turn: Tora Hishigi 40 Normal + a freshly applied 5 affliction tick. Sustained example after a few marked hits on one enemy: ~10-20 affliction/turn from accumulated stacks plus a fresh stack each marked attack. Affliction bypasses DR/barriers/shields, so effective damage is high vs tanky targets.

economy.color_dependency: Mono-Green identity (character_colors=[0]). Green-specific pips on shinra2 (1) and shinra3 (2); rest random. Ignition reduces Green requirement by 1 on both damage skills, easing the only color tax. Light, single-color dependency.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Strong tempo: Rapid Kick has cd 0 (spammable), Ignition cd 1, Tora Hishigi cd 2, Adolla Burst cd 4. Can apply a DoT stack nearly every turn.
economy.ramp_dependency: High. Direct numbers are weak; the kit only becomes threatening through accumulated permanent affliction stacks over many turns. Wants Ignition up before each attack — costs a free action and a turn of setup until the shinra5 passive automates it.

soft_cc: Rapid Kick: taunt 1 turn

internal_synergies: Ignition: Shinra (free, cd 1) is the linchpin: it both cuts Green cost AND enables the permanent affliction stamp on Rapid Kick / Tora Hishigi.
Because Ignition must be re-cast (extra_usable blocks while marked, mark only lasts 1 self-turn), the loop is Ignition -> attack each turn until the passive automates it.
Hysterical Strength (passive) auto-reapplies Ignition on every Harmful skill once below 40 HP, removing the setup tax and letting Shinra attack + stack every turn freely.
Affliction stacks are per_stack and remove_on_death=false, so focusing one enemy compounds DoT and persists through revives/cleanse-resistant deathmark interactions.
Adolla Burst invuln buys survival turns to keep stacking; pairs with the low-HP passive as a comeback survival package.
Stun + taunt give per-attack tempo control while DoT does the real work.
strengths: Affliction DoT bypasses DR, barriers, and shields — extremely effective vs tanks/shield comps.
Permanent, stackable, non-death-clearing DoT gives an unbounded scaling ceiling on a focused target.
Cheap mono-Green economy with cost reduction baked into the gating buff; Rapid Kick is free-flowing (cd 0).
Has both hard-cc (stun) and soft-cc (taunt) plus an invuln panic button — solid self-contained utility.
Built-in low-HP comeback passive that automates the engine when he's most pressured.
weaknesses: No AoE whatsoever — purely single-target; DoT is wasted/split if forced to spread.
Very low burst (25/40 Normal); slow to actually kill — relies on a long game to win.
Ramp is fragile: cleanse/affliction-removal or killing the marked enemy before stacks mature resets his only real damage.
Setup tax pre-passive: must spend Ignition (an action) before each attack to stack, costing tempo.
No healing, no team support, no shields — selfish, fragile bruiser; can be bursted before the engine comes online.
Affliction at 5/hit is slow; against burst comps or short games he underperforms.
win_conditions: Focus-fire one enemy across many turns, stacking permanent affliction until DoT alone outpaces their sustain.
Survive into the late game (invuln + low-HP passive) and let the auto-Ignition engine grind affliction onto priority targets.
Use stun/taunt to control the tempo while the unbounded DoT ramp closes out tanky or shield-heavy compositions.

power_assessment.reasoning: A coherent, well-designed ramp/DoT bruiser with a clear identity and a strong niche (affliction bypasses all mitigation, so he hard-counters tanks/shields). But in isolation he is held back by weak direct numbers (40 peak, no AoE), a slow 5/hit ramp, and dependence on a setup loop and a long game. The permanent non-clearing stackable affliction gives a genuinely high scaling ceiling, and the low-HP passive that automates the engine is a smart comeback mechanic — these lift him above mediocre. He is matchup-polarized: oppressive vs shield/tank comps and grindy games, but soft against burst/cleanse and in short fights. Lands squarely mid-tier.

role: Single-target combo striker / whole-team taunt-tank with rotating stun-silence lockdown; a cheap beginner control/support anchor rather than a damage carry
signature_mechanic: Rotational self-buff combo system: each of the three basic strikes (Kick/Mascot Rush/Rampage) deals 15 and marks Shiro so that her OTHER two damaging skills gain +10 damage AND a rider effect (stun non-strategic / silence / self stun+silence-immunity) for 1 turn. Ganta Fight Song is a permanent taunt channel that banks one Ganta Fever stack per turn; the Ganta Fever passive consumes a stack to extend the active combo buff from ~1 turn to ~3 turns, letting Shiro maintain the +10/rider buff across multiple strikes.

abilities.name: Shiro Kick
abilities.conditional_scaling: Base 15; deals 25 if Shiro is currently marked by Mascot Rush or Shiro Rampage (their +10 damage_mod boost). The buff Kick itself applies empowers her OTHER two skills, not itself.
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Normal dmg. Applies self-mark + damage_mod_effect(+10) tagged to Mascot Rush & Shiro Rampage for ~1 turn (extends to ~3 turns if a Ganta Fever stack is consumed). While the mark is up, those two skills also stun the target's non-Strategic skills for 1 turn (stun_effect(2) with Strategic exclusion).

abilities.name: Mascot Rush
abilities.conditional_scaling: Base 15; deals 25 if marked by Shiro Kick or Shiro Rampage. If Shiro Kick's mark is active, also applies stun (non-Strategic) to target for 1 turn.
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Normal dmg. Applies self-mark + damage_mod_effect(+10) tagged to Shiro Kick & Shiro Rampage (~1 turn, ~3 with Fever). While the mark is up, those two skills additionally Silence the target for 1 turn (silence_effect(2)).

abilities.name: Shiro Rampage
abilities.conditional_scaling: Base 15; deals 25 if marked by Shiro Kick or Mascot Rush. On execute, if Kick-marked it also stuns the target, if Mascot-marked it also silences the target.
abilities.effects_summary: 15 Normal dmg. Applies self-mark + damage_mod_effect(+10) tagged to Shiro Kick & Mascot Rush (~1 turn, ~3 with Fever). While the mark is up, those two skills grant Shiro ignore-STUN and ignore-SILENCE (self CC immunity, ~1 turn). Execute also stuns target if Kick-marked and/or silences target if Mascot-marked.

abilities.name: Ganta Fight Song
abilities.conditional_scaling: Ganta Fever stacks accrue 1 per turn channeled (uncapped) and are spent by the passive to extend combo buffs from ~1 to ~3 turns. The AI custom_behavior simulates 10 AoE damage but execute() deals NO actual damage.
abilities.effects_summary: Permanent (duration -1) taunt on the ENTIRE enemy team, forcing them to target Shiro. Self vulnerability_effect(+5 incoming damage) and a per-turn TICKING_TRIGGER granting 1 Ganta Fever stack each turn. Channeled with channel_cancel hook. No damage. Tradeoff: redirects all enemy fire to Shiro while ramping her combo-extension resource.

abilities.name: Ganta Fever
abilities.conditional_scaling: get_fever_duration(): base buff duration 3; if at least 1 Ganta Fever stack present, consumes 1 stack and returns 7 (extends combo buff from ~1 turn to ~3 turns).
abilities.effects_summary: Passive. When a damaging skill is used, consumes one Ganta Fever stack to extend that skill's combo improvement mark/boost from duration 3 to 7. Enables sustained +10 / rider uptime across multiple strikes. Stacks are banked by channeling Ganta Fight Song.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Hard-capped at 25 per strike (15 base + 10 combo boost). The boost is a flat +10, not stacking, so there is no escalating damage ceiling — Ganta Fever only extends DURATION of the +10, never its magnitude. Across a full uptime rotation she outputs ~25/turn single-target with a stun/silence rider attached.
damage_profile.notes: All damage is Normal type (no barrier/DR bypass). She does ZERO AoE damage despite shiro4 being an ALL-target ability — it is a pure taunt/ramp channel (the 10 AoE in custom_behavior is only an AI scoring hint, not real damage). Reaching 25 requires a prior setup turn (one of the three strikes must mark Shiro before the next benefits). Effective opening turn is just 15. One action/turn, so 25 is the true single-turn ceiling.

economy.color_dependency: None — character_colors is empty [] and all four visible skills cost Random:1. Fully color-agnostic; fits any energy economy. A hallmark of a 'beginner' flagged character (beginner = true in char def).
economy.cooldown_tempo: Extremely fast. Three core strikes are cost 1 / cooldown 0 and can be cast every turn. Only Ganta Fight Song has a cooldown (3) but it is a permanent channel so it is rarely re-cast.
economy.ramp_dependency: Soft. Full +10 uptime relies on Ganta Fever stacks banked by channeling Ganta Fight Song (1/turn). Without channeling, the +10/rider buff only lasts ~1 turn, so she must alternate strikes to keep it live (each strike re-marks for the next). Damage is not gated behind ramp, but sustained rider/lockdown is.

hard_cc: stun (non-Strategic skills only, 1 turn, via empowered Mascot Rush/Rampage)
silence (1 turn, via empowered Kick/Rampage)
permanent taunt on entire enemy team (Ganta Fight Song)
soft_cc: taunt (redirect all enemy targeting to Shiro, permanent while channeled)
invuln_or_counter: self ignore-stun + ignore-silence (CC immunity, ~1 turn, granted by empowered skills under Shiro Rampage's mark)

power_assessment.reasoning: A coherent, low-cost beginner control/tank hybrid with a clever self-marking combo loop, but numerically modest. Strengths: dirt-cheap (4 random pips total, zero color dependency), cooldown-free spammable strikes, and meaningful control density — she can apply a 1-turn non-Strategic stun AND a 1-turn silence on the same target while granting herself stun/silence immunity, all stapled onto 25 damage. The permanent full-team taunt is genuinely disruptive: it can lock an entire enemy team into hitting Shiro, neutering their target selection, while she banks Ganta Fever to keep her combo riders live. Weaknesses cap her: damage is low (15 base, 25 empowered, no scaling beyond the flat +10), all Normal type so fully blocked by barriers/DR, and she has NO sustain/shields/heal — the taunt actively pulls fire onto her AND adds +5 vulnerability, so without external protection she is a liability tank that dies. The combo also has a ramp tax: the +10 and the rider only matter on the SECOND strike of a chain, so her opening turn is a vanilla 15, and she must keep re-marking. Control is real but soft — stun only hits non-Strategic skills (can't lock strategic/channel users), and durations are short (1 turn). She is a solid support-control glue piece who needs a healer/shielder backline to function, not a carry. Lands squarely average.

self-inflicted +5 vulnerability while taunting whole team is a notable anti-synergy without external healing/shields
stun rider only affects non-Strategic skills, a meaningful restriction on its CC value

role: control/disruption specialist — single-target mind-control that stuns and steals the enemy's entire kit
signature_mechanic: Mental Out: stun an enemy and temporarily replace all 4 of Shokuhou's own skills with copies of that enemy's full active kit (at a 1-Random discount). The "Exterior" mark extends the next skill's duration by +4 (2 enemy turns), turning a 1-turn stun-and-steal into a 3-turn lockout and prolonged control of the stolen kit.

abilities.name: Mental Out
abilities.conditional_scaling: If Shokuhou is marked by Exterior, stun+copy duration goes from 3 (1 turn) to 7 (3 turns); consumes the Exterior mark.
abilities.effects_summary: Stuns target enemy for duration 3 (until end of Shokuhou's next turn). Copies all 4 of the target's active abilities onto Shokuhou's action bar for that duration (replacing her own skills), and grants her -1 Random energy cost on those copied skills. With Exterior mark: duration 7 (3 turns). No damage. Hard CC + full kit theft.

abilities.name: Plan to Lose
abilities.conditional_scaling: Exterior mark extends trigger window from duration 2 (1 turn) to 6 (3 turns). Retaliation only fires if Mental Out is off cooldown.
abilities.effects_summary: Invisible anti-stun trigger on self or target ally for 1 turn: if that character would be Stunned, they are fully cleansed of all enemy effects instead, and Shokuhou auto-casts Mental Out (stun + full skill copy) on the enemy that triggered it (if Mental Out is off cooldown). Stun-immunity counter + cleanse + reactive control.

abilities.name: Exterior
abilities.conditional_scaling: Cannot be used while already marked by Exterior. Sets up the +4 duration scaling for the next Mental Out / Plan to Lose / Subordinate Protection.
abilities.effects_summary: Self-buff/setup: Shokuhou takes 10 Affliction self-damage (bypasses her own DR/shields) and raises the cost of ALL her skills by +1 White until she uses a new skill. Applies the permanent 'Exterior' mark that makes her next skill last +4 duration (2 extra enemy turns). No enemy interaction; pure amplifier.

abilities.name: Subordinate Protection
abilities.conditional_scaling: Exterior mark extends invuln from duration 2 (1 turn) to 6 (3 turns); consumes the mark.
abilities.effects_summary: Self becomes Invulnerable for 1 turn (duration 2). With Exterior mark active: 3 turns of invulnerability. Panic button / survivability tool; protects the fragile controller while her stolen kit / stuns play out.

damage_profile.scaling_ceiling: Essentially no innate damage — only 10 Affliction of self-damage from Exterior. Her 'damage' ceiling is entirely borrowed: Mental Out copies the target's full kit, so her offensive output equals whatever the stolen enemy can do (potentially very high if she steals a burst carry), turned back against the enemy team for 1-3 turns.
damage_profile.notes: Profiled in isolation Shokuhou deals 0 direct damage to enemies. The only damage number in her kit is the 10 Affliction self-hit on Exterior. Her threat is control + theft, not raw damage; she scales off the opponent's kit rather than her own.

economy.color_dependency: Light White dependency: 2 of 4 visible skills (Mental Out, Subordinate Protection) need 1 White each; the other two take 1 Random. As a single-color [White] character her kit is cheap and easy to fuel. Exterior temporarily spikes ALL skill costs by +1 White until she acts again, creating a brief White tax while ramping.
economy.cooldown_tempo: Low cooldowns: Mental Out 2, Exterior 2, Plan to Lose 3, Subordinate Protection 3. Mental Out being on a 2-turn CD means near-constant stun/steal pressure. All skills cost only 1 pip, so she is extremely energy-efficient.
economy.ramp_dependency: Soft ramp via the Exterior mark: to get the powerful 3-turn versions of her stun, counter, or invuln she must spend a turn (and 10 self-HP + a temporary +1 White cost on everything) setting up Exterior first. Functional without it (1-turn baseline), but her ceiling requires the 2-step Exterior -> payoff sequence.

hard_cc: Stun (Mental Out, 1 turn base / 3 turns with Exterior)
Reactive Stun via Plan to Lose counter
soft_cc: Full skill replacement on enemy — steals/locks the enemy's entire kit for the stun duration
invuln_or_counter: Invulnerability (Subordinate Protection, 1 turn / 3 turns with Exterior)
Stun-immunity counter that cleanses and retaliates (Plan to Lose)

win_conditions: Lock down the enemy's key threat with Mental Out on repeat (2-turn CD), keeping it stunned while denying its skills.
Set up Exterior -> Mental Out for a 3-turn stun + 3-turn theft of a carry's entire kit, swinging tempo decisively.
Use the stolen enemy abilities to deal damage / apply control the enemy team has no answer to (turn their own carry against them).
Stall safely behind Plan to Lose (stun-immune + cleanse + counter) and Subordinate Protection invuln while allies win the damage race.
internal_synergies: Exterior is the universal amplifier — its mark turns the next Mental Out (3-turn stun + 3-turn skill theft), Plan to Lose (3-turn counter window), or Subordinate Protection (3-turn invuln) into a far stronger version.
Plan to Lose auto-casts Mental Out, chaining her stun/steal off any enemy stun attempt without spending a turn — strong anti-CC tech that also feeds her signature mechanic.
Low cooldowns + 1-pip costs let her cycle Exterior -> payoff every couple turns, sustaining the ramp.
Subordinate Protection covers the turn after Exterior's self-damage and cost tax, protecting the fragile setup.
strengths: Premier single-target lockdown: a 2-CD stun that ALSO steals the target's whole kit is one of the strongest disruption packages in the game.
Borrowed scaling — her effective power tracks the strongest enemy she can steal from, so she punches up against carries hard.
Very cheap and color-flexible (all 1-pip, only mono-White dependency).
Robust self-defense: stun-immunity + cleanse + reactive stun (Plan to Lose) and full invulnerability (Subordinate Protection), both extendable to 3 turns.
Anti-CC counter shuts down enemy stun strategies and turns them into a free Mental Out.
weaknesses: Zero innate damage — entirely dependent on stolen kits or teammates to actually close out a game; can be a passenger if she can't steal anything useful.
Ramp tax: the strong 3-turn versions require spending a turn on Exterior, plus 10 Affliction self-damage and a temporary +1 White cost on everything.
Fragile (no shields/heals on herself beyond timed invuln); if invuln/Plan to Lose are down she is exposed.
All control is single-target — no AoE, struggles against wide/swarm comps where stunning one enemy isn't enough.
Stealing a low-value or already-spent enemy kit wastes Mental Out's huge upside; value is matchup-dependent.
Self-damage from Exterior bypasses her own mitigation (Affliction), chipping her already-thin survivability.

power_assessment.reasoning: Profiled in isolation, Shokuhou is a high-impact control specialist rather than a damage dealer. A 1-pip, 2-cooldown hard stun that simultaneously copies the enemy's entire active kit is an unusually strong disruption-plus-utility package, and the Exterior mark scales it to a 3-turn lockout + 3-turn theft. She also has a clean defensive suite (extendable invuln, stun-immune cleanse + reactive Mental Out). What holds her below the top tier in a vacuum is that she deals essentially no damage of her own (only 10 Affliction self-damage) and depends on having a worthwhile kit to steal and on teammates to convert her control into kills; she is also fragile and single-target only. Net: a strong, tempo-warping support/controller whose real value is highly matchup- and team-dependent.

power_assessment.reasoning: Soul is a well-designed support/enabler with a clean identity but modest standalone power. His personal damage is locked at 30 Affliction/turn and is self-harming, so his value is almost entirely externalized into a partner buff that ramps slowly. Upsides: cheap fast kit (CD1 nuke + free CD1 heal), shield/DR-bypassing Affliction, a genuinely strong AoE Strategic-delay (soft CC vs setup comps), self-sustain, 10% DR, and color-cost smoothing for an ally. Downsides: no hard CC, no ally protection, no energy denial, slow gated ramp, and a hard dependency on a partner (ideally Maka) to mitigate his self-damage and carry his buff. In isolation he reads as a B-tier role-player: high floor, modest ceiling, swingy on team composition. Rated 5/10 standalone; could climb meaningfully in a dedicated Maka duo, drop in solo contexts.

His ceiling is high specifically against defensive metas — Piercing everywhere, shield shatter, permanent Shatter, and a Bypassing DoT make him a clean hard-counter to tanks, shielders, and invuln/regen comps, while his low cooldowns give relentless tempo with no ramp required. abilities.name: Skull Bash
abilities.effects_summary: 20 single-target physical damage; reduces the cooldown of 'Withdraw' by 1 turn. Spammable basic that feeds the Withdraw defensive cycle and the Thug Life passive.
abilities.conditional_scaling: +5 damage from Thug Life passive if Squirtle cast a new skill on an enemy the prior turn (consecutive). Peak 25.

abilities.name: Water Gun
abilities.effects_summary: 20 single-target energy damage AND applies a debuff that prevents the target from reducing damage or becoming invulnerable for 1 turn (anti-tank / DR-and-invuln denial). Cannot be used during Withdraw. The non-damage debuff gains +1 turn duration for every consecutive turn it is reapplied to the SAME enemy (stacking lockdown).
abilities.conditional_scaling: Debuff duration ramps +1 turn per consecutive same-target cast; damage +5 from Thug Life passive when consecutive (peak 25). No damage scaling on the lock itself.

abilities.name: Bubblebeam
abilities.effects_summary: Ongoing 3-turn AoE: deals 5 piercing damage to all enemies each turn, PLUS an extra 5 piercing to any enemy that uses a new skill that turn (punishes acting/aggression). Piercing skips flat and % DR. Becomes 'Hydro Pump' (alt) while Withdraw is active.
